planEntities.name: 2.8.0 BDS Capacities enhanced and meaningful youth engagement supported to promote inclusive and peaceful ​Caribbean SIDS.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntities.description:
Young people in the Caribbean have a significant contribution to make to promoting sustainable development. Creating an environment that is conducive and supportive of youth-led action and youth participation contributes to overall positive social development in the sub-region. 

Young people have been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities derived from increased inequalities of income and opportunity. Nevertheless, despite these difficulties, youth have been at the forefront, helping their communities overcome challenges caused by the pandemic. SHS supports countries in the Caribbean to prioritize actions and policies that build on the potential of youth and address their needs to allow them to exercise their rights.
This sub-outputs aims at: 
- Strengthened capacities of public officials from CARICOM Member States to apply the principles of meaningful youth engagement in programming and policy. 
- Joint action plan developed to advance the YPS agenda in the English and Dutch-speaking Caribbean. 
- Coordination mechanism created to follow-up on this action plan, including considering the launch of a YPS regional coalition. 
- Strengthened Network of Directors for improved knowledge sharing and exchange on youth engagement. 
-Strengthened capacities of Caribbean youth-led organizations on gender equality and advocacy by developing tools for young people to develop their own project ideas and drive social change in their communities.

planEntities.description: This program is designed to improve the well-being, resilience, and protection of migrants, with a focus on those vulnerable to violence, exploitation, and abuse—particularly women, children, and victims of trafficking. It aims to achieve this through the enhancement of national and community-based systems that are more integrated, modernized, and effective. Building on strong partnerships with both government and civil society, the initiative aligns with the Global Compact for Migration's principles of a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach. By strengthening the capacity of various stakeholders and reinforcing their cooperation, the project seeks to create a more coordinated and comprehensive support network for migrants in need.

planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 3.1: Increased capacity to produce sustainable development data and use it for evidence-informed policy-making and legislation
planEntities.description:
Level of UNICEF support to Government to improve the availability and quality of child-related and quality of child-related Sustainable Development Goal indicators is being implemented. The extent is an index will be measured by the following indicators: 
1) Country Office has collaborated with the government to conduct a full Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) or any other household survey which includes at least 20 child-related SDG indicators. 
2) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) the strengthening of national routine/administrative data systems of individual sectors as well as cross sectoral interoperability.
3) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) government efforts to strengthen the overall national statistical system regarding data about children, in alignment with national statistical master plans, or the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics during the reporting year
 4) Extent to which the Country Office supported the inclusion of statistical data for children in planning documents prepared by the government (including sectoral and sub-national ones) and Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) of SDG implementation during the reporting year 
5) Extent to which the Country Office supported good data governance standards regarding data for children (including Responsible Data for Children principles, Ethical Framework for Evidence Generation, Data Quality Framework) and the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics.

planEntities.description:
This activity focuses on two main data points:
A. The extent to which Belize's Health Sector policy/plan (or equivalent guidance document) includes the provision of the following services for the prevention and management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents in Primary Health Care:
1) Promotion of Health Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
2) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
3) Management of neglected tropical diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
4) Screening and interventions on substance abuse in children and adolescents.
B. Health-related interventions for the prevention and management of non-communicable diseases implemented with UNICEF support
1) Use of Primary Health care platform (including by Community Health Workers) to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
2) Use of School Health platform to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
3) Use of Digital platforms to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
4) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs) at primary health care and referral facilities
4) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs) at primary health care and referral facilities
6) Prevention and management of neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
7) Screening and interventions on substance abuse in children and adolescents

planEntities.description:
The mission of the UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) is to build capacity in countries seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security, and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods. The UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) was established as a joint initiative of the UNODC and the WCO in 2004. Faced with such a complex and globalized problem, the CCP embraces a nuanced, holistic and multi-sectoral approach by providing continuous monitoring and oversight, offering a plethora of context-specific training programmes and strengthening cooperation between state agencies and with the private sector. The mission of the CCP is to build capacity in Member States seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods.

At present, the CCP is operational in over 70 Member States. More than 120 Port Control Units (PCUs) and Air Cargo Control Units (ACCUs) have been established since the CCP's inception in 2004. These inter-agency units are equipped to exchange information with their counterparts in other countries using a secure communication application, developed by the WCO, called ContainerComm. This provides PCUs and ACCUs with access to a wealth of information, allowing users to share information about high-risk containers and verify their identification numbers.

The CCP Programme is currently under implementation in the Port of Georgetown in Guyana. In 2022, capacity building programmes to support enhanced profiling of containers was carried for the benefit of the PCU in Georgetown, including exchange programmes with the Port of Hamburg in Germany and other PCUs in the Caribbean basin. UNODC also provided additional of safety and search equipment to the Georgetown PCU. Study visits to Germany port of Hamburg.

planEntities.name: TTO – UNODC Global Programme on Cybercrime: Trinidad and Tobago has increased capacity to identify, investigate, prosecute and adjudicate online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
UNODC’s Global Programme on Cybercrime is designed to respond flexibly to identified needs in developing countries by supporting Member States to prevent and combat cybercrime in a holistic manner.  The key objectives of this programme are:
•	Increased efficiency and effectiveness in the investigation, prosecution and adjudication of cybercrime, especially online child sexual exploitation and abuse, within a strong human-rights framework;
•	Efficient and effective long-term whole-of-government response to cybercrime, including national coordination, data collection and effective legal frameworks, leading to a sustainable response and greater deterrence;
•	Strengthened national and international communication between government, law enforcement and the private sector with increased public knowledge of cybercrime risks.

In 2022, UNODC launched the Project “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes” under the Global Cybercrime Project of UNODC. This project is funded by the Government of Canada and will be implemented until December 2024. The project aims to enhance the capacity of Trinidad and Tobago to identify, investigate, prosecute, adjudicate and prevent online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
Capacity building includes:
•	Cybercrime and digital evidence basics, proactive online investigations: using specialized platforms, such as CPS or ICACCOPS, to detect in real time the distribution of online child sexual exploitation material;
•	Train the trainer workshop in reactive online investigations: using platforms, such as the CyberTipline reporting mechanism, to receive reports from foreign technology companies on cases of online child sexual exploitation;
•	Open-source intelligence applied in investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes;
•	Identifying and handling digital evidence;
•	Criminal investigations involving the dark web, cryptocurrencies, for example.

Likewise, the Project will also facilitate the provision of specialized equipment for identifying, acquiring, analysing, and preserving digital evidence for the units responsible for investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes, as well as activities to support to Civil Society, prevention, and cooperation.
In 2022, the following activities were conducted:
-	17th October 2022- Project Launch “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes”. Organized by UNODC in collaboration with: Attorney General and Minister of Legal Affairs of T&T; Commissioner of Police; CARICOM IMPACS, International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), and the donor Canada. With the participation of 15 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.

Organized by UNODC in collaboration with International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), with the participation of 16 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.

planEntities.name: TTO UNODC TRACK4TIP: Key institutions and relevant stakeholders are strengthened to support the enhanced identification, investigation and prosecution of cases of human trafficking, from a victim-centered approach.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
Justice responses to combat trafficking in persons in migration flows (TRACK4TiP).

TRACK4TIP initiative is a four-year (2019-2023), initiative by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and supported by the United States Department of State. The project is being implemented and reaches eight countries across South America and the Caribbean with actions at the national and regional level among Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Trinidad and Tobago, Curaçao and Aruba.

TRACK4TiP aims to enhance the regional criminal justice response to human trafficking among migration flows within the beneficiary countries following a victim-centered and multidisciplinary approach working at the regional and local levels to identify, prevent and prosecute cases.

To achieve this, TRACK4TIP proposes the implementation of seven main activities organized under three specific objectives that together make it easier for each of the eight beneficiary countries to achieve the main objective of strengthening their criminal justice response in cases of trafficking in persons involving Venezuelan victims migrating in the region.

Objective 1- Capacity Building

To improve victim identification and national referral mechanisms at the country level to better identify and safely report human trafficking cases in the context of migration flows at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities in beneficiary countries.

Activity 1
Enhancement of identification and referral mechanisms at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities in beneficiary countries to safely report human trafficking cases.

Activity 2
A Capacity Building strategy on the use of the National Referral mechanisms to safely report human trafficking cases at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities.

Objective 2 - Knowledge and research

Provide law enforcement and prosecuting authorities in beneficiary countries with reliable information on the modus operandi of criminal networks or individuals that are associated with human trafficking among populations migrating within the region.

Activity 3
Country narratives on the context, investigations, and prosecutions for human trafficking cases at ports of entry, transit points, and destination communities among migration flows.

Activity 4
A Sub-regional Threat Assessment on the current context, dynamics, and trends of human trafficking cases among migration flows involving Venezuelans.

Objective 3 – International Coordination and Cooperation
Promote at the national and regional level, new investigations and prosecutions for human trafficking cases among migration flow involving Venezuelans establishing liaison between National coordination mechanisms and law enforcement agencies and prosecutors with authority to investigate and prosecute TIP at beneficiary countries.

Activity 5
Promotion of current networks and task forces to enhance coordination of law enforcement agencies, prosecutors, and national coordination mechanisms.

Activity 6

planEntities.name: TTO UNODC Global Programme on Money Laundering: Member States have increased capacity to identify, investigate and prosecute money laundering, including Trade Based Money Laundering
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
The UNODC Global Programme against Money Laundering, Proceeds of Crime and Financing of Terrorism (GPML), with the financial support of the Government of Canada, is implementing a three-year capacity building programme on trade-based money laundering (henceforth referred to as ‘the Programme’) for 13 beneficiary countries in the Caribbean and Central America. 

The goals of the Programme are to (i) raise awareness of the public security threats stemming from TBML and (ii) strengthen the capacities of law enforcement and prosecutorial authorities to detect, investigate and prosecute money laundering through trade more effectively. The Programme comprises a series of capacity building activities – national and regional workshops, free trade zones (FTZ) training, development of TBML e-learning modules, and mentoring. 

Based on the findings from the initial fact-finding exercise and the scoping missions conducted in the beneficiary countries in 2019, UNODC GPML developed the concept & methodology paper to deliver the TBML national workshops in Central America and the Caribbean. According to the latter, UNODC GPML adopted a twofold approach for the national TBML workshops: 
i	building capacities through the simulation of a real-life TBML case, and 
ii	presenting the relevant techniques, tools and methods contextualised in the case scenario, which allow the participants to learn and use them more effectively. 
Based on the goals and adopted approach of the Programme, the objectives of the national TBML workshops are as follows: 

•	Provide the participants with the understanding, knowledge and tools required to identify, investigate, and prosecute TBML. 
•	Show the importance of national and international cooperation and coordination for the effective detection, investigation, and prosecution of TBML. 
•	Identify the principal sources of information required for the detection, investigation, and prosecution of TBML. 
•	Link the financial investigation parallel to the criminal investigation to cut the illicit benefits generated from money laundering and its predicate offences. 
•	Build capacities through a learning-by-doing methodology by simulating a real-life TBML case. 

In 2022, GPML provided training to 27 practitioners from Law Enforcement Agencies in Trinidad and Tobago including: Customs, the Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs), Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS), Revenue Administration, intelligence authorities, and the Offices of the Directors of Public Prosecutions on the identification and investigation of trade-based money laundering.

planEntities.name: TTO Airport Communication Programme (AIRCOP) is a collaboration between UNODC – WCO – INTERPOL: Strengthened institutional capacities for the identification, investigation and interception of transnational organized crime at international airports.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
As outlined in the UNODC Strategic Vision for Latin America and the Caribbean, a more harmonized approach to continue supporting Member States on the implementation of specialized cross-border approaches that have demonstrated positive results on detection and interdiction of illegal Trafficking. 
AIRCOP is a  multi agency project based on the cooperation between  UNODC,  INTERPOL and  the World Customs Organisations (WCO) that aims at  strengthening the capacities of participating  international airports in Africa, Latin America, the Caribbean and the Middle East to  detect and intercept drugs, other illicit goods (including firearms, their parts and ammunition) and high-risk passengers (including victims of trafficking in persons and foreign terrorist fighters) in origin, transit and destination countries with the overall objective of  disrupting the illegal criminal networks. 
The increased capacity and knowledge of trained personnel has led to the expansion of the project scope to cover the multiple  threats targeting airports, including all illicit drugs, illicit goods (such as wildlife, counterfeit medicines or weapons) and, as of late, terrorism and trafficking in persons.
In 2022, UNODC signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Government of Trinidad and Tobago for the implementation of the AIRCOP Programme at the Piarco International Airport in Port-of-Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. To date, 8 vetted officers from the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS), the Immigration Department, the Customs Agency have been assigned to form the AIRCOP Task Force.
AIRCOP provides a range of standard and specialized training and mentoring activities, tailored tonational and regional needs. Topics covered include intelligence collection and sharing, targeting, search techniques, counterfeit documents, behavioral analysis, use ofl aw enforcement databases, secure communication procedures and post-seizure investigations, as well as specific thematic issues.
In 2022, UNODC facilitated training for the AIRCOP Task Force in the following areas:
-	AIRCOP Introductory Training
-	AIRCOP Training on Integrity in Law Enforcement
-	AIRCOP Training on Gender and Human Rights in Law Enforcement
-	Specialized Training on the Safe Handling of Synthetic Opiods, use of Raman Drug Testing Devices and Drug Precursor Kits
-	Specialized Training on Intelligence and Data (API and Passenger data)
-	Specialized Training on the Use of the WCO CENComm Platform
-	Exchange of Best Practices amongst AIRCOP JAITFs in Barbados, Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago
Likewise, retrofitting and equipping of the AIRCOP working room was also carried out in 2022. One Raman Drug Testing Device was delivered to the AIRCOP Team for the Identification and Detection of Illicit Substances.

planEntities.description: The Sint Maarten Rule of Law Facilities project supports the design, construction and supervision of resilient, sustainable and effective detention infrastructure, including the long-term redevelopment of Point Blanche Prison and the temporary retrofit of the Simpson Bay Immigration Facility to provide additional detention capacity during construction. planEntities.description: Provide technical cooperation to develop and strengthen national policies, plans, and regulatory systems; and to implement improved health technologies. planEntities.description: Provide technical cooperation to strengthen emergency preparedness and IHR capacities. Specific areas for health emergencies are responding to and controlling the COVID-19 pandemic, documenting after action reviews of COVID-19 response at the national level, delivering training on health EOCs and operational response plans (including incident management systems and national health emergency risk management programs) and event-based surveillance, conducting inter-sectoral simulation exercises involving national authorities, preparing national report on the status of emergency risk management and preparedness in the health sector, developing guidelines to facilitate emergency-related data analysis and reporting, and disseminating health emergency data management systems and GIS maps. Specific areas for IHR are implementing training for national focal points and conducting voluntary external evaluation of national core capacities.

planEntities.name: TTO Support the development and implementation of eco-based solutions (BIOREACH)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
1. Community mapping exercises; identification of economic/agricultural activities and location, demarcation of residential use from agriculture and development uses; identification of vulnerable areas; identification of current and projected use of land resources and how to manage them sustainably; identification of community level incentives for producing and implementing land use plan 
2. Develop a standardised agroecology curriculum for Lead Farmer Training Programme
3. Identify plots of land where diverse agroforestry can take place, and especially cocoa or coconut plantations that require rehabilitation.
4. Business planning support provided to interested farmers/farming households
5.Collect baseline socioeconomic data disaggregated by sex and age
6. Support ongoing research initiatives and testing resilient palms/trees for diseases.
7. Conduct phased rehabilitation of infected plantations, with agroforestry approach to avoid monoculture
8. Produce land degradation maps
9. Conduct ground truthing mission; determine what species exist at the site, which are at risk, patterns of movement/migration, human factors impacting habitats
10. Identify potential ecotourism/agritourism opportunities in established clusters and/or developing tourism opportunities in agricultural areas and estates
11. Review laws/institutional arrangements and regulations for forest and wildland fire management

Aquaculture Production and Harvesting
Engage and facilitate partnerships with development partners (eg UNDP, local NGOs) and public procurement institutions (eg schools, hospitals) to strengthen links between startups, mentoring services and established markets for aquaculture products.

Conduct trainings to strengthen the capacity of aquaculture farmers to adopt good agricultural practices


Crop Production and Harvesting (introduction of sustainability practices)

Provide training for farmers in production, post-harvest handling, food safety and market linkage.

To support demonstration plots for Good Agricultural Practices (including climate resilient agriculture).

Produce an updated Farmer Field Schools (FFS) manual that integrates the national school feeding program

Conduct Training of Trainers (ToT) with extension personnel using the principles of FFS

Develop a School Feeding Programme (SFP) Procurement guidelines for products from small farmers 

Coordinate and facilitate agreements for farmers/ farmers groups  to supply fresh produce to the SFP in at least six schools 

Support the design, training and maintenance of school gardens 

Review and revise national school feeding policy instruments

Assess and publish successful experiences of small farmers/farmer groups (with an emphasis on women and youth groups) which produce and sell healthy and local foods to the national SFP.

Support the review and update of menus, and review and development of standardized recipes to include products from small holder farmers

planEntities.description: The ILO supports Suriname in strengthening and reforming its social protection system toward a universal, adequate and financially sustainable Social Protection Floor. Following the adoption of key social legislation, the ILO assisted the Government in conducting a Comprehensive Review of the social protection system, assessing existing schemes and identifying reform priorities in line with Convention No. 102, Recommendation No. 202 and SDG 1.3. The review informed the development of a National Social Protection Strategy and Action Plan through an inclusive consultation process that strengthened national capacities and social dialogue. Ongoing ILO support includes technical assistance, expert advice, training and advocacy, with attention to gender equality and institutional coordination. (Suriname, DWCP)

planEntities.description: As labour markets in The Bahamas continue to recover from the ongoing effects of multiple crises including Hurricane Dorian and the COVID-19 pandemic, strengthening the employability of persons has emerged as a key national priority.  To address the issue directly, apprenticeships have been defined as a key outcome of The Bahamas second Decent Work Country Programme (DWCP) for The Bahamas, which is being implemented between 2021 and 2026. The first priority of the DWCP, Jobs and Skills, focuses on equipping the workforce with skills that respond to constantly evolving labour market needs and challenges. It gives special attention to marginalized groups including youth, women, and Family Islanders.

planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 5.2: National and regional institutions have capacity, access to finance and can apply technologies to deliver on gender responsive disaster risk reduction, climate adaptation and mitigation
planEntities.description:
A transformation of an Island into a smart island can improve the provision of services in the following sectors: Health: the deployment of telemedicine and e-health services for delivery of efficient services, improving access to diagnosis and care, while also reducing the cost for the healthcare system. Education: the access to open and distance learning opportunities will enable capacity building for teachers and education administrators; equitable access to quality literacy, lifelong learning and skills programmes for children, youth and adults. Agriculture: e-Agriculture services can support efficient and productive farming capabilities among farmers, making rural communities more resilient from both economic and nutritional point of view. planEntities.name: 1.7 BDS REG The SMART FARMS Project supports environmentally sustainable agriculture in farming across the drought-stricken region.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 2.2: National and regional institutions capacity is strengthened to accelerate transition to diversified, resilient and inclusive food systems economies
planEntities.description:
The SMART FARMS Project is aimed to develop environmentally sustainable agriculture in farming across the drought-stricken region. The programme consists of developing and utilizing affordable smart water management throughout IICA’s agriculture programs. The sensors will enable farmers to determine the water needs of crops and monitor the water used in farming. Gender equality will also be addressed as the project considers the inequalities faced by women in a male dominated sector such as agriculture. 
Note that this Initiative invites partnership of UN Agencies and other partners and is still in Resource Mobilization phase.

planEntities.name: 1.10 BDS Quality of Service Review for Fixed Broadband Services in Barbados
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntities.description:
ITU and the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Smart Technology of Barbados has signed the partnership agreement on telecommunication and ICT services. The partnership aims to undertake a Quality of Service Review for Fixed Broadband Services in Barbados. 

This project will conduct a review and evaluate the current levels of quality of service (QoS) for Fixed Broadband Services throughout the country with a view to establish baseline of QoS parameters, implementing QoS standards as well as updating its regulatory framework related to Fixed Broadband Services. The review will include an audit of the fixed Broad Band Services (Internet services) being provided by the service providers in Barbados which will determine the current state of play as well as issues and recommendations for improving the level of fixed broadband QoS in Barbados. The Covid-19 pandemic has underscored the need for high quality of service in telecommunications across all sections but especially of significant importance for online education, health and the financial services sector.

planEntities.name: GUY SubOutput 7.3.1: 'Spotlight initiative' 'Partnership for Peace' - Batterer Intervention Programme
planEntities.parentName: GUY Output 7.3 Support provided to strengthen mechanisms and services for women, children experiencing violence/abuse
planEntities.description:
The Partnership for Peace (PfP) Programme is a court-based accountability programme which uses a psycho-educational approach to ensuring the prevention of continued violence against women on the part of men who are in the court system as perpetrators of domestic violence.  The Batterer Intervention programme is a standardized intervention developed by an expert group of human rights lawyers, clinical psychologists, social workers, and women’s rights advocates.
The programme is premised on basic principles that include the prioritization of the safety and protection of women victims of violence and the acknowledgement of accountability and responsibility by the perpetrator.  The key elements of the programme are:
•	Domestic abuse is conceptualized as part of “pattern of coercive control”.
•	Abuse is solely the responsibility of the perpetrator and survivors should never be blamed for abuse.
•	Counselling is not guaranteed to end the violence and that such intervention is not intended to salvage relationships.

planEntities.name: GUY SubOutput 8.1.3:  'Spotlight Initiative' 'Foundations Programme' - Roll out of Foundations Programme in schools and community-based settings
planEntities.parentName: GUY  Output 8.1 Support provided to national institutions and civil society to promote social norms and culture of non-violence and community engagement for achievement of all development results
planEntities.description:
The Foundations Programme seeks to address gender based violence (GBV) through prevention and targets young persons aged 13 to 24. The Programme is built on the premise that GBV and gender discrimination are influenced by choice, fueled by gender hierarchies and unequal gender relations. The main objectives of the Foundation Programme are as follows:
1. To empower young people to understand GBV and its genesis in gender inequalities and gender-based discrimination.
2. To promote an understanding of the consequences of GBV to partner(s), children, communities and societies in general.
3. To endow young people with knowledge, skills and attitudes for addressing conflict and responding to stress and stressors that arise in relationships.
4. To establish and model an atmosphere of respect within group relations among and between young people.
5. To promote self-sufficiency among young people in taking steps towards improving their relationships and their lives.
6. To create a network of young people who will advocate for non-violent relationships.

In light of the above objectives and reaching the beneficiary population, schools and community settings in Guyana will be targeted.

planEntities.description: The Technology Needs Assessment Project (GEF-6 #9452) was a global support project involving involving 24 countries (Caribbean SIDS: Antigua & Barbuda, Dominica, Jamaica, Suriname & Trinidad & Tobago). The TNA Project identified and prioritised technologies for climate change mitigation and adaptation in developing countries. Technology transfer in project countries is facilitated through improved Technology Needs Assessments and provides targeted financial and technical support to prepare new or updated and improved TNAs, including Technology Action Plans (TAPs), for 9 prioritized technologies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, support adaptation to climate change, in the agriculture and water management sectors. Countries conducted Barrier Analyses and Enabling Frameworks (BAEF) and prepared concept notes for prioritised actions (for GCF funding). Note that the Project was initially scheduled to end in 2022 but was granted extensions to 2023 (March and June variously) to allow countries (e.g. Suriname) time to complete activities.

planEntities.description: CReW+ is a partnership project funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and co-implemented by UNEP and the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) in 18 countries of the Wider Caribbean Region (WCR). The project is being executed by the Secretariat of the Cartagena Convention (CAR/RCU), the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, and the Organisation of the American States (OAS) on behalf of UNEP and the IDB respectively.  The Project will implement innovative technical small-scale solutions in the Wider Caribbean Region using an integrated water and wastewater management approach building on sustainable financing mechanisms piloted through the Caribbean Regional Fund for Wastewater Management (CReW).  The project includes watershed and freshwater basin protection, water conservation and efficiency, and water reuse, and will prioritize technologies for treating wastewater in rural and peri-urban areas that are replicable and sustainable.

It aims to ensure (i) that participating countries have established sustainable national procedures to gather information to put on the BCH, and (ii) that they have the expertise to use, access and participate efficiently to the BCH. planEntities.name: Antigua and Barbuda Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility Project
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The Project, "Supporting Antigua and Barbuda's Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility and transition" (GEF-7 #10281) addresses priorities to transition Antigua and Barbuda's transportation and energy sectors towards a low-carbon trajectory. Total allocation is $3,245,000. As a small island developing state (SIDS), Antigua and Barbuda’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions represent just 0.0015% of the world’s total. However, the country’s per capita GHG emissions are higher than those of Spain and France. Antigua and Barbuda’s biggest challenge is the energy sector, which, due to fossil fuel combustion activities, accounts for 76% of the country’s total emissions. These two sectors rely almost entirely on imported petroleum-based fuels. Electricity generation is responsible for close to 40% of total GHG emissions generated from heavy fuel oil thermal power plants and experiences high distribution grid inefficiencies. As a result, the emission intensity per MWh of the electricity consumed is around 1000 kg of CO2 per MWh generated, almost double the global average. The transport sub-sector is similarly problematic, with road transport accounting for more than 20% of total national GHG emissions. Under business as usual (BAU) conditions overall emissions are expected to rise considerably over the next decade, primarily due to increases in electricity demand and growth in individual transport usage. BAU estimations indicate that the private vehicle fleet could grow at an annual rate of 6.5% per year.  Project activities will put in motion the transformation of both the power and transport sectors of Antigua and Barbuda, transitioning these from the current scenario of fossil fuel dependence to a future where low-carbon and climate resilient technologies are predominant. The Project will strengthen and inform political and public support for the uptake of low-carbon and climate-resilient electric transport and power generation systems. Activities include: reducing technological, financial and modal barriers through technical assistance and investment in pilot projects; building local capacity in related areas; and implementing regulations, policies and standards to secure a sustainable transition into the future and avoid potential environmental contamination. The Project has been extended to 30 April 2027

planEntities.name: Improving Environmental Management through Sustainable Land Management in St. Kitts and Nevis
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Improving Environmental Management through Sustainable Land Management practices in St. Kitts and Nevis (GEF-6 #9785). The objective is to transform degraded forest landscapes into biodiversity and climate-friendly areas of sustainable agricultural/agro-forestry production that together can provide economic opportunities for the country’s population while also sustaining ecosystem services and globally significant biodiversity. There are 3 components: 1) Integrated and strengthened environmental planning and management to support island sustainability; 2) Mainstreaming of biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management and climate change mitigation into key development and resources management sectors; 3) Knowledge management and dissemination for Sustainable Land Management, Biodiversity, and Climate Change.  The Project has been extended to June 30, 2027.

planEntities.name: BAH Meeting the Challenge of 2020 in The Bahamas
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: National project GEF-6 (#9791) to manage and strengthen Marine Protected Areas in The Bahamas and integrate into broader landscape planning in order to reduce pressures on ecosystem services and biodiversity from competing resource uses. The Project is executed across 5 project sites which includes the MPAs: Andros West Side National Park (AWSNP), Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park (ECLSP), Moriah Harbor Cay National Park (MHCNP), Bonefish Pond National Park (BPNP), & Lucayan National Park (LNP).  Targeted activities include: ecosystem zoning plans; provision of infrastructure, staffing and equipment for all 5 MPAs; species conservation and monitoring plans developed and implemented for AWSNP, ECLSP, LNP, and MHCNP; pilot renewable energy installations and energy efficiency measures at BPNP, ECLSP and LNP; and engagement of farmers in agricultural areas bordering the MPAs. The Project commenced in 2020, was disrupted by COVID-19 and received extensions, with implications for rescheduling of activities and related expenditures in ensuing years. Project was scheduled for closure by May 2026, but has been granted an extension to 30 November 2028.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Resilience of Agricultural Lands and Forests in Dominica
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Strengthening Resilience of Agricultural Lands and Forests in Dominica in the Aftermath of Hurricane Maria (GEF-6 #9978) builds capacity to restore, rehabilitate and sustainably manage forest lands in the vicinity of the Morne Trois Piton National Park. It commenced in 2020 but was disrupted by the COVID-19 Pandemic. It comprises 3 Components: 1) Restoration and rehabilitation of denuded forest areas around Morne Trois Pitons National Park - to reforest and implement supporting measures and initiatives that promote restoration of ecosystem services and reduce land degradation; 2) Promotion of sustainable agriculture in areas around Morne Trois Pitons - promoting behavior change and adoption of sustainable agricultural practices by land users near the National Park; 3) Institutional strengthening, education and training to address land degradation - developing new policies and regulations to address land management practices identified in the wake of Hurricane Maria as contributing to the severity of negative impacts on ecological functioning, livelihoods, and human health and security. The Project has received extensions from delays related to COVID-19 impacts and other implementation challenges and has applied for a further extension. Project expenditures between 2020-2021 = $128,976.

planEntities.name: BAH Integrated Landscape Management for land degradation, food security and climate resilience in the Bahamas
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Integrated Landscape Management for Addressing Land Degradation, Food Security and Climate Resilience Challenges in The Bahamas (GEF-7 #10694). A national, technical assistance project to enhance climate resilient food production across productive agricultural landscapes through sound Integrated Landscape Management and Land Degradation Neutrality approaches in The Bahamas.  The project considers long-term solutions to address problems of land degradation and increase implementation of sustainable land management (SLM) practices through an integrated landscape management planning approach, with restorative measures that reduce the drivers of land degradation and mitigation of loss of productivity within agricultural and natural ecosystems, while enhancing resilience to climate change. The Project has been extended to 30 September 2027 to facilitate completion of activities. Total Budget is $5,717,580. The Project has applied for an extension.

planEntities.name: Support the Shift to Electric Mobility in Saint Lucia
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: This SLU National Child Project (GEF-7 #10283) is funded under a Global Support Programme implemented by UNEP to accelerate the introduction of electric mobility in countries. The SLU national Project will accelerate the introduction of electric mobility through capacity-building and electric vehicle demonstration and prepare for scaling-up and replication through the development of electric mobility policies, business models and finance schemes. The total allocation for the St. Lucia national Project is $785,688. The national Project is implemented within 4 Components: 1) Institutionalization of low-carbon electric mobility; 2) Short term barrier removal through low-carbon e-mobility demonstrations; 3) Preparing for scale-up and replication of low-carbon electric mobility; and 4) Long-term environmental sustainability of low-carbon electric mobility.  The Project has suffered COVID-19 related delays and received a 1st approval of extension to 2027-01-31. A total budge of $755,688 is available for the Saint Lucia national project.

planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Regional Project "Advancing Conservation in the Eastern Caribbean" (GEF-6 #9979): supports biodiversity conservation in 4 Organization of Eastern States (OECS) countries through enhanced political will and capacity building for improved management of marine protected areas (MPAs), marine management areas (MMAs) and protected areas (PAs). Activities will also support development of a Regional Conservation Caucus in the OECS. Implemented by UNEP Cartagena Convention Secretariat, with executing agency: Conservation Council of Nations (CCN). Project expenditures between 2019-2021 = $583,723. Project has been extended again to 31/10/2025 to achieve closure. *Note that there are no specific national allocations and expenditures per country are averaged. A No-Cost Extension was granted to 19 November 2024; the Project has been further extended to 30 June 2026.

planEntities.name: BDS REG: Invasive Alien Species (IAS) Prevention in Barbados & the Eastern Caribbean
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The regional Project, "Preventing COSTS of Invasive Alien Species (IAS) in Barbados and the OECS Countries" (GEF-6 #9408): promotes, prevention, early detection, control of and management frameworks for invasive alien species (IAS) that emphasize a risk management approach by focusing on the highest risk invasion pathways of Barbados and OECS countries (no-cost extension to 31 March 2024). It is executed by the Centre for Agriculture and Bioscience International, CABI. The Project commenced in 2018 and was disrupted by the COVID-19 Pandemic and was extended several times and is now scheduled for completion by 30 September 2026. There were no specific national allocations for the 7 participating countries, but total project expenditures between 2018 and 2021 amounted to approximately $1,856,500. The Project is under Terminal Evaluation and in the closure phase.

planEntities.name: BAH Pine Islands: Forest/Mangrove Innovation and Integration (Grand Bahama, New Providence, Abaco and Andros)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
The Project was commenced in 2015 and the Inception Workshop convened in 2016. It has been much delayed, and disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The total project budget = $1,584,919; total expenditures between 2016-2021 = $1,268,505.
The Project aims to build on recent advancements in the forestry sector by integrating biodiversity values, ecosystem services values and precepts of sustainable forest management and land-use into enhanced land-use planning in The Bahamas. The project addresses a number of environmental priorities through its three components: 1) : The institutional systemic support & associated capacity building; 2) The expansion and improved management of forest and mangrove sector; 3) Sustainable Livelihoods:  Developing the concept of multi-functional conservation by enabling coastal communities thru effective provisioning of forest ecosystem services while promoting sustainable practices and community management. The Project has been extended to 31 March 2026.

planEntities.name: The Path to 2020 - Antigua & Barbuda
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The 2019 GEF-6 (#9402) Project promotes protection and sustainable use of biodiversity and protected areas, under the umbrella of the Environmental Protection and Management Act (EPMA) of 2019. Executing Agency is the Department of the Environment, Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment. Main government & other partners include the Ministry of Agriculture, the Caribbean Agricultural Research & Development Institute (CARDI) & the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA). Project has 3 Components: 1) Strengthening regulations, institutions and financing mechanisms for the national Protected Areas System; 2) Expansion of protected areas in support of species conservation; 3) Pilot livelihood financing mechanisms that support conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and plant genetic resources in the newly designated Shekerley Mountain Management Area (SMMA). The project was extended to 31 December 2026.

planEntities.name: St. Lucia Southeast Coast Project - Integrated Ecosytem Management and Restoration of Forests
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The GEF-6 (#9406) Project The project enables sustainable economic development of the South East Coast by maintaining healthy ecosystems, sustainable livelihoods and securing global environmental benefits (GEBs). The Project promotes a more cohesive, ecosystem-based approach to development, including interrelated development planning and restoration of ecosystem services, and the establishment of sustainable management and natural resource use best practices. The objectives are change patterns of degradation on SLU's Southeast Coast, reduce impoverishment of local populations and loss of global environmental goods. The Project 3 Components: 1) Ecosystem Management - establishing effective ecosystems management mechanisms; 2) Rehabilitated Landscapes - supported through improved mechanisms for land use planning and collaborative investment decision-making; 3) Sustainable Livelihoods - identifying economic opportunities, incentives and livelihoods for primary natural resources users. Key national IP is the Department of Sustainable Development. The Project has been extended to 31 March 2027 with a total budget of $4,428,145.

planEntities.name: Sustainable Land Management in the Commonwealth of Dominica  (GEF-6, #9667)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Land degradation is a major concern in Dominica, driven mainly by development pressures, livelihoods challenges, and meteorological events in a physically vulnerable landscape. Despite the importance of agriculture for Dominica’s economy, the mountainous terrain of the country and variations in soil quality mean that only 20% of the land is suitable for agriculture (although an estimated 24.7% of the land is being farmed) due to erosion risks and potential water saturation during heavy rainfall. The island's central mountainous zone remains heavily forested and provides critical water catchment services as well as most of the protected landscapes in the country, while lower elevations continue to lose forest cover and is being degraded. The Project’s objective is the establishment of landscape level planning, information and coordination frameworks to support sustainable agriculture and sustainable watershed management in Dominica. The Project commenced in 2018, has experience delays and disruption from the COVID-19 Pandemic and has been extended several times. Project expenditures between 2018-2021 = $490,256. Project is in closure stage.

planEntities.name: ANT & BAR: Sustainable Pathways: Protected Areas and Renewable Energy (SPPARE)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The Sustainable Pathways: Protected Areas and Renewable Energy (SPPARE) (GEF-5, #5390) Project commenced in 2015 and encountered several delays, as well as disruption from the COVID-19 Pandemic. The Project Objective involved demonstration of an integrated and self-sustaining approach to environmental stewardship in a Small Island Developing State (SIDS) and to enhance financing and management of protected areas through innovations in renewable energy capacity in Antigua and Barbuda. The Project had 4 Components: 1) Development of Sustainable Island Resource Financial Plan - implementation of the environmental legislation and management of protected areas through the establishment of relevant strategies; the outcome is the development of the financial strategy for the implementation of the legislation and the management of protected areas. 2)  Pilot expansion of Sustainable Island Resource Protected Areas: Boggy Peak National Park (BPNP) - establishing a model-managed protected area that is sustainably managed and financed; the outcome is a model managed protected area that is financially self-sustaining. 3) Renewable Energy in support of Protected Areas Systems Pilot - installation of renewable energy technology to ultimately support the established pilot protected area; the outcome is at least 100,000 tons of CO2 equivalent emissions avoided as direct impact of the pilot with immediate plans for 1,000,000 tCO2. 4) Enhancement of Forest Systems - developing a public awareness strategy for reducing fires in forest ecosystems and establishing a carbon sink through the restoration of forested areas; the outcome is fires reduced nationwide by 20% by Project end.

planEntities.name: SLU - Iyanola Natural Resource Management of the North East Coast Project (GEF-5 #5057)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The Iyanola Project within St. Lucia's northeast coast aims for increased management effectiveness and sustainable use of the North East Coast’s natural resource base to generate multiple global environmental benefits.  The Project will enhance land use planning; develop a regulatory framework and improve capacity for the production of biodiversity friendly goods and services in inland forest and coastal communities, in order to create a platform for strengthening of the national enabling environment, to increase conservation and management effectiveness of terrestrial and coastal marine habitats and ecosystems in the Iyanola NE Coast region. The Project commenced in 2015 but has experienced several delays, was disrupted by the COVID-19 Pandemic and has received several extensions. It is in its closing stages.

planEntities.description:
Young people in the Caribbean have a significant contribution to make to promoting sustainable development. Creating an environment that is conducive and supportive of youth-led action and youth participation contributes to overall positive social development in the sub-region. 

Young people have been significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, exacerbating pre-existing vulnerabilities derived from increased inequalities of income and opportunity. Nevertheless, despite these difficulties, youth have been at the forefront, helping their communities overcome challenges caused by the pandemic. SHS supports countries in the Caribbean to prioritize actions and policies that build on the potential of youth and address their needs to allow them to exercise their rights.
This sub-outputs aims at: 
- Strengthened capacities of public officials from CARICOM Member States to apply the principles of meaningful youth engagement in programming and policy. 
- Joint action plan developed to advance the YPS agenda in the English and Dutch-speaking Caribbean. 
- Coordination mechanism created to follow-up on this action plan, including considering the launch of a YPS regional coalition. 
- Strengthened Network of Directors for improved knowledge sharing and exchange on youth engagement. 
-Strengthened capacities of Caribbean youth-led organizations on gender equality and advocacy by developing tools for young people to develop their own project ideas and drive social change in their communities.

planEntities.description:
Level of UNICEF support to Government to improve the availability and quality of child-related and quality of child-related Sustainable Development Goal indicators is being implemented. The extent is an index will be measured by the following indicators: 
1) Country Office has collaborated with the government to conduct a full Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) or any other household survey which includes at least 20 child-related SDG indicators. 
2) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) the strengthening of national routine/administrative data systems of individual sectors as well as cross sectoral interoperability.
3) Extent to which the Country Office supported (technically and/or financially) government efforts to strengthen the overall national statistical system regarding data about children, in alignment with national statistical master plans, or the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics during the reporting year
 4) Extent to which the Country Office supported the inclusion of statistical data for children in planning documents prepared by the government (including sectoral and sub-national ones) and Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) of SDG implementation during the reporting year 
5) Extent to which the Country Office supported good data governance standards regarding data for children (including Responsible Data for Children principles, Ethical Framework for Evidence Generation, Data Quality Framework) and the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics.

planEntities.description:
This activity focuses on two main data points:
A. The extent to which Belize's Health Sector policy/plan (or equivalent guidance document) includes the provision of the following services for the prevention and management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents in Primary Health Care:
1) Promotion of Health Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
2) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
3) Management of neglected tropical diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
4) Screening and interventions on substance abuse in children and adolescents.
B. Health-related interventions for the prevention and management of non-communicable diseases implemented with UNICEF support
1) Use of Primary Health care platform (including by Community Health Workers) to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
2) Use of School Health platform to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
3) Use of Digital platforms to promote Healthy Lifestyle and Prevention of NCD risk factors, such as lack of physical activity, overweight and obesity, alcohol and tobacco use
4) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs) at primary health care and referral facilities
4) Management of non-communicable diseases in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs) at primary health care and referral facilities
6) Prevention and management of neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) in children and adolescents (0-19 yrs)
7) Screening and interventions on substance abuse in children and adolescents

planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.1: Support provided to promote inclusive, competitive, and resilient business ecosystems
planEntities.description: The pineapple value chain is a priority value chain in the Government of Suriname's drive to diversify its economy from heavy reliance on the extractive industry. In 2018-2019, in response to a request by the Government of Suriname, FAO, UNIDO and ITC applied the Accelerator for Agriculture and Agroindustry Development and Innovation Plus (3ADI+), a joint value chains and market systems development initiative, to the pineapple sub-sector. Moving from this solid preparatory phase to implementation, the joint programme will foster stakeholder cooperation and engagement and promote SDG-compliant public and private investments in innovation at each value chain stage (i.e. production, processing, and distribution). To assure a long-term sustainability of the action, the technical component will involve a strengthening of the innovative capacities of national institutes and public extension and market promotion services. In sum, the programme represents a unique opportunity to channel investments into productive activities and generate incomes for poor rural communities.

planEntities.parentName: GUY Output 7.1 Institutions are supported to protect democratic norms, ensure transparency, deliver accountability and enhance the rule of law
planEntities.description:
The mission of the UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) is to build capacity in countries seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security, and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods. The UNODC-WCO Container Control Programme (CCP) was established as a joint initiative of the UNODC and the WCO in 2004. Faced with such a complex and globalized problem, the CCP embraces a nuanced, holistic and multi-sectoral approach by providing continuous monitoring and oversight, offering a plethora of context-specific training programmes and strengthening cooperation between state agencies and with the private sector. The mission of the CCP is to build capacity in Member States seeking to improve risk management, supply chain security and trade facilitation in seaports, airports and land border crossings in order to prevent the cross-border movement of illicit goods.

At present, the CCP is operational in over 70 Member States. More than 120 Port Control Units (PCUs) and Air Cargo Control Units (ACCUs) have been established since the CCP's inception in 2004. These inter-agency units are equipped to exchange information with their counterparts in other countries using a secure communication application, developed by the WCO, called ContainerComm. This provides PCUs and ACCUs with access to a wealth of information, allowing users to share information about high-risk containers and verify their identification numbers.

The CCP Programme is currently under implementation in the Port of Georgetown in Guyana. In 2022, capacity building programmes to support enhanced profiling of containers was carried for the benefit of the PCU in Georgetown, including exchange programmes with the Port of Hamburg in Germany and other PCUs in the Caribbean basin. UNODC also provided additional of safety and search equipment to the Georgetown PCU. Study visits to Germany port of Hamburg.

planEntities.description:
Under the UNODC Global Firearms Programme, and in close cooperation with CARICOM IMPACS, UNODC is currently implementing the Project “Support to the implementation of the crime prevention and criminal justice component of the Caribbean Roadmap to counter illicit firearms trafficking and misuse across the Caribbean in a sustainable manner by 2030”. The project is funded by Germany and aims to support the implementation of the Caribbean Roadmap in specific areas related to its crime prevention and criminal justice component and reduce the scourge of armed violence in the region. It also seeks to contribute to regional efforts to prevent and counter illicit circulation, misuse of firearms and their links to other serious crimes, in particular transnational organized crime.
 
In 2022, the Global Firearms Programme implemented the following programmes in, or with the participation of Trinidad and Tobago:

-	Legislative review assessing national legislation on firearms and organized crime in compliance with international and regional instruments, consolidated in one final report shared with the country.
-	Legal workshop with Attorney General’s Office and relevant national stakeholders to discuss results of legislative review conducted by the programme and tailor findings with their feedback.

In the Caribbean region, UNODC embarked on cooperation with the CARICOM Implementation Agency for Crime and Security (IMPACS), to support Member States in the development and implementation of regional maritime crime strategy based on agreed approaches endorsed by the International Maritime Organization. In 2022, in an effort to support the development of the regional Maritime Crime Strategy, UNODC conducted missions to several CARICOM Member States, including the Bahamas, Barbados, Dominican Republic, Guyana, Jamaica, Suriname and Trinidad and Tobago to assess needs and define the goals of the strategy, as well as to promote the buy-in of Member States. UNODC continues to work with CARICOM IMPACS for the finalization of this strategy in 2023.

planEntities.name: TTO – UNODC Global Programme on Cybercrime: Trinidad and Tobago has increased capacity to identify, investigate, prosecute and adjudicate online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
UNODC’s Global Programme on Cybercrime is designed to respond flexibly to identified needs in developing countries by supporting Member States to prevent and combat cybercrime in a holistic manner.  The key objectives of this programme are:
•	Increased efficiency and effectiveness in the investigation, prosecution and adjudication of cybercrime, especially online child sexual exploitation and abuse, within a strong human-rights framework;
•	Efficient and effective long-term whole-of-government response to cybercrime, including national coordination, data collection and effective legal frameworks, leading to a sustainable response and greater deterrence;
•	Strengthened national and international communication between government, law enforcement and the private sector with increased public knowledge of cybercrime risks.

In 2022, UNODC launched the Project “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes” under the Global Cybercrime Project of UNODC. This project is funded by the Government of Canada and will be implemented until December 2024. The project aims to enhance the capacity of Trinidad and Tobago to identify, investigate, prosecute, adjudicate and prevent online child sexual exploitation and trafficking in persons facilitated by information and communications technologies.
Capacity building includes:
•	Cybercrime and digital evidence basics, proactive online investigations: using specialized platforms, such as CPS or ICACCOPS, to detect in real time the distribution of online child sexual exploitation material;
•	Train the trainer workshop in reactive online investigations: using platforms, such as the CyberTipline reporting mechanism, to receive reports from foreign technology companies on cases of online child sexual exploitation;
•	Open-source intelligence applied in investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes;
•	Identifying and handling digital evidence;
•	Criminal investigations involving the dark web, cryptocurrencies, for example.

Likewise, the Project will also facilitate the provision of specialized equipment for identifying, acquiring, analysing, and preserving digital evidence for the units responsible for investigating online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes, as well as activities to support to Civil Society, prevention, and cooperation.
In 2022, the following activities were conducted:
-	17th October 2022- Project Launch “Strengthening Trinidad and Tobago capacities to effectively prevent and counter online child sexual abuse and exploitation and related crimes”. Organized by UNODC in collaboration with: Attorney General and Minister of Legal Affairs of T&T; Commissioner of Police; CARICOM IMPACS, International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), and the donor Canada. With the participation of 15 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.
-	18th October 2022- Workshop for the Assessment: Multisectoral Response and Capacities.
Organized by UNODC in collaboration with International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC), with the participation of 16 Institutions, NGOs and UN Agencies.
-	25-26th October, 2022- UNODC in cooperation with INTERPOL delivered “Awareness raising session on child sexual exploitation online” 
With the participation of the: Office of the Attorney General and Minister of Legal Affairs of T&T; Commissioner of Police; CARICOM IMPACS, and NCB INTERPOL T&T. With the participation of 25 persons.
-	26th October 2022 - UNODC in coordination with the NGO TTV Solnet, delivered a Webinar on the “Threat of cybercrime: safe use of social networks, world trends, sexual crimes, grooming, sexting and sextortion. Protection strategies for the use of the internet”. 
With the participation of 51 Venezuelan women in Trinidad and Tobago.
-	22th November, 2022- UNODC in coordination with the NGO TTV Solnet, delivered a Webinar on the “Threat of cybercrime: safe use of social networks, world trends, sexual crimes, grooming, sexting and sextortion. Protection strategies for the use of the internet”. 
With the participation of 25 Venezuelans women’s in Trinidad and Tobago.

In 2022, the following activities were conducted:
- January 2024. Multisectoral response and capacity (MRC) assessment of national policies, programs, and capabilities to prevent and combat online child sexual abuse and exploitation. 
- 4th- 7th March 2024- Introductory workshop in criminal investigations involving the dark web and cryptocurrencies. 21 participants (9 Female and 12 Male). 
- 6th- 7th March 2024- Workshop on preventing online child sexual abuse and exploitation. For parents, teachers, and host community members.
