planEntities.name: El país ha fortalecido sus capacidades para la gestión del riesgo de desastres y emergencias de salud con un abordaje multiamenaza
planEntities.parentName: OU9 Capacidades del Estado fortalecidas en procesos de diseño e implementación de normas, marcos legislativos y políticas y para la planificación planeación, asignación, ejecución y seguimiento presupuestario que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios y oportunidades de bienestar, desarrollo, protección y participación, incluyendo el enfoque de género e interseccionalidad.
planEntities.description:
En este periodo se generaron diversas actividades orientadas a fortalecer la capacidad del país en la gestión de riesgos de desastres y emergencias en salud, tales como: 
- La implementación de los nuevos subsistemas de información incorporando un componente de calidad de datos para lograr identificar brechas a lo largo del curso de vida.
- El apoyo en los procesos de planificación, revisión, implementación, monitoreo y evaluación de la estrategia de gestión integrada (EGI) de las enfermedades arbovirales, incluyendo la movilización de recursos para facilitar los procesos.
- El mantenimiento del sistema de vigilancia para el seguimiento de la parálisis fláccida aguda.
- Las campañas de seguimiento y puesta al día de polio y sarampión en el contexto de la pandemia de COVID-19.
- El Plan de implementación de la CIE-11 incluyendo iniciativas de fortalecimiento de la calidad de los datos con sistemas de información interoperables.
- La respuesta y control de la pandemia de la COVID-19 fortaleciendo: liderazgo, coordinación, planificación y seguimiento de las estrategias; procesos de vacunación; vigilancia, equipos de respuesta rápida e investigación de casos; manejo de casos; aspectos operativos y logísticos; mantenimiento de servicios de salud esenciales durante un brote; entre otros.
- La implementación de intervenciones integradas a fin reconocer las amenazas y determinar aquellas que representan un riesgo prioritario para la salud pública.
- El fortalecimiento del sistema de vigilancia de infecciones respiratorias.
- La implementación de intervenciones integradas a fin mitigar el riesgo de que emerjan o reemerjan agentes patógenos infecciosos.

planEntities.name: Las autoridades nacionales, provinciales y municipales habrán desarrollado  y fortalecido herramientas y capacidades para mejorar el acceso y la calidad de los servicios de salud para el VIH, las ITS, la tuberculosis y la HV y la ETMI Plus, con énfasis en el primer nivel de atención
planEntities.parentName: OU9 Capacidades del Estado fortalecidas en procesos de diseño e implementación de normas, marcos legislativos y políticas y para la planificación planeación, asignación, ejecución y seguimiento presupuestario que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios y oportunidades de bienestar, desarrollo, protección y participación, incluyendo el enfoque de género e interseccionalidad.
planEntities.description:
Durante este periodo, se destaca el fortalecimiento de las capacidades nacionales y subnacionales para la mejora de la calidad de los servicios y el acceso, a través de acciones concretas tales como: 
•	El fortalecimiento de la sociedad civil de tuberculosis en el marco de la estrategia ENGAGE TB de WHO. Con apoyo el apoyo de la Oficina país se conformó ObservaTB, grupo de diversas organizaciones y persona afectadas por tuberculosis.
•	El apoyo a la sociedad civil de VIH y tuberculosis para participar de la comisión nacional intersectorial  de respuesta al VIH, las hepatitis virales y la tuberculosis.
•	La expansión de la implementación de la estrategia de prevención combinada/Prep.
•	El fortalecimiento del sistema de información de personas con VIH para recolectar los indicadores de la cascada del continuo de atención.

planEntities.name: El Estado habrá fortalecido las capacidades para abordar el derecho a la salud y otros derechos relacionados en todos los niveles
planEntities.parentName: OU9 Capacidades del Estado fortalecidas en procesos de diseño e implementación de normas, marcos legislativos y políticas y para la planificación planeación, asignación, ejecución y seguimiento presupuestario que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios y oportunidades de bienestar, desarrollo, protección y participación, incluyendo el enfoque de género e interseccionalidad.
planEntities.description:
Durante este periodo, se propició el efectivo acceso al derecho a la salud, especialmente de las poblaciones más vulneradas, considerando intersecciones como género, etnicidad y condición migrante, desde el enfoque de curso de vida. Esto incluyó diversas acciones tales como: 

-  Formación de equipos de salud en la respuesta  integral frente a las violencias por motivos de género. 
- Actividades de difusión y elaboración de materiales para la prevención y atención de las violencias, específicamente en poblaciones migrantes . 
- Alianzas interagenciales a fin de ampliar el alcance de actividades dirigidas a la promoción de derechos y la equidad en salud. 
- Acciones de sensibilización, formación y comunicación para promover mayor acceso a la salud dirigidos a la comunidad y al personal de salud. 
- Apoyo a iniciativas que abordaron la interculturalidad en el acceso a la salud en comunidades originarias y otras poblaciones vulnerables, generando diagnósticos sobre los principales obstáculos y facilitadores en el acceso.

planEntities.name: Las autoridades nacionales y subnacionales habrán fortalecido, desarrollado e implementado sus capacidades para la integración de enfoques y consideraciones de género, equidad, derechos humanos y/o etnicidad en las  estrategias de salud y la planificación operativa
planEntities.parentName: OU9 Capacidades del Estado fortalecidas en procesos de diseño e implementación de normas, marcos legislativos y políticas y para la planificación planeación, asignación, ejecución y seguimiento presupuestario que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios y oportunidades de bienestar, desarrollo, protección y participación, incluyendo el enfoque de género e interseccionalidad.
planEntities.description:
Se colaboró en la elaboración e implementación de estrategias de sensibilización y capacitación sobre enfoques interculturales en distintos niveles interjurisdiccionales relacionados con el sistema de salud, a través de acciones como: 

- La ejecución del programa de capacitación para Introducir y capacitar en la metodología de diálogo de saberes a referentes de APS provinciales, equipos de salud y facilitadores interculturales, entre otros y promover la construcción del perfil de facilitador/a intercultural (rol, responsabilidades, funciones, alcances) en la provincia de Salta (Tartagal y Embarcación). Elaboración un diagnóstico participativo orientado a identificar fortalezas y oportunidades en el acceso al sistema de salud de la provincia. 
- La promoción de la Red de Cuidado Perinatal para Pueblos Indígenas con foco en la prevención del embarazo no intencional en las adolescencias. Dispositivos en las provincias de Salta (Orán y Tartagal) y Jujuy (Ledesma y La Quiaca). Operativos en colocación de LARCS, consejerías y capacitación a equipos de salud. Difusión de materiales adaptados interculturalmente. Entrega de Tablets a agentes sanitarios y facilitadores interculturales.

planEntities.parentName: OU9 Capacidades del Estado fortalecidas en procesos de diseño e implementación de normas, marcos legislativos y políticas y para la planificación planeación, asignación, ejecución y seguimiento presupuestario que garanticen el acceso equitativo a servicios y oportunidades de bienestar, desarrollo, protección y participación, incluyendo el enfoque de género e interseccionalidad.
planEntities.description:
Durante 2023, se destacan las acciones orientadas a acelerar la implementación de la ley de salud mental a través del diseño de políticas multisectoriales, concretamente: 
•	Fortalecimiento del enfoque de salud mental comunitaria en el 2do nivel de atención mediante acciones como la inauguración de Centro de salud mental y vivienda protegida en Rosario, provincia de Santa Fe
•	Procesos de externación de instituciones monovalentes fortalecidos en Rosario y La Rioja
•	Red de intercambios e instancias de capacitación entre equipos de las 5 provincias involucradas en la implementación en Iniciativa Especial de Salud Mental fortalecida
•	Implementación de mhGAP en 19 jurisdicciones articulando con mhGAP Comunitario
•	Kit de promoción de la salud mental en jóvenes y adolescentes elaborado y validado, en conjunto con las direcciones nacionales de salud mental y de juventudes del Ministerio de Salud.
•	Apoyo técnico para el estudio de factibilidad y del plan de implementación del observatorio para suicidio provisto al Ministerio de Salud.

planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Capacities at national/ subnational levels are strengthened to design and implement policies for inclusive, green and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description:
To conduct legal and economic studies on Armenia's  integration into regional and global value chains, including in the field of industry, and the impact of COVID-19. 
To organize stakeholder consultations at the national and regional levels to analyse and discuss key features of the EAEU member States integration into regional and global value chains and the impact of COVID-19. 

To develop three evidence-based policy options for the way forward for more resilient, diversified and sustainable value chains in Armenia and the Eurasian region as a whole, and, with a view to promoting cooperative ties and export of industrial products with higher value added, set out in a policy brief (e.g. for national and regional stakeholders to discuss potential pros and cons of the developed policy recommendations). Also to organize policy briefings and regional stakeholders.

To organize launch events to communicate policies that govern resilient, diversified and sustainable value chains post-COVID-19. To translate national studies conducted in the framework of the project into Russian.

planEntities.name: The Ministry of Environment has a strengthened capacity to fulfill commitment under the Vienna Convention on the Protection of the Ozone Layer and the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
planEntities.parentName: 5.3 Ecosystems and population vulnerability is reduced through increased resilience to climate change and disasters
planEntities.description:
Institutional strengthening projects have been funded by the Executive Committee since its seventh meeting to provide financial support to Article 5 countries to enhance national capacities for the timely and effective implementation of ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out activities. These projects support coordination between the concerned country, the Executive Committee, the Multilateral Fund Secretariat and the implementing agencies, and have been instrumental in ensuring broad compliance with the Montreal Protocol.

In Armenia, the institutional strengthening project pursues several interrelated objectives. These include the adoption and implementation of legislation and regulations to control and monitor the import and use of Montreal Protocol controlled substances and related equipment; the accurate and timely collection and reporting of data on the consumption of all Montreal Protocol controlled substances; and the strengthening of coordination among national agencies and stakeholders in support of the objectives of the Montreal Protocol. The project also supports oversight of the timely implementation of hydrochlorofluorocarbon (HCFC) phase-out and hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) phase-down activities and the associated reductions in the consumption of controlled substances. In addition, it promotes awareness-raising and information exchange on Montreal Protocol-related issues and supports regional cooperation and participation in Montreal Protocol processes.

planEntities.name: The metrology system of Armenia is enhanced through the institutional strengthening of the National Body for Standards and Metrology
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Capacities at national/ subnational levels are strengthened to design and implement policies for inclusive, green and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The “Support to Quality Infrastructure in Armenia “project, funded by the European Union (EU), and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) will support an upgrade of the metrology system of Armenia through institutional strengthening of the National Body for Standards and Metrology, and improving legal, regulatory and governance systems in line with international recommendations and best practices. The main outcomes of the project will be to increase Armenia’s participation in the international (BIPM and OIML) and regional (COOMET) metrology communities, prepare NBSM calibration laboratories for international recognition (accreditation or CMC’s published) and further develop the institutional capacity (legal, regulatory, governance and leadership) of NBSM in line with international recommendations and best practice

planEntities.name: 5.2.1.3. Promoting the use of renewable energy for productive activities
planEntities.parentName: 4.3 Green and sustainable investments are promoted to drive equitable and export-oriented growth
planEntities.description:
UNIDO supported the Amasia Wool Factory in the Shirak region in the application of innovative and renewable energy technologies in the agro-processing sector by equipping the facility with a solar water heater. A second solar water heater was installed in Paravakar at a fruit, herb and molasses production enterprise established by a producer who migrated from the Russian Federation in 2019.

The installed equipment contributed to a reduction in production costs for the final products and served as a practical demonstration of the application of renewable energy solutions in the agro-industry sector.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - MSMEs and social enterprises, including women-owned businesses, are set up and sustained for the benefit of the furthest behind
planEntities.description:
Dairy processing, and meet processing units established, consumer awareness on selected sheep products raised, and
agricultural and livestock fairs organized.
Considering the vast presence of women in sheep production (including also milk, meat and wool processing), the project will thoroughly analyze these value chains through the gender lens, to identify and assess  existing gender disparities and inequalities and will ensure that a gender-responsive approach is applied throughout the project implementation and monitoring, according to FAO corporate Policy on Gender Equality, and Environmental and Social Management Guidelines.  Special attention is given to a gender-sensitive approach to ensure full participation of women within the project.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.9 - Pilot integrated training and grant/loan programme for Young Farmers
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - MSMEs and social enterprises, including women-owned businesses, are set up and sustained for the benefit of the furthest behind
planEntities.description:
AMAL Young Farmers’ Programme developed and the selection mechanism established, business development trainings provided to pre-selected applicants, sector-specific trainings, support and mentoring provided to selected beneficiaries. Gender mainstreaming strategy will consist of three major elements:

1. Ensuring sufficient capacities to implement the project in a gender-responsive and socially inclusive manner, and to ensure sustainability. 

2. Ensuring gender-responsive and socially inclusive monitoring and evaluation for effective project implementation. 

3. Mainstreaming gender and social inclusion issues in all outputs and activities. 
In particular, the following particular actions will be taken:

•	Activities 3.1: The needs of both young women and men will be included on the strategic planning of the programme under this activity.
•	Activity 3.2: The development of the selection criteria will be gender-responsive. The selection panel will be composed of both women and men, and quotas for women and men, including from vulnerable groups, will be established. The call will be disseminated through the channels of information identified under activity 2.4, so all can be engaged. 100 men and 100 women will be selected.
•Activity 3.3: The content of the soft-skills development trainings will be gender sensitive and will promote social inclusion.

Gender mainstreaming strategy for this project will be the following:
 Policy reviews, advice, discussions and training will include gender balance , social inclusion and human rights considerations;
 The project team will support the creation, development and/or expansion (depending on the country) of women’s cooperatives and associations, and will promote the engagement of women in mixed cooperatives and associations 
 All monitoring and reporting of the project will be gender responsive, disaggregated by sex (and
also by age when relevant), and corrective measures will be taken when necessary so that both
men and women can actively benefit from the project;
 All assessments conducted within the project will include gender and social inclusion
considerations.
 The project team will also work to promote gender issues in fisheries in the CACFish agenda and
discussions.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.7 - Strengthen technical capacities of national specialists on disease-free seed potato production
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Enhanced human capital and a skilled workforce are available in key sectors
planEntities.description:
Organize a training course on testing viral, fungal and bacterial diseases on meristem derived in vitro plants and on seed crops in the field; Organize a training course on seed potato production in the field and carry out continued on-the-job training; Prepare and publish manual of procedures for potato disease diagnostics and eradication; Organize a study tour/external training for 3 potato researchers/seed experts to a foreign country with advanced disease-free seed potato production system etc.
Equal opportunities will be provided to women and men researchers and experts working at the laboratory, greenhouse and field levels, so part of participants of trainings will be women. In particular, the project team will ensure that women working in laboratories receive intensive on-the-job trainings on tissue culture and virus detection techniques, and that women working in seed potato production will receive trainings on modern crop management technologies. The participation will be monitored in a sex-disaggregated manner, and corrective actions will be taken to ensure that the project is fully inclusive.

planEntities.description:
1) Country-level analysis reports (Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Montenegro, Serbia and Uzbekistan) developed to support the beneficiary countries in the following 3 areas and findings shared:
-	Gaining an in-depth understanding of the nature and causes of changing dietary patterns and malnutrition through a food system lens
-	Reviewing the effectiveness of related existing policies and programmes
-	Identifying the opportunities for cross-sectoral collaboration between stakeholders (UN agencies, academia, civil society, government in particular)
2) the WHO Regional Office for Europe has developed a classification to guide countries in restricting food marketing: the WHO Regional Office for Europe nutrient profile model (WHO NP). Use of the WHO NP model can assist in evaluating the status of HFSS food marketing in Member States and determining the effectiveness of existing initiatives and approaches to restricting such marketing.
Despite all the efforts, exposure to marketing of unhealthy products remains a major issue, demanding to protect all children equally. 
Children are likely to be exposed to advertisements while watching TV. It is important to get an idea of the extent this is happening. And  research on the current situation is the first monitoring step recommended to be taken by Member States.
Therefore, WHO CO AZE supported the Research on the TV marketing of unhealthy food products targeting children in Azerbaijan.  For this purposes, WCO AZE supported training of three researchers in previous year,  and starting from June 2023, they started recording, analysing and coding TV programmes from 4 channels popular among children.  It is planned to publish  the results in 2024.

planEntities.name: 2.2.2.12 - Creation of right conditions to set up a Passenger Information Unit (PIU) in Azerbaijan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2 - National capacities are enhanced to generate evidence-based policies and decisions
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to improved and streamlined passenger processing efforts, enhance travel facilitation and border security in Azerbaijan. The project aim is to support the on-going efforts of the Government of Azerbaijan to strengthen API/PNR in Azerbaijan in compliance with the international standards set by ICAO, IATA, WCO and assist with creating the right conditions to set-up Passenger Information Unit (PIU) in the future . The project will achieve the objective through (1) PIU Legal Assessment:  legislative framework and governance structure for establishing a PIU as solid national legislation needs to be in place, setting out rules on passenger data collection and specifying provisions on the use, transfer and retention of data. Furthermore, the legislation needs to comply with relevant international standards including those related to privacy and data protection (2) Awareness Raising:  IOM will organize workshops and study visits for API/PNR Working Group members. Ensuring a thorough understanding of the concept as it is crucial in helping the States to operationalize PIU (3) Stakeholder Analysis and Technical Assessment: to assess Azerbaijan’s existing technical capacities including the ICT architecture of the law enforcement sector, identify gaps for the solid PIU system and share recommendations for potential PIU solutions and specifications. The main guarantee that these efforts will be durable and sustainable is the fact that the process is deeply rooted in Azerbaijan’s national priorities, political willingness and international commitments

planEntities.name: 2.2.2.13 - Improved national capacity for sustainable inland transport connectivity
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2 - National capacities are enhanced to generate evidence-based policies and decisions
planEntities.description:
The aim of the project is to provide an elearning platform to facilitate training but also to undertake targeted training and capacity building within countries to develop sustainable transport and connectivity action plans. The objective of the project is to support the ECE Working Party on Transport Trends and Economics (WP.5) in fulfilling its mandate to assume the unique role of a transport “think tank” in the framework of ITC. The objective of the working party is to enhance the understanding of the main inland transport trends and developments and strengthen international cooperation to develop sustainable Euro-Asian transport links. Promoting a better understanding of trends and developments including cyber threats surrounding Electrical Vehicles and their charging infrastructure through capacity building and the development of knowledge products

In 2025: Two further in-person sessions of the Coordination Committee on the Trans-Caspian and Almaty-Tehran-Istanbul Corridors which is convening periodically as a group of friends of the Chair of the Working Party on Transport Trends and Economics (WP.5). Location of the meetings yet to be determined. The Coordination Committee convenes on the basis of a an agreed 2023-2025 biennial programme of work based on 5 thematic clusters: 1. transport infrastructure harmonization; 2. transport documents and digitalization; 3. harmonization of tariffs and time schedules; 4. border crossing efficiency and 5. economic viability, climate change resilience and environmental performance. Typically every country is represented at every meeting by 2-3 representatives from either the Ministry of transport and/ or railway and customs authorities.

UNHCR continues the interventions at Empowering the communities of its persons of concern to take active part in decisions and programs affecting their lives. In this regard, one of the pursued direction is Supporting the refugees and asylum seekers in Azerbaijan through awareness raising and mobilization. In order to achieve this goal, it is planned to implement Activities identified by communities; maintain and reinforce Communication with communities; promote Community volunteers incentives; maintaining Refugee Reception Center; organizing Workshops with refugees on outreach. 

In addition, with the goal related to establishing broader prospects of durable solutions for the UNHCR's persons of concern, UNHCR Azerbaijan has planned to Mainstream and monitor the access to legal employment by delivering Protection counselling through service contractor; Monitor and support the access to residence and citizenship documents; Strengthen advocacy for secure legal status of refugees.

planEntities.description:
1) In 2023,  strategic partnership with Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency was strenghtened by initiation of dialogue on several projects, including  FEEDCities. By the end of the year, three meetings on  the scope of the FEEDCities in Azerbaijan, area of implementation and contractual  details were held. The objectives of the FEEDCities research are:
1. To describe the characteristics of the food being sold at street vending places, map their location, characterize the street food offer at selected vending places and describe the costumers present and the street foods purchased.
2. To assess the nutritional composition of the ready-to-eat foods sold in the street.
3. To map the spatial distribution of food advertisements and to describe the typology and contents of food advertisements.   
2) Expert team composed of WHO national and international experts, as well as representatives from Republican Hygiene and Epidemiology Center (HEC) visited selected Hygiene and Epidemiology Centers (HEC) in Sabunchu, Sabail, Ganja, Masalli, Astara districts, . The visits aimed to assess institutional capacities of these HECs in delivering essential public health functions and to identify the structural and functional refinements needed for better contribution to public health in Azerbaijan.
 During the visit experts conducted unstructured interviews with directors of HECs and public health workers, The information collected was used to produce a report with key recommendations for reform to the Ministry of Health. 
3)The World Health Organization (WHO) organized a meeting in Azerbaijan, with representatives from key health agencies to create a shared understanding of strengthening the country's public health system. Participants represented MoH, SAMHI, TABİB, the Food Safety Agency, The State Customs Committee, Public Health and Reforms Center, Azerbaijan Medical University, Ministry of Emergency Situations, and the Azerbaijan State Advanced Training Institute for Doctors. During the meeting, participants identified their institution’s role in delivering essential public health services and agreed on the need for having a platform to strengthen collaboration in addressing main public health challenges. 
Participants agreed to expand the group to include the Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, State Committee for Family, Women and Children and Health Committee of the Parliament. The idea of a Public Health Symposium, involving national and international partners, was explored to raise awareness and discuss global health trends, fostering enhanced cooperation.

planEntities.name: 2.1.2.3 - Strengthen primary health care and comprehensive essential health services
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2 - National primary health care and nutrition systems are strengthened to ensure universal coverage and quality, inclusive and high-impact interventions
planEntities.description:
1) WHO Azerbaijan Country Office held the first seminar of the long-term action plan for supporting the adaptation of competencies of public health workers in Azerbaijan to international standards in the field. To assess the knowledge and skill competencies of the public health workforce in the country members of the "Public Health Capacity Group", staff of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts attended the seminar. During the workshop, the participants were introduced to the "Competency Framework" model set by the WHO – ASPHER, in which they discussed and evaluated their own competencies. Moving forward, the plan was to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals to develop competencies defined by international standards. The action is funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance and TABIB.

2) WHO Azerbaijan hosted a workshop with experts from health education and health provider institutions, to develop small-scale COPC intervention plans in Nasimi district. The goal was to improve health outcomes in the District via collaboration between healthcare providers and the community while considering population characteristics and prioritizing health problems. On the first day, participants visited the District's health centers to observe and collect data on the population’s health and identify common health issues. For the remaining days, they worked on community characterization, prioritization of health issues, and a detailed assessment of health problems. The working groups then developed a comprehensive COPC intervention plans for the District. This workshop was organized under the public health focus areas of the APR funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the SAMHI, TABIB, and supported by Nasimi District Executive Power of Baku.

3) In this seminar, the participants  studied the "Public Health Competency Framework" developed by the WHO–ASPHER and self-assessed their competencies. The seminar was attended by members of the "Capacity Group on Public Health" representing MoH, TABIB and SAMHI, teachers of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts. Discussions were held on the individual learning plans presented at the seminar and the gaps between international standards and local competencies identified in the evaluations. The outcome of the seminar is that Participants have become familiar with the ASPHER competency framework, which identified their learning needs and developed time-bound individual learning plans with the support of WHO experts. The long-term aim is to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals develop competencies defined by international standards.

4) Zaur Aliyev, Chairman of the Board of the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance, Vugar Gurbanov, Executive Director of the Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB), and Dr. Hande Harmancı, World Health Organization (WHO) Representative in Azerbaijan, visited the Shamakhi district to assess the efforts undertaken by the WHO Country Office in Shamakhi to strengthen primary health care (PHC) services. The purpose of the visit was to familiarize themselves with the work carried out until now and discuss future collaborations between WHO and the country's health institutions in this field. 

WHO Azerbaijan has so far implemented the PHC Demonstration, Shamakhi Fellowship Program, and other PHC-related activities in the district to develop an accessible, quality, and comprehensive primary health care model, improve the knowledge and skills of local medical workers, and strengthen the medical staff's capacity for PHC. 

5) Agencies responsible for planning and delivering public health services in Azerbaijan, online meeting brought together again representatives from  Ministry of Health, SAMHI, TABİB, Food Safety Agency of The Republic of Azerbaijan, The State Customs Committee of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Public Health and Rgeforms Center, Azerbaijan Medical University,, Ministry of Emergency Situations and Azerbaijan State Advanced Training Institute for Doctors, the Ministry of Ecology, Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, State Committee for Family, Women and Children as well as the Health Committee of the Parliament. The session aimed to create a shared understanding of the need to renew the public health system in Azerbaijan and the role that each institution can play. A notable outcome was the formation of a collaborative working group dedicated to strengthening Azerbaijan's public health policy framework and underscored a collective commitment to advancing the nation's public health landscape.

planEntities.description:
1) Pandemic Fund Meeting
WHO Azerbaijan developed the joint proposal, “Pandemic Fund Participatory OneHealth Disease Detection in Azerbaijan (PF-AZE-PODD)” for funding to address the ongoing challenges presented by pandemic threats. PF-AZE-PODD project aimed to establish a community level early warning system through One Health approach by creating teams of “One Health Workers”, supported by digital platform for early detection and alarm verification with integration into existing national surveillance system for strengthened identification and response to unexpected human and animal health events leading to improved prevention of epidemics and pandemics.
 Developed proposal was presented and discussed with senior government officials from MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, MoF, Heydar Aliyev Foundation, Agrarian Services Agency and Azerbaijan Food Safety Agency to align it with National Priorities and Investment plans. Proposal components and application process were introduced and discussed. The key points were discussed during final Ministerial Sessions and proposal was approved by the Minister of Health. 

2) A delegation from WHO Azerbaijan has started an official visit to Nakhchivan

During this meeting, extensive discussions were held on various topics, including primary health care, emergency medicine, laboratory services, public health, and medical education. 

The WHO Azerbaijan team has started a 3-day visit to Nakhchivan, led by Dr. Hande Harmanci, WHO Representative to Azerbaijan, in response to an invitation from the Ministry of Health of the Nakhchivan Autonomous Republic.

As part of the visit's framework, the WHO delegation is expected to become familiar with with the healthcare system reforms implemented in the Autonomous Republic in recent months, the efforts aimed at enhancing the quality of medical services, and the projects planned for the near future. In addition to visiting Nakhchivan city, they will also visit the Ordubad and Sharur regions, where they will inspect the newly established Family Health Care Centers.

3) The two-day workshop brought together experts from the Ministry of Health, Republic Hygiene and Epidemiology Center, Regional Hygiene and Epidemiology Centers, Public Health and Reforms Center, and WHO. The goal was to raise awareness on the need for transforming the public health system to address the health challenges affecting people living in Azerbaijan. Using the framework of the essential public health functions, participants engaged in discussions to identify main strengths, weaknesses, threats and opportunities. The information collected was used to inform the development of a report with key recommendations for reform to the Ministry of Health. The methodology for engagement used in he workshop also supported strengthening collaboration between the participants, with a view to strengthen public health in Azerbaijan

4) In collaboration with faculty members from Azerbaijan Medical University (AMU) Public Health Faculty and Medical Education Department, and ASATID, a survey was planned to assess the public health competencies of senior medical students of the Public Health Faculty using the WHO-ASPHER competency framework.    In addition, the same survey was adapted for faculty members so that the programme could evaluate the extent to which these competencies were gained in the program, and they were also asked to answer. 94 medical students and 30 faculty member participated in the study. The mean scores across categories in ASPHER competencies reveal strengths and areas for improvement. The findings of the survey were presented at a Public Health Congress in Turkey. The survey will continue on residents and public health practitioners. This result of the study will facilitate the identify learning needs, inform curriculum development process, and contribute to public health education strengthening in Azerbaijan.

5) WHO Azerbaijan Country Office held the first seminar of the long-term action plan for supporting the adaptation of competencies of public health workers in Azerbaijan to international standards in the field. To assess the knowledge and skill competencies of the public health workforce in the country members of the "Public Health Capacity Group", staff of the Faculty of Public Health of Azerbaijan Medical University, and WHO experts attended the seminar. During the workshop, the participants were introduced to the "Competency Framework" model set by the WHO – ASPHER, in which they discussed and evaluated their own competencies. Moving forward, the plan was to prepare evidence-based recommendations on changes in medical education curricula to help Azerbaijan's public health professionals to develop competencies defined by international standards. The action is funded by USAID and implemented by WHO in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, the State Agency for Mandatory Health Insurance and TABIB.

The event brought together about 30 journalists, social media influencers, and representatives from local health agencies to enhance their skills in identifying and combatting misinformation and disinformation related to vaccination, especially concerning their impact on public health.
During the workshop, participants received briefings on various topics, including risk communication and community engagement, the media's role in health emergencies, routine immunization, the concept of the infodemic, and its management. planEntities.name: 2.1.2.32 - Support to enhance national capacity on vaccination
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2 - National primary health care and nutrition systems are strengthened to ensure universal coverage and quality, inclusive and high-impact interventions
planEntities.description:
1) To support Azerbaijan’s government efforts on ensuring the successful uptake of routine childhood vaccination, series of training for HCWs were organized in four regions of Azerbaijan (Goygol, Yevlakh, Minghechevir, Gobustan) that are the regions with lowest vaccination among under 6 years old children together with UNICEF and in collaboration with MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, and regional executive power offices. The main goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization.  During the event, 136 PHC workers were trained.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF

2) The interactive events aimed to build trust and demand for vaccines among parents, by providing them with accurate information about vaccines and dispelling myths and misconceptions about their safety and efficacy. 

As part of the campaign, 500 families with children who missed their routine immunizations have been personally invited to the meeting with trusted health-care professionals. In a single day of activities, about 70% of the un- and under-immunized children received their vaccines while nearly 80% of attending parents had initially delayed or declined vaccination of these children. 
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, SAMHI, UNICEF
Beneficieries: population, parents

3) WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted trainings on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. 
This event was dedicated to underscoring the significance of child vaccination. A series of events organized in the regions, titled "Embracing Scientific Evidence Over Myths: Vaccination Awareness Training," was held under the motto "Leave no one behind" in accordance with the WHO's European Immunization Agenda 2030. The primary goal of the training was to enhance the skills of healthcare workers in those regions based on best practice guidelines for routine immunization. 
The event involved 132 pediatricians and nurses from Shirvan and 76 healthcare workers from Lankaran and surrounding cities.
Stakeholders: MoH, TABIB, AzPc 

4) To raise awareness on vaccination, WHO, the Azerbaijan Pediatric Society (AzPC), and TABIB conducted awareness-raising events on October 27 and November 17 in Shirvan and Lankaran cities, respectively. During the events, Board Members of AzPC and experts from the Ministry of Health engaged in discussions with parents on vaccine hesitancy and addressed their queries. The primary goal of the meetings was to enhance parents' awareness regarding vaccination while dispelling misconceptions about vaccines. The two events involved 73 parents who had initially refused vaccination.

5) To support Azerbaijan’s government in promoting routine childhood vaccination, various educational materials were developed:
1. Questions & Answers Brochure: Addresses key questions and dispels vaccine myths. Printed and distributed during European Immunization Week and other vaccine-related events, with 197,750 copies.
2. Brochure on Vaccine-Preventable Diseases: Provides fundamental vaccine information. 7,750 copies delivered, more to be distributed after approval of the new national immunization calendar.
3. Measles Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed to vaccine facilities via TABIB at immunization events. Additionally, 203,000 flyers printed and are being distributed during awareness events.
4. Rubella Poster and Flyer: 5,300 posters distributed via TABIB at immunization events. Furthermore, 203,000 flyers printed and are being disseminated during events.

planEntities.name: 2.1.2.36 - Strengthen emergency medical care services
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2 - National primary health care and nutrition systems are strengthened to ensure universal coverage and quality, inclusive and high-impact interventions
planEntities.description:
Over a recent period, a comprehensive effort was made to enhance the capacity and knowledge of healthcare professionals in Azerbaijan, focusing on emergency care systems (ECS), through various educational initiatives and collaborations.

The initiatives began with a three-day ECS Training course on Basic Life Support (BLS) and Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) Train-the-Trainer (ToT) for 19 health workers from emergency units. This was followed by a capacity group study visit to Turkish universities, where participants gained firsthand experience in emergency care system organization, case management, and emergency unit design. A significant number of healthcare education professionals, 152 from ASATID and AMU, attended ToT sessions in January and February, highlighting the commitment to training educators in these critical areas.

A pivotal development was the completion of the HEAT assessment at eight project hospitals, leading to a final report that underscores the ongoing evaluation and improvement efforts in healthcare facilities. Concurrently, a “ECS Workshop for Curriculum Development” was held, attracting 68 representatives and culminating in a comprehensive report that outlined the curriculum development process for medical education in Azerbaijan, with plans for further development of educational materials.

Further, the ECS Capacity Group Study Visit to Türkiye marked another collaborative effort under the Health Professionals’ Education focus area, signifying international cooperation. Throughout a three-month period, 266 participants completed BLS and ACLS training programs at SUM-Sim, demonstrating a broad engagement with the training programs. Specialized training, such as the PHTLS Training Program, was also conducted for emergency care doctors and candidate trainers, enhancing the specialized skills required for emergency care.

ECS Webinar sessions played a crucial role in reaching out to a wider audience, with 550 participants in the initial sessions and a total of 1170 participants in subsequent series, highlighting the scalability of digital learning platforms. Community engagement was also a priority, as evidenced by CPR Awareness Community Events and Training, which educated over 300 people in CPR skills, and a first aid awareness training session for UNDP Baku office employees.

The summer period saw 257 physicians from TABIB successfully completing BLS and ACLS training courses at SUM-Sim, indicating the training's appeal to medical professionals. The academic landscape was further enriched with the launch of the Department of Emergency Medicine and the implementation of instructional materials for the 4th year Emergency Medicine clerkship, developed by WHO experts.

Additional ToT training courses in PHTLS and BLS & ACLS were conducted, reaching more participants and extending the training's impact. The procurement of BLS and ACLS mannequins and the advancement of medical devices and equipment procurement demonstrate the logistical support backing these educational endeavors.

This narrative chronicles a multi-faceted approach to improving emergency care education and capacity in Azerbaijan, featuring international collaboration, comprehensive training programs, and significant community engagement efforts. WHO Azerbaijan CO held a community engagement demonstration to promote and raise awareness of the importance of learning cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) skills among the guests of the high-level regional meeting of WHO/Europe and local health authorities (MOH, TABIB, SAMHI) on the "Fit-For-Purpose Hospitals" event on 6 June. Guests included around 200 government representatives, hospital practitioners, and partners from across the WHO European Region Guests. CPR is a vital first response during sudden cardiac arrest. It is not necessary to be a medical professional to perform CPR; anyone can learn these skills. The participants had a chance to learn about and practice CPR on the special mannequin under the supervision of our doctors during the event.

planEntities.parentName: Produit 2.1.1 - Produit 2.1
planEntities.description:
Le projet consiste à mettre en œuvre les activités entrant dans le cadre de la riposte du Ministère de la Santé du Bénin en réponse à la COVID-19. A long terme, ce projet contribuera au rehaussement du plateau technique sanitaire du Bénin, ainsi :
PAUPPI Phase 1: 
l'acquisition d'un (01) laboratoire mobile P3 y compris ses équipements,
l'acquisition de deux ambulances médicalisées y compris les équipements
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
PAUPPI - Phase  2: 
l’acquisition, l’installation et l’équipement de deux (02) laboratoires nationaux de niveau P3 à Ouidah et à Parakou

PAUPPI -Phase 3:
l’acquisition, installation et équipement d’unités de soins en matériaux préfabriqués à Abomey, Lokossa, Parakou et Porto-Novo (d’une capacité respective de 85 lits pour les sites de Abomey, Lokossa, Parakou et  90 lits pour le site de Porto-Novo."

planEntities.name: Strengthen technical capacities for development and implementation of policy, strategy and investment programmes on food loss and waste reduction
planEntities.parentName: Authorities have the knowledge and tools to make their economic measures and policies more competitive, sustainable, inclusive and resilient
planEntities.description:
The project has been designed to support BiH in developing a national strategy and action plan for reducing food waste and loss, in alignment with national policies, context and EU requirements. 

The Action will address the following issues: 
1) Lack of hard data of FLW which show in which VCs and where in the VCs the problem is the most pressing, what the impact is and what the causes are. This lack of concrete information hampers targeted solutions finding and therefore prevents the implementation of a FLW reduction strategy at national level.
2) Lack of skills in measuring, accounting and reporting of FLW at national level. Measuring is essential to know how big the problem is and where, so that policies, strategies and targeted action can be developed.
Project beneficiaries will be trainers, extension specialists and other staff of national institutions, government, NGOs and CSOs, as well as farmer/fisher organizations, food processors, retailers, horeca actors and to some extent household consumers. The project will collaborate with and benefit from external international institutions (e.g., UNDP), providing technical advice and knowledge in FLW measurement and accounting, FLW reduction methodologies, and publicity, awareness raising and information dissemination.

planEntities.description: The Project will address the issue of existing gender economic inequalities from several angles to maximize the intervention’s impact. The Project will be structured in the format of Phase I of the two-phased intervention with the total duration of approximately six years - consecutive Phase II is already envisioned at this stage. Under Outcome 1 the activities will aim at mainstreaming gender considerations into policy-making, as well as institutional budgeting, planning, programming, and monitoring processes, hence establishing the enabling environment for women farmers, women-led agri-businesses, cooperatives, associations and networks. Under Outcome 2 an integrated approach to addressing the problem of rural women’s limited access to economic opportunities taking into consideration strengthening resilience to climate change risks is being developed both from the supply and demand sides. From the supply side work will be done to establish access to finance mechanisms which will be accessible to the primary beneficiaries through the public sector grants and mobilized private sector finance. From the demand side the main objective is to capacitate women beneficiaries through establishing networking platforms and providing all-encompassing training in business and farm management, digitalization and other skills with the use of FAO’s proprietary Farmer Field Schools (FFSs).

planEntities.name: Strengthening Bosnia and Herzegovina’s resilience to address the impact of the Ukraine war on food security and incomes of most vulnerable groups
planEntities.parentName: Authorities have the knowledge and tools to make their economic measures and policies more competitive, sustainable, inclusive and resilient
planEntities.description:
Having high dependence on fertilizers, natural gas and petroleum from the Russian Federation and moderate dependence on selected agricultural commodities from Ukraine, Bosnia and Herzegovina has already experienced inflationary pressure resulting from the war in Ukraine. According to the IMF, the country's average consumer price inflation is projected to skyrocket and reach 6.5% in 2022, and these increase in poverty and reduced food affordability and possible food shortages will have a disproportionately more drastic effect on the most vulnerable groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As this downward economic trend in more limited access to food is projected to deteriorate further, the current meal provision services will need to re-assess their capacities and changes in demand not to leave too many needy behind.

FAO and UNDP are implementing this Joint Programme with the following objectives:
•	Assess the impact of the war in Ukraine on smallholder farmers and agri-food producers’ access to finance, seeds, fertilizers and other agricultural inputs and the resulting effects on the past and projected agricultural outputs.
•	Analyze the degree of the country’s dependence on other import and export markets for key agricultural commodities in the context of the intraregional trade and food security scenarios.
•	Assess food security demand by the most vulnerable as well as map the food centres’ infrastructure and develop concrete recommendations for policy and technical measures that contribute to zero hunger in the country. 
•	Support entity-level institutions and donor partners with evidence-based adaptive contingency planning and emergency response programming in the areas of food security and social protection, with the focus on the access to food by the most vulnerable groups.

These interventions contribute to SDGs 1 and 2, as well as to the UNSDCF Outcomes 1 (Inclusive and sustainable growth) and 3 (Inclusive health and social protection systems).
