planEntities.description:
The Vidas Negras Strategy, the United Nations Interagency Strategy to Combat Racism in Brazil, is part of the agenda of the UN Interagency Thematic Group on Gender, Race and Ethnicity  - commonly known as IATG-GRE -, which is led by UN Women. Five subgroups make up the IATG-GRE and the institutional locus of the Vidas Negras Strategy is the third subgroup, in this case led by UNFPA.
During 2021, the main actions developed were:

planEntities.name: UNiTE to End Violence against Women
planEntities.parentName: 6.2 Evidences produced and communication and advocacy strategies implemented and capable of supporting planning and transparent decision-making, combating violence and crime and, promoting human rights and access to justice, with due consideration to gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age
planEntities.description: UN Brazil promoted between November 20 and December 10, 2021, the annual edition of the UN Secretary-General's campaign “UNiTE by 2030 to End Violence against Women Campaign”. Developed since 2008, it supports the 16 Days of Activism to End Violence against Women and Girls. In 2021, the initiative completes three decades of international mobilization. All over the world, the UN addressed the theme: “Orange the World: END VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN NOW!” The UN Brazil campaign called for joint efforts and actions to guarantee life and dignity to all women and girls, including in the recovery from COVID-19. The pandemic exacerbated risk factors for violence against women and girls, including unemployment and poverty, and reinforced many of its root causes, such as gender stereotypes and prejudiced social norms.

planEntities.name: Free and Equal Campaign
planEntities.parentName: 6.2 Evidences produced and communication and advocacy strategies implemented and capable of supporting planning and transparent decision-making, combating violence and crime and, promoting human rights and access to justice, with due consideration to gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age
planEntities.description: The UN Free & Equal Campaign is being implemented in Brazil since 2014. This main goal of UNFE is to promote and protect the human right of LGBTI+ people. In 2021, besides producing communication pieces raising awareness on LGBTI+ human rights and the challenges these people face, UNFE in Brazil is also directly sensitizing important stakeholders, such as journalists and digital media platforms, to combat hate speech and stigmatization against LGBTI+ people. These efforts will continue in 2022, alongside the implementation of capacity building sessions for trans people.

planEntities.name: UN WOMEN Multistakeholders partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment (HeforShe, Unstereotype Alliance and WEPs)
planEntities.parentName: 5.1 Public policies and private initiatives reinforced and encouraged for full employment and decent work, with an emphasis on the promotion of fundamental principles and rights at work, with special attention to the most vulnerable groups and to the promotion of gender, race, ethnicity and age equality and democracy in the workplace
planEntities.description:
Multistakeholders partnerships for a transformative change towards gender equality and women’s empowerment are established by UN Women Brazil to address stereotypes in marketing and communications (Unstereotype Alliance); to engage men as allies (HeForShe); to ensure the workplace is an enabling environment for women (WEPs). The key objective is to ensure that the private sector recognizes the importance and benefits of gender equality, and actively promotes it within and beyond their circles of influence, resulting in cultural and social change at organizational, community and institutional levels, influencing the public agenda. Mobilizing the private sector, not only as a funding source, but as strategic partners for the promotion of decent work for women, providing concrete measures and targets for reaching gender equality in the workplace.   

The Unstereotype Alliance, a thought and action platform that uses advertising as a force for good to drive positive change. It seeks to eradicate harmful gender-based stereotypes. The alliance is focused on empowering women in all their diversity (race, class, age, ability, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, language, education, etc.) and addressing harmful masculinities to help create a gender equal world. The Alliance brings together a powerful growing global coalition of leading industry players behind the common goal of eliminating gender bias and harmful gender stereotypes from their advertising.

The HeForShe solidarity movement for gender equality, which provides a systematic approach and targeted platform on which men and boys can engage and become change agents towards the achievement of gender equality. Achieving gender equality in our lifetimes requires an innovative, inclusive approach that both recognizes men and boys as partners for women’s rights and acknowledges the ways in which they also benefit from this equality. HeForShe invites men and boys to build on the work of the women’s movement as equal partners, crafting and implementing a shared vision of gender equality that will benefit all of humanity.
The Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) are a set of Principles to which companies and organization commit and which offer guidance to business on how to promote gender equality and women’s empowerment in the workplace, marketplace and community. Established by UN Global Compact and UN Women, the WEPs are informed by international labour and human rights standards and grounded in the recognition that businesses have a stake in, and a responsibility for, gender equality and women’s empowerment.

planEntities.description: UN Women seeks, with this project, to support Belém do Pará municipality in designing a municipal participatory care system that recognizes the value of paid and unpaid care work, responds to the needs of women and those who require care and promotes a co-responsibility culture in society to realize women’s economic rights and opportunities. The project aims to ensure that women paid care workers and women who undertake unpaid care work have access to decent work, as well as to promote a coresponsibility culture in society, to not overburden women with unpaid care work and, thus support their economic empowerment.

planEntities.name: UNDRR - Contribution of the Regional Scientific and Technical Advisory Group (R-STAG) in Brazil

planEntities.description:
Recognizing the importance of research, scientific and technical information for disaster risk reduction, UNDRR established a Scientific and Technical Advisory Group (STAG), which provides technical advice and support in the formulation and implementation of activities carried out by the disaster risk reduction community. Each regional office of UNDRR operates its own regional version of the STAG (R-STAG). The work of the R-STAG encompasses all aspects of the scientific and technical dimensions of risk reduction, with particular emphasis on the needs of developing countries. 

For the STAG in the Americas and the Caribbean, UNDRR partners with two Brazilian cientific institutions: CEMADEN (Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais) & the Paula Souza Centre (Centro Estadual de Educação Tecnológica Paula Souza). UNDRR and the two institutions collaborates to: i) produce knowledge in areas of evidence-based decision-making for disaster risk reduction in Brazil; ii) build capacities of national and subnational governments in areas of DRR data management and local risk understanding.

planEntities.name: UNDRR - "Making Cities Resilient 2030" - Implementation of Risks & Resilience Capacities Assessment Tools (QRE & Scorecard)
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description:
The Making Cities Resilient 2030 initiative held technical assistance workshops across Brazil to support local governments in applying risks assessment and disaster resilience capacities assessment tools, namely the Quick Risk Estimation tool (QRE) and the Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities.

The Scorecard is a tool for disaster resilience planning offered by UNDRR, with the design support of USAID, European Commission, IBM, and AECOM. It provides a set of assessments that allow local governments to assess their disaster resilience, structuring around UNDRR’s Ten Essentials for Making Cities Resilient. It also helps to monitor and review progress and challenges in the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction: 2015-2030 and supports the baseline analysis for preparation of the disaster risk reduction and resilience strategies.

The Quick Risk Estimation (QRE) tool serves the purposes of identifying and understanding current and future risks to both human and physical assets. The QRE Tool is not a full scale risk assessment, rather a multi-stakeholder engagement process to establish a common understanding. 

In Brazil, UNDRR technically supported the use of the QRE tool in Abaetetuba (PA), Barcarena (PA), Camaragibe (PE), Jaboatão dos Guararapes (PE), Olinda (PE) and Recife (PE). Whereas the use of the Scorecard was assisted in Porto Alegre (RS), Natal (RN), Santo André (SP), Campinas (SP), Petropolis (RJ), Nova Iguaçu (RJ), Barcarena (PA), Camaragibe (PE), Jaboatão dos Guararapes (PE), Olinda (PE), Recife (PE). All in all, 10 Brazilian cities received the technical support of UNDRR, via the MCR2030 initiative and UNDRR's partners' support (i.e., ICLEI, CEMADEN), to perform risk and resilience capacities assessment at the local level.

planEntities.name: UNDRR - "Making Cities Resilient 2030" - National Pilot of the Food Systems Scorecard Addendum
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Evidence produced to support decision-making in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race and ethnic equality throughout the life course.
planEntities.description:
The "Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities: Food System Resilience – Addendum"  was developed by UNDRR and Baylor University, with the support of FAO and WFP. The tool completes the disaster resilience capacities assessment performed by the Scorecard by delving into food systems resilience and food security issues at the city-level. It covers issues of food production, supplies, transport and services, and assess their integration into disaster resilience governance arrangements, policies and projects. 

In Brazil, the tool was nationally piloted in November 2022 in Porto Alegre (RS).

planEntities.name: UNDRR - "Making Cities Resilient 2030" - Post Disaster Recovery Support Pack to Metropolitan Recife
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description:
Aiming to support the Municipality of Recife and nearby cities in recovering from the May-2022 rain-related disaster and to accelerate the implementation of urban resilience and climate change actions to socio-environmental disasters in the city, the Secretariat of the Regional Coordination Committee of the MCR2030 initiative in the Americas and the Caribbean, composed of the Committee's co-chairing agencies, UNDRR and ICLEI, offered a Post Disaster Recovery Support Pack to the most afftected cities of the Metropolitan Region of Recife (Recife, Camaragibe, Olinda e Jaboatão dos Guararapes).

Outcomes:
i)	Support the analysis of risk management and climate change capacities in Recife, in order to identify challenges and discuss opportunities for improvement.
ii)	Build the capacities of Recife's local government and promote understanding on the implementation of resilience projects and early warning system. 
iii)	Enhance dialogue between Recife and MCR2030 cities and service providers, with a focus on the Resilience Hubs network, to carry out joint projects on the topic of disaster risk reduction at the local level, share good practices, and exchange in-depth knowledge about urban resilience.

planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description:
In early 2022, UNDRR's Regional Office for the Americas and the Caribbean has added the resilient development of Amazonian municipalities as a strategic objective of the "Making Cities Resilient 2030" (MCR2030) initiative's framework. 

During the 1st Regional meeting of ICLEI South America in the Amazon, held in Barcarena, from August 1 to 3, UNDRR allied with the regional co-chair of MCR2030 to support ICLEI's Forum of Pan-Amazonian Cities in three aspects: building technical capacity for local DRR and resilience, improve access to sustainable finance, and grow the international influence of Amazonian cities - focusing on Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador.

On October 25, representatives of the UNDRR Regional Office for the Americas and the Caribbean and ICLEI South America participated in the event co-organized with the City of Barcarena, a member of MCR2030 initiative, to raise awareness of local resilience and disaster risk reduction in the municipalities of the Pará State, Brazil.

planEntities.description: The project "Educational resources for quality education for all: restructuring of the YouTube Edu platform" aims to restructure YouTube Edu, a large broadcasting platform of educational videos, in order to promote among lower and upper secondary education students and teachers quality educational resources as a tool in the teaching-learning process. The target audience of this project are students, teachers, school community, and education personnel.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 465BRZ0002 Criança Esperança Management
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The Criança Esperança Programme is a multi-stakeholder partnership promoted by Globo TV and UNESCO. It is a multi-donor Social Mobilization and Fundraising Campaign, which has been promoted for the past 29 years. It provides technical and financial support to social projects implemented by NGOs in all regions of Brazil.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ3006  Support to culture of peace and dialogue initiatives for the sustainable development of communities affected by the dam spill tragedy of Fundão (2015, City of Mariana, Brazil)
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: This UNESCO crosscutting (SHS, SC and CLT) 3-year project is focused on fostering local sustainable development, promoting human rights and preserving the historical and intangible heritage affected by the dam collapse (2015) in the region of the city of Mariana (based in the vicinities of Ouro Preto, coincidentally a World Heritage Site since 1980). The project shall also involve the SC expertise, particularly the experience of UNESCO's International Hydrological Programme (IHP) and the MaB programme, in actions of participatory water monitoring and preservation of local biodiversity.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 465BRZ3007 Criança Esperança Programme Fund
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The Criança Esperança Programme is a multi-stakeholder partnership promoted by Globo TV and UNESCO. It is a multi-donor Social Mobilization and Fundraising Campaign, which has been promoted for the past 29 years. It provides technical and financial support to social projects implemented by NGOs in all regions of Brazil.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ3007 Impact evaluation of the social programme "Gol do Brasil" of the Brazilian Confederation of Football (CBF)
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Evidence produced to support decision-making in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race and ethnic equality throughout the life course.
planEntities.description: The present project envisages a full-fledge impact evaluation of the main corporate social responsibility project of the Brazilian Confederation of Football (CBF), called "Gol do Brasil". "Gol do Brasil" was launched in 2017 by CBF as a programme to improve social and education indicators of low-income children between 6 to 12 years old. The project is currently implemented in two Brazilian cities (Barueri and Ribeirao Pires).

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ3008 Early Childhood Comes First
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description:
This project is a social development initiative carried out in partnership with Petrobras - with a focus on improving the social assistance services for Early Childhood (children 0 to 6 years old and pregnant women) offered by Civil Society Organizations ( CSOs) as part of the social assistance policy.
Its main objective is to empower Civil Society Organizations working with children from 0 to 6 years of age to provide a basic conceptual, theoretical and methodological framework on the subject of early childhood, providing support to increase the impact of their intervention in promoting development Early Childhood Education.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ3010 Understanding the history of Africa - Strengthening educational spaces sensitive to ethnic-racial discrimination
planEntities.parentName: 6.2 Evidences produced and communication and advocacy strategies implemented and capable of supporting planning and transparent decision-making, combating violence and crime and, promoting human rights and access to justice, with due consideration to gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age
planEntities.description: This project aims to provide opportunities for a better understanding of the historical and cultural origin of African matrices in Brazil and their contributions to the construction of Brazilian identity. It foresees the reprinting of the General History of Africa collection in Portuguese and its respective synthesis, to distribute it to important stakeholders and educators. Webinars to launch this new edition will be developed to broaden the public debate on preventing stigma and racial discrimination in educational spaces.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3010 Strengthening social participation and control mechanisms for Human Rights Public Policies
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: This relatively new project is the third one signed by UNESCO with the Brazilian Human Rights Secretariat. The project was designed after concluding that many of the Brazilian human rights counsellors often lack further experience in the area and needed more technical knowledge (or recycling) in the fields in which they were supposed to provide advice for the Brazilian Government. Although the project will support all advisory committees of the Human Rights Secretariat, it will have a particular focus on capacity-building initiatives for counsellors of five major advisory committees: CDDPH, CNCD, CONADE, CONANDA and, finally, CNDI (all the councils are described in the next section).

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3019 Challenges to improve the Social Assistance System in the city of São Paulo
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The purpose of this project is to prepare the conditions for the Secretariat of Social Assistance in the city of São Paulo to consolidate the National Social Assistance system in the city, promoting well-being and social protection of families, children, adolescents and youth, disabled people and the elderly, improving the services rendered by the Secretariat and by private selected organizations in order to improve the synergy between them.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3049 Observatory of Justice Policies and National School of Conflict Prevention and Resolution
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The main objective of the project is to map and monitor the access to justice in Brazil through an observatory that will (i) allow the promotion of public policies and promote strategies of nonjudicialization, through professional development and training of civil servants and civil society, and (ii) strengthen the National School of Conflict Prevention and Resolution of the Ministry of Justice and Public Safety.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3051 Support the consolidation of social development policies to promote and strengthen citizenship actions in Brazil
planEntities.parentName: 5.1 Public policies and private initiatives reinforced and encouraged for full employment and decent work, with an emphasis on the promotion of fundamental principles and rights at work, with special attention to the most vulnerable groups and to the promotion of gender, race, ethnicity and age equality and democracy in the workplace
planEntities.description: This technical cooperation agreement intends to support the consolidation of social development policies for the promotion and strengthening of citizenship in Brazil, through the improvement of programs and services, managerial tools and technologies.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ3005 Ethical Connections of the Third Sector
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: This Project is a social development project aimed at qualifying non-governmental organizations (NGOs), partners of Petrobras. It aims at creating capacities, contributing to strengthen the management of Petrobras's NGOs partners, reinforcing the good governance of these NGOs, accountability, transparency, practice of ethics and integrity, in line with compliance practices, enhancing the results and positive impacts generated by the projects developed.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3050 - Innovation for human rights education policies for the city of Sao Paulo
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The following project is a partnership between the Human Rights and Citizenship Secretariat (Secretaria de Direitos Humanos e Cidadania de Sao Paulo) and the UNESCO Brasilia Office. The project is expected to improve the city policies on human rights and culture of peace by reinforcing the concept of "right to the city" and also reinforcing the transversality of human rights throughout all city secretariats, particularly the municipal education secretariat.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 586RLA2001 South-South cooperation to strengthen the integrated management and sustainable use of water resources in the context of Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP)
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Strengthened participatory regional and subnational governance models for natural resource management, ecosystem services and climate change adaptation and mitigation in urban and rural areas
planEntities.description: The project aims to support the formation and consolidation of technical, institutional and legal capacities for the integrated management and sustainable use of water resources in Latin America and the Caribbean, and the Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP).Through the exchange of experiences, knowledge and best practices, this project will contribute to institutional consolidation and to adoption of policies associated with the Millennium Development Goals and the Sustainable Development in the context of post-2015 Development Agenda.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2005 Expansion and modernization of IBICT actions related to collection activities, storage, systematization, analysis, dissemination and preservation of data and information relating to STI
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: This project aims to expand and modernize the Brazilian Institute of Science and Technology Information (IBICT) actions in order to consolidate its institutional competencies in collection, storage , systematization , analysis, dissemination and preservation of data and information related to STI. Created in 1954, the IBICT is the Brazilian organization responsible for promoting capacity-building and developing the infrastructure related to science and technology for the production, socialization and integration of scientific and technological knowledge.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2010 Support for the technical and institutional preparation of ADASA for the 8th World Water Forum
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Strengthened participatory regional and subnational governance models for natural resource management, ecosystem services and climate change adaptation and mitigation in urban and rural areas
planEntities.description: The objective of this project is to provide the ADASA technical and institutional capacities to enable the Agency to work with the Government of the Federal District in the preparation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of the 8th edition of the World Water Forum, which will take place in Brasilia, March 2018, with the 1st edition of this event to occur in the southern hemisphere.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2023 Development of institutional capacities for processes of formulation, implementation and evaluation of public policies of Science, Technology, Innovation and Communications in Brazil
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: The project provides structural mechanisms to the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology, Innovation and Communications (MCTIC) to reinforce and implement the Brazilian National Strategy for Science, Technology and Innovation (Estratégia Nacional de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação - ENCTI, 2016-2019). The project is also an important enabler for the fullfilment of SDG 9 in Brazil, particularly its target "b" ('Support domestic technology development, research and innovation in developing countries, including by ensuring a conducive policy environment for, inter alia, industrial diversification and value addition to commodities").

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2024 Promoting STI and economic public policies through the development of the technological parks and the local ecosystem of innovation in the state of Goias
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: The project intends to help the Brazilian state of Goias to implement its mid-term STI strategy for 2020-2023 by the enhancement of the technical capacity of the seven existing technological parks of the state (parques tecnológicos) as important drivers for local sustainable development.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2022 Strengthening the work of the Brazilian National Water Agency (ANA) and of the Brazilian Water Sector organizations in the preparatory actions for the 8th World Water Forum
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Strengthened participatory regional and subnational governance models for natural resource management, ecosystem services and climate change adaptation and mitigation in urban and rural areas
planEntities.description: The Project aims to expand and strengthen the technical, policy development and institutional mobilisation capacities of the entities of the Brazilian National Water Resources Management System and Brazilian Water Sector organizations in engaging with national and international agendas related to the 8th World Water Fórum (to be held in Brasilia, Brazil, in March 2018), as well as its preparatory actions for their participation in the event and contribution to its success.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ2025 Fostering local sustainable development in the economic area of the SUAPE industrial and harbour complex
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: Under this new partnership evolving from social matters already partially covered in the first project document (2016-2018) with UNESCO, the BRZ Office shall now provide external consultants and technical advice on inclusive sustainable development strategies to help the SUAPE harbour administration in a long-term investment and sustainable development plan for the surrounding area. This new 3-year project will now shift from previous SHS components to SC priority areas such as the protection of local biodiversity, a more harmonic relation with the local marine enviornment and other pilot initiatives on biodiversity, including nature-based solutions.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ5003 Free Education
planEntities.parentName: 5.1 Public policies and private initiatives reinforced and encouraged for full employment and decent work, with an emphasis on the promotion of fundamental principles and rights at work, with special attention to the most vulnerable groups and to the promotion of gender, race, ethnicity and age equality and democracy in the workplace
planEntities.description: The Free Education Project consists in the development of an interactive platform to provide capacity building, enhancement and the insertion of young people in the workplace through technological solutions that enable the creation of educational itineraries adaptable to the user's profile, as well as free learning using mutual collaboration mechanisms. The Project aims to implement an educational platform for youth and ensure they have the necessary skills to match them with job opportunities in the industry sector aiming to reduce unemployment rates among youth and promote training and lifelong skills.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ5004 Media and Education
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The project aims to continue disseminating MIL in Brazil, mobilizing partners to cooperate in developing innovative national MIL initiatives. The main output will be an online MIL platform in Portuguese that will have an on-line course on MIL for teachers and students. This platform can also be useful for Portuguese speaking African Countries. The platform will be a hub for collaborative and innovative projects on MIL in Portuguese. A local network of Universities already working on MIL will promote conferences and workshops as outreach activities to further engage local stakeholders, especially among public policy makers, private sector, academia and civil society.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ5015 Knowledge and Information Management of the Participatory Urban Planning of the City of São Paulo
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: The Project aims to use innovative and efficient participatory methodologies and tools for urban planning in the City of São Paulo, using strategies to manage information and knowledge to develop urban planning public policies for the city of São Paulo.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ5016 Open Government: Transparency and Prevention of Corruption
planEntities.parentName: 6.1 Legislation, public policies and institutional capacities strengthened and aligned with international human rights standards to protect, prevent and respond to violence, crime, exploitation, neglect and discrimination, including against groups in situations of greater vulnerability or emergency, considering gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age, ensuring democratic and transparent governance with broad social participation and access to justice
planEntities.description: The Project aims to promote the dialogue between government and society through open government initiatives, in order to ensure progress towards sustainable development goals, especially those related to institutional strengthening of public administration, in order to make them more effective and responsible at all levels. The main objectives are to implement programmes and actions that promote transparency, integrity and prevention of corruption in public administration, and to improve the relationship with civil society and private sector.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ5017 Innovation to Improve Public Municipal Administration
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The Project aims to strengthen a municipal policy of innovation and modernize public service provision through improved communication channels with the citizens. The technical cooperation will diagnose, analyze, and plan initiatives that are specific to the development of innovation indicators and the management of information through TICs in the municipality of São Paulo, to promote the strategic use of innovation by the Municipal Secretariat of Innovation and Technology of the municipality of São Paulo as a tool to improve public municipal administration and improve the provision of services to citizens.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ5018 Consumers Rights in Knowledge Societies
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 The country is supported to strengthen its institutional capacities in order to promote sustainable production and consumption, as well as the management of natural resources in rural and urban areas
planEntities.description: The project aims to improve the management of information and knowledge of Brazilian National System of Consumer Protection through institutional strengthening of the National Secretariat of Consumers, also by improving public policies aimed at improving consumer protection Brazil and promoting the National Plan of Consumption and Citizenship.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570RLA4000 Recovery of the Rio de Janeiro National Museum
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: The project is part of the Global Project "Museu Nacional Vive" and continues the work carried out for the restoration of the Paço São Cristóvão and the reconstruction of the National Museum through the project 914BRZ1075, with the Ministry of Education. The planned strategies and inputs aim at the restoration of the Palace and attached structures, as well as technical studies and interventions for the implementation of the Museum, considering UNESCO instruments and the premises contained in the Project "Museu Nacional Vive", established in the Governance Structure signed in 17 December 2019 between the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), Fundação Vale and UNESCO.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ1075 Annual SDG 4-Education 2030 agenda workplan (2018-2019-AE), agency execution, with the Ministry of Education - National Museum Rio de Janeiro
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: A fire occurred on 2 September 2018 which destroyed one of the most important scientific and anthropological institutions in Latin America, the National Museum at Rio de Janeiro, constituting the greatest tragedy for Brazilian culture and education in recent times. After the fire, an Emergency UNESCO Mission was mobilized to act at the National Museum, in coordination with national and local authorities and technical teams. The Mission contributed to planning the first rescue and emergency actions and the final report proposed a plan of action for the reconstruction of the National Museum.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4018 Shared Management of Brazilian Cultural Heritage
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: This project aims to enlarge the social appropriation and the capacity of shared management of Brazilian Cultural Heritage, involving federative entities, private sector and civil society organizations.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4019 Safeguard of the Cultural and Linguistic Heritage of indigenous peoples recently contacted and of indigenous peoples living near borders in the Amazon region
planEntities.parentName: 6.1 Legislation, public policies and institutional capacities strengthened and aligned with international human rights standards to protect, prevent and respond to violence, crime, exploitation, neglect and discrimination, including against groups in situations of greater vulnerability or emergency, considering gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age, ensuring democratic and transparent governance with broad social participation and access to justice
planEntities.description: This project aims to develop safeguard actions to protect the cultural and linguistic heritage of indigenous peoples living near borders in the Amazon region with another Latin America countries, with special attention to indigenous people who were recently contacted.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4020 Strengthening and modernizing cultural public policies in Federal District
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: This Project aims to promote the strengthening and modernizing cultural public policies in the Federal District considering its transversal and strategic dimensions to sustainable and integrated development, based on several principles, such as valorization of cultural citizenship, widened access to cultural goods and rights, preservation of cultural and historical heritage focusing on the creative economy. In this sense, it's also aimed to position Brasilia as the cultural capital of Brazil, strengthening the concepts of avant-garde territory, originality, and creativity, where diversity, tradition, and innovation coexist.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3025 Project "Resgate Barão do Rio Branco"
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Evidence produced to support decision-making in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race and ethnic equality throughout the life course.
planEntities.description: This Project aims to strengthen skills and to broaden the reach of Project Rescue of manuscript and historical documentation already existing abroad regarding Brazil called "Barão do Rio Branco", as well as instigate its institutional enhancement, focusing on the need of identification, preservation of historic information and promotion of represented cultural heritage, be certainly or potentially, by its documental collection.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4021 Instruments and strategies for sustainable development of the Historic Centre of Salvador, Bahia Connected as:
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Expanded institutional capacities for the strengthening and articulation of public policies in the areas of infrastructure, cities, energy, transport systems and urban mobility that are safe and environmentally sustainable, technologically enhanced and deconcentrated to reduce territorial inequalities
planEntities.description: The objective of the Project aims is to train Mário Leal Ferreira Foundation - FMLF, public agents, private and social actors for the application of urban instruments foreseen in the Urban Development Director Plan, aiming the conception of strategies and projects directed to the requalification of cultural heritage and sustainable development of the Historic Centre of Salvador, Bahia.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4022 Shared Management of the arqueological site Cais do Valongo and conception of a territory museum
planEntities.parentName: 6.1 Legislation, public policies and institutional capacities strengthened and aligned with international human rights standards to protect, prevent and respond to violence, crime, exploitation, neglect and discrimination, including against groups in situations of greater vulnerability or emergency, considering gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age, ensuring democratic and transparent governance with broad social participation and access to justice
planEntities.description: The project aims to promote the conservation and shared management of the Arqueological Site Cais do Valongo, inscribed at the World Heritage List on July 9 2017, through the creation of a Territory Museum on the protected area. The project will consider transversality between municipal institutions and a strategic dimension for the integrated and sustainable tourism-cultural development of the port region of the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil and it will be based on principles of recognition of memory and cultural diversity, enlargement of access to cultural goods and services and preservation of historical and cultural heritage.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4023 Improvement of the Management Capacities of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Brazil
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The project aims to improve the management capabilities of the national intangible heritage policy, with the purpose of decentralizing and disseminating its principles and instruments, strengthening the integrated action of the various public and civil society bodies, for the sustainability of intangible cultural assets.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ4024 Promotion of tourism in cultural and natural heritage sites, the creative economy and other tourism and sustainable development policies
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The project pursues to promote the strengthening of the governmental policy for the development of tourism, through the valorization of the cultural and natural heritage, creative economy and other transversal policies, based on the intersectoral and interinstitutional articulation. Also it aims to promote creativity and diversity, and the achievement of a diversification of the national tourism, and the implementation of the UN 2030 Sustainable Development Goals Agenda.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 570BRZ1017 WITH RACISM, THERE IS NO DEMOCRACY
planEntities.parentName: 6.2 Evidences produced and communication and advocacy strategies implemented and capable of supporting planning and transparent decision-making, combating violence and crime and, promoting human rights and access to justice, with due consideration to gender, race, ethnicity, origin, nationality and age
planEntities.description: The project aims to disseminate and enhance the culture and history of African peoples among the school community, in line with the implementation of National Law, which establishes the mandatory theme "Afro-Brazilian History and Culture" in the national education curriculum in Brazil. The project's main activity is translating into Portuguese and the publication of volumes IX, X, and XI of the General History of Africa Collection. The target audience includes teachers from the public school system, the school community, education professionals and managers, human rights professionals, researchers, general managers, and others interested in the education of ethnic-racial relations.

planEntities.name: SDG ECD  Joint Programme
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description:
The Joint Program SDG Fund was created within the framework of the UN's international reform process and relies on resources from several countries. It aims to encourage countries to accelerate the achievement of the 17 SDGs in an integrated manner, with the support of the UN System.
In Brazil, the Joint SDG Fund – support for the Happy Child Program, is based on evidence that investment gaps in Early Childhood and their families/caregivers are an obstacle to achieving sustainable development.

By supporting the Criança Feliz PCF Program, focusing on Early Childhood development, the Joint SDG Fund seeks to accelerate the SDGs in the country.

planEntities.name: UNAIDS PAHO/WHO  UNODC  ILO  UNESCO  Country Envelope
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: Resources earmarked for activities implemented by cosponsors at the national level are funded with a country envelope, adjusted according to the programmed activities in line with each agency's mandate. Ministry of Health 2021 HIV priorities: Priority 1: Reduce the mortality of people living with HIV and TB-HIV co-infection; Priority 2: Expand and strengthen the diagnosis and treatment of STIs, tuberculosis and leprosy; Priority 3: Reduce vertical transmission of syphilis and hepatitis B and eliminate vertical transmission of HIV; Priority 5: Expand access to health promotion and prevention actions for the most vulnerable populations; Priority 6: Foster scientific and technological development to fight leprosy; Priority 7: Qualify Management and Governance

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3047 Public policies for the rights of elderly people: Empowerment for all ages in Brazil
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: The decline in fertility rates in Brazil in the last decade has had profound implications upon the demographic trend of its pyramid with a clear trend towards a growing elderly population. If the current trend continues, the Brazilian Institute of Statistics and Geography (IBGE) estimates that by 2050 the age segment above 60 years old will represent 30% of the total Brazilian population. UNESCO's ideals of lifelong learning, education for all (EFA), media literacy and access to culture and science as fundamental human rights are few of the areas where the Brazilian Government could benefit from UNESCO's expertise.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ1102  Higher Education and the National Education Plan: the commitment to quality and training for work and citizenship
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: This project aims to promote Brazilian higher education by improving innovative actions implemented by the Ministry of Education's Secretariat of Higher Education (SESu). The project proposal consists in expanding new methodologies for teachers' and managers' training; studies evaluating access, permanence and insertion in the labor market; improvement of health residency programs; incentive to improve academic-institutional management; and strategies internationalization for higher education.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ1115 Development of Strategies and Tools for Monitoring and Evaluating the Implementation of Public Educational Policies according to the Goals of the National Education Plan - PNE and the Articulated Action Plan - PAR
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: This Project aims to improve the institutional capacity of the Management, Articulation and Educational Projects Department (DIGAP), at the National Education Development Funs (FNDE) through the review of processes, provision of subsidies for the review of standards, and definition of strategies for improving effectiveness in the application of education resources, with regard to infrastructure of schools and educational spaces, education staff training, and acquisition of teaching material. The proposed results should contribute to the achievement of greater effectiveness of the public resource and the provision of more efficient school structures.

planEntities.name: UNESCO 914BRZ3053 Provision of capacity-building opportunities for the young population of Rio de Janeir
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course

Adolescent and Youth programmatic area are focused on National policies and programmes strengthened for incorporation of the human rights and needs of adolescents and youth at national and subnational levels, through gender equality and culturally sensitive approaches, particularly for girls, Afro-descendants and vulnerable youth populations.
In 2021, through the “Observatório da Juventude”, created at the end of 2019, young leaders from all over Brazil were permanently articulated to monitor the establishment of the goals of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) in relation to youth.  For the second year, the experience of “Roda das Juventudes Já!” selected 30 young people from different identities and territories of the country in a space of collective construction for solutions against gender violence, using the methodology of design thinking. As part of the celebrations of the International Day of the Girl Child  (October 11th),  UNFPA CO partnered with Plan International Brazil and delivered a virtual forum for adolescents on hate speech prevention and encouraged healthy and safe internet use. The “Roda de Diálogos sobre Violëncia Contra a Mulher com Deficiência” was carried out by UNFPA CO as part of the reflections regarding the 3rd transformative result, the 16 days of activism and the International Day of Disabled Persons (December, 3rd).
In 2022, the program developed a pilot project for young people with disabilities; focused on youth participation in international conferences; approached municipalities; and established a partnership with the National Science Olympics.

planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description:
PrEP Project - Salvador
MAIN GOAL
Encouraging the adherence of transgender women and transvestites to the treatment of HIV Pre Exposure Prophylaxis and expand information on HIV/AIDS, syphilis and viral hepatitis, as well as combination prevention in Municipalities of Salvador and Lauro de Freitas through the implementation of the PrEP Trans Project.

SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES:
a) Train navigators to act in peer education (combined HIV/STI prevention, offer of voluntary testing, support for linking to health services through agents navigators, and support for treatment adherence);
b) Promote HIV counseling, PrEP and emotional support to the beneficiary public for bonding the PrEP programs available in Salvador;
c) Provide support actions in Telemedicine in the social, psychological and health fields for the key project population;
d) Disseminate the combined prevention strategy, with an emphasis on PrEP, through educational materials communication, communication channel and online events.

Bora Saber Project in Boa Vista (RR) and Belém (PA)
OBJECTIVE
Increase the access to HIV testing and ensure the link to health services for ART initiation and retention based on the 90/90/90 Goals.


GOALS
•        Increase the uptake of HIV testing among adolescents and youth 15- 24 by 30% 
•        Linkage of at least 90% of all HIV positive cases diagnosed to health services for treatment initiation

STRATEGY 
HIV testing will be conducting during outreach activities. Youth and adolescents will be visiting hot spots with high concentration of most vulnerable populations such as MSM, transgender, migrants and refugee, to promote peer HIV/AIDS/STI prevention, and offer voluntary HIV testing, counseling and inputs, and combination prevention. The activities performed in a non-health service environment (more community-based), can access these populations better and can deliver healthcare in a way that a formal health care structure cannot. The navigators (peers) will escort the HIV positive cases to health services for immediate ART initiation. Additionally, retention groups will support the adherence to ART. A consultative group will be established to follow up the project, with participation of municipal health representatives, NGOs, youth and adolescent networks, and UNFPA. 


BENEFICIARY POPULATION
Adolescents and youth from key populations including men who have sex with men, transgender, migrants and refugees.  The project will target adolescents and young people in hot spot areas including cruising areas, venues, and migrant and refugee shelters. 

The project will use established platforms to articulate a multi-sectoral response to engage partners from outside the health system. Community links are also key to a successful HIV response, as Brazil clearly demonstrated in the past.  The engagement and participation of youth and adolescents will be key to the success and UNFPA will work with existing networks of young people living with HIV and LGBTI groups to ensure their full involvement in all stages of the project, including their full participation in the coordination mechanism to be established at municipal level.

planEntities.description: Strengthen the Brazilian prevention, response and services on GBV, in the states of Amazonas and Roraima in the northern region of the country, whose government capacities were severely affected due the COVID-19 pandemic. The proposal aims to fully meet the needs of vulnerable populations of women, adolescents, girls, indigenous, LGBTQI+, incarcerated women, migrant women in forced displacement at risk of SGBV, and survivors of gender based violence living in most deprived communities and geographical areas. The proposed interventions will be focusing in three specific strategic areas as follows: 1) strengthen GBV prevention among populations in most vulnerable conditions through raising awareness community based interventions and behavior change communication strategies; 2) strengthen the capacities of GBV safe spaces/public services focusing on healing, empowerment and recovery of survivors, and enable the access of women and girls survivors of GBV to the intersectoral protection network (health, justice, security and social assistance); 3) strengthen the local government capacities by supporting the development of public policies and initiatives, and providing training cycles for public professionals from health, justice, security and social assistance.

The Project main strategies: 
Strategy 1 - Human rights training for 700 obstetric nurses and midwives, focusing on sexual and reproductive rights. In partnership with Fiocruz (Scientific institution for research and development in biological sciences - Ministry of Health).
Strategy 2 - Leadership Training for 50 midwifery leaders. In partnership with the Brazilian Association of Midwives and Obstetric Nurses (ABENFO).

South-South Collaboration - The Project also maintains a dialogue and collaboration with UNFPA Colombia and Mexico and its initiatives in partnership with the J&J Foundation to strengthen midwifery.

planEntities.description:
Through the Situation Room initiative, UNFPA Brazil promotes the sharing of experiences between CSOs in the north and northeast regions of Brazil, also provides training on human rights issues and facilitates dialogue with representatives of public authorities in the north and northeast regions of Brazil. It also provides financial support for initiatives related to gender-based violence. In addition, UNFPA Brazil has the Mulher Segura Platform, with the mission of to create bridges between citizens, public authorities and civil society committed to combating violence against women, in order to facilitate access to qualified information and rights provided for by law, in addition to the exchange of experiences among women. We seek to foster a collaborative and important space, in permanent articulation with the population and local networks - a space that goes beyond the listing of local services, no matter how extensive our database may be. 
UNFPA promoted support to the CSO in the state of Rio de Janeiro. These black social organizations received support for the development of entrepreneurship and income generation projects, through training processes, specialized technical consultancy and application of seed capital and individualized support, for accountability, through community facilitators.
The partnership between the Secretary of State for Women of the Federal District (SMDF) and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) aims to contribute to the strengthening of the institutional actions of the Federal District Government in order to expand public policies aimed at women, implemented by the SMDF that guarantee the promotion of women's rights and the fight against all types of violence, in addition to the inclusion of women in the process of social, economic, political and cultural development of the country, with a focus on the defense of human rights. In the context of the 2030 Development Agenda, formulating, implementing and monitoring programs, initiatives and/or strategies and technical cooperation projects with reference to international evidence and good practices is part of the country's investments to leverage local and national and equitable socio-economic and equitable development. for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this way, the partnership between SMDF and UNFPA aims to promote human rights, gender equality and the prevention of violence against women and girls by contributing to the organization of innovative strategies and methodologies that promote female empowerment and full access to education and the job market, respecting the specificities of race/color, gender identity and sexual orientation. It is expected at the end of the project the implementation of intersectoral actions and the advancement of the Agenda of Public Policies aimed at Women in the Federal District, so that the needs, rights and expectations of women are effectively incorporated into the policies of the Government of the Federal District. (GDF).

planEntities.name: UNIDO - Addressing the energy, water, food and climate nexus through organic waste to energy solutions in the Metropolitan Region of Recife
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Public policies, private initiatives and institutional capacities strengthened to promote the improvement of value chains, stimulating innovation, entrepreneurship and associativism, improving competitiveness to promote productive inclusion and sustainable economic development
planEntities.description: The project is based on an official request of the Government of the State of Pernambuco. It aims to lay the foundation for a larger project to be implemented in partnership with the Government, private sector and with support of international climate finance. The project addresses the sensitive energy, water, food and climate nexus in the Metropolitan Region of Recife (RMR) by promoting the use of organic waste to energy solutions (WTE). The project is of cross-sectoral nature and contributes to the implementation of several federal, state-level and urban policies and regulations, such as the Solid Waste Plan of RMR, the State Plan for Solid Residues of Pernambuco, the Recife Sanitation Plan, the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), as well as the recently adopted 2050 National Energy Plan with its ambitious renewable energy targets. Solid waste management, water and sanitation, energy security and climate change adaptation are major interrelated concerns of the Metropolitan Region of Pernambuco (RMR), which includes 15 municipalities, provides livelihood for around 4 million people and hosts major industries in the region. The overall objective of the project is to address the energy, water, food and climate nexus by promoting the use of organic waste to energy (WTE) solutions in the Metropolitan Region of Pernambuco (RMR). The project comprises a 16 months preparatory phase, which foresees the development of relevant assessments for two pilot projects and the formulation of a project document for the main phase. The preparatory phase includes the following results: 1. Assessment of the Camaragibe landfill and recommendations for environmental improvement, including the identification of investment opportunities for organic WTE; 2. Assessment of organic WTE investment opportunities (e.g. biogas, biomethane) on the island of Fernando de Noronha; 3. Formulation of a project document for the main phase and mobilization of climate finance for the implementation.

planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description: Coordinated by UNFPA Brazil CO and with participation of 20 UNCT members was an important support to provide evidence-based advocacy and technical assistance in working with adolescents and youth within the actions coordinated by the different UNCT members. The Group aims at establishing a space for dialogue between governments, civil society and UN agencies on the topic of Youth, providing technical assistance to the UNCT and strengthening articulation and joint work in initiatives focusing on Brazilian youth. The Group did not carry out activities originally planned to 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and funds expired in December. Activities restarted in May 2021, after the renewal of funds and updating of focal points. The first action was about Durban+20, named "Cinema do Futuro". In 2022, the group hired a UNV to map youth organizations that work to combat climate change.

planEntities.description:
Objective: Coping with the Multiple Burden of Malnutrition in Schoolchildren.
Main partners in Brazil: Brazilian Cooperation Agency of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (ABC/MRE), the Ministry of Health, through the General Coordination of Food and Nutrition of the Department of Health Promotion (CGAN/DEPROS/MS).
Activities: Raising evidence and exchange of successful experiences between Brazil and other countries that also face the problem. 
Partner countries: Colombia and Peru.
The partnership is divided into two main axes: strengthening the South-South cooperation space and support for the actions of the United Nations Decade of Action for Nutrition, which runs until 2025.

planEntities.name: WFP Beyond Cotton Project
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Public policies and institutional capacities strengthened in the areas of education, health, social assistance, food security and nutrition and decent work in order to address the needs of the most vulnerable groups and promote gender, race, ethnicity throughout the life course
planEntities.description:
The Project works in a complementary way to other South-South cooperation initiatives conducted by the Brazilian government in the cotton sector in Africa. A main dimension of this Project is the link with Food and Nutrition Security (FNS) since it is possible to encompass the discussions around the conceptual structure of the food system. This means covering from the means of production, the forms of processing, supply, marketing and distribution, the choice and consumption of food, including individual and collective food practices, to the generation and disposal of waste.
Four countries benefits from the project: Kenya, Tanzania, Benin and Mozambique

planEntities.name: Ratification, implementation and reporting on international labour standards
planEntities.parentName: Policy and legal frameworks and institutional capacities strengthened to address gender inequality and human rights, in line with national and international commitments
planEntities.description:
The Government of Botswana has requested for ILO technical support in facilitating a knowledge sharing and ratification of six instruments that the Government has identified for prioritized ratification, namely the Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930, the Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 1981 (No. 155), Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 2006, the Employment Policy Convention, 1964 (No. 122), the Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190), and the Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 (No. 169).

During 2026, the ILO will provided support to the Government of Botswana i.e. select Government Ministries led  by the Ministry of Labour & Home Affairs towards ratification, implementation and reporting on prioritized ILO Conventions i.e. Strengthened capacity of national partners  to ratify, and implement international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

planEntities.name: Enhanced institutional capacities of national partners to produce, compile and use the tools provided to promote decent work.
planEntities.parentName: Increased availability and use of high-quality, disaggregated data by a more diverse range of stakeholders
planEntities.description: Botswana, through Statistics Botswana, conducted the Household Income and Expenditure Survey named Botswana Multi-Topic Household Survey (BMTHS). The survey takes a year to be completed. Data collection ran from November 2024 to Mid-October 2025. In 2024, the ILO supported Statistics Botswana to incorporate the 19th ICLS in this non-Labour Force Survey (LFS) source, as well as informality. As Botswana has already adhered to the 19th ICLS in the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS), it was important to ensure that the standard is also applied in the BMTHS, so that the labour market indicators compiled in QLFS are comparable to the labour market indicators compiled in this BMTHS. Furthermore, the BMTHS is used to produce poverty indicators. Given the relationship between employment (or lack of) and poverty, it is essential that employment is well defined in BMTHS, to examine the relationship between poverty and employment in Botswana. Furthermore, this source will allow Botswana to report on SDG 1.1.1 (Working poverty rate), again, highlighting the reason why employment should be well defined in HIES. Statistics Botswana  has requested ILO support for data analysis and report on the labour market indicators from this source. The above is expected to contribute towards improved labour modules in other statistical sources, by introducing the new standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). During 2026 the ILO will provided supported Botswana to produce a thematic report on the experience of youth in the labour market. This report is almost ready for dissemination and ILO is expected to provide support for the dissemination of this report.
