planEntities.name: 1.2.1.3- Programa Cocoa Life en la República Dominicana – Fase II
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.1- Incrementada la conservación y uso sostenible del capital natural y fortalecidos la producción y consumo sostenible
planEntities.description: El presente proyecto constituye la segunda fase de implementación de la iniciativa Global de Mondelēz, Programa Cocoa Life (CLP) en la República Dominicana. Esta fase estará dedicada a coordinar la implementación del CLP en el país, facilitando el diálogo entre las partes interesadas y la interacción del programa dentro de las políticas nacionales del sector del cacao en el país. Se establecerá un sistema de monitoreo y se reportará el progreso de implementación de los proyectos que se ejecutan el marco del CLP en la República Dominicana. Se establecerá una estrategia de visibilidad de las acciones y se documentarán y socializarán las lecciones aprendidas. Asimismo, se verificará que las actividades del CLP en DR cumplan con las políticas de Género y prevención del trabajo infantil.

planEntities.name: 1.2.1.4- Plan de Manejo para la Eliminación del Uso de Hidroclorofluorocarbonos en República Dominicana (HPMP). Segunda Fase.
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.1- Incrementada la conservación y uso sostenible del capital natural y fortalecidos la producción y consumo sostenible
planEntities.description: La Segunda Fase del Plan de Manejo para la Eliminación del Consumo de Hidroclorofluorocarbonos (HPMP-II) tiene como objetivo la reducción gradual de 15.36 toneladas de sustancias con potencial de agotamiento del ozono hasta el año 2020, lo que permitirá alcanzar el 40% de la línea base de consumo establecida como compromiso del país ante el Protocolo de Montreal para la protección de la capa de ozono. Esta meta representa un 5% por encima de las obligaciones de reducción hasta el 2020 de países que operan bajo el Artículo 5 del Protocolo y expresa la vocación de la República Dominicana en la preservación del medio ambiente global.

planEntities.name: 1.2.1.4- Plan de Manejo para la Eliminación del Uso de Hidroclorofluorocarbonos en República Dominicana (HPMP). Segunda Fase.
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.1- Incrementada la conservación y uso sostenible del capital natural y fortalecidos la producción y consumo sostenible
planEntities.description: La Segunda Fase del Plan de Manejo para la Eliminación del Consumo de Hidroclorofluorocarbonos (HPMP-II) tiene como objetivo la reducción gradual de 15.36 toneladas de sustancias con potencial de agotamiento del ozono hasta el año 2020, lo que permitirá alcanzar el 40% de la línea base de consumo establecida como compromiso del país ante el Protocolo de Montreal para la protección de la capa de ozono. Esta meta representa un 5% por encima de las obligaciones de reducción hasta el 2020 de países que operan bajo el Artículo 5 del Protocolo y expresa la vocación de la República Dominicana en la preservación del medio ambiente global.

planEntities.name: 1.2.1.6- Transformando las Cadenas de Valor de Turismo
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.1- Incrementada la conservación y uso sostenible del capital natural y fortalecidos la producción y consumo sostenible
planEntities.description:
El proyecto busca reducir la emisión de gases de efecto invernadero y mejorar la eficiencia en el uso de los recursos en los eslabones más relevantes de la cadena de valor del sector de turismo: alojamiento, alimentos y bebidas, y la realización de reuniones, conferencias y eventos. A través del proyecto se ha apoyado al gobierno en el desarrollo de una Hoja de Ruta Nacional para el Turismo Sostenible, se ha provisto de asistencia técnica y capacitación a hoteles y otros actores clave del sector para la implementación de buenas practicas ambientales en áreas como eficiencia energética, gastronomía sostenible o reducción de plásticos de un solo uso.  

"Los gobiernos y las empresas de la cadena de valor adoptan estrategias, políticas y enfoques para reducir y monitorear las emisiones de GEI, la contaminación y mejorar la eficiencia de los recursos en el sector turístico.
"

planEntities.description:
Objectives: "The purpose of the event is three-fold:
• Reflect on the importance of carnivals and festivals, to strengthen their socioeconomic role for sustainable development.
• Identify measures to promote carnivals and festivals as mechanisms to enhance integration, cultural exchange, tourism diversification and the mobility of artists.
• Contribute to build and consolidate north-south-south peer-to-peer networks in the Cultural and Creative Industries domain of ´performance and celebrations´."







"⮚	To foster the creation of networks and the sharing of relevant management practices and experiences among site managers of Caribbean World Heritage sites, and sites inscribed on national Tentative Lists, linked with enslavement, memory, legacies and resilience.  
⮚	To encourage the development and implementation of holistic management strategies at World Heritage sites by leveraging the role that cultural and creative industries can play to contribute to their protection and promotion.
⮚	To raise awareness on the history of enslavement, its abolition and its modern consequences in the Caribbean through cultural heritage and cultural and creative industries, thus contributing to fight against racism and supporting contemporary creations on the themes of memory, legacies, resilience.
To support the development of sustainable tourism strategies within World Heritage sites and sites inscribed on national Tentative Lists, linked with memory, legacies, and resilience, and to contribute to educate and to deconstruct the discourses based on the concept of race that justified these systems of exploitation."





"•	Create new insertion opportunities for Hip-hop Caribbean artists within the UNESCO Transcultura Programme geographical scope, in the European Hip-hop and alternative art market
•	Enable a joint action and intercultural creative dialogue space between artists within the UNESCO Transcultura Programme geographical scope and the Afrocaribbean diaspora in Europe.
•	Enhance competitiveness and the positioning of Hip-hop as a cultural tool for integration, inclusive entrepreneurship and the artistic development of youth. "


"1. To shed light on the creative potential and capacities of artists and culture professionals living with any type of disability;
2. To advocate for cultural rights of artists and culture professionals living with any type of disability;
3. To promote the artistic work of artists and culture professionals living with any type of disability and facilitate networking among them."

planEntities.description: Analizar las condiciones del mercado de acuerdo a las distintas dimensiones que componen la funcionalidad de los mercados para monitorear y vincularlo con los índices de seguridad alimentaria.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.104- Clasificación Integrada de la Seguridad Alimentaria en Fases (CIF)
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Generar evidencias sobre la situación de seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de la población, de modo que permita el diseño de planes, programas y proyectos.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.105- Estudio Cerrando brechas de nutrición (FNG)
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Análisis de las necesidades nutricionales de los distitintos grupos de población. El análisis permite idetificar el costo de las dietas nutritivas en un hogar promedio. Los resultados del estudio informarán los programas de protección social y las políticas públicas sentitivas a la nutrición.

planEntities.name: 2.2.2.29- Fortalecimiento de la respuesta integral al VIH, con enfoque en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional.
planEntities.parentName: 2.2.2- Instituciones públicas y privadas (ONGs) del nivel nacional amplían y mejoran las intervenciones en VIH e ITS  a fin de avanzar en el cumplimiento de las metas de acción acelerada
planEntities.description:
"Mejoramiento de la alimentación y nutrición en las personas con VIH y al personal de los Servicios de Atención Integral (SAI) a través de la formación de huertos urbanos como parte de la estrategia de consejeria nutricional que a su vez resultan en medios de vida más resilientes.
De igual forma, la mejora de la nutrición permite aumentar la adherencia al tratamiento ARV y mantener una buena calidad de vida."

planEntities.name: 2.2.2.30-  Promoción de iniciativas de intercambio de experiencias, buenas prácticas y cooperación Sur-Sur para el fortalecimiento de capacidades del sistema de protección social mediante la inclusión de personas viviendo con VIH y la implementación de actividades que incentivan la integración social y el acceso a medios de vida que aseguren dietas nutritivas y saludables.
planEntities.parentName: 2.2.2- Instituciones públicas y privadas (ONGs) del nivel nacional amplían y mejoran las intervenciones en VIH e ITS  a fin de avanzar en el cumplimiento de las metas de acción acelerada
planEntities.description: Fortalecer las políticas, los programas y las capacidades de las instituciones de gobierno en la República de Guatemala y la República Dominicana para la inclusión de personas viviendo con VIH en los programas de protección social, particularmente en los que promueven la integración social y comunitaria, y el acceso de esta población a medios de vida resilientes.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.106- Diplomado en nutrición
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Esta accion forma parte de los compromisos asimidos  para fortalecer las compatencias tecnicas del personal responsable del diseno e implementacion de las politicas, programas y proyectos con incidencia en nutricion con el proposito de eficientizar la respuesta al contexto nutricional actual, desde un enfoque integral e interinstitucional, esta focalizado  a representantes de instituciones de Gobierno del sector salud y nutrición.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.107- Posicionamiento de la fortificación del arroz como política pública para la prevención de las deficiencias de micronutrientes
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Fortalecimiento de las capacidades de Gobierno en el monitoreo de la calidad y cumplimiento de los requerimientos nutritivos del arroz fortificado. De igual forma, realización de actividades de incidencia para incluir el arroz fortificado en las compras gubernamentales.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.108-  Fortalecimiento de las capacidades gubernamentales en nutrición para mejorar la atención a la población escolar
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Acompañamiento a instituciones gubernamentales para fortalecer el impacto de las acciones de salud y nutricion en el estado nutricional de los escolares.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.109-Definición de la estrategia de educación nutricional
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1- Apoyada la formulación, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas, con enfoque de derechos, para la salida sostenible de la pobreza, promoción de la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional, y reducción de las desigualdades económicas y sociales
planEntities.description: Activación de la mesa de la estrategia multi-sectorial de comunicación social y educación nutricional para generar cambios de comportamiento.

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.67-Proyecto “Acciones Anticipadas Basado en Pronósticos (FbF)” para el fortalecimiento del sistema y herramientas de pronósticos
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.3- Incrementada la resiliencia, especialmente de la población más vulnerable, ante emergencias de salud pública y riesgos de desastres
planEntities.description: Este proyecto se basa en la definición, validación y ajustes de umbrales y detonantes de inundaciones bajo modelo FbF para la cuenta del Yaque del Norte, así como la definición de procedimientos estándar (SOP) de las instituciones técnico científicas y del sistema de prevención, mitigación y respuesta a emergencias para fortalecer las capacidades en responder a inundaciones antes de un impacto.

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.68-Definición de una estrategia de asistencia humanitaria, gestión de riesgos y sistemas de alerta temprana (SAT)
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.3- Incrementada la resiliencia, especialmente de la población más vulnerable, ante emergencias de salud pública y riesgos de desastres
planEntities.description: Acompañamiento a instituciones gubernamentales para la definición de una estrategia país que defina los mecanismos de asistencia humanitaria y gestión de riesgos, tanto para funcionar nacionalmente como a nivel regional. Esta estrategia incluye componentes de almacenaje, importación, tránsito y exportación humanitaria (corredor humanitario), y telecomunicaciones

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.69-Mesa de protección social adaptativa
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.3- Incrementada la resiliencia, especialmente de la población más vulnerable, ante emergencias de salud pública y riesgos de desastres
planEntities.description: La mesa de protección social adaptativa es un espacio de coordinación entre agencias del sistema ONU, instituciones de Gobierno y la sociedad civil para fortalecer las capaciades de respuesta en emergencias del sistema de protección social.

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.70- Definición de una estrategia nacional de cambio climático
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.3- Incrementada la resiliencia, especialmente de la población más vulnerable, ante emergencias de salud pública y riesgos de desastres
planEntities.description: Asistencia técnica para acompañar al Gobierno en sus prioridades nacionales ante el cambio climático

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.71-Fortalecimiento de las capacidades nacionales y locales del sistema de prevención, mitigación y respuesta ante desastres
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.3- Incrementada la resiliencia, especialmente de la población más vulnerable, ante emergencias de salud pública y riesgos de desastres
planEntities.description: Acompañar a los socios nacionales del SNPMR a aumentar sus capacidades para dar respuesta a crisis y emergencias.

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.72- Los actores clave del Gobierno mejoran sus capacidades en materia de logítica humanitaria

planEntities.parentName: 3.1.3- Mejorados los sistemas de protección de personas refugiadas, migrantes y sus descendientes
planEntities.description: Complemento al gobierno en la respuesta de seguridad alimentaria ante el COVID-19 y a los efectos climáticos del Huracán Fiona con operaciones adicionales de transferencias basadas en efectivo y alimentos en especie que amplían el alcance humanitario.

planEntities.description: El Proyecto de Desarrollo Sostenible y Apropiado en Territorios Rurales - DESATAR inició en 2022 y culmina en 2027, con USD 31 millones, buscando atender 10000 familias. El objetivo es contribuir a reducir la pobreza de los pequeños productores rurales pobres de la cuenca baja del río Guayas. Los componentes son: C1. Apropiación de innovaciones y mejores prácticas validadas e introducidas en el territorio. C2 Mejora de capacidades técnicas, cooperativas, empresariales y de prestación de servicios con un enfoque de inclusión y de sostenibilidad ambiental. C3 Mejora de competencias técnicas y transversales de los jóvenes. C4: OPs (mujeres y jóvenes) e instituciones públicas cuentan con recursos de conocimiento y comunicación para el aprendizaje, escalamiento, contribución a políticas. Este es un proyecto clasificado por el FIDA como Transformador de Genero.

planEntities.parentName: 3.5 Normas e instrumentos de política desarrollados para fortalecer la  protección social contributiva, su gobernanza, cobertura, calidad y  sostenibilidad, y la adaptación frente a las crisis, en coordinación con el  régimen de protección social no contributiva, con foco en las poblaciones  en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad, pobreza e informalidad.
planEntities.description: Fortalecer la actual institucionalidad de la protección social ante la pérdida del empleo en Ecuador, con la finalidad de dotar a la economía de un mecanismo contra-cíclico permanente que permita atenuar los efectos negativos en el empleo y en los ingresos de los trabajadores formales e informales, y evitar una posible caída en pobreza y en condiciones de vulnerabilidad. A través de una vinculación adecuada entre políticas activas y pasivas de empleo, que considere las brechas de género, y la institucionalización de la participación de los actores sociales, se prevé promover una mejor y más rápida reinserción de los trabajadores al mercado laboral.

planEntities.description:
"Se ha colaborado con 25 organizaciones de mujeres afrodescendientes, proporcionándoles una agenda política y de incidencia que aborda derechos económicos, sociales, una vida libre de violencia y aspectos políticos. En julio de 2023, en la reunión nacional de mujeres afrodescendientes, presentaron su agenda a las autoridades nacionales. Estas autoridades se comprometieron a utilizar la agenda como referencia para sus políticas y programas sectoriales.

También se apoyo con productos comunicacionales (proveedor Livemarketing) y la entrega de tablets en colaboración con el Ministerio de Agricultura y Ganadería

planEntities.name: Apoyo para la implementación de los ODS
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Capacidades fortalecidas, normas, políticas e instrumentos producidos para  la implementación de un piso de protección social, sensible a los  grupos en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad y a las emergencias, que  mejore cobertura, calidad, equidad, gobernanza y sostenibilidad del  sistema, promoviendo una adecuada articulación entre los regímenes  contributivos y no contributivos y la provisión de servicios sociales.
planEntities.description:
El PNUD ha trabajado junto al Grupo de Desarrollo de las Naciones Unidas (UNDG, por sus siglas en inglés), en el diseño de una estrategia coherente y efectiva para el soporte en la implementación de la agenda para el desarrollo sostenible. El componente de transversalización busca generar conciencia entre todos los actores involucrados y ayudar a los gobiernos a aterrizar la agenda a nivel nacional y local para, finalmente, incorporarla en sus planes, estrategias y presupuestos en todo el territorio. 

El componente de aceleración se enfoca en asistir a los gobiernos para acelerar el progreso con respecto a las metas de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible, a través de la provisión de herramientas que ayuden a identificar las barreras principales que limitan los avances y a priorizar objetivos según el contexto. El componente de soporte de política apunta a proveer asesoría coordinada y combinada en el diseño de políticas que ayuden a los países a alcanzar las metas de los ODS.

planEntities.description: Junto a 250 adolescentes (entre 15 y 18 años) y 26 docentes de la unidad educativa “Miguel Moreno” ubicada en la ciudad de Cuenca se implementa una intervención de cambio conductual. Se promovió a través del uso de metodologías pedagógicas basadas en la reflexión colectiva y el diálogo (tertulias) el cambio de perspectiva y comportamiento sobre violencia de género y discriminación junto a la comunidad educativa. Se tiene resultados favorables ya que los participantes han comenzado a dejar de normalizar la violencia y cuestionar las normas sociales sobre los estereotipos de roles de género. (Lab Aceleración – PNUD)

La plataforma fue diseñada, testeada y será difundida junto a las y los jóvenes, estos han participado en los procesos de toma de decisión. La herramienta levanta información de los usuarios para generar un registro de este grupo poblacional y poner a disposición de hacedores de política datos que insuman los programas a favor de las juventudes. planEntities.parentName: 1.4 Capacidades fortalecidas, estrategias y herramientas desarrolladas para  la comunidad educativa, que reduzcan la exclusión y el rezago escolar;  faciliten la recuperación de los aprendizajes y la reducción de la brecha  digital; promuevan los servicios de desarrollo infantil; aseguren el acceso a  servicios básicos de agua, saneamiento e higiene y fomenten un ambiente  libre de todo tipo de violencia y discriminación.
planEntities.description: El objetivo general del Programa Multianual de Resiliencia (MYRP) de ECW para Ecuador fué garantizar el acceso continuo a una educación inclusiva y equitativa de calidad para aproximadamente 105 000 refugiados, migrantes y niños y jóvenes de las comunidades de acogida. Asegurar que los niños, niñas y adolescentes en situación de movilidad humana y de las comunidades de acogida accedan al sistema educativo, aprendan, y prosperen, a pesar de los desafíos generados por la pandemia COVID-19. En conjunto con el Ministerio de Educación de Ecuador y el Grupo de Trabajo de Educación de la plataforma GTRM (R4V), se diseñó el Programa Plurianual con el fin de promover el acceso a la educación de la población migrante y refugiada de Venezuela en Ecuador. Este Programa Plurianual dió continuidad al programa First Emergency Response (FER), financiado por Education Cannot Wait (ECW) durante 2019 y 2020. En la "FER", UNESCO actuó como Sub-beneficiario.

planEntities.name: Asistencia técnica en formulación de leyes y marco de políticas públicas para la incorporación del enfoque de Derechos Humanos y los estándares internacionales sobre acceso a la información pública
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 Capacidades estatales, nacionales y locales fortalecidas para la  administración de justicia, y para la prevención, detección, respuesta y  reducción del impacto de la inseguridad y la violencia criminal.
planEntities.description: La UNESCO aboga por el acceso a la información como una libertad fundamental y un pilar clave en la construcción de sociedades del conocimiento inclusivas. La organización promueve los derechos y valores señalados en el artículo 19 de la Declaración Universal de Derechos Humanos. El acceso a la información es parte integrante de la libertad de expresión y un instrumento importante para promover el estado de derecho u otros derechos, a fin de fomentar la confianza. Es un facilitador del desarrollo sostenible en ámbitos como la salud, el medio ambiente, la lucha contra la pobreza y la lucha contra la corrupción. La UNESCO ayuda a los Estados Miembros a cumplir e implementar tratados y acuerdos internacionales, normativa y estándares relacionados con el acceso universal a la información, así como a contribuir a las sociedades pacíficas (ODS 16). En septiembre de 2015, la Asamblea General de Naciones Unidas designó a la UNESCO como la agencia de la ONU responsable del monitoreo global del indicador 16.10.2 de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible (ODS) respecto del "número de países que adoptan e implementan garantías constitucionales, legales y/o normativas para el “acceso público a la información. En este contexto, la UNESCO propicia y coordina espacios de asistencia técnica, abogacía e intercambio de buenas prácticas de alcance regional, que van dirigidos a funcionarios públicos y asambleístas conectados con los temas de Derechos Humanos y de acceso a la información pública, en seguimiento al mencionado ODS 16 y su incidencia en el fortalecimiento de la democracia y del Estado de Derecho. La asistencia se enfoca en un proceso de transferencia de conocimientos y fortalecimiento de capacidades para facilitar la incorporación en los procesos de diálogo legislativo y de política pública, de los Estándares Internacionales sobre acceso a la información pública, tales como la Ley Modelo 2.0 sobre Acceso a la Información Pública de la OEA.

planEntities.name: Actualización de conocimientos y fortalecimiento de capacidades de la policía nacional en los temas de libertad de expresión, acceso a la información pública y seguridad de periodistas
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 Capacidades estatales, nacionales y locales fortalecidas para la  administración de justicia, y para la prevención, detección, respuesta y  reducción del impacto de la inseguridad y la violencia criminal.
planEntities.description:
El trabajo de la UNESCO con las fuerzas policiales, en el marco de su mandato en el ODS 16, se inicia tempranamente en el año 2013, con el Ministerio del Interior de Túnez, a través de un programa orientado al fortalecimiento de capacidades en los temas de derechos humanos, libertad de expresión y seguridad de los periodistas. Esta iniciativa es parte de un esfuerzo más amplio para implementar el Plan de Acción de la ONU sobre la Seguridad de los Periodistas y el Problema de la Impunidad, encabezado por la UNESCO y aprobado por la Junta de Jefes Ejecutivos de la ONU el 12 de abril de 2012, con la intención de coordinar los esfuerzos de varios actores en esta área. Este programa de la UNESCO tiene como objetivo mejorar las relaciones a veces tensas entre fuerzas de seguridad y periodistas, así como promover la libertad de expresión, en particular en el contexto de transiciones democráticas y situaciones de posconflicto. Al mismo tiempo, la organización apoya la consolidación de
cuerpos de seguridad transparentes, que respeten la libertad de expresión y el derecho a la información, y promueve la rendición de cuentas y el estado de derecho, en línea con el respeto por los derechos humanos. Esta iniciativa de la UNESCO está compuesta por varios recursos de conocimiento y de asistencia técnica, tales como el Manual de Formación sobre Libertad de Expresión y Orden Público, el MOOC para oficiales de policía sobre Libertad de Expresión y Seguridad de Periodistas, y las sesiones presenciales de alcance nacional y regional dedicadas al fortalecimiento de capacidades de la policía, destacándose el "Taller regional para formadores de academias y escuelas de policía de América Latina". Este taller tuvo lugar del 23 al 26 de noviembre de 2022, en Bogotá, Colombia, con la participación de academias y centros de entrenamiento policiales de 13 países de América Latina.

planEntities.parentName: 1.7 Capacidades fortalecidas y estrategias desarrolladas para atender el  déficit habitacional y de espacios públicos, y para garantizar el derecho  a la ciudad.
planEntities.description: Con el objetivo de mejorar la calidad de vida y la resiliencia de la comunidad de Pile, (Manabí, Ecuador), el proyecto busca apoyar a los portadores del tejido tradicional del sombrero de paja toquilla, a través de la implementación de medidas de salvaguarda de los valores vinculados a su patrimonio cultural inmaterial. Se busca ademas fortalecer sus capacidades para la inserción económica en actividades turísticas y agrícolas sostenibles, contribuyendo a la sostenibilidad de esta práctica patrimonial. El proyecto se da como objetivo la promoción de la autonomía de la mujer y el liderazgo de los jóvenes en la salvaguardia de su patrimonio cultural inmaterial.

planEntities.name: 70 MMR staff members received in house and off job training
planEntities.parentName: Capacity of public sector is strengthened to develop strategies and policies for enterprise, job creation and employment.
planEntities.description: A total of 20 staff members have been trained through special international courses, enhancing their skills and expertise. Additionally, 70 staff members from MMR received both in-house and off-job training, focusing on developing their technical capacity in the fish value chain. Furthermore, 50 fishers have been trained in essential skills such as engine mechanics, boat skipping, and refrigeration. These initiatives are complemented by the ongoing digitalization of institutional working systems, which aims to improve efficiency and effectiveness across operations.

planEntities.name: Digitalization of institutional working systems
planEntities.parentName: Capacity of public sector is strengthened to develop strategies and policies for enterprise, job creation and employment.

planEntities.name: Promotion of agribusiness ventures
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: The promotion of agribusiness ventures is a key focus, alongside efforts to introduce improved stoves in rural households, which aim to enhance energy efficiency and sustainability. Additionally, the procurement of equipment and materials for the ex situ conservation of animal genetic resources is underway, supported by technical assistance for establishing these conservation initiatives. To further support agricultural research, infrastructure for sorting, extraction, curing, and packaging vegetable and fruit seeds is being constructed at a designated research station. A mini-postharvest research laboratory is also being built in Halhale, along with the construction of another new mini laboratory. Furthermore, trials on bio-pesticides and fungicides are being conducted to explore sustainable pest management solutions. These initiatives collectively contribute to the enhancement of agricultural practices and resource conservation.

planEntities.name: Equip Agri Statistics office at HQ and Zobas as well as front line extension officers with essential data collection  tools,
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: Efforts are underway to equip the Agri Statistics office at headquarters and in Zobas, as well as frontline extension officers, with essential data collection tools. This initiative includes conducting surveys, data collection, and analysis, alongside carrying out an agricultural census to gather vital information. To strengthen human resources, staff upgrading opportunities for MSc and PhD programs, as well as short-term training abroad, are being implemented. Additionally, scientific visits to research stations are encouraged to foster knowledge exchange and collaboration development with regional laboratories and research institutions. The procurement of laboratory equipment, general materials, reagents, chemicals, facilities, and consumables is also prioritized to enhance research capabilities. Furthermore, the maintenance of the vaccine production laboratory and laboratory buildings, as well as the service and maintenance of laboratory equipment, are essential for ensuring operational efficiency. Finally, efforts are being made to rehabilitate the Ghinda regional laboratory, further supporting the advancement of agricultural research and statistics.

planEntities.name: Procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: The procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools is essential for ensuring the longevity and efficiency of agricultural operations. This includes the acquisition of spare parts and maintenance supplies, as well as the supply, installation, and commissioning of three automatic weather stations. Additionally, laboratory equipment and chemical reagents are being procured to support various agricultural functions. To ensure high standards, a seed quality control and certification system is being established, along with a national pest surveillance system. Technical assistance is also being provided to develop a registration system for animal drugs and biologics. Furthermore, office facilities are being procured for four existing and eight new animal quarantine stations, accompanied by necessary lab equipment and chemical reagents. Efforts are underway to develop an agro-mapping and agro-geospatial information system, as well as an agriculture market information system. Lastly, the procurement of equipment and materials aimed at expanding the agricultural innovation system will further enhance the sector's overall productivity and resilience.

planEntities.name: Maintenance of seed conditioning and processing plants
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: Efforts are underway to maintain seed conditioning and processing plants, ensuring they operate at optimal efficiency. This includes the procurement of mobile seed conditioning and processing machines, as well as a chips-making machine. Additionally, small-scale fruit peeling, drying, and processing machines are being purchased to support local food production. The procurement of vitro plants will enhance the propagation of high-quality crops, while both expendable and non-expendable items are being acquired to support various agricultural functions. In vitro multiplication is being implemented for seed potatoes, bananas, sweet potatoes, date palms, and aloe vera, promoting diverse agricultural outputs. Furthermore, new materials for various staple crop seeds are being introduced, accompanied by experiments and trials to assess their viability. Foundation seed production is also a priority, along with ongoing trials on bio-pesticides and fungicides to explore sustainable pest management solutions.

planEntities.name: Develop Recipes and complementary foods from aquatic foods
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description:
Initiatives are being launched to develop recipes and complementary foods derived from aquatic sources, enhancing nutritional options for communities. A Social Behavior Communication Change (SBCC) strategy is being crafted to encourage increased fish consumption among households and communities. As part of this effort, procurement of aquatic food packaging and labeling materials is essential to promote these products effectively. Nutrition materials and equipment are also being acquired to support these initiatives, alongside a comprehensive fish consumption survey to gather valuable data.

In addition, new parameters are being introduced for research, including analyzing shelf life, assessing seaweed, and cultivating various purpose-driven microbes. To improve local fish distribution, procurement of eight ready-made retail fish shops and five solar-powered refrigerated fish transporting trucks is underway. The construction of ten solar-powered ice-producing facilities will further enhance fish preservation and quality.

Moreover, the procurement of 20 long line drum haulers and complete long line fishing gear for artisanal boats will support local fishermen. Plans include establishing fish drying facilities and renovating existing fish processing facilities to improve operational efficiency. Additional procurement of fishing inputs, the erection of ice plants, and the acquisition of water trucks are all part of a comprehensive approach to enhance the fishing industry. Finally, hatcheries are being established to support sustainable fish production and resource management.

planEntities.name: Participatory Small Scale Irrigation Development Programme(PASIDP II)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: The Programme  Development Objective (PDO) is to provide “improved income and food security for rural households on a sustainable basis”. The project consists of three components namely: A) Investment in Small-scale Irrigation Infrastructure; b) Investment in Capacity for Sustainable Agriculture; and c) Programme Management, M&E, and Knowledge Management. In addition, the programme will support linkages to markets and services so that smallholder farmers can increase their productivity, competitiveness and incomes. It will also enhance their resilience against external shocks and those induced by adverse weather and climate conditions, such as drought. The programme thus aims to improve farmers' prosperity, food security and nutrition.

planEntities.name: Rural Financial Intermediation Programme (RUFIPIII)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: To improve livelihoods and to reduce vulnerability and poverty through increased incomes and better risk management through financial and non-financial measures. The programme aims to provide access to a range of financial products and services including savings, credit, micro-insurance and money transfers for rural households while building sustainable rural financial institutions (supported RUSACCOs and their secondary structure (the Unions) and MFIs. The Programme will be implemented over a 6-year period and consist of four components: (1) Building capacity of institutions and clients; (2) Improving regulation, supervision and institutional discipline (3) Facilitating funds flow and diversification of RFI business, and (4) Programme Management. Component 1 focuses on building the capacity of RFIs (RUSACCOs and MFIs) and more importantly their clients.

planEntities.name: Lowlands Livelihood Resilience Project (LLRP)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: To Improve Livelihood Resilience of Pastoral and Agro-Pastoral Communities in Ethiopia.The project seeks to increase resilience including: (i) absorptive capacity, through rangeland and natural resource management interventions, strategic investments and improved basic social service delivery, which will help communities and pastoral and agro-pastoral system to absorb drought shocks and reduce asset losses, (ii) adaptive capacity, through livelihood improvement and by helping beneficiaries adopt climate smart agriculture and investing in research systems that will contribute towards better adapting to changing climate; and (iii) transformative capacity, through market linkages, small scale irrigation, and livelihood diversification, that provide a basis for more fundamental socioeconomic changes and help beneficiary reduce their risk. It is a joint project of the World Bank and IFAD.

planEntities.name: Advancing Decent Work and Inclusive Industrialization Programme (ONEILO Siraye) in the garment, textile and other priority sectors
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description:
The programme aims to contribute to the national development priorities by supporting the establishment of a socially sustainable and responsible textile and garment industry. The plan is to achieve this through interwoven interventions at the factory, sectoral and national levels; to advance productivity and business competitiveness, improve safety at work, enhance working conditions, uplift industrial relations and strengthen the industry’s compliance with national and international labour standards.
This intervention is a comprehensive and coordinated ILO response to a need expressed by the Ethiopian constituents and other key industry stakeholders to advance decent work and inclusive industrialization in key priority sectors identi-fied in the country development plan. 
Specific objectives of this project:
1.Improved worker wellbeing in terms of income, safety, equality, rights, voice and representation; 
2. Higher industry productivity and competitiveness; 
3. Enhanced accountability and transparency in labour administration.                                      
4. Gender Equality and Women Leadership Development

planEntities.name: PROSPECTS - Inclusive jobs and education for refugees and host communities in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.3: Peace architecture and related instruments strengthened to prevent, mitigate and manage conflict and promote peace, reconciliation and social cohesion at national and local level.
planEntities.description:
The project objective is to strengthen decent work in Ethiopia in order to mitigate stress factors and support inclusive socio-economic enablers for access to labour markets and empowerment of forcibly displaced persons and host communities.

Specific objectives: 
1. Refugees and IDPs and their host communities, particularly women and youth, have the skills required for successful transition to, and engagement with, jobs/livelihoods.
2. Increased job/self-employment for host communities, refugees and IDPs.
3. The enabling environment for decent work, legal protection, and social protection is strengthened and expanded to build inclusion and diminish vulnerability of refugees and IDPs and their hosts.

planEntities.name: ProAgro – Promotion of Decent Work in Agribusiness
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description:
This project puts forward an integrated strategy, combining policy support and social dialogue, skills development, value chain development and entrepreneurship training, with the ultimate objective to create decent jobs opportunities for women and young men in the agribusiness sector

Specific objectives: 
1. A more conducive ecosystem in the selected region for decent jobs creation and sustainable investment
2. Selected value chains in the agribusiness sector are more competitive and have boosted their job quality and creation potential.
3. Quality and more demand oriented TVET and training that increase employability and job prospects.
4. Enterprise development mechanisms in place for the agribusiness sector.

planEntities.name: Global Programme on Skills and Lifelong Learning_Ethiopia component
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to contribute to address the challenges faced by Ethiopia’s TVET system by improving its quality, relevance and inclusiveness. A more demand-driven approach that facilitates the development of relevant skills for different economic sectors is implemented.

Specific objectives:
1. Capacity of tripartite constituents to identify and address current skills mismatches, decent job creation and sustainable investment increased
2. Core work skills training contribute to greater employability of trainees
3. An effective and inclusive Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) system established
4. Disadvantaged groups have increased employability through inclusive skills development
5. Skills governance systems and management of TVET strengthened with greater private sector engagement

planEntities.name: Improving synergies between Social Protection & Public Finance Management
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.4: Social protection programs and systems strengthened to enhance resilience of the most vulnerable people.
planEntities.description:
The action supports governments’ efforts to expand or refine life-course risk protection measures including their financing basis and redistributive effects and considering the broader demographic, strategic, economic and fiscal context within which they are to be realised.

Specific objectives:
1.. Producing a financing strategy for social protection with short-term and medium-term options;
2.. Extending social security to informal economy workers and supporting wage legislation related to social protection; and
3. .Building the capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (MoLSA) to effectively monitor the social protection system.

planEntities.name: Addressing Drivers and Facilitating Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration in the Contexts of Disasters and Climate Change in the IGAD Region (MPTF Compact Migration)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity at national and subnational levels for climate and disaster risk management strengthened to build resilience.
planEntities.description:
This joint programme contributes to facilitating pathways for regular migration in the IGAD region and minimizing displacement risk in line with the vision and guiding principles of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly, and Regular Migration

Specific objectives: to improve regional and national migration governance in the context of the adverse impacts of climate change and environmental degradation through different actions that each address the relevant objectives of the GCM (Objective 1 Collect and utilize accurate and disaggregated data as a basis for evidence –based policies;  Objective 2 Minimize the adverse drivers and structural factors that compel people to leave their country of origin; and Objective 5 Enhance availability and flexibility of pathways for regular migration)

planEntities.name: Strengthening Ethiopia's capability to address forced labour and human trafficking
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
The project provides technical support to national and regional stakeholders to mainstream internationally aligned forced labour and human trafficking indicators in national data collection instruments and to raise awareness in the whole-of-society to the problem of human trafficking and forced labour in Ethiopia.

Specific objectives:
preparing the foundations for targeting long-term, sustainable options for improving the protection of Ethiopian workers from the risk of human trafficking and forced labour;
improving evidence-based policy making and intra-governmental coordination and collaboration to effectively address forced labour and human trafficking.

planEntities.name: FAIRWAY
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description:
The project addresses underlying causes of decent work deficits at their source through national-level interventions in selected countries of origin in East (Ethiopia, Kenya, and Uganda), West (Nigeria) and North Africa (Morocco).

Specific objectives:
1. Private sector, employers’ and workers’ organizations engaged for decent work for migrant workers. 
2. Gender-responsive policy frameworks are developed or strengthened for fair recruitment and decent work and regulatory compliance.
3. Discriminatory attitudes towards women and men migrant workers are diminished; and
4. Migrant workers have improved access to information and support services throughout the migration cycle.

planEntities.name: Provision of Emergency Shelter and Camp Coordination and Camp Management Assistance for population affected by the northern Ethiopia crisis and Covid-19 related health services for Humanitarian actors in Tigray (CC.0041)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: Provision of Emergency Shelter and Camp Coordination and Camp Management Assistance for population affected by the northern Ethiopia crisis and Covid-19 related health services for Humanitarian actors in Tigray.Through direct implementation and sub-grant agreements with selected partners, IOM’s Rapid Response Fund Mechanism will provide direct assistance through the distribution of 3,600 emergency shelter kits to 3,600 households (18,000 beneficiaries) and the construction of 5,400 units of two household shelters each, benefiting 10,800 households (54,000 beneficiaries) in sites prioritized through the Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI) Cluster. The emergency shelters will be procured in line with the standard Shelter/NFI Cluster kits contents and specifications and transported to Mekelle for further distribution through partners in targeted locations.

planEntities.name: Wellbeing of crisis-affected populations in displacement-affected locations is strengthened through site management support (SMS/CCCM), including site planning & development, coordination & information management, community participation and capacity building.(CC.0042)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description:
Wellbeing of crisis-affected populations in displacement-affected locations is strengthened through site management support (SMS/CCCM), including site planning & development, coordination & information management, community participation and capacity building.  Site/Area Coordination and Information Management, including meetings organized at displacement locations (i.e. Site & Woreda/Sub-City levels), and sharing of site and area-level information products.
• Site Planning, Development, Maintenance and Upgrades, such as site feasibility assessments, design of site plans for new, converted or extended sites; partitioning of communal living spaces; installation of communal facilities, Infection prevention and Control (IPC) measures, etc.
• Community Participation/Self-Governance, including through support of community self-governance structures and running of a Community Feedback Mechanism (CFM)
• Capacity Building of Key stakeholders (for staff, authorities, partners and other stakeholders) on key CCCM concepts and protection mainstreaming  view of the continuing risks posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, IOM will mainstream COVID-19 mitigation and prevention measures across its interventions. For example, IOM does not encourage large community events, and instead uses community leadership structures and locally designed and relevant COVID-19 IEC material to train community leaders to cascade COVID-19 awareness messages to the wider community, and IPC measures are included in envisaged sit e upgrades and maintenance.

planEntities.name: Wellbeing of populations affected by the Northern Ethiopia Crisis is strengthened through camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) support to IDPs and host community(CC.0051)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Wellbeing of populations affected by the Northern Ethiopia Crisis is strengthened through camp coordination and camp management (CCCM) support to IDPs and host community.The proposed response under this project will provide an important contribution to the humanitarian response in Ethiopia, also in light of the unfolding COVID-19 pandemic situation, which has increased needs for targeted humanitarian response. The direct support to CCCM programming can help with prevention measures in overcrowded IDP sites that are particularly vulnerable to the spread of COVID-19. IOM will continue providing integrated assistance with WASH, Health and Shelter, to ensure agreed standards are met and protection mainstreaming incorporated throughout its intervention. IOM integrates COVID-19 prevention and mitigation measures in all programming, such as ensuring social distancing, water, and soaps in distribution locations.

planEntities.name: Wellbeing of crisis-affected populations in internally displaced persons (IDP) sites in Oromia, Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples (SNNP), and Somali regions is strengthened through site management support (CC.0056)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: Wellbeing of crisis-affected populations in internally displaced persons (IDP) sites in Oromia, Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples (SNNP), and Somali regions is strengthened through site management support. This project aims to increase the provision of support and wellbeing of crisis-affected populations in displacement-affected locations through Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), including site planning and development, coordination and information management, community participation/mobilization and capacity building. IOM will target 30 sites prioritized by the CCCM Cluster in Dire dawa, Woredas in East and West Hararge (Deder, Goro Gutu, Kersa, Meta, Mieso, Chinaksen, Bordode, Tulo), of Oromia, Amaro Special Woreda, Segen Zuria , Karat Zuria, of Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples (SNNP) and Babile in Somali regions. Beneficiaries under this project will be Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs in sites or site-like settings, and depending on needs and access, IDPs in the host community in some instances, under IOM’s CCCM interventions.

planEntities.description: Wellbeing of Populations Affected is Strengthened through Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) Support to IDPs and Host Community.Through the proposed project, IOM intends to further scale up its ongoing CCCM emergency response in the targeted areas in Wag Hamra Zone and will provide assistance along the four pillars of CCCM with essential protection mainstreaming respecting COVID 19 preventive measures. planEntities.description: Ethiopia Crisis Response - Migration Emergency Funding Mechanism (MEFM).Given the time required to procure more emergency shelter items and NFIs and have those items arrive into Ethiopia, IOM Ethiopia is planning to start procuring relevant essential NFIs and pre-position them in order to be able to urgently and timely respond to the needs.

planEntities.name: Supporting the Establishment of a Humanitarian Programme for Africa 2022 (DP.1940)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: Supporting the Establishment of a Humanitarian Programme for Africa 2022.The Programme will be applicable for activation in the following scenarios: a) Sudden onset disaster/crisis response: In circumstances where a sudden event, whether a natural disaster or conflict, leads to quickly escalating humanitarian needs which the international community is called to respond to, and where no prior humanitarian response was in place, or where humanitarian needs have greatly outpaced existing capacity. Instances of large-scale natural disasters would logically apply in this case.  b) Protracted displacement crises suffering from a deterioration in humanitarian conditions: Humanitarian contexts in which a humanitarian response and presence are in place, albeit at a low to mid-level scale, and where an outbreak of violence or other type of disaster leads to an exponential increase in humanitarian needs, which current resources and capacity levels on the ground cannot match

planEntities.name: Improving the Protection of Vulnerable Migrants in Ethiopia through Tailored Direct assistance and Referral (DP.2276)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Improving the Protection of Vulnerable Migrants in Ethiopia through Tailored Direct assistance and Referral.The project aims to contribute to the efforts of the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to protect and empower migrants in vulnerable situations, with a focus on the most vulnerable groups such as unaccompanied migrant children (UMC), victims of trafficking (VoTs), women and girls, elderly people, migrants with disabilities). To achieve this, IOM will implement initiatives under two components.The first outcome will aim to increased migrants in vulnerable situations' levels of resilience to irregular migration by ensuring the provision of tailored direct assistance, improving the accessibility and quality of services at Migrant Response Centres across the country, and improving access to livelihood alternatives upon return in communities of origin.The second outcome of the project will look at increasing duty bearers', first of whom the Government of Ethiopia (GoE), capacity to assist migrants through strengthened case management and referral systems.

planEntities.name: Provision of Shelter, Settlements, and WASH Assistance for Populations Affected by the Northern Ethiopian Crisis (DP.2312)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Provision of Shelter, Settlements, and WASH Assistance for Populations Affected by the Northern Ethiopian Crisis.With the support of the Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA), IOM aims to fill gaps identified in the current response implemented by IOM and other humanitarian partners, focusing on the Shelter and Settlements sector. Protection will be mainstreamed through all proposed interventions, including gender-based violence (GBV) safeguards, through staff and partner capacity building, ensuring gender balance in operational teams, and implementation of adequate Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) mechanisms.

planEntities.description: Emergency Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) support to Crises affected population of Tigray Region, Ethiopia.The proposed intervention will provide live-saving humanitarian assistance focusing on WASH interventions to targeted internally displaced people (IDPs) in Tigray region. The proposed project intervention will target the affected population in cluster-identified priority locations in Tigray region of Ethiopia. The project will mainly focus on lifesaving water and sanitation support for IDPs in conflict affected areas, as well as hygiene promotion and ongoing capacity building for local communities and distribution of lifesaving WASH NFIs. To ensure well-coordinated response, IOM work in collaboration with National and sub-national WASH cluster focal points,Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Health and protection clusters to ensure overall coordination and inclusive response.

planEntities.name: Life-saving, multi-sectoral emergency assistance and protection to vulnerable displaced persons in Ethiopia (DP.2356)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Life-saving, multi-sectoral emergency assistance and protection to vulnerable displaced persons in ETHIOPIA.IOM will continue delivering life-saving humanitarian assistance through the following programs: DTM, WASH, SMS and support to migrants returning from KSA. IOM is prioritizing WASH response over S/NFI programming for this proposal; while both sectors represent serious gaps across Ethiopia, IOM will be able to complement this project with shelter/NFI programming implemented through other projects in Tigray, thus ensuring a multi-sectoral response. In view of the COVID-19 pandemic, integrating WASH into Shelter responses is deemed critical. Protection will be mainstreamed by capacity building field staff, government stakeholders and beneficiaries.

planEntities.name: Multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to IDPs in Konso, SNNPR (DP.2361)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: IOM propose a multi-sectoral approach encompassing WASH, SNFI, Protection, Nutrition, CCCM and Education activities, to enable the provision of holistic support to vulnerable communities in Konso Zone of SNNP region. The project will provide critical and life-saving solutions, whilst strengthening and reinforcing community-based structures, and building resilience of targeted communities. IOM will provide multi-sector support for IDPs in conflict affected areas of Konso, to ensure social cohesion within the targeted communities IOM will include around 10% of the displacement affected vulnerable host communities.

planEntities.name: 2021 IOM COVID-19 Strategic Response and Recovery Plan (DP.2395)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: 2021 IOM COVID-19 Strategic Response and Recovery Plan.One year into the pandemic, the mix of overlapping crises with a rise in extreme poverty, political instability, conflict, disasters and food insecurity have driven humanitarian needs to new levels and further intensified ongoing humanitarian crises that, if left unaddressed, will have long-term impacts on fragility, risks of displacement and human suffering. In line with its COVID-19 Strategic Response and Recovery Plan (SRRP), this global project encompasses life-saving assistance and response to humanitarian needs, initiatives to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on migrants and societies, as well as support to recovery and resilience integrating longer-term sustainable development planning. This project focuses on four strategic priorities at the community, national and regional levels across 37 countries and nine regional offices. Ensure continuation of services, mitigate risks and protect people. Scale up public health measures and strengthen mobility-sensitive health systems. Mitigate the socio-economic impact of COVID-19, restart human mobility and empower societies; and inform response and recovery efforts and strengthen evidence-based decision-making.

planEntities.name: Regional Migrant Response Plan (RMRP) for the Horn of Africa and Yemen to provide protection and assistance for vulnerable migrants in Yemen (DP.2400)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: Regional Migrant Response Plan (RMRP) for the Horn of Africa and Yemen 2021 - 2024 to provide protection and assistance for vulnerable migrants in Yemen.The MRP provides an essential strategic framework to ensure a whole of society approach to address the needs of vulnerable migrants and host communities in the key countries along the Eastern and Horn of Africa (EHoA) and Yemen route and ensure continuity of services along the route.  IOM Ethiopia will conduct the following activities: Activity 2.1.1: Establish partnerships with local shelter NGOs to support vulnerable returnees who are unable to return to their areas of origin, including alternative care arrangements for UMC unable to reunify with their families. Through this partnership, provide assistance to 100 UMC who are unable to return to their areas of origin, including alternative care arrangements. IOM will also provide technical assistance regarding migrant protection, especially in the context of child protection.   Activity 2.1.1: Offer tailored in-kind support (including, but not limited to food, medical assistance (referral to health facilities), NFIs) for returnees from areas in conflict who have been able to join relatives in other regions of Ethiopia,   Activity 2.1.1: Provide family tracing and reunification to 300 UMC in Ethiopia in collaboration with the Ministry of Women, Children and Youth (MOWCY) and UNICEF.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support programming to GBV survivors and conflict affected populations in Northern Ethiopia (Tigray and Amhara)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: Strengthening the provision of Mental Health and Psychosocial Support programming to GBV survivors and conflict affected populations in Northern Ethiopia (Tigray and Amhara).The proposed project is strategically relevant and in line with respective humanitarian needs reports and strategies, including the Multi-Sector Rapid Needs Assessment conducted in the target areas. This project targets IDPs from Tigray (Mekelle, Shire, Adwa and Shiro), and Amhara (Gondar, Dabat and Debark). This provision of life-saving assistance will strengthen the existing service provision in selected IDPs sites including expanding into newly accessible sites through capacity building of relevant actors, provision of psychosocial counseling for GBV survivors and vulnerable populations, group discussions, community awareness linked to service provision; GBV risk mitigation education and referral including for Clinical Management of Rape (CMR).

planEntities.name: Provision of Direct Protection Assistance and GBV Response Services to Affected Populations in Oromia and Somalia Regions of Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: Provision of Direct Protection Assistance and GBV Response Services to Affected Populations in Oromia and Somalia Regions of Ethiopia.The overall goal of this project is to strengthen the provision of direct protection assistance, including gender-based violence (GBV) response services to internally displaced persons (IDPs) and IDP returnees in Oromia (East Hararge) and Somalia regions (Fafan). The interventions will be in line with IOM’s Institutional Framework for Addressing GBV in Crises and IOM’s Protection Policy.

planEntities.name: Emergency Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) support to Crises affected population of Somali region, Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Emergency Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) support to Crises affected population of Somali region, Ethiopia.The proposed intervention will provide live-saving humanitarian assistance focusing on WASH interventions to targeted internally displaced people (IDPs) in Tuliguled woreda (Somali region), cluster-identified priority locations for intervention. The project will mainly focus on lifesaving water and sanitation support for IDPs and conflict affected areas, as well as hygiene promotion and ongoing capacity building for local communities. To ensure a well-coordinated response, IOM will work in close collaboration with National and sub-national WASH cluster focal points, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Health and protection clusters to ensure overall coordination and inclusive response.

planEntities.name: Sanitation for All (DP.2469)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: This project seeks to provide an innovative solution to an unaddressed need within humanitarian responses: the of a lack of suitable access to sanitation for people with incontinence and very young children. These individuals are either not provided with a solution to their sanitary needs, or provided with disposable solutions, thereby being both expensive, difficult to safely dispose of within humanitarian contexts, and not environmentally friendly. This project seeks to meet the needs by proposing a solution that is sustainable and better for the environment, reduces the burden on caregivers, and promotes the local economy through local production through a financially sustainable model.

planEntities.name: Multi-purpose Cash Response for Food Insecure Households impacted by Drought (DP.2480)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: IOM, along with implementing partners, will target these food insecure populations through unconditional, unrestricted multi-purpose cash assistance (MPC) in order to address basic household needs like food, livelihoods, shelter, WASH as well as education and health. Considering that the needs of affected people are diverse, cash-based assistance will enable beneficiaries to prioritize their most pressing needs in a dignified manner. Accountability to the Affected Populations (AAP) will be addressed through inclusion of community and vulnerable groups as well as a feedback and complaints mechanism that will enable community groups to raise issues of concern.

planEntities.name: Humanitarian and protection assistance to vulnerable migrants in Yemen and Horn of Africa (DP.2489)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: Humanitarian and protection assistance to vulnerable migrants in Yemen and Horn of Africa.The East and Horn of Africa is a region of origin, transit, and destination for hundreds of thousands of migrants, the majority of whom travel in an irregular manner often relying on unscrupulous smugglers to facilitate movement along the Eastern Route via Somalia, and Djibouti with the hope of crossing the Gulf of Aden into Yemen and onwards towards the Gulf states with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia as the main destination for the majority. The persistent vulnerability of migrants in irregular situations is one of the specific drivers of migration and determinants of IOM’s response through the Regional Migrant Response Plan (MRP). This project focuses mainly on providing life-saving assistance to vulnerable migrants and host communities. Additionally, IOM is providing quality, timely and inclusive protection assistance and services to migrants and host communities, but is also flexible and includes activities which build evidence, partnerships, and coordination to enhance humanitarian response and migration management throughout the migration.

The persistent vulnerability of migrants in irregular situations is one of the specific drivers of migration and determinants of IOM’s response through the Regional Migrant Response Plan (MRP). This project focuses mainly on providing life-saving assistance to vulnerable migrants and host communities. planEntities.name: Facilitating durable solutions and recovery to displacement affected communities in the Somali Region (DS.0058)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of this project is to contribute to the efforts of the Somali regional authorities to provide durable solutions for internally displaced persons (IDPs) by helping them meet the criteria for a durable solution, as relevant, based on the 2010 IASC Framework on Durable Solutions, and support sustainable recovery efforts in the Somali Region. This will be attained by improving the conditions for the sustainable socio-economic inclusion of returning and relocated IDPs and host communities.

planEntities.description: The proposed project aims to contribute to enhancing social cohesion, economic resilience and gender responsiveness of displacement-affected communities through  area-based and community-based peacebuilding and recovery processes and increased access to sustainable livelihoods.

planEntities.name: PSEA Risk Assessment (DX.0078)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: IOMs Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) will conduct two rounds of a prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA) risk assessment and mapping. The goal of the multi-round assessments are to ensure that adequate safeguards and appropriate actions related to sexual exploitation and abuse are in place nationally. Additional indicators specifically related to Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and Gender Based Violence (GBV) will also be part of this process.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the Evidence Base on Human Mobility Along the Eastern Corridor Under the Migrant Response Plan (MRP) , Djibouti-Ethiopia-Kenya-Somalia (DX.0101)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The objective of this one-year project is to enhance migrant protection and assistance through data collection, analysis, and dissemination in Ethiopia, Somalia, Djibouti and Kenya. The proposed project will respond to current information needs about risks and vulnerabilities which have been/or have the potential of being exacerbated by the conflict in Ethiopia and overall fragility in the region.

planEntities.name: Social and economic integration of ex-combatants and strengthening of receiving communities(FC.0185)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description:
Social and economic integration of ex-combatants and strengthening of receiving communities.This proposed initiative is informed by 1) the GoE’s formal request to IOM to provide technical assistance in terms of re-integration support to ongoing DDR activities; 2) a series of consultations and information sharing with key government, UN and donor agencies; and 3) lessons documented from IOM’s institutional experiences in DDR at global and national level. Applying lessons learned from the implementation of DDR activities for the BPLM in Benishagul Gumuz Regional State, IOM will adopt a multiple track approach comprising: 
Structural mechanisms that provide tailored livelihood options for reintegration and that initially cover individual and family basic needs to ex-combatants and Activities that aim to enhance public participation, capacity building support through community-based approach.

planEntities.name: Facilitate Safe and Regular Migration through Ethical Recruitment of Migrant Workers from Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: IOM plans to partner with MoLSA to contribute to the efforts by the Government of Ethiopia in protecting Ethiopian migrant workers and promoting ethical, rights-based and migrant-centered recruitment practices. To achieve this, IOM will adopt a two-pronged approach whereby it will seek to (1) increase the capacity of Government stakeholders, particularly MoLSA, Ethiopian diplomatic missions and Private   Employment Agencies to promote ethical recruitment practices and migrant workers’ rights; and (2) to support MoLSA and Private Employment Agencies (PEAs) in adopting guidelines and practices in line with the International Recruitment Integrity System (IRIS).

planEntities.name: Provision of Life saving primary healthcare and MHPSS service for IDPs in Tigray and Amhara, regions(MP.0084)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: IOM currently provides essential primary health care services across 19 IDP sites in Tigray and Amhara regions. IOM proposes to continue to deliver quality lifesaving primary healthcare services, including mental health and psycho-social support (MHPSS), by deploying five mobile health and nutrition teams (MHNTs) to IDP return sites that have limited to no healthcare service access and by deploying health personnel to accessible health facilities. Prioritization of the Woredas was done focusing on areas hosting large numbers of IDPs with no healthcare services and prone to disease outbreaks due to poor living conditions. Limited access to health services is attributed to the collapse of the health care system and insecurity which limits movements to facilities. In addition, health facilities which are accessible in these areas are observed to be non-functional due to understaffing and/or damaged infrastructure.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Through this collaboration with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), IOM will capitalize and build on its health technical and operational expertise to better respond to humanitarian and public health emergencies globally. IOM will strengthen its capacity to rapidly respond to humanitarian and public health emergencies through the recruitment of personnel dedicated to improving staff capacity for rapid response and assess of IOM's existing health information systems and conducting capacity building trainings.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
