planEntities.description: The proposed project aims to contribute to the improvement of health conditions for crisis-affected populations in Ethiopia through the delivery of essential health services and effectively respond to outbreaks in Northern Ethiopia (Tigray, Amhara regions) for a period of 6 months. The implementation will involve direct IOM implementation as well as system strengthening/capacity building to the health bureaus to adequately respond to public health emergencies and outbreaks.

planEntities.name: Provision of emergency primary health care integrated with gender-based violence, mental health, and psychosocial support services conflict and drought affected population in Tigray, Afar and Somali Regions in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: Under the objective “Accessible essential lifesaving health services for targeted vulnerable populations[1] are accessible, alongside adequately preparing for, and responding to health emergencies”, IOM proposes to continue to deliver quality lifesaving primary healthcare services, including mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), by deploying four mobile health and nutrition teams (MHNTs) to IDP return sites that have limited to no healthcare service access utilizing local rental vehicles. The MHNTs will provide medical consultations, routine immunization, nutrition screening, hygiene promotion and health education, and provide reproductive health services. In the event of outbreaks, IOM will support with provision of operational costs to Zonal and Woreda health office rapid response teams (RRTs) responding to the outbreak including COVID-19. The MHNTs will encompass Nurses/ Midwifes/ Counsellors/GBV case workers/psychologists/social workers to address the mental health and psychosocial needs of the affected population. For MHPSS, individual/group counseling, psychological first aid, referrals, MHPSS awareness sessions, socio-relational, cultural, and recreational activities, and awareness raising will be conducted

planEntities.name: Improving the Protection of Victims of Internal and Transnational Trafficking in Ethiopia (PX.0164)

planEntities.description: Through the proposed project, IOM plans to contribute to the efforts of the Government of Ethiopia in improving the protection of victims of internal and transnational trafficking through a victim-centered and trauma-informed approach, with a focus on institutional capacity and assistance to male victims . This will be done through a three-pronged approach which will look at (1) Institutionalizing TIP Referral Mechanisms between State Actors and Civil Society  ; (2) supporting the mainstreaming of internal trafficking in the planning and review meetings of the National and Regional Task Forces, leading to the formulation of government recommendations to address internal child trafficking in the 2020/2025 national action plan; and (3) improving Comprehensive Services for Victims of Trafficking.

planEntities.name: Better Migration Management - Phase III (PX.0412)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: The Better Migration Management (BMM) programme intends to improve migration management in the region and to address Trafficking in Persons (TiP) and Smuggling of Migrants (SoM) from and within the East and Horn of Africa (EHoA) region. The programe responds to the EU Strategy on Combating Trafficking in Human Beings (2021-2025) as well as the EU action plan against migrant smuggling (2021-2025).   IOM has been implementing this programme in Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda since 2017.

planEntities.name: Cooperation on Migration and Partnership to Achieve Sustainable Solutions (COMPASS) 2.0 (PX.0499)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The Cooperation on Migration and Partnerships to Achieve Sustainable Solutions (COMPASS) was established in 2021 and is a multiyear comprehensive protection pro achieve long-term results in three interconnected outcome areas to contribute to migration governance systems, multistakeholder cooperation, and services that facilitate safe, orderly, and regular migration as well as protect and uphold the rights of migrants. The programme will focus on systemic changes that are critical to: addressing the underlying causes of migrants’ vulnerability, gender inequality and exclusion, including in humanitarian and fragile settings; supporting rights-based policies and legislation; equitable access to essential protection services; strengthening local partnerships for migrant inclusion and social cohesion; reinforcing data-driven responses; and influencing social behaviors and norms.

planEntities.name: Reducing Vulnerabilities Leading to Onward Movements among Vulnerable Migrants in Eastern Sudan
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The objective of the proposed project is to reduce vulnerabilities leading to onward movement and build resilience of migrants in eastern Sudan, aligning with the overall common goal of the joint programme. IOM will work towards the following three project outcomes in order to contribute to the project objective: 1)  The enhanced coordination between the MRRC Khartoum and MRCs in Gedaref and Kassala in Sudan and its referral partners improves the protection environment for vulnerable migrants in the target states. 2)   Migrant and host communities co-exist harmoniously through improved community resilience in the target states. 3)  Vulnerable Ethiopian migrants in Gedaref and Metema have consistent access to direct assistance and support for safe and dignified return and sustainable solutions.

planEntities.name: Africa Regional Migration Program(PX.0299)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The Africa Regional Migration Program (ARMP) has hit its stride in the first two years of its current three-year planning cycle. Valuable implementation lessons have been learned, and the unprecedented test of the COVID-19 pandemic has strengthened the cohesion and integration of the program from its recent roots as four separate programs. The proposed final year of the current three-year cycle builds on this hard work and sets the scene for wider and deeper engagement on the critical migration management issues facing program countries in coming years.

planEntities.name: Establishment of a government-run multi-purpose migrant return assistance centre in Addis Ababa
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.

planEntities.name: Special Measure for the EU-IOM Joint Initiative on Migrant Protection and Reintegration (Horn of Africa) (RR.0261)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: Vulnerable migrants and Migrants stranded and/or in transit in targeted countries will benefit from direct and specialized protection assistance, assisted voluntary return , and greater information on the dangers of and alternatives. Returnees assisted with AVRR or VHR from target countries under this Action will benefit from post arrival assistance and tailored/needs-based reintegration assistance . For returnees from Europe, the programme will also assist forced returns, upon request of sending country and country of origin. Communities experiencing a high concentration of returns and/or hosting many stranded and in transit migrants will benefit from community-based projects as a complement to individual reintegration assistance, leading to improved governance, service delivery, sustainable livelihood opportunities, and cohesion. Communities of transit and/or of origin will also benefit from greater information on the dangers of and alternatives to irregular migration. Private sector actors and organisations engaged in employment/economic activity relevant to returnees will be supported where relevant Migration partitioners, policy makers and the wider public will benefit from data, research and innovation produced as well as from Migrants management tool developed and disseminated Government at national and local levels, CSOs, partner organisations as well as other Institutions and organizations involved in migration management and assistance to vulnerable people will benefit from close collaboration and capacities strengthened. ECOWAS will be supported on some key migration related initiatives

planEntities.name: Facility on sustainable and dignified return and reintegration in support of the Khartoum process – Kenya
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The project objective is to strengthen the mechanisms which protect and assist migrants along migration routes and ensure safer and better governed migration. The project will focus on capacity building which ensures the transfer of knowledge, technical and operational capacities to relevant state and non-state actors to ensure they are equipped to better protect and assist returning migrants through the life of the programme and beyond. Additionally, the project will facilitate assisted voluntary return which takes place from host countries with a specific focus on Djibouti, Sudan and Somalia as well as other members of the Khartoum Process in the Horn of Africa and along key migration routes. Lastly the project will facilitate reintegration activities which are open to both returnees from host countries on the indicated routes as well as from Europe.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The proposed intervention will provide live-saving humanitarian assistance focusing on shelter interventions, to targeted internally displaced persons (IDP) and only 10% of vulnerable affected households (HH) from host communities. The proposed project intervention will target the affected population in cluster-identified priority locations in Amhara, Oromia, Somali and Tigray regions of Ethiopia. The project will mainly provide live-saving emergency shelter-NFI assistance. Key activities include distribution of In-kind emergency shelter and non-food items (ES/NFI) and Shelter repair assistance including cash for rent support and housing, land, and property (HLP) support.

planEntities.name: Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFI) assistance to populations affected by the Northern Ethiopia Crisis (SN.0151)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The proposed intervention will provide lifesaving humanitarian assistance focusing on Shelter and NFI (S-NFI) interventions to targeted internally displaced persons (IDP) and vulnerable affected households (HH) in host communities. The proposed project intervention will target the affected population in cluster-identified priority locations of Tigray, Amhara and Afar regions in Ethiopia. Key activities include distribution of In-kind non-food items (NFI), and rehabilitation of unfinished buildings while also piloting a host community neighboring approach. The rehabilitation of unfinished buildings and host community neighboring approach will be coupled with Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) support ensuring that targeted beneficiaries are supported with a legal tenure documentation. Assistance will be provided in kind. To ensure a well-coordinated response, IOM works in collaboration with national and sub-national emergency shelter and NFI (ESNFI) cluster, Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) and protection clusters to ensure overall coordination and inclusive response. Under the proposed project, IOM will assist 4,760 HHs (24,800 individuals). Primary target locations for the proposed response as per the Shelter cluster priority allocation are four woredas under the Northwestern Zone and Mekelle of Tigray Region, as well as North Wello in Amhara region, and Wasi/Zone 5 in Afar region. IOM seeks to continue the provision of lifesaving and life-sustaining S-NFI services to individuals in prioritized communities in the targeted woredas.

planEntities.name: Emergency Response in Ethiopia: Addressing the Humanitarian Needs of Displaced Populations and Vulnerable Returnees in Gambella, Oromia, Somali and Southern Nations Nationalities and Peoples (SNNP) Regions
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The conflict in the Tigray Region of Ethiopia, coupled with pre-existing humanitarian needs and the COVID-19 pandemic context in Northern Ethiopia, has created a concerning evolving humanitarian situation, as numerous civilians have been displaced within Tigray, and into neighbouring Sudan. Since 28 June 2021, after the withdrawal of federal forces and a unliteral cease fire, the situation within Tigray improved in terms of access and movement. However, challenges such as supply chain issues, electricity blackouts, the freezing of all bank accounts, and shutdown of the internet and phone network in all of Tigray Region prevail. Notwithstanding, many people have been returning to Mekelle particularly in the last three weeks.

planEntities.name: Camp Coordination and Camp Management and Emergency Shelter and Non-Food items (NFI) assistance for conflict affected populations in Northern Ethiopia(CC.0053)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The conflict in northern Ethiopia which began in November 2020 has spread from Tigray to Amhara and Afar regions resulting in the displacement of over two million people and the destruction of houses and household items (source: IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) August 2021).1 The displacement context in Ethiopia remains fluid as the country continues to experience conflict and natural disaster driven displacements. As the conflict spreads and deepens, it is expected to affect more people and cause further sporadic displacement and increase needs particularly in northern Ethiopia. As a result of increased displacement, the needs under the Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI) and Camp Coordination and Camp management (CCCM) sectors in northern Ethiopia are immense. While most internally displaced persons (IDPs) (62% approx.) are seeking shelter with relatives and friends, many of the displaced (77% approx.) are living in crowded locations and sub-standard collective centers. Proposed interventions under this project address urgent gaps and needs identified through multi-sector assessments in Tigray and Amhara regions. IOM’s response under this project will include: 1) CCCM interventions and 2) provision of Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFIs).

planEntities.name: ITU-ILO Joint programme on boosting decent jobs for youth in Africa's digital economy (Ethiopia)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: Within the framework of the ITU-ILO Joint regional programme on boosting decent jobs for youth in Africa's digital economy, exploration of youth employment opportunities in the digital economy in Afar and Somali regions in Ethiopia has been undertaken. An ILO-ITU assessment report on “Youth employment opportunities in the digital economy in Ethiopia: Afar and Somali regions prepared based on desk research and field missions and a validation workshop held. The report/results from this assessment were shared during a validation workshop that was held in November 2021. The report aims to fill existing knowledge gaps on how the digital economy can drive decent job creation in Ethiopia, focusing primarily on young refugees and host community members in two refugee-hosting regions: Afar and Somali. It also highlights interlinkages with the renewable energy sector to potentially support infrastructure, skills building and job creation opportunities. As a follow up to the findings of the report, the support by the PROSPECTS initiative, and further to the launch of the Digital Transformation Center (DTC) in Ethiopia, there are ongoing discussions on how to enhance digital skills and interconnectivity to explore areas of collaboration in digital skills training in Jijiga and Somali regions where one of the DTC training nodes are located and in Jijiga where an ILO training center is established.

planEntities.description:
The project seeks to support the national statistical systems in improving their capacities, with the National Statistical Office in the lead, to support the mainstreaming of data innovations into official statistical production processes, including geospatial information, big data and other non-traditional data sources, to meet information needs for policy areas identified by the country. The goal is to integrate new methods, data sources, and technologies into existing national statistical systems, explicitly not to create parallel data infrastructures at the country level. 

Ethiopia is one of the participating countries under the project. UNSD will support the National Statistical System in the use of innovative data sources, methods, and technologies to meet priority data needs in up to three policy areas. This support will include the development of in-country skills and capabilities through the provision of capacity development workshops and follow-up support in areas identified by the country.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The project aims to formulate enabling policy environments and strengthen capacities of policymakers and MSME entrepreneurs to enhance MSME resilience to external shocks and risks, including the COVID-19 pandemic, in Cambodia, Ethiopia, the Philippines and Zimbabwe. The project will improve the capacity of policymakers to plan and implement coherent policy mechanisms promoting MSME resilience. It will also strengthen MSME entrepreneurial capacities for resilience and competitiveness for the inclusive and sustainable recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. To upscale impact and sustainability, the project will forge extensive partnerships within and across target countries. It will pursue synergies with regional MSME supporting strategies such as the African Union SMEs Strategy and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation’s Small and Medium Enterprises Working Group Strategic Plan for 2021-2024, in addition to pursuing coherent interventions with MSME supporting programmes of government departments, UN Country Teams and development partners in target countries.

This data governance framework underpins (1) policies and regulations, (2) a national data strategy and leadership, (3) a data ecosystem, (4) and investment in data technologies as pillars for an effective data governance framework.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.

The proposed programme on strengthening institutional capacity of duty-bearers and empowering rights-holders for advancement of gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) in Ethiopia” is fully aligned with the UN Women Strategic Note (2021-2025) which is derived from and contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSCDF 2020-2025), which outlines the United Nation’s vision and strategic focus in Ethiopia.  

The overall goal of the programme is to strengthen institutional capacity of duty-bearers and empower rights-holders to further advance gender equality and women’s empowerment (GEWE) to promote cohesive, just, inclusive and democratic society in Ethiopia.

Irish Aid funding will ensure that UN Women’s consistent work in gender equality and women’s rights through governance and civil society support can be strengthened in Ethiopia. Over 50 percent of the funding will be directly funneled to local civil society organizations working on women’s rights, which will strengthen the participation of rights-holders and increase the voice of women in the grassroots level.

planEntities.name: Women and girls who have experienced/are experiencing GBV or are at risk of GBV benefit from provision of and access to quality services and empowered to increasingly engage in  decision making and leadership in GBV response, mitigation and prevention
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: This objective of this UN Women multi-country programme is to provide survivors of GBV and those at risk of GBV with livelihoods and agency to facilitate their access to lifesaving humanitarian services and facilitate their voices in promoting GBV accountability  in humanitarian contexts. The impact of the programme will be to more effectively mitigate, prevent and respond to GBV amongst  crisis affected communities. UN Women interventions focus on three outcomes, two of them to be jointly achieved with UNFPA.  The three key outcomes of the program cover aspects of social norm programming that will contribute  to protection and empowerment of crisis affected women and girls in priority countries; scaling up partnerships with local  WLOs/WROs and strengthening their capacities to participate in humanitarian decision making; increasing access and improving  quality of services provided to crisis affected women and girls (refugees, IDPs and in host communities) both in relation to  protection and livelihoods/income generation.

planEntities.name: Promoting Localized Gender Accountability to Address Inequality and GBV in Humanitarian Crisis
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: In implementing this pilot project, UN Women will be leveraging and applying its coordination mandate to ensure the integration of gender into humanitarian response planning and action in the field level. UN Women provision of sustained and official, mandated capacity will complement GenCap’s short-term and/or other ad-hoc support placements and ensure that momentum towards systematic integration of gender into the processes of humanitarian coordination is not lost once the short-term deployments end their support to the Humanitarian Country Teams (HCTs).  This is particularly critical in ensuring accountability for humanitarian leadership with regards to their policy prescribed obligations to gender in humanitarian action (GiHA), including maintaining the GiHA systems and processes established, once the short-term gender capacity ended.  As the mandated entity to ensure the integration of gender and the empowerment of women and girls across the UN’s output – including in humanitarian settings - UN Women is uniquely placed to provide this longer-term capacity in humanitarian crises.  This is buttressed by the findings of the recently conducted IASC’s internal evaluation on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women and Girls  which concludes that the humanitarian system’s lack of gender capacity – both globally and at the field level - is directly correlated to the lack of prioritization of the gendered needs of women and girls beyond GBV and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA).

planEntities.name: Strengthening the interagency Ethiopia PSEA Network through the establishment of communitybased complaint and mechanisms (CBCMs) as well as survivor-centred support services as response  to sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) amongst internally displaced people (IDP) communities in Tigray (i.e. Mekelle, Shire and Axum) region of Ethiopia.
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: The overarching goal of the proposed project is to strengthen the interagency Ethiopia PSEA Network  to engage directly with regional humanitarian stakeholders/focal points and affected communities of internally displaced people (IDPs) in Tigray (Mekelle, Shire and Axum) regions of Ethiopia (i.e., especially women and children) by establishing and creating meaningful access to safe, anonymous and confidential community-based complaint mechanisms (CBCMs) for SEA reporting. This will also  include establishment of/support to a sub-regional PSEA Networks through capacity building activities. In addition, close consultation with affected IDP populations on preferred CBCMs will be ensured in order to establish support that is survivor-centred; rights-based; age, disability and gender sensitive; non-discriminatory; and culturally appropriate. As such, the proposed project aim to call attention to the stigmatisation of SEA reporting amongst at-risk IDP communities in the the region, ensuring access to and information on established survivor-centred services (i.e factoring in intersectional gender- and ability-based differences in literacy levels and in meaningful access to tools amongst the affected).

planEntities.name: Strengthening the inter-agency PSEA Network through increased community engagement (CE), the establishment of community-based complaint mechanisms (CBCM) and enhanced engagement with all clusters/sectors
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: Building on the previous EHF-funded projects and other work supporting the inter-agency Ethiopia  PSEA Network, the overarching goal of the proposed project is to strengthen the inter-agency PSEA Network to engage directly with humanitarian stakeholders (PSEA Network members, PSEA focal points, and cluster partners) and crisis-affected communities (Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities), with specific attention to women and children, and considering intersectional differences, across Ethiopia. This will be done by increasing community engagement (CE) efforts as well as establishing and creating meaningful access to safe, anonymous, and confidential communitybased complaint mechanisms (CBCMs) for SEA reporting. Close consultations with crisis-affected populations on preferred CBCMs will be ensured before, during, and after the process to ensure established support is survivor-centred, rights-based, gender, age, and (dis)ability sensitive, nondiscriminatory, and culturally appropriate. Furthermore, the project will help to establish, revitalise, and support the regional PSEA Networks across Ethiopia through capacity-building and awareness-raising activities for PSEA Network members, PSEA focal points, and cluster partners. As the PSEA Network is relatively new, these activities will be channeled through the 254 trained focal points at national in Addis Ababa and regional levels in Somali, Oromia, SNNP, Gambella, Tigray (Mekelle and Shire), Afar and Amhara (i.e. the eight sub-national level networks). This will create a multiplier effect whereby focal points increase their capacities and engagement with clusters to indirectly support the other Network members and humanitarian stakeholders. As such, the proposed project aims to call attention to the stigmatisation of SEA reporting amongst atrisk communities across Ethiopia, ensuring access to information on established survivor-centred services (factoring in intersectional gender, age, and ability-based differences in literacy levels and meaningful access to tools) amongst the affected populations. Finally, by including cluster partners in the proposed activities, this project will advance the PSEA agenda beyond the Protection Cluster and enhance multi-cluster PSEA engagement.

planEntities.name: Strengthen gender mainstreaming throughout the humanitarian programme cycle in general, and EHFfunded projects in particular
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: The overarching goal of this proposed project is to strengthen inter-agency gender mainstreaming and advance the Gender in Humanitarian Action agenda. This will be done by creating clear and practical tools which can be easily implemented including a Protection and Gender Mainstreaming Pocket Guide for humanitarian responders and Information, Education, and Communication materials on advancing gender equality for humanitarian responders and crisis-affected communities. In addition, this project  will strengthen capacities on gender mainstreaming of Clusters at national and regional levels, NGOs, and CSOs, with a particular focus on EHF-fund recipients. This will be done by providing trainings on the Protection and Gender Mainstreaming Pocket Guide, Gender in Humanitarian Action, Sex and Age Disaggregated Data (SADD), and the Gender and Age Marker (GAM). In line with the localization agenda and UN Women’s mandate, this project will include CSOs, specifically Women Led Organizations and Women Rights Organizations, in capacity building opportunities. The above will help ensure that EHF-funded projects provide a more gender-sensitive response considering intersectional differences.

planEntities.name: UN Women Strategic Note 2021-2025
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description:
The UN Women Ethiopia Country Office’s program contributes to the UN’s shared goals in supporting the Government of Ethiopia to achieve its sustainable development and humanitarian priorities, and commitments to the 2030 Development Agenda.  Four strategic priorities are identified in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2020-2025 that address multidimensional poverty, inequalities, social exclusion, and marginalization, with a focus on youth, women, and girls; supporting the transition to an inclusive and diversified economy; deepening Ethiopia’s democratic transition and promoting peace; and promoting a green and resilient economy.  These priorities comprise the outcomes that the UN development system, including UN Women ECO, will work to accomplish:
1.	All people in Ethiopia enjoy the rights and capabilities to realize their potential, in equality and with dignity
2.	All people in Ethiopia live in a cohesive, just, inclusive, and democratic society
3.	All people in Ethiopia benefit from an inclusive, resilient, and sustainable economy
4.	All people in Ethiopia live in a society resilient to environmental risks and adapted to climate change 
UN Women’s Strategic Plan (2022-2025) sets out the global vision to ‘Achieve gender equality, the empowerment of all women and girls, and the fulfilment of their human rights’.  This goal frames UN Women ECO’s work and guides its contributions to Ethiopia’s UNSDCF, and frames ECO’s program contributions to UN Women’s global outcomes and indicators, which are organized in four thematic priority areas; ending violence against women and girls; governance and participation in public life; economic empowerment and resilience; and peace and security, humanitarian action, and disaster risk reduction.  
ECO’s Strategic Note’s program outputs and strategies have been further shaped through consultations with partners, staff, and stakeholders, enabling a shared understanding of UN Women’s comparative advantages in Ethiopia.  These include a strong relationship with the GoE; a recognized normative role; capacities to engage in and contribute to complex, sensitive, and structural gender inequality issues; and experience convening and collaborating with women’s movements and partners in civil society, including young women, traditional leaders and faith-based groups, and the media.  The program’s design further responds to the findings and recommendations of the review of ECO’s previous SN program and other assessments.

planEntities.name: Preventing Violence Against Women and Girls and Delivering Essential Services to Survivors in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: This programme will contribute to UN Women’s ultimate goal of women and girls living a life free of violence. Noting the gap in the existing legal and normative framework, the programme  supports the capacity building of women’s organizations and local authorities to advocate for the adoption of gender equal family laws (includes laws on marriage, inheritance, joint administration of property) in Somalia and Afar regions that is in line with federal and international laws. The programme also supports an effective response to combat violence against women through enhancing the skills of judicial and law enforcement personnel on handling and responding to VAWG cases, including through strengthened judicial mechanisms, and using data-based evidence through regular monitoring, enhancing the understanding of the current discriminatory dynamics that may undermine the right of women survivors of violence to have access to justice, as well as their rights to have access to human rights-based protection services.For women and girls to enjoy greater freedoms and rights within their community, the programme will address the root and structural causes of violence through effective prevention strategies that reduce social acceptance of VAWG and change discriminatory attitudes and behaviors. Beneficiaries and target communities will include boys, girls, men, women, religious and cultural leaders, school communities and the media. The programme also supports the rehabilitation and reintegration of survivors of violence through enhancing the capacities of essential service providers including legal, social and health care providers.

planEntities.name: Addis Ababa Safe City and Safe Public Spaces with Women and Girls Programme
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description:
The overall aim of the project is to create safe and empowering public spaces for women and girls free from sexual harassment (SH) and other forms of sexual violence against women and girls (SVAWG). Focusing on the below Safe Cities Free of Violence against Women and Girls Global Programme outcome areas
•	Develop and effectively implement comprehensive laws and policies to prevent and respond to sexual violence in public spaces
•	Attitudes and behavior related to women’s and girls’ rights to enjoy public spaces free from sexual violence transformed

planEntities.name: Increased Participation and Effective Representation of Women in Leadership in Ethiopia: The Road to Equitable Development
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description:
The overall goal of UN Women’s Programme on Women in Leadership and Governance is to increase the effective participation and representation of women in leadership in Ethiopia, particularly focusing on the legislative and executive branch of the Government. 

The ‘Increased Participation and Effective Representation of Women in Leadership in Ethiopia: The Road to Equitable Development’ aims to contribute to three outcomes: 
I)	A pool of interested diverse and capable women leaders and decision makers is formed 
II)	 Women are perceived as equally legitimate and effective political leaders as men; 
III)	Women are promoted as leaders in gender sensitive political institutions

planEntities.name: Support women's effective engagement in electoral processes
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description: The project aims to ensure that Ethiopia's electoral process  is gender responsive by supporting the National Election Board of Ethiopia( NEBE)  to mainstream gender throughout the entire election management process and facilitate  greater political participation and representation of women. The project supported the NEBE to conduct a series of interventions to (a) enhance NEBE's internal capacity on gender sensitivity and elections; (b) promote gender-sensitivity across NEBE's key electoral intervention; (c) to undertake lessons learned on its inclusion mandates. Currently, support is being provided to NEBE to produce video  documentation of the 6th general election and to conduct action-oriented research on violence against women in elections (VAWE).

planEntities.name: Presidential Leadership Programme for Women Leaders
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description: The project aims to ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision making in political, economic, and public life by focusing on 180 women leaders that are in middle level  leadership position across different parts of the country including those in developing regions of Ethiopia such as Gambella, Benshangul-Gumuz, Afar and Somali where women’s representation in leadership is visibly low. The project intends to create a pool of transformative and able women leaders and decision makers to ensure increased participation and effective representation of women at higher leadership positions in public, private and CSO sectors in Ethiopia by enhancing  knowledge and skill by women leaders that is evidenced during their day-to-day leadership style where they are expected to demonstrate the different skills. The project also equips these women leaders with skills to enable them to promote gender responsiveness and  sensitivity in their respective institutions.

planEntities.name: Increased Participation and Effective Representation of Women in Leadership in Ethiopia: The Road to Equitable Development -2022 - 2026
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description:
The ‘Increased Participation and Effective Representation of Women in Leadership in Ethiopia: The Road to Equitable Development’ program aims at contributing to the overarching goal: ‘Women fully and equally participate in leadership and decision-making and women and girls benefit from gender-responsive governance’ by addressing multifaceted barriers that hinder women including young women and women with disabilities from equally and effectively participating in public and political life as leaders and decision makers. It also aims to contribute towards gender responsiveness of key democratic and governance institutions including parliament and regional councils, local governments, political parties and electoral management bodies in Ethiopia. 
The Outcomes of the programme are: 
i)	Unequal power relations, gender norms and discriminatory behaviours and practices are transformed in targeted communities and institutions to promote the participation of women in leadership and decision-making processes. 
ii)	Public institutions review, design, draft, adopt and implement gender sensitive legislations, policies, practices, and procedures (incl. their accountability mechanisms) that promote leadership and participation of women (including young women, women with disabilities) 
iii)	Women’s (including young women, women with disabilities) voice, agency and leadership is increased through improved knowledge and strengthened capabilities

planEntities.name: Gender Equality Roadmap: Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: The project aims to prepare an attainable and synergetic gender equality roadmap that will pave the way towards achieving gender equality and women’s empowerment in Ethiopia. The main objectives of the gender equality roadmap include: Strengthening the government’s commitment to gender equality and women’s empowerment as enshrined in international and regional instruments as well as national laws, policies, strategies and plans; laying out strategic pillars and actionable sequenced interventions  to ensure gender equality and the economic, social and political empowerment of women aligned to international, regional and national commitments to achieve GEWE; establishing clear role and responsibilities; institutional, monitoring and accountability and coordination mechanisms ensure meaningful mainstreaming of gender in policies, strategies, plans and programmes; supporting the adequate resourcing of GEWE interventions through the systematic implementation of GRB and mobilization of resources from national and international sources; and promoting strategies for the transformation of gender norms, attitudes and behaviors  to bring GEWE.

It includes (1) Providing technical support to GOE to develop, implement and track a Multi-sectoral National Prevention Roadmap with particular focus on Key and vulnerable population, ; (2) Providing Technical Assistance to improve testing and treatment through case finding, targeted testing, optimized treatment and adherence to treatment to reach the 95-95-95 targets, (3) Providing Technical Advice to achieve the path to elimination and reach EMTCT rate less than 5%, provide TA to scale up pediatrics ART; (4)  and Providing Technical Assistance to scale-up and  implement of PrEP and VMMC programs to reach communities in need

It includes  (1) to advocate with government and build capacity of the Network of People Living to  implement the national Stigma and Discrimination Advocacy and Communication Strategy to remove social and legal impediments to access HIV services by key and priority populations; (2)  Build capacity of PLHIV,  judicial officers, prison administrators in HIV, legal literacy and human rights; (3) Develop an Advocacy and Communication Strategy for HIV and human rights; (4) Advocate and provide TA for implementation of a multisectoral implementation of the Gender Assessment findings including GBV, SRH, Education Plus for AGYW.

planEntities.name: Epidemic control and Sustainable response

Collaborate with PEPFAR in developing and implementation of COP22 and COP 23, (2) Providing TA to develop the national advocacy and communication strategy for the implementation of the Domestic Resource Mobilization Strategy; (3) Providing TA for harmonizing M&E systems to strengthen  national capacity for generating quality and timely data and evidence on the impact interventions in the revised NSP including updating the national M&E Framework and NASA; (4)  Mobilization and support  a coordinated implementation of HSTP II  that will guide the health sector response towards UHC, to address HIV integration; (5) Mobilize and support a coordinated UN System  in support of  improved HIV and Public Health management in Humanitarian settings.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: This consists in ensure an overall management with excellence and effectiveness. it includes (1) Strengthening skills, competencies, and diversity of workforce to deliver UNAIDS mandate; (2) Ensuring cost-effective use of human and financial resources, including monitoring and reporting; (3) Support introduction of new business processes to promote innovation and lower operating costs; (4) Contribute to Secretariat's engagement in key governance and UN system wide reform initiatives/Planning and implementation of the UN Joint teamProgram. planEntities.name: Inclusive Digital Economies Action (IDEA) in Ethiopia: Refugee Response
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4: Displacement affected persons enabled to find safe, dignified and voluntary solutions to rebuild their lives in sustainable ways.
planEntities.description: The project aims to increase refugees’ and host communities’ participation in the digital economy through three key activities: (1) promoting a savings-for-investment culture among refugees and host community members in savings groups and cooperatives by building financial literacy and digitizing group activities; (2) enabling access to finance through savings-led, digitally enabled services; (3) enhancing a community of practice and cooperation through eco-system level debates related to inclusivity bottlenecks and opportunities in the digital finance sector.

planEntities.name: Women's Digital Financial Inclusion Advocacy Hub
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The Women’s Digital Financial Inclusion (WDFI) Advocacy Hub, led by Women’s World Banking and the United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) with the support of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, is a catalyst for collective action unifying local, regional, and global stakeholders with the common objective of accelerating progress in Women’s Digital Financial Inclusion. In Ethiopia, the objective is to convene a Coalition of local stakeholders to discuss, strategize and collaborate for greater impact. UNCDF will support the members of the Coalition by facilitating access to trainings and insights, and by channelling financial resources to support the implementation of innovative practical solutions. At the global level, the Hub will create unified messages on the priority issues identified by the Coalition in partnership with global organizations, as well as open opportunities for country stakeholders to gain visibility at global platforms.

planEntities.name: Access to affordable clean Energy
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.3: Institutions and systems strengthened, and solutions adopted to reduce pollution and increase access to clean, affordable and sustainable energy.
planEntities.description: The project aims to support energy service providers to pilot and scale-up solar PAYGO technologies to enhance adoption and utilization of solar energy technologies for household and productive uses in off-grid areas through leveraging digital services. The overall objective of the project is to create a catalytic effect in adoption of solar energy technologies through viable PAYGO business models which are targeted to the needs of households and businesses living in the off-grid areas of the country. UNCDF supports energy service providers through provision of performance-based grants (based on number of PAYGO solar energy products sold and number of people impacted)  and tailored-made technical assistances to improve the operation of energy service providers.

planEntities.name: Innovation for Development (joint project with UNDP)-Technical Assistance to MSMEs and Financial Institutions
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: The technical assistance component under the Innovation for Development project targets to strengthen the capacities of MSMEs and financial institutions to enhance flow of funding through development of  innovative financial products tailored to the needs of the MSMEs in Ethiopia and thereby contribute to entrepreneurship development and job creation.

planEntities.name: DFS for resilience
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: This is a digital financial services program with two broad objectives. The objectives are support on policy and distribution of financial services. The programme supports building the capacity of regulators via provision of trainings, exposure market visits  and provision of supporting tools to be able measure performance of the industry and institutions. The first objective entails multiple projects. The second segment of the program focuses on the distribution side of the program where it implements support for innovative distribution network, new use cases that are beyond payments, development of industry working group for DFS and regional harmonization on DFS space. The program has a focus on women, youth, and MSMEs.

planEntities.name: Migration and Remittances Development Program

planEntities.description: Regional multi-year program with a focus on making finance work for migrants through the following workstreams, enabling policy and regulation, open digital payment ecosystem, inclusive innovation and empowered customers

planEntities.description: The Capacity Strengthening for Industrial Development project  is designed to  strengthening national capacities towards industrial transformation and make contribution to the attainment of goals set in the Growth and Transformational Plan ( I & II). The key project interventions include  provision of industrial sector wide advisory services; formulation of policies/strategies and solutions for enhanced growth in the industrial as well as manufacturing sector; building institutional capacity of Ministry Of Industry  and selected  development institutions  to promote their effectiveness  in industrial  planning, implementation as well as monitoring  and evaluation.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: Strengthening the Capacity of the forest sector at strategic and operational levels through creating Multi-functional landscapes in rural and urban areas by reducing   extreme events of vulnerability with in poor communities.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.4: Governance and planning capacities strengthened at national and sub-national levels to promote sustainable urban development, especially in primary and secondary cities/towns
planEntities.description: The project is designed to promote greater use of Integrated Solid Waste Management & Urban Green Infrastructure approaches in Ethiopian cities and towns.

planEntities.name: Integrated Landscape Mgt IAP
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: This project proposes an integrated approach to foster sustainability and resilience for food security through three interrelated components. Based on an integrated approach that brings together capacity to achieve food security with the need to restore and sustainably manage key environmental resources. It does this through three interrelated components: Component 1 ensures effective multi-stakeholder platforms are in place to support the dissemination and uptake of integrated approaches; Component 2 develops specific approaches and puts in place effective mechanisms to scale up across target sites and, more widely, in the country; and Component 3 establishes systematic monitoring, assessment, learning and knowledge management mechanism that supports influencing at a wider scale in Ethiopia – and via the Regional Hub project – across other SSA countries under the IAP. Infusing all components is a commitment to gender-responsive development, in which women stakeholders within smallholder communities play a central role in economic and environmental transformations.To enhance long-term sustainability and resilience of the food production systems by addressing the environmental drivers of food insecurity in Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: Climate Change Adap Growth: Imp. CRGE in Highland Areas
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity at national and subnational levels for climate and disaster risk management strengthened to build resilience.
planEntities.description: The objective of the proposed project is to mainstream climate risk considerations into federal, regional and Woreda-level planning processes so that local communities across the Ethiopian highlands are more resilient to climate change. To achieve this objective, the project will support improved land use planning and decision-making to respond to flood and drought at a Woreda-level. The project will also reduce the vulnerability of local communities in the Ethiopian highlands to climate change through the implementation of climate-smart watershed restoration and management measures. The above-mentioned objective will be achieved through three integrated and complementary outcomes.

planEntities.name: Enhanced Management of protected Area Estate
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: This project will contribute in the mid-term to long-term impacts by reducing the threats to wildlife, agro-biodiversity and forest ecosystems, decreased IWT, Reduced Poaching, Decreased Unsustainable Use of Natural Resources, and Decreased Overgrazing. Driven by low risk and high profitability, the trade in wildlife products and live animals continues to flourish. Ethiopia has been identified as a key transit (as well as source) country for wildlife products and live animals. The proposed project is seeking to implement solutions that will counter the threats to biodiversity and overcome the barriers to effective management of protected areas and to combatting illegal wildlife trade. It seeks to achieve the project’s objective: to build Ethiopia’s capacity for biodiversity conservation through increased effectiveness of protected area management and implementation of measures to reduce Illegal Wildlife Trade and poaching.

planEntities.name: Governance and Democratic Governance Participation Program
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: This is a five-year, multi-stakeholder programme that aims to support the country sustain efforts towards strengthening institutional capacities and frameworks for strengthening good governance and deepening democratic participation. The Governance and Democratic Participation Programme (GDPP) is a five-year, multi-stakeholder programme spanning from April 2017 to March 2021 managed by UNDP. The main objective of the programme is to support the country sustain efforts towards strengthening institutional capacities and frameworks for strengthening good governance and deepening democratic participation in line with the Constitution, the Growth and Transformation Plan II, and International Human Rights Conventions to which Ethiopia is a signatory. Progress in these areas are critical and will enable the country to deliver on the Sustainable Development Goals. This programme on governance and democratic participation builds on progress made and lessons learned from the DIP to support interventions aimed at addressing governance bottlenecks, issues of inclusive, transparency and accountability, and to nurture the development of a more responsive system of governance and peaceful coexistence.

planEntities.description: The overall objective of the programme is to bring about a transformational change in unleashing the growth potential of micro and small-scale enterprises by 2020. Major outcomes of the program revolve around improving knowledge and skills of entrepreneurs, promoting employability skills of youth, facilitating establishment and expansion of businesses with business development service and facilitate improved access to finance for entrepreneurs.

planEntities.name: Climate Change Adaptation in the lowlands ecosystems of Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: To promote climate change adaptation and sustainable economic growth among communities in Ethiopia’s lowland ecosystems. The project seeks to remove the barriers that have hindered land users and government stakeholders from building their resilience and adaptive capacity, particularly those vulnerable communities represented by women and youths in the targeted lowland ecosystem of Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: Capacity Building CBIT Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.2: Normative frameworks, institutions and systems strengthened for conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit sharing from the use of biodiversity and natural resources to ensure environmental sustainability for development.
planEntities.description: Capacity Building project seeks to close the existing technical and institutional capacity challenges related to climate transparency in Ethiopia. strengthen national transparency related institutions to lead, plan, coordinate, implement, monitor, and evaluate policies, strategies, and programs to enhance transparency, including the identification and dissemination of good practices for institutional strengthening and national network of practitioners; support on how to integrate knowledge from transparency initiatives into national policy and decision-making; and assist the deployment and enhancement of information and knowledge management structure to meet the needs of Article 13 of the Paris Agreement.

planEntities.name: Electoral Support project
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description:
A project is being implemented to support the National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) to ensure credible, inclusive and peaceful general elections which will take place in 2021. With the opening of the political space and the return of several opposition parties, the Ethiopian political landscape has witnessed dramatic changes.  It is expected that the 2020 general elections will greatly depart from previous election rounds and will witness true and effective political competition.  The Government is committed to ensure credible, inclusive and peaceful elections; this political will has materialized in a change in the leadership of the National Electoral Management Board (NEBE) and the amendment of the NEBE law.  The new law is expected to strengthen NEBE’s independence and institutional arrangements, thus enabling the Board to manage the elections in a more transparent and effective manner.  The Government also committed to introducing new IT based solutions to improve voters’ registration and results management systems, in an attempt to showcase transparency and efficiency of the electoral management process.  The government is keen on introducing a Biometric Voters Registration (BVR) in the upcoming elections.  Moreover, with the national census planned to take place in 2019, there is high likelihood that the country would witness political debates on the delineation of electoral constituencies following the issuance of the new census data.  
Against this backdrop and in anticipation of a standalone elections support project, UNDP intends to secure technical support to NEBE in identifying most suitable and adapted ‘solutions’ for the interim period that would ensure credible, inclusive and peaceful elections.  The main objectives are two-fold: a) assisting NEBE in undertaking required analysis to support an evidence-based decision-making process internally; and b) providing technical assistance necessary for improving the image of NEBE through improved external engagement with the media and the general public.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Institutional Education Information System for Data-Driven EIE and Resilience to Crises Project
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description:
In 2019, a case study in Ethiopia was carried out to map the data-for-resilience landscape through consideration of its components – production, processing and use of data, as well as their facilitative environment. Based on the findings and recommendation of the case study was that the use of institutional information systems in its present form is limited because of challenges related to timeliness, quality, relevance, access, and availability, leading to: 
• Duplication and/or fragmentation of data 
• Weak coordination around data sharing and use
• Confusion and fatigue among providers of data
• Inefficient use of human and financial resources
Recommended actions to strengthen institutional information systems to increase resilience include: 
• Strengthen the institutional environment (policy, legal frameworks, etc.) to lay a solid foundation for sustainable EIE data production, sharing and use
• Harmonize data production tools and processes to optimize resources and avoid fragmentation  
• Enhance systematic EiE Data coordination through to enhance data sharing and use to meet common objectives
Building on the recommendations of the case study, UNESCO embarked in the second phase of the aimed to strengthen the capacities of the MoE to identify and address the educational needs of learners and educators affected, or at risk of being impacted by emergencies. By bringing together governments and partners from across the humanitarian and development community, the UNESCO/ECW project designed to tackle the challenges facing EiE and institutional education information systems in a holistic manner by involving the entire data chain.  The project implementation period is from April 2021- December, 2022 with the budget of USD 436,799.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.5: 2030 Agenda integrated in development plans and budget allocations at national and sub-national level with adequate financing mobilized.
planEntities.description:
The programme aims to strengthen national capacity to improve availability of population data in scope and quality. In this regard, the programme supports population censuses, Demographic and Health Surveys and the strengthening of Civil Registration and Vital Statistics. To assist in improving quality of population data, capacity will be strengthened for the adoption of modern technology such as use of hand held digital devices in data collection and web-based digital dissemination systems.

The programme also supports the establishment of a web-based multi-sectoral Integrated Management Information System (IMIS) at federal and regional levels to expand access to, and promote wider utilization of data. 

The programme supports the conduct of population projections disaggregated by age and sex to assist in the design of sectoral development plans and to provide Common Operational Datasets on Population Statistics (COD-PS) at national, regional, zonal and wereda levels to guide humanitarian preparedness and response. 

Capacity strengthening support in the use of new methodologies and techniques such as model-based Small Area Estimation (SAE) techniques and geo-spatial analysis will be provided.

planEntities.description:
UNICEF will continue to support risk-informed and shock-responsive nutrition emergency action in line with the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action and through the Government’s Health Extension Programme, as well as through partnerships with non-governmental organizations. Furthermore, UNICEF Nutrition, Health, social protection and WASH programmes will support the Government of Ethiopia in strengthening resilience of the health system and communities to withstand and recover from humanitarian situations, including droughts, floods (that are aggravated by climate change), conflicts and population displacements within the country and from outside the country. Over the last few years, UNICEF has supported care for acutely malnourished children in over 20,000 facilities across the country in over 100 woredas, while leading the emergency nutrition cluster coordination at national and sub-national levels. UNICEF will continue to carry out these roles in the 2020-2025 Country Programme.

1. Improved coordination among health facilities and multisector platforms to strengthen resilience, improve preparedness and response to nutrition emergencies with skilled service provider and adequate supplies.

2. Increased access and quality of routine nutrition screening and services for communities to ensure that acutely malnourished children are transferred and treated with adaptation to the Covid 19 context.

3. Increased capacity of the trained workforce on nutrition through enhanced pre- and in-service training.

planEntities.name: Improve diets through lifecycle  caregivers of early and middle-childhood, adolescents and pregnant/lactating women increase their demand for and have access to improved quality of nutrition services and diets to prevent chronic malnutrition.
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Implementation and scale-up of proven, effective, and quality comprehensive and integrated nutrition services (specific and sensitive) in Ethiopia is urgently needed if the country is to achieve the nutrition goals as highlighted in the NNP II and the Food and Nutrition Policy. The Comprehensive, integrated Nutrition Services package (CINuS) is an evidence-based set nutrition intervention implemented in more than 400 woredas by several partners. CINUS is a minimum package at all levels of health care in Ethiopia and integrates nutrition-sensitive and nutrition-specific actions across multiple sectors beyond health facilities. In addition, if the goals of agriculture are to be aligned with our aspirations for healthy diets, diversity must be prioritized alongside the critical goal of enhancing staple crop productivity. Using its membership in various platforms, UNICEF will continue to collaborate with mandated UN Agencies to advocate for diversified diets along with adapting food value chains to ensure that children and pregnant women have access to nutritious food throughout the year. This multi-system approach is crucial to stop stunting.

planEntities.name: Prevention of micronutrient deficiencies   boys and girls aged 6-59 months, adolescents and pregnant/lactating women have access to micronutrient programs to prevent deficiencies
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Micronutrient deficiencies, specifically vitamin and mineral deficiencies, remain one of the main risk factors for infection and chronic disease morbidity and mortality amongst all ages. Micronutrient deficiencies are a major public health problem in Ethiopia, with women and children most at risk. Dietary inadequacy of consumed nutrients, low bio-availability of key micronutrients from plant-based diets and prevalent infections are major contributing factors for micronutrient deficiencies in Ethiopia. There are multiple interventions that contribute to reducing malnutrition, including vitamin and mineral supplementation, food fortification, promotion of dietary diversification, and diverse homestead food production, as well as public health measures such as immunization, improved sanitation malaria and parasite control. These are complementary interventions; some are population-based while others are targeted at specific age groups or consumer groups.

planEntities.name: Nutrition multisectoral Policy Support  National and Regional government mechanisms and systems have the capacity to implement the multi-sectoral policy with an accountability framework, and enhanced coordination including for humanitarian and development nexus
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description:
UNICEF will continue to provide technical assistance to the government for coordination of nutrition partners at national level and supporting a functional sector coordination group at regional levels and in selected woredas. The Nutrition Programme will specifically endeavour to further institutionalize coordination and planning between the main ministries and regional bureaux. Those interventions will support the increase and sustain coverage of key nutrition specific and sensitive interventions from breastfeeding and supplementation to appropriate feeding practices.
Expenditures to support NNP-II objectives nearly doubled from USD181 million in EFY 2006 to USD330 million in EFY 2007. The increase in funding was largely driven by investments in nutrition-sensitive programmes over time, including the ONE WASH National Program (which began in EFY 2007) and the Productive Safety Net Program-IV (PSNP-IV). The Nutrition Programme, working closely with UNICEF’s Social Policy and Inclusion Programme, will work to increase budget allocations dedicated to high impact nutrition services and thus to improved survival, health and development outcomes. UNICEF will support tracking funding and expenditures for nutrition in Ethiopia across sectors, disaggregated by regions and the development of investment cases budget briefs and advocacy papers.

UNICEF will continue to provide technical assistance to ensure that health facilities enter quality nutrition data into the District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2). DHIS2 will be used to aggregate statistical data collection, validation, analysis, management, and presentation. UNICEF’s Nutrition and Health Programmes aim to work with the government to use monthly DHIS2 reports to rank woredas on a six monthly-basis according to their performance on delivering the routine and outreach services from supplementation to screening and treatment of acute malnutrition. Triangulation between DHIS2 and hot spots mapping will also be implemented to ensure that highly vulnerable areas receive the highest attention. This would facilitate prioritization of the low performing woredas while the high performing ones would need only light monitoring and support. The UNICEF Nutrition Programme instituted the End-User Supply Monitoring system to improve supply management for treatment and care of severely malnourished children. UNICEF will continue to support the Government of Ethiopia and implementing partners with and supply chain and logistics management across different administrative levels and with obtaining and acting on feedback from the end-users (caregivers and other community members). The system will be scaled up to all nutrition commodities (Vitamin A and IFA for example) over the course of this country programme 2020-2025.
