planEntities.description:
The general objective of the project is to contribute to agro-industry development, employment and improved income earning opportunities in high agriculture productive areas of the country. Specifically, the project  supports the inclusive and sustainable development of the four pilot integrated agro-industrial parks in the regions of Oromia (Bulbula), Sidama (Yerga Alem), Amara (Bure) and Tigray (Baeker).
Main activities include linking farmers and cooperatives to agro-processors and the industrial parks; establish and strengthen food quality, safety, and traceability system along the value chains; ensure environmental sustainability and circular economy practices in the parks, and ensure gender parity, safety and security of female workers in the parks.

planEntities.name: Support for the integrated agro-industrialization process in Ethiopia- PROSEAD component 5
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The main purpose of the project is to establish a coordination and governance framework to harmonize IAIP stakeholders’ interventions and sequence activities, as well as to address issues affecting agro-industrial performance in Ethiopia. Key activities include establishment of coordination and governance structure of IAIPs; facilitate policy dialogues and map issues and challenges;  and establish communication and disseminations systems  to disseminate lessons learned and best practices.

planEntities.name: Capacity and entrepreneurial skills development for sustainable agro-industrialization
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to support inclusive and sustainable agro-industrial development in four regions of Ethiopia.
Specific interventions include: support for enabling infrastructure for IAIP and related RTCs; support in developing capacity and skills for sustainable agro-industrialization. The integration of small holder farms, small scale processing enterprises and allied industries into commercial value chains as well as developing human capacities and skills along the value chain as well as the capacities of rural populations to benefit from new agribusiness employment opportunities, are some of the interventions this project focuses on.

planEntities.name: Inclusive and sustainable industrial development for job creation in Ethiopia and Senegal
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: The project aims to: i) create more and better jobs, ii) provide training and skills development and iii) stimulate private sector investment. In Ethiopia, it will focus on the Integrated Agro-industrial Parks (IAIPs) and Rural Transformation Centres (RTC) being piloted to address unemployment, skills development challenges for youth and women, technology transfer and investment for MSMEs.

planEntities.name: Improved Rural Livelihoods through Supporting the Moringa Value Chain Development in Southern Nations, Nationalities and Peoples' Region, Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.1: Policies, regulations and institutions strengthened to create decent jobs and to promote equal access to finance for micro, small and medium enterprises to invest in their productivity and competitiveness.
planEntities.description: The aim of this project is  to scale-up moringa production and productivity (specifically M. Stenopetala and M. Oleifera), strengthen the value chain through integrated utilization of natural resources, and improve value addition through processing and marketing in a sustainable way. To realize its objectives, the project will focus on improving food and nutrition security and livelihood of rural households, targeting especially rural women, through the development of an inclusive and sustainable Moringa Value Chain. In particular, the project will: i) Enhance sustainable production and productivity of moringa through integrated utilization of natural resources; ii) Improve value addition of moringa through processing and marketing of moringa products; iii) Strengthen a nutrition-sensitive moringa value chain through inclusive agri-food systems, promotion of nutritious products and a conducive enabling environment.

planEntities.name: Technical Assistance Project for the Up-Grading of the Ethiopian Leather and Leather Products Industry
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: The main objective is to increase the competitiveness and turnover of the Ethiopian MSEs working on leather footwear and products industry. Moreover the projects support the Ethiopian Enterprise Development Institution in extending its services throughout the establishment of a creative hub, aimed at supporting talented young and women.

planEntities.name: Improving the Sustainability and Inclusiveness of the Ethiopian Coffee Value Chain through Private and Public Partnership
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: The project is aimed to Increase the social, environmental and economic sustainability of the coffee value chain through: (i) Increase in productivity and sustainability (cultivated area and yield), (ii) improvement of quality, (iii) increase export and, (iv) Recognition in international markets of the intrinsic qualities of the Ethiopian Arabica coffee.  One important output of the Project is the establishment of the Coffee Training Center, the first in its kind in Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: UNIDO partnership model for de-risking investments in the Ethiopian coffee sector
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: The project is aimed at establishing a responsive framework for enabling the development of private sector initiatives operating in the Ethiopian coffee value chain.

planEntities.name: TRAINING INSTITUTE FOR COMMERCIAL VEHICLE DRIVERS IN ETHIOPIA; A private public partnership project to support specialized skills development in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: This is a Private Public Development Partnership project established with the partnership of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), Volvo Group, Selam  Children’s Village (SCV) and Federal Transport Authority to support the establishment of a Commercial Vehicles Drivers (CVD) Training academy in Ethiopia.The overall objective of the project is to create productive employment opportunities for Ethiopian youth, both young women and men, in commercial vehicle driving and improve the shortage of skilled labor in transport enterprises. The project will ultimately reduce road traffic accidents and improve the health of the truck drivers around the country. It will also contribute to the efforts of the government in transforming the driving schools in the country.

planEntities.name: Capacity building to upgrade the livestock value chain in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.3: Institutions and systems strengthened, and solutions adopted to reduce pollution and increase access to clean, affordable and sustainable energy.
planEntities.description: The project aims to develop meat export market, improve the competitiveness of meat value chains and livestock industry in Ethiopia, through targeted capacity building technical interventions in the value chain, attracting investment, and promoting meat export.The project main intervention focus are: Systematic research and analysis - map existing baseline situations, analyze institutional and capacity limitations, and assess priority markets for diversification of export of livestock products; Knowledge sharing and technology transfer - organize workshops, training and study tours for value chain operators/actors, policymakers, and cooperatives; Institutional development - provides technical support to veterinary institutions, export abattoirs, and feed industries and strengthens the link between value chain actors; Provide policy support -review existing livestock development policies and legal frameworks and support the development of new policies; Promote multi-stakeholder partnership - Strengthen collaboration between private and public sectors and foster South-South cooperation in the livestock sector to improve the competitiveness of meat production, and Export facilitation - facilitate meat export market diversification and consultation with potential meat importing countries.

planEntities.name: Sustainable Textile Investment and Operation in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.3: Access to innovation, new technology and finance is increased, fostering an inclusive and diversified green economy.
planEntities.description: The project is to promote the ESG performance of the local textile enterprises and Chinese industries and upgrading the capacity and competence of the national regulatory body through trainings and improved ICT applications for performance monitoring and to create easy information access platform for the international buyers and manufacturers. The project will develop interactive on-line platform (which will be administered by ETIDI) that will be used and promote textile industries based on their score in reference to the ESG performance. The project will implement two main components: (i) Documenting best ESG practices and establishing open access digital platform for sharing best practices; (ii) Upgrading the technical capacity of Chinese textile and garment industries, local SMEs, and counterpart, thereby improving the target industries’ ESG performance and upgrading the capacity of ETIDI and ETGAMA to provide reliable and consistent technical supports to the target industries.

planEntities.name: Capacity-building and job creation for youth and women in the textile sector in migration prone areas of Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: As a follow up of the in depth assessment conducted within the SINCE project1 inception phase, the present project has been developed for contributing to reduce irregular migration from Northern and Central Ethiopia by creating greater economic and employment opportunities. The general objective of this project is to support the Government of the FDR of Ethiopia (GoE) in the creation of decent and productive job opportunities for young women and  men through the development of strategic sectors such as the textile and garment industry. This will be done through the development of local capacities (at managerial, technical and institutional levels) in the textile industry through a public private partnership approach.

planEntities.name: Phase 2: Improving public health by solar-powered water sanitation systems in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: The overall purpose of the project is to improve water supply, public health and general environmental quality, while reducing the likelihood for the reoccurrence of violent conflicts due to water shortages by introducing an innovative water sanitation system utilizing environmentally friendly slow sand filtration and photovoltaic electricity generating technologies. This will be achieved through technology demonstration, removal of existing barriers in access to information and technical knowledge, capacity building to better absorb and domestically replicate such technologies, knowledge management activities, identification of viable, sustainable and suitable business models.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the quality compliance capacity of the honey value chain for greater market access
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.2: Access to decent jobs, employment and livelihood opportunities in formal and informal sectors improved particularly for youth and women.
planEntities.description: The objective of the project is to strengthen the capacity of quality infrastructure institutions and service providers to serve the honey value chain development, enhance compliance capacity of honey SMEs to foreign standards and regulations and promote a culture of quality among stakeholders in the honey sector, to ultimately improve market access and increase export opportunities of honey products from Ethiopia to foreign markets.

planEntities.name: Leather Initiative for Sustainable Employment Creation
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: To enhance the economic competitiveness by strengthening an inclusive and sustainable development of the Ethiopian leather value chain. In this context, concrete actions will be undertaken in order to: i) Improve quality and quantity of hides and skins (H&S - including grading system, training, awareness raising) by supporting the leather value chain from slaughter houses to tanneries; ii) Support tanneries (processing and producing finished leather) towards integration into the leather global value chain through competitiveness gains/environmental compliance, including the creation of a LIDI Regional centre. Iii) Promote investments in/around Modjo Leather City (including MSMEs clusters) for both domestic and foreign companies.

planEntities.name: Supporting business-friendly and inclusive national and regional policies, and strengthening productive capabilities and value chains, Ethiopia National Level Component
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.3: Access to innovation, new technology and finance is increased, fostering an inclusive and diversified green economy.
planEntities.description: The Project leverages intermediary organizations and business membership networks to strengthen investment promotion capabilities, business support programmes, marketing, monitoring, and partnerships. UNIDO’s investment retention and mobilization support to investment promotion institutions, primarily EIC, is undertaken across all sectors including agro-processing, manufacturing, infrastructure development and the tourism sectors in support to PCP Ethiopia and PROSEAD interventions and Integrated Agro Industrial Parks (IAIPs) to support ongoing efforts of IPDC, and RPDCs.

Ethiopia.name: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
Ethiopia.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Enhancing Effective and Victim-Centered Criminal Justice Responses to Trafficking in Persons in Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: The project aims to strengthen the Rule of Law through more accessible, accountable and effective criminal justice systems by enhancing the strategic and operational capacity of Ethiopia to respond to the crime of Trafficking in Persons and ensure access to justice and fair treatment for victims of TIP. There are two main objectives: 1) Strengthen the capacity of the Witness Protection Directorate to effectively provide victim and witness assistance and protection in cases of TiP; and 2) Enhance effective criminal justice responses to prevent, suppress and punish child trafficking in particular the problems of children in domestic servitude and commercial sexual exploitation.

planEntities.name: Better Migration Management II Programme
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2: Capacities and mechanisms strengthened at the national and sub-national level for enhanced protection of human rights, rule of law, access to justice and protection for vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: The project aims to improve the management of safe, orderly and regular migration in the region and support national authorities in addressing the smuggling of migrants and the trafficking in human beings within and from the Horn of Africa. The project is a regional and implemented for Djibouti, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda.

planEntities.name: National Integrated Programme for Ethiopia Sub-programme II: Criminal Justice and Integrity
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description: The Programme is aimed at supporting the Federal Democratic Republic Of Ethiopia's efforts against corruption and strengthening of the criminal justice institutions by improving the effectiveness of investigation, prosecution, access to justice, fair trial and execution of penal sanctions, and by securing the protection of vulnerable groups.

planEntities.name: Global Action for Business Integrity
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity to improve the performance of institutions and promote participation, transparency and accountability increased at national and subnational level.
planEntities.description: In line with the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) - the only legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument to prevent corruption, the project aims to strengthen business integrity through collective action. Objectives of the project include:  (1) To advance or effectively implement legislative reforms to prevent and counter corruption; (2) To increase governments' knowledge of legal frameworks and practices to prevent and counter corruption in and with the private sector (UNCAC Art. 37 and Art. 39);  (3) To improve communication among the public sector, the private sector, civil society and academia by providing a common venue for further interaction, dialogue and knowledge-sharing; and (4) To provide guidance to companies and small- and medium-sized enterprises on adopting and implementing anti-corruption systems and programmes.

planEntities.name: Mainstreaming prevention of gender-based violence in the Ethiopian Integrated Agro-Industrial Parks (IAIPs)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.2: Gender inequalities and violence reduced, rights and accountability mechanisms strengthened and opportunities for women and children enhanced.
planEntities.description: The objective of the services under this UN to UN agreement is to deploy protocols for the prevention of gender-based violence (GBV) in the management and operations of the pilot IAIPs and contribute to the overall IAIP development programme in Ethiopia. The services will complement other ongoing technical assistance activities promoting gender equality in the agro industry sector, mitigating the risk of GBV, building resilience of women and other socially vulnerable for their integration in the IAIPs, and add value, to tackle women insecurity from harassment, threat of, physical and sexual violence in the agro parks.

planEntities.name: WB- 3R FOR CONFLICT-AFFECTED COMMUNITIES (Tigray)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.4: Social protection programs and systems strengthened to enhance resilience of the most vulnerable people.
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to rebuild and improve access to basic services and build climate-resilient community infrastructure in conflict-affected areas of the Tigray region. The project will be operational in 5 Woredas (Abergele, Asgede, Hawzen,Hintalo and Ofla) in Tigray with focus on Health, Education and WASH.UNOPS will undertake the Response - Resilience- recovery activities with below outcomes
- Recovery plan developed
- Renovation and/or reconstruction of facilities (education, health and WaSH)  
- Support to kick-start provision of services in local basic services facilities where renovation / recovery is completed.
- Strengthening institutions for resilience.

planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The project objective is to improve the access to water supply and sanitation facilities for IDPs in Qoloji camp in Ethiopian Somali Regional State  as a response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

planEntities.name: Humanitarian Assistance in basic social services and sanitation for IDP returnees.
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description:

-        Improve the sanitation facilities of IDP returnee.
-        Improve the awareness of the affected community on WaSH practice.
-        Help IDP returnee schoolchildren not to stay behind in school performance.                                                                                  Direct beneficiaries:
The project will directly address the needs of around 400 primary school students in Sasiga wereda who dropped out of school due to conflict. 
Benefit around 500 community members by availing sanitation facilities. 
20 teachers teaching in the school.

Education and Health Ministries and their lower level offices which includes regional Bureau, zone departments and woreda offices. The Sasiga Woreda health and education office who are striving to fulfil the health and education needs of the catchment.
The Ministry of Peace and its reporting commission called Disaster Risk Management Commission and its lower level offices which includes the regional and zonal commissions. The Sasiga Woreda Disaster Risk Management office who is working in the peaceful resettlement of IDPs in the Woreda.

planEntities.name: Procurement of Wheat
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: The government of Ethiopia Ministry of Finance has requested UNOPS to procure 400,000 metric tones of Wheat that will be used as a market stabilization strategy for the inflated cost of food items observed following COVID 19 pandemic.

planEntities.name: Eco-Friendly Latrines to Improve Sanitation in Schools of Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Providing eco-friendly latrines to support the Ethiopian Government’s vision of a cleaner, healthier society through improving hygiene and sanitation services for schoolchildren in in ten schools in Addis Ababa in collaboration with Italian Development Corporation and Addis Ababa Education Bureau.

planEntities.name: Incinerators Design, Supply, Installation & Commissioning
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.

The projects intends to  avail a functional, effective and standardized waste management system that will address public health problems through construction of pharmaceutical waste disposal facility in eight cites i.e., Adama, Hawassa, Bahir Dar, Dessie, Dire Dawa, Mekele, Jimma and Nekempte.

planEntities.name: Activity 1: Provide unconditional, nutrition-sensitive, cash-based and in-kind food assistance to crisis-affected populations and transitory clients of the PSNP
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: In partnership with the Government and the humanitarian actors in Ethiopia, WFP provides food and nutrition assistance support (in-kind and cash based) to shock-affected populations in targeted area, to meet their basic food and nutrition needs. WFP mobilises resources for food/cash transfers and undertakes procurement and transport. WFP delivers food/cash resources to distribution points; final distributions are implemented through the regional disaster risk management bureau and woreda/kebele level government staff, monitored by WFP field staff.

planEntities.name: Activity 2 Support treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition for crisis-affected children aged 6-59 months and PLWG
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: WFP undertakes primary transport; secondary transport and final distribution at health centres is implemented by the either the regional bureau of health or the regional disaster risk management bureau or an NGO partner. WFP field staff monitor deliveries and distributions at health centres.

planEntities.name: Activity 3: Provide unconditional, nutrition-sensitive, cash-based and in-kind food assistance, school feeding and nutrition support to refugees
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: WFP delivers food or cash to food distribution points in refugee camps; final distributions to refugees are by the government's Agency for Refugee and Returnee Affairs, monitored by WFP field staff.

planEntities.name: Activity 4: Provide safe, nutritious and reliable daily meals to primary school children and support to the Ministries and Bureaus of Education and Agriculture in scaling up nutrition-sensitive school feeding programmes
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1: Young people, especially those left behind in education and employment, are equipped with the knowledge and skills required to access decent jobs and participate in civic life.
planEntities.description: WFP supports the scaling up of school feeding programmes (traditional and homegrown), for the provision of safe, nutritious and reliable daily meals to primary school children to meet their basic food and nutritional needs and to increase school enrollment and attendance. WFP mobilises resources, procures food and undertakes the primary transport. The regional bureaux of education undertake secondary transport and deliver food to schools. The schools cook food for school meals. WFP field staff monitor deliveries and provision of meals. For Home Grown School Meals, WFP provides cash and trains government staff in food procurement from local suppliers.

planEntities.name: Activity 5 - Provide nutrition-sensitive social protection, climate risk management services and capacity strengthening support for smallholder farmers, pastoralists, refugees and returnees most vulnerable to climate shocks
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 4.1: Government of Ethiopia’s capacity at national and subnational levels for climate and disaster risk management strengthened to build resilience.
planEntities.description: WFP supports efforts to complement the PSNP with other resilience-building interventions, including: (i) improving the quality of public works, especially soil and water management, building on the corporate resilience building approach; and (ii) weather-indexed livestock and crop insurance, financial services, and livelihood diversification for smallholder farmers, pastoralists, refugees, and returnees.

planEntities.name: Activity 6: Provide climate-sensitive cash-based food transfers to PLWG and children aged 6-23 months, SBCC to communities, training to outreach workers and capacity strengthening to the private sector and Government to contribute to national and regional efforts to reduce stunting and prevent all other forms of malnutrition
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: WFP provides children aged 6-23 months and pregnant and lactating women with restricted cash assistance to purchase nutrient-dense foods from local retailers.  WFP supports technical assistance for local production and marketing of specialized nutritious foods by the private sector, focusing on small and medium-sized enterprises and particularly those owned by women. Other activities includes messages on nutrition, child feeding and care, gender equality and HIV.

planEntities.name: Activity 7: Provide advisory and technical services to federal and regional government and the private sector for strengthening food assistance delivery platforms and national and regional systems, including social safety nets programme management, early warning and emergency preparedness systems, and supply chain solutions and management
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: In collaboration with FAO, IFAD, World Bank and other actors, WFP  strengthens national, regional and local capacities in the areas of early warning, emergency preparedness and response, contingency planning and forecast-based financing, shock-responsive and inclusive safety net programmes, and supply chain management.

planEntities.name: AF_ETH PILLAR 1 (UHC) One billion more people are benefiting from universal health coverage
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Based on SDG indicator 3.8.1 (Improve coverage of essential health services irrespective of gender, age or disability), which is calculated based on major programs tracer interventions for reproductive, maternal, newborn and child health, communicable diseases, and noncommunicable diseases, and health service access which all inturn have their respective tracer indicators  for which data were available. Therefore, to achieve SDG target 3.8 of UHC for all by 2030, at least more people will need to have access to essential health services in each five-year period between 2015 and 2030 ensuring that UHC reaches the poorest, the most marginalized, women, children, and people with disabilities. It also include strengthening health governance for improved transparency, accountability, responsiveness and empowerment of communities including strengthening their health and care workforce, produce and analyze information on financial protection, equity and health expenditure and use to track progress and information decision making. Improving regulatory capacity and supply of quality-assured and safe health products including through pre-qualification services.

planEntities.name: AF_ETH PILLAR 2 (HEM) One billion more people better protected from health emergencies
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: Based on SDG indicator 3.d.1 (International Health Regulations (IHR) capacity and health emergency preparedness). Work to reach this goal will make the world better prepared for health emergencies by measurably increasing the resilience of health systems for a population of 1 billion people. WHO will measure this goal based on the Organization’s activities supporting countries to strengthen their preparedness for health emergencies. Improving the safety of any population improves the safety of everyone. Being “better protected” does not provide any absolute estimation of safety. WHO recognizes that further work is necessary to achieve a more precise description and measurement of parameters such as epidemic risk and resilience of systems. The Organization will, therefore, work together with relevant partners across all sectors.

planEntities.name: AF_ETH PILLAR 3 (HPO) One billion more people enjoying better health and well-being
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.3: Equitable access to basic social services is strengthened, benefitting vulnerable, marginalized and displacementaffected people.
planEntities.description: WHO will contribute to people enjoying better health and well-being through (1)  promoting safe and equitable societies through addressing social determinants (road safety, violence prevention, health in all policies, and integrating social determinants of health in planning, implementation and monitoring of health policies and programmes. (2) promoting and strengthening equitable access to safe, healthy and sustainably produced food through One Health approach including AMR (3) supportive and empowering societies through addressing health risk factors (4) promote healthy environment through improved air quality, implementing COP 26 to build climate resilient health system and low carbon and sustainable health system (5) Creating an enabling environment for healthy setting.

planEntities.description: This strategy builds on two primary goals based on the current state of the eradication effort: Goal One to permanently interrupt all poliovirus transmission in endemic countries and avert polio induced disabilities and Goal two to stop CVDPV transmission and prevent outbreaks in non-endemic countries.

planEntities.name: Réalisation de l’étude STED (Skills for trade and Economic Diversification) pour l’identification des besoins en compétences du secteur agricole   Pojet PAPG1
planEntities.parentName: Produit 2.1.2 - Formation technique et professionnelle
planEntities.description:
L’étude a pour objectif de procéder à une analyse des besoins en compétences du secteur de l’agriculture, notamment dans les filières sélectionnées par le projet PAPG1 de manière à disposer d’informations complètes sur les besoins actuels et émergents en compétences et emploi du secteur.  
Les résultats de cette étude vont permettre d’élaborer des curricula utiles et pertinents pour répondre aux besoin du secteur agricole en compétences et main d’œuvre qualifiée, assurant ainsi une amélioration de l’employabilité dans le secteur, d’améliorer la compétitivité des entreprises à travers la mise à disposition d’une main d’œuvre qualifiée nationale et d’avoir un outil d’orientation pour informer les décideurs, chercheurs d’emplois et entreprises sur les métiers d’avenir et métiers nécessaires pour assurer la relance post covid et la croissance du secteur agricole.  
La première étape de l’étude STED est le diagnostic du secteur. Cette étape a été lancée en décembre 2021 et a été basée essentiellement sur les recherches documentaires et les consultations de terrain avec les acteurs concernés. En plus des acteurs au niveau central, les consultations ont été également menées auprès des acteurs provinciaux au niveau des six provinces ciblées par le projet à savoir : Woleu-Ntem, Ogooué-Lolo, Ogooué-Ivindo, Haut-Ogooué, Ngounié et Nyanga. 
La première version du rapport de l’étude dans le secteur a été partagée en Mars 2022 avec les partenaires institutionnels. Elle a fait l’objet d’une réunion au niveau du ministère de l’agriculture
Conformément à la méthodologie STED, la restitution, discussion et enrichissement de résultats de l’étude STED s’est effectuée lors l’atelier « Technique et de Prospective STED », organisé 12 et 13 avril 2022 à Libreville et a réuni les parties prenantes de l’écosystème agricole (gouvernement, partenaires sociaux, secteur privé, experts). 
Les travaux de l’atelier se sont déroulés durant deux jours et ont permis d’atteindre les objectifs suivants : 
- Discussion et analyse des résultats préliminaires de l’étude en s’appuyant sur les connaissances et l'expertise des participants, les consultants et experts mobilisés ; 
- Discussion et validation des compétences et métiers identifiés qui sont demandés par le secteur agricole 
- Proposition des recommandations pour résoudre les problèmes identifiés au niveau de la formation entravant le développement du secteur, notamment les écarts constatés entre l’offre et la demande des compétences du secteur agricole
- Contribution à la formulation d’une stratégie de développement des compétences dans le secteur agricole et des modalités de sa mise en œuvre

planEntities.name: Réalisation du Plan de Développement stratégique de l"Ecole Nationale de Développement Rural  Projet PAPG1
planEntities.parentName: Produit 2.1.2 - Formation technique et professionnelle
planEntities.description:
Le plan de développement stratégique (PSD) de l’ENDR intervient dans le cadre de la rénovation et de la réorientation de la vision de cette Ecole. Il servira de document de référence aussi bien en interne que pour les partenaires externes et va permettre à l’école de renforcer son positionnement institutionnel et de jouer pleinement son rôle en tant que principal pourvoyeur de main d’œuvre qualifiée agricole dans un contexte de fortes mutations qui repositionne l’agriculture et le développement rural au cœur des transformations structurelles de l’économie gabonaise.
La première version du PSD, résultat d’un état des lieux et de la consultation des parties prenantes pour donner à cet établissement une orientation et qui tienne compte des enjeux actuels en matière de formation agricole, a été finalisée et partagé avec le ministère en charge de l’agriculture. Des séances de travail lui ont été consacrées durant le mois d'avril 2022. Les commentaires et les recommandations formulées ont été intégrés dans la version finale.
A titre de rappel, la démarche méthodologique pour l’élaboration du PSD s’est basée sur les éléments suivants : 
- Analyse du contexte économique, social, institutionnel, politique, technologique et environnemental dans lequel évolue l’école 
- Réalisation d’une manière participative, un diagnostic organisationnel de l’ENDR en mettant en exergue les interactions avec son environnement externe.  Ce diagnostic comporte une analyse SWOT de l’école qui a permis de faire ressortir les forces et les faiblesses internes de l’école ainsi que les opportunités et menaces de son environnement externe. 
- Rédaction de la première version du plan stratégique de développement et la présenter aux parties prenantes en vue de sa discussion et validation 
- Finalisation du plan de développement avec l’intégration des commentaires et recommandations du BIT et des parties prenantes gabonaises.

planEntities.parentName: Produit 2.1.2 - Formation technique et professionnelle
planEntities.description:
Formation de formateurs des conseillers agricoles sur les outils Coops (Think Coop, Start Coop et My-Coop) et GERME (TREE, CREE et Germe Niveau 1)
Cette formation vise la mise en place d’un pool de 21 conseillers d’agricoles qui seront formés dans les outils du BIT et qui seront capables d’assurer une formation et un suivi de proximité des bénéficiaires ultimes pour améliorer les performances des unités économiques mises en place par les jeunes entrepreneurs et impulser l’autonomisation économique des communautés rurales. Ces appuis faciliteront la fixation des jeunes dans leurs terroirs, développera l’employabilité et garantira sur l’ensemble de la chaine de valeur les conditions préalables à la mise en place d’une main d’œuvre de qualité.  la formation a ciblé 21 conseillers agricoles qui sont affectés aux 21 départements du projet PAPG1 ; et qui auront la mission d'accompagner les jeunes pour   la création et la gestion des coopératives agricoles, et la création et la gestion  d’entreprise et  la formation entrepreneurial d’une cible faiblement alphabétisée.
Renforcement des capacités des conseillers d'emploi du PNPE (ex ONE) sur Germe niveau 1 et Germe Vert 
 Cet atelier vise à transformer les conseillers  d'emploi en formateurs certifiés qui accompagneront  des jeune pour la création et la gestion des entreprises, à l’orientation à l’emploi et la création et la gestion  d’entreprise et la formation entrepreneuriale d’une cible faiblement alphabétisée.
Le PNPE partenaire stratégique dans le cadre de ce projet utilise la méthodologie GERME qu’elle a positionné comme option stratégique dans la création et la gestion d’entreprise des jeunes. Une vingtaine de formateurs dans tous le pays mettent en oeuvre les formations au profit des jeunes. Ces formateurs dans le cursus avaient besoin de compléter au niveau des outils pour d’une part prendre en charge les besoins de la cible peu ou pas instruite et d’autre part aider à créer des entreprises vertes ou à "écologiser" les entreprises existantes pour contribuer efficacement à la protection de l’environnement

planEntities.name: A joint Human Security approch to strengthening prévention of and protection and empowerment in mixed migration towards Gabon
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - Renforcement des capacités institutionnellles
planEntities.description:
Prévue pour une période de 18 mois, le programme conjoint  Approche conjointe de la sécurité humaine pour renforcer la prévention et l'autonomisation dans le cadre de la migration mixte vers le Gabon intitulé "prévention et l'autonomisation dans la migration mixte vers le Gabon" (UNICEF, UNODC, UNHRC et OIM)  consistera à améliorer de manière significative la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais dans ses efforts de prévention de gestion des migrations mixtes au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais par le biais d'une approche intégrée basée sur la sécurité humaine pour mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains. L’objectif de ce programme conjoint vise donc  à améliorer la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et à aider le gouvernement à mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains, par le biais d'une approche intégrée fondée sur la sécurité humaine. Le programme aborde également les questions des migrants ayant un statut juridique spécifique, notamment les demandeurs d'asile, les réfugiés provenant de pays confrontés à l'instabilité, les apatrides, les enfants non accompagnés et autres migrants avec des besoins spécifiques.
Comme principales réalisations, un cadre de securité humaine a été dévéloppé, une collecte des données sur la traite des personnes est en cours avec un volet formation des agents étatiques pour la pérénisation de l'activité ainsi que la publication des données collectees. 
En outre, une ONG d’implémentation  est entrain de procéder à l'intégration d'au moins 20 migrants vulnerables et victimes de traite sur l'étendu du territoire. Egalement en cours, le developpement d'une campagne de sensibilisation sur les questions migratoires basée sur le cadre de sécurité humaine, le pacte mondial sur les migrations et le pacte mondial pour les réfugiés.

planEntities.name: Enhancing IOM’s leadership in migration law and policy in West and Central Africa
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - Renforcement des capacités institutionnellles
planEntities.description:
Le projet vise à établir un réseau d'experts juridiques dans la région, afin d'appuyer la réforme des lois et des politiques migratoires. Il couvre également la liaison avec la CEEAC, la Communauté Economique des Etats de l'Afrique centrale, afin de concrétiser la collaboration entre l’OIM, la Commission de la CEEAC, et ses Etats membres, en vue d’avancer de manière coordonnée pour la mise en œuvre du Pacte mondiale pour des migrations sûres, ordonnées et régulières, ainsi que sur les priorités conjointes de l’OIM et de la CEEAC en matière de mobilité, gouvernance des migrations, protection, inclusion, sécurité, développement, changement climatique et résilience, entre autres sujets.                L'engagement de l'OIM avec la Commission de la CEEAC a été considérablement stimulé grâce à MIRAC, avec le développement de priorités stratégiques conjointes et l'adoption d'une feuille de route conjointe pour la période 2022 - 2024. La collaboration avec la Commission s'est accrue, notamment dans les domaines de la gouvernance des frontières, de la santé et de la migration, ainsi que de l'environnement et du changement climatique. La retraite de planification stratégique conjointe CEEAC-OIM a également abouti à la création d'un groupe de travail interdépartemental sur la migration au sein de la Commission, reconnaissant la nature transversale de la migration et la nécessité de travailler en dehors des silos traditionnels, dans la perspective de l'examen des progrès de la mise en œuvre du Pacte mondial pour les migrations dans la région, auquel la CEEAC s'est également engagée, sous la forme d'un MIDCAS relancé.

En ce qui concerne le réseau d'experts juridiques, 11 pays sont désormais représentés au sein d'un groupe professionnel dynamique visant à promouvoir une réforme juridique et politique de la migration fondée sur les droits, à renforcer et à centraliser l'expertise locale, et à favoriser les connexions et les débats entre experts et décideurs politiques. Le groupe, ainsi que son comité directeur, sont soutenus par des termes de référence détaillés, approuvés par les membres lors de la réunion inaugurale du réseau au Togo, en novembre 2022. Le réseau est appelé à devenir un point de référence faisant autorité en matière d'expertise sur le droit de la migration dans la région de l'AOC, et les échanges sont déjà dynamiques, les membres impliquant d'autres personnes dans leurs conférences et symposiums, et produisant des mémoires clés sur l'état du droit de la migration au niveau national. Enfin, la compilation des textes clés de la région par les experts juridiques a été initiée en 2022, et le développement de la base de données qui en résulte est en cours, rendant plus accessibles les documents politiques et juridiques importants en matière de migration.

planEntities.name: A joint Human Security approch to strengthening prévention of and protection and empowerment in mixed migration towards Gabon
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - Renforcement des capacités institutionnellles
planEntities.description:
Prévue pour une période de 18 mois, le programme conjoint  Approche conjointe de la sécurité humaine pour renforcer la prévention et l'autonomisation dans le cadre de la migration mixte vers le Gabon intitulé "prévention et l'autonomisation dans la migration mixte vers le Gabon" (UNICEF, UNODC, UNHRC et OIM)  consistera à améliorer de manière significative la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais dans ses efforts de prévention de gestion des migrations mixtes au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais par le biais d'une approche intégrée basée sur la sécurité humaine pour mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains. L’objectif de ce programme conjoint vise donc  à améliorer la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et à aider le gouvernement à mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains, par le biais d'une approche intégrée fondée sur la sécurité humaine. Le programme aborde également les questions des migrants ayant un statut juridique spécifique, notamment les demandeurs d'asile, les réfugiés provenant de pays confrontés à l'instabilité, les apatrides, les enfants non accompagnés et autres migrants avec des besoins spécifiques.
Comme principales réalisations, un cadre de securité humaine a été dévéloppé, une collecte des données sur la traite des personnes est en cours avec un volet formation des agents étatiques pour la pérénisation de l'activité ainsi que la publication des données collectees. 
En outre, une ONG d’implémentation  est entrain de procéder à l'intégration d'au moins 20 migrants vulnerables et victimes de traite sur l'étendu du territoire. Egalement en cours, le developpement d'une campagne de sensibilisation sur les questions migratoires basée sur le cadre de sécurité humaine, le pacte mondial sur les migrations et le pacte mondial pour les réfugiés.

planEntities.name: A joint Human Security approch to strengthening prévention of and protection and empowerment in mixed migration towards Gabon
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - Renforcement des capacités institutionnellles
planEntities.description:
Prévue pour une période de 18 mois, le programme conjoint  Approche conjointe de la sécurité humaine pour renforcer la prévention et l'autonomisation dans le cadre de la migration mixte vers le Gabon intitulé "prévention et l'autonomisation dans la migration mixte vers le Gabon" (UNICEF, UNODC, UNHRC et OIM)  consistera à améliorer de manière significative la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais dans ses efforts de prévention de gestion des migrations mixtes au Gabon et soutiendra le gouvernement gabonais par le biais d'une approche intégrée basée sur la sécurité humaine pour mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains. L’objectif de ce programme conjoint vise donc  à améliorer la gestion de la migration mixte au Gabon et à aider le gouvernement à mieux identifier et protéger les migrants ayant des besoins spécifiques, notamment les victimes de la traite des êtres humains, par le biais d'une approche intégrée fondée sur la sécurité humaine. Le programme aborde également les questions des migrants ayant un statut juridique spécifique, notamment les demandeurs d'asile, les réfugiés provenant de pays confrontés à l'instabilité, les apatrides, les enfants non accompagnés et autres migrants avec des besoins spécifiques.
Comme principales réalisations, un cadre de securité humaine a été dévéloppé, une collecte des données sur la traite des personnes est en cours avec un volet formation des agents étatiques pour la pérénisation de l'activité ainsi que la publication des données collectees. 
En outre, une ONG d’implémentation  est entrain de procéder à l'intégration d'au moins 20 migrants vulnerables et victimes de traite sur l'étendu du territoire. Egalement en cours, le developpement d'une campagne de sensibilisation sur les questions migratoires basée sur le cadre de sécurité humaine, le pacte mondial sur les migrations et le pacte mondial pour les réfugiés.

planEntities.name: 1.1.3.2 - Rénforcement des capacitiés nationales et regionales des forces d’application de la loi, des procureurs et du sytéme judiciaire et rénforcement de la cooperation entre les Etats membres de la CEEAC pour luttre contrôle la criminalité liée aux espéces sauvages et le traffic illicite des ressources naturelles.
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - Renforcement des capacités institutionnellles
planEntities.description:
Le projet vise à renforcer les capacités de détection et de répression des agents chargés de détecter et de combattre le trafic illicite de ressources naturelles et à améliorer la mise en œuvre du système de justice pénale dans la CEEAC.
Le projet cible spécifiquement les services répressifs sous un angle d'éco-sécurité. En effet, le projet contribue à concrétiser et affiner la politique d'éco-sécurité de la CEEAC en lui fournissant des cadres institutionnels mieux adaptés pour répondre aux enjeux liés à l'éco-sécurité, en renforçant le cadre juridique des Etats sur les questions d'éco-sécurité, en développant les capacités existantes en matière de renseignement sur l'écosécurité et sur la criminalité liée aux espèces sauvages, et en renforçant les capacités des acteurs en charge de l'écosécurité à travers des formations adaptées.
Par conséquent, dans le cadre du projet, ce concept d'éco-sécurité pourrait être compris comme la stratégie régionale pour sécuriser et gérer durablement les ressources naturelles (faune, flore / foresterie et exploitation minière) de l'Afrique centrale

planEntities.parentName: Produit 3.1.2 - Développement de programmes et politiques de protection sociale
planEntities.description:
Appui à l'accélération de la lutte contre les maladies non transmissibles y compris la lutte contre les facteurs de risques (tabagisme, alcool, alimentation saine…); Appui à la promotion de la santé et l'environnement. Réalisation de l'enquête CAP chez les jeunes de 18 à 35 ans  vis-à-vis des produits du tabac nouveaux et émergents dans les provinces du Woleu Ntem, de l’Ogooué Maritime et de la Ngounié (population masculine plus consommatrices que la population féminine, Absence d’activités sur le terrain du Programme de lutte contre le tabagisme, difficultés d’achat des produits électroniques du fait de leur coût encore relativement élevé)
Réalisation d’un atelier ayant permis d’obtenir l’engagement de 68 personnels de 22 ministères sur la lutte contre la nicotine et les produits du tabac nouveaux et émergents dans le contexte d'une lutte antitabac élargie.
Renforcement des capacités de 33 acteurs de la lutte antitabac sur le cadre juridique relatif à l'interdiction de l'ingérence de l'industrie du tabac dans les politiques de santé au Gabon et sur les moyens et les outils de riposte
Appui à l’analyse de données provisoires (2020-21) et de la politique fiscale du tabac entre les administrations douanières et fiscales et l’OMS afin de pouvoir définir les causes de la stabilité des prix des paquets de cigarettes qui n’ont pas évolué depuis 5 ans malgré le changement du droit d’accise
Organisation d’une campagne nationale de sensibilisation « Mois sans Tabac » Mai 2022 (plus de 700 personnes sensibilisées, envoi de messages de sensibilisation aux 1 800 000 abonnés de Libertis, affichage sur 5 grands panneaux publicitaires et message de sensibilisation à la télévision)
Appui à la promotion de la santé et l'environnement (sensibilisation sur la gestion des produits chimiques dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet Chemobs. Plus de 2000 personnes ont été sensibilisés dans les 9 provinces sur la gestion des produits chimiques. Pendant un mois plus 25 affiches grand public ont été déployés sur Libreville pour sensibilisés les 800 000 habitants de la capitale). Un projet de texte sur l'observatiore intégré de gestion des produits chimiques a été élaboré et est dans le circuit de signature. L'inventaire des PCB a été réalisé dans 5 provinces.

planEntities.name: "EU INNOVATIVE ACTION FOR PRIVATE SECTOR COMPETITIVENESS IN GEORGIA (EU IPSC)"
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.Improved competitiveness and social responsibility of private sector
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed UN Joint Programme (UNJP) is: to enhance entrepreneurship and business sophistication by strengthening the capacities of government and local entities to develop and operate clusters and supporting companies directly with strategic investments and better connect to diaspora groups, while also demonstrating the effectiveness of these strategies to businesses. This will be achieved through support to a range of entities in developing specific clusters for the benefit of enhancing geographically constrained value chains for improving cluster coordination, marketing, innovation, public private dialogue and more. It will also be done through strategic investments in companies that are deemed necessary to facilitate improvements in the cluster. This will also be enhanced by a sustained effort to consolidate evidence-base, clustering-related policy and implementation capacities and connect local businesses to diaspora communities, for the purpose of knowledge and technology transfer and financing.

The Joint Programme will include four specific outputs/results:
1.	Strengthened capacities of policy-makers and other stakeholders to identify and develop clusters
2.	Development and functioning of the clustering approach in the packaging and seeds/seedlings sectors
3.	Development and support of strategic investments in companies deemed necessary to improve the cluster.
4.	Mainstreaming Migration in SME Development

FAO objectives:
- Seedling certification is promoted through support to the private sector (nurseries) to enhance the production of orchard and grapevine seedlings in Georgia
- Supporting state and private sector actors in promoting seedling certification through legislative and capacity-building activities and technical support

planEntities.name: "EU INNOVATIVE ACTION FOR PRIVATE SECTOR COMPETITIVENESS IN GEORGIA (EU IPSC)"
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.Improved competitiveness and social responsibility of private sector
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed UN Joint Programme (UNJP) is: to enhance entrepreneurship and business sophistication by strengthening the capacities of government and local entities to develop and operate clusters and supporting companies directly with strategic investments and better connect to diaspora groups, while also demonstrating the effectiveness of these strategies to businesses. This will be achieved through support to a range of entities in developing specific clusters for the benefit of enhancing geographically constrained value chains for improving cluster coordination, marketing, innovation, public private dialogue and more. It will also be done through strategic investments in companies that are deemed necessary to facilitate improvements in the cluster. This will also be enhanced by a sustained effort to consolidate evidence-base, clustering-related policy and implementation capacities and connect local businesses to diaspora communities, for the purpose of knowledge and technology transfer and financing.

The Joint Programme will include four specific outputs/results:
1.	Strengthened capacities of policy-makers and other stakeholders to identify and develop clusters
2.	Development and functioning of the clustering approach in the packaging and seeds/seedlings sectors
3.	Development and support of strategic investments in companies deemed necessary to improve the cluster.
4.	Mainstreaming Migration in SME Development

FAO objectives:
- Seedling certification is promoted through support to the private sector (nurseries) to enhance the production of orchard and grapevine seedlings in Georgia
- Supporting state and private sector actors in promoting seedling certification through legislative and capacity-building activities and technical support

planEntities.name: "Human Rights for All - Phase 2"
planEntities.parentName: 1.2. National legislation and policies to eliminate discrimination, enhance human rights and equal access to justice in Georgia
planEntities.description:
“Human Rights for All – Phase 2” is a joint initiative of the European Union (EU) and the United Nations (UN). It will be implemented as a joint programme by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). The UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) will be the Administrative Agent and UNDP Georgia, the Convening Agent.
The JP will build directly on the achievements of “Human Rights for All – Phase 1,”2 which was likewise a partnership between the EU and the UN agencies. It will continue to strengthen and promote human rights in areas covered in Phase 1 while identifying and tackling human rights issues in new areas. The JP will seek to bringing tangible result to the local level through various forms of engagement, including with dedicated support to local authorities.
The overall objective of the project - Citizens of Georgia, and primarily those in vulnerable situations, enjoy better protection of their human rights – complies with the national priorities of Georgia enshrined in the Constitution and major policy documents of the country, as well as with the international obligations of Georgia, including EU-Georgia Association Ageeement, Sustainable Development Goals and UN human rights treaties.
UNDP and OHCHR will work in close coordination to achieve the overall objective of the JP, inter alia, through the support to the implementation and monitoring of national human rights policy and related frameworks, improvement of the independent investigation of crimes committed by law-enforcement officials, combatting torture and other forms of ill-treatment, protection of personal data, addressing challenges to the protection of human rights in the regions of Georgia and human rights of minority groups and persons in vulnerable situations, including LGBTQI and persons with disabilities, and increasing awareness of human rights among rights-holders.
The Action has five specific objectives (SOs):
SO1: Relevant public bodies (duty-bearers) develop, implement and monitor national human rights policy and related frameworks
SO2: Law-enforcement and human rights protection bodies effectively implement their duties related to policymaking and enforcement with due oversight and transparency
SO3: The human rights of minority groups and persons in vulnerable situations are recognised in law and protected in practice
SO4. Local authorities more effectively protect human rights of all citizens, primarily those in vulnerable situations and minority groups
SO5. Citizens are informed on, favourable to and supportive of human rights for all and efforts to protect them.

planEntities.name: USAID Partnering for Resilience Program
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Improved socio-economic conditions, resilience and self-reliance in conflict-affected communities
planEntities.description:
The USAID-funded Partnering for Resilience Program is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with four UN Agencies: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) and United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women). The project aims to foster the peacebuilding and conflict transformation with an ultimate goal to promote an enabling environment for sustainable peace. The project builds on the success and lessons learned from previous and current interventions of UNDP and UN partner organizations in support of conflict-affected communities and the lasting peace in general. The project expects to achieve the following results: 
1.1: Increased public support for conflict transformation and lasting peace (UNDP, UNICEF, UN Women)
1.2: Improved capacity of youth in business education and increased demand for production and trade (FAO, 
1.3: Enhanced community resilience by improved access to diverse sources of social services (UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF)

2.1: Increased exposure for changemakers to international and/or unique opportunities (FAO, UNICEF)
2.2: Sustained professional networks and partnerships across dividing lines (UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA)

3.1: Robust contextual information generated (FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, WHO)
3.2: Complexity-aware monitoring of programmatic implementation established (UNDP).

planEntities.name: "EU INNOVATIVE ACTION FOR PRIVATE SECTOR COMPETITIVENESS IN GEORGIA (EU IPSC)"
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.Improved competitiveness and social responsibility of private sector
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed UN Joint Programme (UNJP) is: to enhance entrepreneurship and business sophistication by strengthening the capacities of government and local entities to develop and operate clusters and supporting companies directly with strategic investments and better connect to diaspora groups, while also demonstrating the effectiveness of these strategies to businesses. This will be achieved through support to a range of entities in developing specific clusters for the benefit of enhancing geographically constrained value chains for improving cluster coordination, marketing, innovation, public private dialogue and more. It will also be done through strategic investments in companies that are deemed necessary to facilitate improvements in the cluster. This will also be enhanced by a sustained effort to consolidate evidence-base, clustering-related policy and implementation capacities and connect local businesses to diaspora communities, for the purpose of knowledge and technology transfer and financing.

The Joint Programme will include four specific outputs/results:
1.	Strengthened capacities of policy-makers and other stakeholders to identify and develop clusters
2.	Development and functioning of the clustering approach in the packaging and seeds/seedlings sectors
3.	Development and support of strategic investments in companies deemed necessary to improve the cluster.
4.	Mainstreaming Migration in SME Development

FAO objectives:
- Seedling certification is promoted through support to the private sector (nurseries) to enhance the production of orchard and grapevine seedlings in Georgia
- Supporting state and private sector actors in promoting seedling certification through legislative and capacity-building activities and technical support

planEntities.name: USAID Partnering for Resilience Program
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Improved socio-economic conditions, resilience and self-reliance in conflict-affected communities
planEntities.description:
The USAID-funded Partnering for Resilience Program is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with four UN Agencies: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) and United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women). The project aims to foster the peacebuilding and conflict transformation with an ultimate goal to promote an enabling environment for sustainable peace. The project builds on the success and lessons learned from previous and current interventions of UNDP and UN partner organizations in support of conflict-affected communities and the lasting peace in general. The project expects to achieve the following results: 
1.1: Increased public support for conflict transformation and lasting peace (UNDP, UNICEF, UN Women)
1.2: Improved capacity of youth in business education and increased demand for production and trade (FAO, 
1.3: Enhanced community resilience by improved access to diverse sources of social services (UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF)

2.1: Increased exposure for changemakers to international and/or unique opportunities (FAO, UNICEF)
2.2: Sustained professional networks and partnerships across dividing lines (UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA)

3.1: Robust contextual information generated (FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, WHO)
3.2: Complexity-aware monitoring of programmatic implementation established (UNDP).

planEntities.name: "Human Rights for All - Phase 2"
planEntities.parentName: 1.2. National legislation and policies to eliminate discrimination, enhance human rights and equal access to justice in Georgia
planEntities.description:
“Human Rights for All – Phase 2” is a joint initiative of the European Union (EU) and the United Nations (UN). It will be implemented as a joint programme by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). The UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) will be the Administrative Agent and UNDP Georgia, the Convening Agent.
The JP will build directly on the achievements of “Human Rights for All – Phase 1,”2 which was likewise a partnership between the EU and the UN agencies. It will continue to strengthen and promote human rights in areas covered in Phase 1 while identifying and tackling human rights issues in new areas. The JP will seek to bringing tangible result to the local level through various forms of engagement, including with dedicated support to local authorities.
The overall objective of the project - Citizens of Georgia, and primarily those in vulnerable situations, enjoy better protection of their human rights – complies with the national priorities of Georgia enshrined in the Constitution and major policy documents of the country, as well as with the international obligations of Georgia, including EU-Georgia Association Ageeement, Sustainable Development Goals and UN human rights treaties.
UNDP and OHCHR will work in close coordination to achieve the overall objective of the JP, inter alia, through the support to the implementation and monitoring of national human rights policy and related frameworks, improvement of the independent investigation of crimes committed by law-enforcement officials, combatting torture and other forms of ill-treatment, protection of personal data, addressing challenges to the protection of human rights in the regions of Georgia and human rights of minority groups and persons in vulnerable situations, including LGBTQI and persons with disabilities, and increasing awareness of human rights among rights-holders.
The Action has five specific objectives (SOs):
SO1: Relevant public bodies (duty-bearers) develop, implement and monitor national human rights policy and related frameworks
SO2: Law-enforcement and human rights protection bodies effectively implement their duties related to policymaking and enforcement with due oversight and transparency
SO3: The human rights of minority groups and persons in vulnerable situations are recognised in law and protected in practice
SO4. Local authorities more effectively protect human rights of all citizens, primarily those in vulnerable situations and minority groups
SO5. Citizens are informed on, favourable to and supportive of human rights for all and efforts to protect them.

The USAID-funded Partnering for Resilience Program is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with four UN Agencies: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) and United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women). The project aims to foster the peacebuilding and conflict transformation with an ultimate goal to promote an enabling environment for sustainable peace. The project builds on the success and lessons learned from previous and current interventions of UNDP and UN partner organizations in support of conflict-affected communities and the lasting peace in general. planEntities.parentName: 5.3. Innovative and climate-friendly technologies used for inclusive green economy, energy efficiency and clean energy production to enhance NDCs (Nationally Determined Contribution) and support long-term decarbonization strategies
planEntities.description:
Funded by the European Union, the EU4Environment programme aims to preserve and better utilise natural capital, improve environmental well-being and stimulate sustainable economic growth in six Eastern Partnership countries, namely Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine.

By bringing together environmental and economic actors, the programme supports policy and legislative reforms, promotes greener planning and investment, stimulates the uptake of innovative technologies, encourages new business models and contributes to the creation of green jobs. It also promotes improved environmental governance, strengthened management of protected areas and forests and the advancement of sustainable trade.

planEntities.parentName: 5.3. Innovative and climate-friendly technologies used for inclusive green economy, energy efficiency and clean energy production to enhance NDCs (Nationally Determined Contribution) and support long-term decarbonization strategies
planEntities.description: The project addresses a number of barriers to the safe management of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in Georgia. These include the absence of a comprehensive regulatory framework for PCB management, limited awareness of PCB presence in dielectric oils, the lack of PCB testing within electricity generation and distribution companies, financial constraints and technical capacity gaps.

planEntities.name: The technical competencies and sustainability of the conformity assessment bodies are strengthened for the fruits and vegetables value chain
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.Improved competitiveness and social responsibility of private sector
planEntities.description:
The Global Quality and Standards Programme (GQSP) in Georgia aims at strengthening the capacity of conformity assessment bodies (CABs) serving the fruits and vegetables value chain, ultimately contributing to upgrading the producer's ability to comply with market requirements. The intervention is structured along with the following three outputs:
1. Conduct an in-depth analysis of Georgia’s fruits and vegetable value chain, particularly looking at quality-related challenges and identifying related capacity building needs.
2. Capacity building of CABs to ensure quality infrastructure services are capable of proving compliance with EU market requirements.
3. Define, in a broader context, the development needs of the laboratory infrastructure in Georgia, in view of meeting the needs of today and the future and serving the growing export base of the country.
The overarching goal of the intervention is to align Georgia’s quality infrastructure institutions and services to the needs of the national production and potential export of fruits and vegetables, in view of accessing foreign markets, particularly the EU market.

planEntities.name: "EU INNOVATIVE ACTION FOR PRIVATE SECTOR COMPETITIVENESS IN GEORGIA (EU IPSC)"
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.Improved competitiveness and social responsibility of private sector
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed UN Joint Programme (UNJP) is: to enhance entrepreneurship and business sophistication by strengthening the capacities of government and local entities to develop and operate clusters and supporting companies directly with strategic investments and better connect to diaspora groups, while also demonstrating the effectiveness of these strategies to businesses. This will be achieved through support to a range of entities in developing specific clusters for the benefit of enhancing geographically constrained value chains for improving cluster coordination, marketing, innovation, public private dialogue and more. It will also be done through strategic investments in companies that are deemed necessary to facilitate improvements in the cluster. This will also be enhanced by a sustained effort to consolidate evidence-base, clustering-related policy and implementation capacities and connect local businesses to diaspora communities, for the purpose of knowledge and technology transfer and financing.

The Joint Programme will include four specific outputs/results:
1.	Strengthened capacities of policy-makers and other stakeholders to identify and develop clusters
2.	Development and functioning of the clustering approach in the packaging and seeds/seedlings sectors
3.	Development and support of strategic investments in companies deemed necessary to improve the cluster.
4.	Mainstreaming Migration in SME Development

FAO objectives:
- Seedling certification is promoted through support to the private sector (nurseries) to enhance the production of orchard and grapevine seedlings in Georgia
- Supporting state and private sector actors in promoting seedling certification through legislative and capacity-building activities and technical support

planEntities.description:
Sous activités:
- Faire un diagnostic des infrastructures existantes, des opportunités en formation et cartographie des acteurs associatifs.
- Renforcer les capacités (matériel, réhabilitation d'infrastructures, gestion de centre de jeunes, activités sociales…) d'un centre multifonctionnel.
- Former 100 jeunes (Hommes et Femmes) en entreprenariat et soutien aux initiatives socio-culturelles et fournir des kits adaptés au fonctionnement.
- Identifier des groupements d’intérêt économique des femmes et des jeunes et former leurs membres sur la gestion organisationnelle, l'entreprenariat et pratiques agricoles résilientes.

- Appuyer l'identification et le financement de 10 micro-projets agricoles transfrontaliers de cohésion sociale et d’utilité communautaires à travers un comité local mis en place à cet effet.
- Appuyer la production et à l’aménagement de parcelles agricoles communautaires pour renforcer la cohésion sociale.
- Organiser /redynamiser deux (2) marchés transfrontaliers en faveur des populations vivant dans les localités frontalières de la Guinée et de la Côte d'Ivoire.
