planEntities.name: 1.1.7.12 - Support policy development, advocacy and an increase in the knowledge base in the areas of GBV and SRH to resulting supportive regulations/ strategies/plans that address harmful practices and ensure universal access to comprehensive GBV and SRH information and services across development and humanitarian contexts
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.7 - Government and key stakeholders at all levels have greater capacity and resources to develop and implement policy, legal and accountability frameworks to advance human rights, access to justice, promote gender equality and reduce vulnerabilities
planEntities.description:
UNFPA will provide required technical assistance to the MOWECP at national and district level in selected geographies, in review and revision of the existing laws and policies on GBV, SRH and harmful practices, such as draft of Revised Penal Code, draft of the Elimination of Sexual Violence and discriminatory law at sub-national level. UNFPA will assist the government in requiring the revisions of the policies and programmes. Further, UNFPA will work closely with the UN Gender Thematic Working Group, UN Human Rights Working Group, National Commission on Violence Against Women (NCVAW), provide support in coordinating the GBV Sub Cluster,  national and sub-national parliament and other relevant partners in strengthening capacity to monitor the implementation of the GBV and harmful practices policies/ strategies. The key activities will be carried out during the 10th CP are as follows:
●	Policy dialogues on the revision of Penal Code and endorsement of Sexual Violence Law with national and sub-national government, parliamentarian, CSO, academic, religious and community leaders, young people and media; 
●	Joint advocacy and analysis with UN Gender Thematic Working Group and UN Human Rights Working Group on addressing discriminatory laws related to gender inequality, gender-based violence and harmful practices including:
-	Conducting joint assessment and mapping of existing laws and policies on GBV, harmful practices and human rights, undertaken and identifies violations and priorities for intervention; and 
-	Strengthening National Human Rights Institution and Women’s CSO network.
●	Provide technical support to national and sub-national governments in the implementation of the National Strategy on the Prevention of Child Marriage and the 2030 Roadmap on the Prevention of Harmful Practices including:
-	Development of manual for strengthening reproductive health and Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) for child marriage prevention;
-	Conducting public education and advocacy on national data availability on harmful practices; and
-	Conducting evaluability and impact assessment on the implementation of National Strategy on Child Marriage Prevention and the 2030 Roadmap on the Prevention of Harmful practices.
●	Advocacy dialogues with national and subnational government, parliamentarian, CSO, academic, religious and community leaders, young people and media to address the need of data for evidence based policy on GBV and harmful practices including:
-	Development of policy recommendation, policy paper and draft of supportive regulation on GBV and harmful practices prevention; 
-	Development of protocols and operational guideline on Gender and GBV Integration, people with disability and psychosocial support   in humanitarian situation; and
-	Strengthen the leadership, role and function of the national GBV, older person  and disability sub clusters.

planEntities.name: 1.1.7.14 - Technical support and advocacy on developing, implementing and monitoring a model on gender transformative community mobilization programming to address harmful masculinity and promote positive gender norms
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.7 - Government and key stakeholders at all levels have greater capacity and resources to develop and implement policy, legal and accountability frameworks to advance human rights, access to justice, promote gender equality and reduce vulnerabilities
planEntities.description:
In an effort to address pervasive gender stereotypes, promote shared power, control of resources and decision-making, and support women’s empowerment for the prevention of GBV and harmful practices, UNFPA Indonesia aims to implement innovative interventions that have a transformative impact on gender roles. Gender Transformative Programming (GTP) addresses institutional, social and cultural dynamics that influence the behaviors and vulnerabilities of women and men in Indonesian society. A critical part of this approach is engaging men and boys, youth and adolescents as partners and agents of change in support of positive gender norms for gender equality and addressing negative forms of masculinities (harmful masculinity) that promote violence and conflict. 
The key activities will be carried out during the 10th CP are as follows:
●	Provide technical support and advocacy for innovative intervention targeted gender transformative community mobilization programme in 4 districts for prevention of GBV and harmful practices with operational research to document what works including:
-	Development of document for integrating gender transformative at national and sub national level including the Road Map for male involvement and adaptation of National SOP on male involvement;
-	Strengthening the capacities and competencies of selected district government to implement the integration of gender transformative programme into GBV prevention and RH programme;
-	Monitoring the implementation of of the gender transformative programme integration into GBV prevention and RH programme at selected district; and
-	Documenting lesson learned and good practices on the implementation of the gender transformative programme integration into GBV prevention and RH programme for evidence based advocacy at national and sub national level

In selecting districts for UNFPA support, priority will be given to underserved districts with particularly vulnerable groups of women and girls, such as resettled populations, female-headed households, women with disabilities, women living with HIV and young women and girls.

As the first phase was successfully implemented, the SMART Fish programme is extended under a country project of UNIDO - SECO Global Quality Standards Programme (GQSP). planEntities.description:
The overall goal of this project is to strengthen preparedness and resilience of prisons in Indonesia against the current and future public health emergencies. To this end, this project seeks to realize three outcomes:
1.	Prison systems are prepared with adequate strategies against public health emergencies, including COVID-19;
2.	Prison officers have the knowledge and capacity to contribute to pandemic preparedness and to implement response measures; and
3.	Prison systems are equipped with adequate facilities and infrastructure against public health emergencies.

planEntities.name: 4.1.1.22 Data Insights for Social and Humanitarian Action (Phase 1 and 2)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1 - Government and key stakeholders have increased capacity to design policies and incentives that promote innovation and to implement and scale up innovative policies, technologies and practices to accelerate the achievement of SDG targets
planEntities.description:
Global Data Access Initiative (GDAI) is an initiative managed by UNOPS and the Executive Office of the Secretary General (EOSG) across UN Global Pulse (UNGP) in collaboration with UN agencies (World Food Program (WFP), the UN Development Program (UNDP), private sector partners, and foundations. GDAI aspires to catalyst the formation of a connected and cohesive ecosystem of “plug-and-play” data and AI products and services including the responsible access to, use, and reuse of data thereby accelerating the attainment of the SDGs. 

GDAI will build and deploy two scalable, productionized solutions to problems faced by frontline organizations focusing on natural disaster response and recovery in close collaboration with, and informed by the needs of WFP and UNDP: Vulnerability mapping and population assessment and; Disaster damage assessment. In building these solutions, the team will take an approach that aims at scalable products for these use cases and beyond. This will result in a collection of “plug-and-play” data and AI products and services that can be used to accelerate the delivery of solutions in pursuit of the SDGs whilst generating insights into how to best evolve and, over time, realise the vision of GDAI beyond natural disaster response and recovery.

UNOPS is tasked for the provision of operational services to the UN Global Pulse to operationalize SDG specific use cases leveraging data from private sector and other entities across countries in Asia. 

In 2023, GDAI was renamed DISHA (Data Insights for Social and Humanitarian Action) to better reflect the goal of the initiative and to show what the personnel wants to achieve with the data. DISHA keeps being a unique partnership between the UN and private firms and foundations, working day to day in different regions on the same goal. The partners are UN Global Pulse, McKinsey & Company, Google.org, the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation and the Jain Family Institute.

planEntities.description:
WFP partnered with the Government to enhance understanding on anticipatory action and assess the feasibility for its implementation in Indonesia. 
In partnership with the Ministry of Social Affairs, WFP assessed the local climate hazard risk profile and existing early warning and response mechanisms through a scoping exercise conducted in five provinces across Indonesia. These assessments have included discussions with local communities on how they address and respond to weather extremes and climate shocks. The results of this scoping exercise will inform WFP’s contribution to implementing anticipatory action. 

Further contributing to a strengthened common understanding on anticipatory action, WFP facilitated the participation of the Meteorological, Climatological and Geophysical Agency in the 6th Asia Pacific Dialogue Platform on Anticipatory Action in Bangkok, Thailand. The Agency gained additional knowledge on anticipatory action and shared progress and good practices from Indonesia, particularly on impact-based forecasting. Engagement at this regional event contributed to strengthened dialogue with the Coordinating Ministry of Human Development and Cultural Affairs on anticipatory action, along with other partners within the Risk-Informed Early Action Partnership (REAP). Such engagement will continue in 2023 in the form of enhanced policy dialogue on anticipatory action.

planEntities.name: 5.1.1.7 - Advocate with National and State Governments to institutionalize risk informed programming principles across 5 sectors (Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Child Protection)  ; build capacity and provide implementation support at various levels ( including Gram Panchayats)
planEntities.parentName: Output 5.1.1 - Effective institutional, legislative and policy frameworks in place to enhance sustainable environment and natural resource management and implementation of climate change and disaster risk reduction at national and sub-national levels.
planEntities.description:
UNICEF supported states to prioritize Risk Informed Programming for all the UNICEF priority sectors. The support included supporting the states to roll out Comprehensive School Safety Programme(CSSP),  enhancing capacities of departments and NGO/civil society partners to build resilience through CPiE framework, Child Protection in Schools through CSSSP & CBDRR, CCI safety security plans across UNICEF supported states. The support helped bring convergence in addressing Child Protection issues in emergencies such as ensuring Safety Security of Children at CCIs, Child friendly spaces in Flood/ Cyclone shelters, registration of missing children, tracking of child trafficking during and post disaster situations, even COVID 19 Pandemic situation. UNICEF assisted Education, CP, Nutrition and WASH section in conducting training of  government functionaries on EPR. Established Inter- Agency coordination mechanism across states for unified preparedness and response. UNICEF, through government systems and partner organizations  built capacity of  50,000 healthcare workers including counsellors, psychiatrists, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), and frontline workers across the country for supporting Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) during the  pandemic.
Shock responsive and risk Informed GPDPs (ISP) has been advocated in all the UNICEF supported states.  In Assam, intensive technical support has been provided to 101 GPs in Goalpara, Barpeta and Darrang (all aspirational districts) and 41 GPs in Dhemaji and Majuli (flood prone and tribal dominated) to include risk informed and shock responsive costed activities for children and women in preparation of GPDPs with active participation of children and women in the planning process. In the state of Bihar, training package on risk-informed programme integrated in the trainings organized by BSDMA and BIPARD, 242 Officers (F 38, M 204) trained in three days residential trainings. Assistance in establishing Centre of Excellence in Disaster Management in visioning exercise, annual planning and resource allocation, mobilized USD 700,000 for 2021-2022 from Disaster Management Department. UNICEF Chhattisgarh advocacy with the government led to cash transfer benefit to 17,677 migrant workers. Employment of more than 150 days to 42,397 FRA Families (initially it was for 100 days). Additionally, over 6000 migrant workers have been linked with social protection schemes, livelihood etc. as reported from 12 districts. About 2.6 Million women got work under the scheme (MGNREGA), which is 50.08%. of the total workers employed.
Supported State Government technically to develop communication materials and messages on CSSSP in consultation with C4D where DRR led the process of communication and resource materials development. CSSSP has also been piloted in 400 schools, whereas 382 Nodal Teachers and 102 Government Officials were trained on Comprehensive approach of School Safety. UNICEF extended technical support to state departments of education in the development of modules and guidance on safe school reopening of schools and Early Childhood Development centres along with continued advocacy for ensuring COVID-19 responsive behaviours. Seventeen  state governments utilized these protocols and guidelines in reopening schools and early childhood development centres safely in a phased manner.
Knowledge products were developed for children through comic books on 5 key hazards. Technical support extended for capacity building of state IAG institution & CSO network on CCC and EPRP, 60 CSO partners from 45 organizations were sensitized on Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian actions. Partnership with Indian Institute of Technology, Gandhinagar developed climate risk assessment and sectoral advisories towards preparedness planning and response actions.
With UNICEF’s support, eight states developed and implemented catch up and learning recovery programme to address and mitigate learning loss for 15.83 million children (48 per cent girls). Rajasthan’s accelerated learning programme led to addressing the learning loss of 4,500 children (55 per cent girls) in 140 remote locations through 140 Shiksha Sahayat (60 per cent women). In Maharashtra and Assam around 3.5 million children (48 per cent girls) benefitted from reading and literacy skills through respective state reading programmes. In Odisha, 78,000 children (46 per cent girls) in geographically remote areas were reached through 9,800 pre-service student teachers through an innovative, state led internship programme. 
UNICEF, with its development partners advocated for immediate restoration of comprehensive services for children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in facilities in 13 states and in community-based programmes in 12 states ensuring uninterrupted services to children and women even during the periods of shocks and stresses. In the 12 UNICEF focus states, protection, promotion and support of breastfeeding and complementary feeding was delivered through home visits, adjusted small group meetings, telephone, social media and other digital platforms. In eight states, 300 largest maternity and Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counselling centres in public health facilities were strengthened to ensure continuity of breastfeeding during the COVID-19 pandemic.
UNICEF worked with state and local governments in implementing expanded social protection programmes on food security, maternity benefits, rural works programmes and humanitarian cash transfers, reaching 449,912 households including vulnerable children.  UNICEF built evidence and advocated for effective policy response for vulnerable internal migrants through portable social protection for women and children and supported registries to deliver emergency cash transfers for migrant families.
In Bihar UNICEF facilitated establishing a Centre of Excellence in Disaster Management and Inter- Agency coordination mechanism in place  in six districts for unified preparedness and response. District Climate Action Plan initiated in the district of Gaya. Formulated Lightning Prevention and Management guideline for the state. Trained14246 Focal Teachers (F4592, M 9654) from elementary schools including Govt., Private, Madrassa on Comprehensive School Safety and Security. Contents developed on gender equitable and differential gender risks for integrating in Chief Minister School Safety Program.
In 17 Prog. states, capacity of line-departments and Partners, strengthened through advocacy, technical assistance and training on risk-informed programming and Emergency Preparedness. E.g. in Bihar22868 personnel (F 14654, M 8214) including frontline functionaries, Youths and CSOs trained on DRR, Climate change and EPR. UNICEF advocacy led to allocation of USD 4.59 million for FY 2021-22 for School Safety programme by Education Department. 
School safety programme (a collaboration between DRR, Education, WASH, CP, Health, ..), reaching children in more than 145,000 schools in 10 states with harmonised programme elements such as safe-Saturday, a peer-to-peer learning programme enabling learning of life-saving knowledge and skills for children.
UNICEF Bihar supported safe school reopening through technical assistance in the preparation of SOPs, guidelines and SBCC materials. About 1246 children in schools are availing the benefits of soap bank, Pad bank and mask banks, created by children through voluntary contributions in the schools. To ensure the schools are ready for reopening, UNICEF Hyderabad conducted training for over 2000 teachers with the support of APHRDI.GIDM with UNICEF technical support developed an e-course on school safety that includes safe school reopening and protocols for COVID prevention.

planEntities.description:
During 2021, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) strategies were developed and rolled out to inform and engage communities to adopt COVID-19 Appropriate Behaviours (CAB). The interventions addressed vaccine hesitancy and misinformation especially among vulnerable communities and hard to reach areas, contributing to building trust in vaccines and limiting vaccine hesitancy. 
RCCE continues to be the main pillar in UNICEF pandemic response across states focusing on those furthest left behind particularly the marginalized communities to adopt COVID-19 appropriate behaviour (CAB and CAB plus). States supported with community engagement mechanism (RCCE for emergency preparedness and climate change) to create demand for community led DRR interventions and create safe behaviour and positive social norms
UNICEF supported the mapping and training of 2500 NGOs and Civil Society Organizations that are actively engaged in community engagement on COVID Appropriate Behaviour (CAB) and vaccine demand generation. A cadre of over 265,000 village and ward volunteers of the Government of Andhra Pradesh involved at the household level were trained on social mobilization on COVID-19 specific and sensitive issues. In Gujarat, a youth led campaign was designed by UNICEF to promote CAB Plus and vaccination.
In Odisha, UNICEF supported the Department of Health and Family Welfare to train members of the Indian Association of Pediatrics and the Indian Medical Association to dispel myths around vaccination and advocate on issues related to CAB Plus practices. Over 600,000 people across 14 districts were reached on CAB and vaccination through edutainment methods using mobile vans with trained drivers and facilitators. 
Targeted campaigns by 1,300 temporary social mobilisers, 297 consultants and over 500,000 frontline workers, CSOs and youth have helped more than 76-million people adopt CAB and access vaccination. As part of the response, non-traditional and new community partnerships (65 nos. - combining national and state level) have supported vaccine promotion efforts in 460 districts. 
UNICEF engaged with faith leaders, traditional healers, academia, cooperative societies, associations, women and youth groups, community radio stations through numerous platforms in urban and rural areas through partnerships;  cross sector coordination efforts helped amplify the messages to hard-to-reach areas, helping over 75 million people, including 5 million tribal minorities, to adopt safe practices and access vaccines.
Engaging face-to-face with communities was limited due to movement restrictions and other pandemic containment measures. This limited the number of sessions planned by partners with communities. Multimedia campaigns supported as part of the COVID-19 response were able reach communities with information instead of also engaging them.  Quickly evolving situations required quick changes in response mechanisms. Addressing rumours, vaccine eagerness amongst some groups and hesitancy in others required distinct communication approaches. Youth were engaged to contain rumours floating through social media, whereas in many states, house visits by frontline functionaries were used to motivate people to come for vaccination camps for maximizing coverage.

planEntities.parentName: Output 5.1.1 - Effective institutional, legislative and policy frameworks in place to enhance sustainable environment and natural resource management and implementation of climate change and disaster risk reduction at national and sub-national levels.
planEntities.description:
Amidst continued high prevalence of the COVID-19 pandemic UNICEF  has  set  out  disaster-risk  reduction,  climate  change  and pandemic  management as its priorities. Working closely with the government and its partners UNICEF support in building capacities of local governance (urban/rural) for localization of preparedness has resulted in strengthening  resilience  of  children  and  reduced  disruptions  in services delivery. UNICEF supported state offices and government counterparts to develop multisectoral emergency preparedness for response plan to address shocks and stress, cyclone preparedness for Gujarat, West Bengal and Odisha, flood response plans for Assam, Bihar, Kerala, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh. UNICEF supported the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) and  State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) across states with extensive technical support to develop child sensitive Disaster Management Plan. Uttar Pradesh is spearheading evidence-based preparedness & response planning as part of system strengthening at the State Integrated Disaster Control Centre (SIDCC). A framework has been developed to train affected population to give feedback on development and disaster issues. Climate and hazard risks are integrated into the Gram Panchayat Development Plans.
UNICEF extended technical support to 12 state Governments to set up GO-NGO coordination and building capacity of 2000 NGOs, in various states and  for Covid-19 management and humanitarian works. These organizations were trained on Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Actions, an on multi-sectoral risk informed planning. The key sectors such as WASH, Health, Education, Child Protection, Inclusive Social Policy, C4D and CAP were engaged to integrate risk informed planning in their respective sectors.

planEntities.description:
The YuWaah Skills Platform (YSP) was initiated in the wake of the pandemic, as an e-learning solution to empower youth with skills and abilities to thrive and connect them to opportunities in apprenticeship, entrepreneurship, employment and social impact. It is initiated under the global partnership of UNICEF, Generation Unlimited, and Microsoft and Accenture on the Passport to Earning initiative, supported by a learning management system hosted on the Microsoft Community Training (MCT) Platform. A tri-partite led Young Warrior NXT initiative was launched, that will deploy large-scale life skills delivery solutions to support 14-24-year-old youth with foundational life skills. It targets 5 million youth in 2022, through 10-12 projects in partnership with life skills practitioners.  Currently, seven pilots have been shortlisted with an approximate reach of 90,000. 
Additionally, a chatbot-based solution reached 0.2 million in 2021, with 11 life-skills learning activities in 12 languages. This was done in response to adolescents missing socio-emotional learning due to online classes.The Youth Innovation Platform (UNIsolve) enabled young people to access age-appropriate content and tools on how to employ design thinking and social innovation to identify, investigate and solve for hyperlocal problems to drive social impact.   
The #YoungWarrior campaign, a youth-led movement to combat COVID-19,  triggered 6.6 million actions from 4.3 million young people. Young people have taken up actions such as capacity building, creating safe spaces and performing various tasks on U-Report such as learning how to counter misinformation or registering for vaccinations. New partners such as the Central Board for Secondary Education, University Grants Commission, and All India Council for Technical Education were brought onboard. The campaign brought together more than 1300 partners including various other Government partners. 
To engage the more marginalized constituencies of young people who do not have access to internet-enabled devices, YuWaah is also piloting low-tech and no-tech channels for engagement.
Intensive Flood Preparedness campaign reached to 1.2 million people (F 0.57, M 0.63 million) in 1400 villages, significantly improved community’s preparedness to face floods, Community Feedback Mechanism established on flood preparedness, received feedback from 5395 respondents using Kobo collect tool. The framework for building capacities of affected population on providing feedback on issues related to development and disasters is being piloted in 6 hazard prone districts of UP. Results from this pilot are being used for designing a mechanism for reaching out to the affected population, sharing information, increasing participation of communities and building feedback systems.

planEntities.name: 5.1.1.7 - Advocate with National and State Governments to institutionalize risk informed programming principles across 5 sectors (Health, Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Child Protection)  ; build capacity and provide implementation support at various levels ( including Gram Panchayats)
planEntities.parentName: Output 5.1.1 - Effective institutional, legislative and policy frameworks in place to enhance sustainable environment and natural resource management and implementation of climate change and disaster risk reduction at national and sub-national levels.
planEntities.description:
UNICEF supported states to prioritize Risk Informed Programming for all the UNICEF priority sectors. The support included supporting the states to roll out Comprehensive School Safety Programme(CSSP),  enhancing capacities of departments and NGO/civil society partners to build resilience through CPiE framework, Child Protection in Schools through CSSSP & CBDRR, CCI safety security plans across UNICEF supported states. The support helped bring convergence in addressing Child Protection issues in emergencies such as ensuring Safety Security of Children at CCIs, Child friendly spaces in Flood/ Cyclone shelters, registration of missing children, tracking of child trafficking during and post disaster situations, even COVID 19 Pandemic situation. UNICEF assisted Education, CP, Nutrition and WASH section in conducting training of  government functionaries on EPR. Established Inter- Agency coordination mechanism across states for unified preparedness and response. UNICEF, through government systems and partner organizations  built capacity of  50,000 healthcare workers including counsellors, psychiatrists, Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs), and frontline workers across the country for supporting Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) during the  pandemic.
Shock responsive and risk Informed GPDPs (ISP) has been advocated in all the UNICEF supported states.  In Assam, intensive technical support has been provided to 101 GPs in Goalpara, Barpeta and Darrang (all aspirational districts) and 41 GPs in Dhemaji and Majuli (flood prone and tribal dominated) to include risk informed and shock responsive costed activities for children and women in preparation of GPDPs with active participation of children and women in the planning process. In the state of Bihar, training package on risk-informed programme integrated in the trainings organized by BSDMA and BIPARD, 242 Officers (F 38, M 204) trained in three days residential trainings. Assistance in establishing Centre of Excellence in Disaster Management in visioning exercise, annual planning and resource allocation, mobilized USD 700,000 for 2021-2022 from Disaster Management Department. UNICEF Chhattisgarh advocacy with the government led to cash transfer benefit to 17,677 migrant workers. Employment of more than 150 days to 42,397 FRA Families (initially it was for 100 days). Additionally, over 6000 migrant workers have been linked with social protection schemes, livelihood etc. as reported from 12 districts. About 2.6 Million women got work under the scheme (MGNREGA), which is 50.08%. of the total workers employed.
Supported State Government technically to develop communication materials and messages on CSSSP in consultation with C4D where DRR led the process of communication and resource materials development. CSSSP has also been piloted in 400 schools, whereas 382 Nodal Teachers and 102 Government Officials were trained on Comprehensive approach of School Safety. UNICEF extended technical support to state departments of education in the development of modules and guidance on safe school reopening of schools and Early Childhood Development centres along with continued advocacy for ensuring COVID-19 responsive behaviours. Seventeen  state governments utilized these protocols and guidelines in reopening schools and early childhood development centres safely in a phased manner.
Knowledge products were developed for children through comic books on 5 key hazards. Technical support extended for capacity building of state IAG institution & CSO network on CCC and EPRP, 60 CSO partners from 45 organizations were sensitized on Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian actions. Partnership with Indian Institute of Technology, Gandhinagar developed climate risk assessment and sectoral advisories towards preparedness planning and response actions.
With UNICEF’s support, eight states developed and implemented catch up and learning recovery programme to address and mitigate learning loss for 15.83 million children (48 per cent girls). Rajasthan’s accelerated learning programme led to addressing the learning loss of 4,500 children (55 per cent girls) in 140 remote locations through 140 Shiksha Sahayat (60 per cent women). In Maharashtra and Assam around 3.5 million children (48 per cent girls) benefitted from reading and literacy skills through respective state reading programmes. In Odisha, 78,000 children (46 per cent girls) in geographically remote areas were reached through 9,800 pre-service student teachers through an innovative, state led internship programme. 
UNICEF, with its development partners advocated for immediate restoration of comprehensive services for children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in facilities in 13 states and in community-based programmes in 12 states ensuring uninterrupted services to children and women even during the periods of shocks and stresses. In the 12 UNICEF focus states, protection, promotion and support of breastfeeding and complementary feeding was delivered through home visits, adjusted small group meetings, telephone, social media and other digital platforms. In eight states, 300 largest maternity and Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counselling centres in public health facilities were strengthened to ensure continuity of breastfeeding during the COVID-19 pandemic.
UNICEF worked with state and local governments in implementing expanded social protection programmes on food security, maternity benefits, rural works programmes and humanitarian cash transfers, reaching 449,912 households including vulnerable children.  UNICEF built evidence and advocated for effective policy response for vulnerable internal migrants through portable social protection for women and children and supported registries to deliver emergency cash transfers for migrant families.
In Bihar UNICEF facilitated establishing a Centre of Excellence in Disaster Management and Inter- Agency coordination mechanism in place  in six districts for unified preparedness and response. District Climate Action Plan initiated in the district of Gaya. Formulated Lightning Prevention and Management guideline for the state. Trained14246 Focal Teachers (F4592, M 9654) from elementary schools including Govt., Private, Madrassa on Comprehensive School Safety and Security. Contents developed on gender equitable and differential gender risks for integrating in Chief Minister School Safety Program.
In 17 Prog. states, capacity of line-departments and Partners, strengthened through advocacy, technical assistance and training on risk-informed programming and Emergency Preparedness. E.g. in Bihar22868 personnel (F 14654, M 8214) including frontline functionaries, Youths and CSOs trained on DRR, Climate change and EPR. UNICEF advocacy led to allocation of USD 4.59 million for FY 2021-22 for School Safety programme by Education Department. 
School safety programme (a collaboration between DRR, Education, WASH, CP, Health, ..), reaching children in more than 145,000 schools in 10 states with harmonised programme elements such as safe-Saturday, a peer-to-peer learning programme enabling learning of life-saving knowledge and skills for children.
UNICEF Bihar supported safe school reopening through technical assistance in the preparation of SOPs, guidelines and SBCC materials. About 1246 children in schools are availing the benefits of soap bank, Pad bank and mask banks, created by children through voluntary contributions in the schools. To ensure the schools are ready for reopening, UNICEF Hyderabad conducted training for over 2000 teachers with the support of APHRDI.GIDM with UNICEF technical support developed an e-course on school safety that includes safe school reopening and protocols for COVID prevention.

planEntities.name: Key Activity 1.1.2.2: Monitoring places of detention and prisons under the authority of the Ministry of Justice, formulating policy and legislative recommendations and provision of technical support to justice and law enforcement officials on prevention of torture, and advocacy with the Government to strengthen the integration of human rights in counter-terrorism measures and for preventing conflict and violent extremism.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 :  National institutions and mechanisms are supported to promote and advocate for more inclusive social cohesion and peace-building.
planEntities.description:
As part of its efforts to contribute to the United Nations objective of sustainable peace and security, OHCHR engaged in promoting human rights in the administration of justice to enhance measures for conflict prevention, building social cohesion and respect for the rule of law. For this purpose, OHCHR continued to implement its detention and trial monitoring programme particularly focused on observing the trials of ISIL suspects, to monitor compliance with procedural guarantees, detention safeguards and fair trial standards in Iraq.
During the period 1 January to 31 December 2023, OHCHR conducted XXXX visits to places of detention conducting at least XXXX detention monitoring interviews with XX male and XX female detainees and monitored the prison conditions in both the Federal Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.

planEntities.name: Key Activity 1.1.2.3: Monitoring and reporting of trials and advocacy on adherence to promote due process and fair trial standards in criminal courts, including juvenile courts, particularly for trials under the Anti-Terrorism Laws, and provision of technical assistance to and advocacy with government for reform of criminal justice law and policy.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 :  National institutions and mechanisms are supported to promote and advocate for more inclusive social cohesion and peace-building.
planEntities.description: As part of its efforts to contribute to the United Nations objective of sustainable peace and security, OHCHR engagement in promoting human rights in the administration of justice enhances measures for conflict prevention, building social cohesion and respect for the rule of law. For this purpose, OHCHR continued to implement its detention and trial monitoring programme particularly focused on observing the trials of ISIL suspects, to monitor compliance with procedural guarantees, detention safeguards and fair trial standards in Iraq. In 2023, OHCHR monitored XXXX trials in Iraq with the following breakdown: Baghdad (XXX), Bara (XX), Erbil (XX), Kirkuk (XX) and Mosul (XX); XX cases of domestic violence and XX civil cases in Baghdad related to violence against women; XX trials monitored at the Rusafa Juvenile Court; and XX anti-corruption trials.

planEntities.name: Key Activity 1.1.2.4: Documentation of the six grave child rights violations and analysis of patterns and trends and impact of violence and insecurity on children and support with the finalization of the Action Plan to stop and prevent the recruitment and use of children by the Popular Mobilization Forces, and reintegration of children released by armed actors
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 :  National institutions and mechanisms are supported to promote and advocate for more inclusive social cohesion and peace-building.
planEntities.description:
From 1 January to 31 December 2023, the United Nations verified XXXX grave violations against XXX children (XXX boys, XX girls) including the killing (XX) and maiming (XX) of XXX children (XX boys, XX girls), recruitment and use of XX children (XX boys, XX girls), abduction of XX children (X boys, X girls), and rape and other forms of sexual violence against (X girls), denial of humanitarian access (XX incident), and attacks on schools (X incidents). In addition, XX grave violations against XX children (X boys, X girls), which occurred in previous years, were verified in 2023. The violations were attributed to PKK (XX), ISIL (XX), and Iraqi Security Forces (XX). XX violations were unattributed as they resulted from Explosive Remnants of War (ERW) and Improvised Explosive Devices (XX), unknown armed penetrators (XX) and crossfire (XX). ERW was the leading cause of child casualties (XX), ground engagement (XX) and airstrikes (XX). The violations occurred in Anbar (X), Babil (X), Baghdad (XX), Basra (XX), Dahok (XX), Diyala (XX), Erbil (X), Kirkuk (XX), Maysan (X), Muthana (X), Nasiryiah (X), Ninewa XX), Salah Al-Din (Xx), and Sulaymaniyah (XX).

On 26 June, the CTFMR delivered a child protection skills and knowledge-based training, benefiting 40 personnel from various departments of the Popular Mobilization Forces to support the implementation of the action plan to prevent the recruitment and use of children and  institutionalize the protection for children in Iraq. UNAMI and UNICEF joint engagement and training, on 20 June, led to the establishment of the Human Rights Directorate within the PMF with the objective to promote the protection for children and promote  human rights values and standards within the PMF.

On 23 July, UNAMI jointly with jointly with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement, Ministry of Interior and Office of the National Security Advisor, UNICEF and other international organizations conducted a mission to Jeddah 1 Rehabilitation Centre to assess the situation and services being provided to children returning from the Al Hol camp in Northeast Syria.

Following the visit to Iraq from 12 to 24 November 2002, by a three-member delegation of the United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances, the Committee adopted a full report of the visit at its 24th session in Geneva in March 2023.
Further details will be shared towards the end of December 2023.

planEntities.parentName: Output  3.1.1 : National and sub national information management and research systems increase the generation, analysis and dissemination of quality and timely disaggregated data essential for evidence-based service delivery
planEntities.description: UNESCO, UNICEF and WFP to support the government to establish an effective Education Management Information System (EMIS) . This tool will facilitate the availability of relevant, timely and critical education data that will be important for evidence-based planning and decision making at national, directorate and school level resulting in more effective delivery of services. This data will also be crucial in informing education development partners of areas in need of support in assisting the government to improve the education sector. UNESCO is the leading organization on the development of the EMIS system at central level and UNICEF and WFP will lead in the downstream part of the project with trainings at Director of Education and school level. WFP support will be focusing on the development of the School Feeding Module as part of the broader EMIS system and ensuring EMIS will be deployed in all the schools under the School Feeding programme.

planEntities.description:
Progress towards the achievement of the Result:
The security environment in Iraq remained fragile and protection of civilians continued to be a concern particularly in the context of security incidents resulting involving armed groups or pro-government militias. HRO monitored and documented security related incidents, harm to civilians and protection concerns From 1 January to 10 December 2020, HRO documented 458 security related incidents that resulted in 514 civilian casualties [198 deaths (including 15 women, 17 children, and 316 injuries (including 22 women, 46 children)], representing a 43 per cent decrease compared to the same period in 2019. UNAMI attributed 72 per cent civilian casualties to ISIL remnants in Iraq, 22 per cent to unknown armed groups, 5 per cent to Turkish forces, five per cent to pro-Government forces and the remaining one per cent to other armed actors, including pro-Government militias. Of the total, 36 per cent civilian casualties were caused by Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs), 36 per cent by small arms fire, 10 per cent by the use of indirect fire (mortars), 5 per cent by air strikes and the remaining 13 per cent in explosive remnants of war or unexploded ordnance (UXOs), hand grenades and summary executions. Turkish military air strikes targeting the positions of PKK elements in the northern Iraq remained a concern as these air strikes also resulted in civilian casualties and/or caused damage to civilian property.
The Country Task Force on Monitoring and Reporting (CTFMR) documented 29 grave violations against children, affecting a total 20 children 17 girls and 3 boys (8 use of military schools in Kirkuk governorate and Salah al Din governorates, 11 abductions- late verification-, 7 cases of sexual violence (all girls), 1 case of recruitment and use of a boy, 1 case of attack on hospital and 1 case of denial of humanitarian access. On 2 May 2020, during a military operation against ISIL in the district of Yathrib, Salah al Dine Governorate, a boy used in the Popular Mobilization Forces was killed by an ISIL sniper and his body transferred to a local hospital.
HRO, jointly with UNICEF and Office of the SRSG Children and Armed Conflict, engaged with the Government of Iraq to finalize the National Action Plan on the recruitment and use of children and support their rehabilitation and reintegration. The support and technical assistance by UNAMI aligned the draft action plan with international standards. HRO , jointly with UNICEF and Justice Rapid Response, an international non-governmental organization, implemented a training programme for members of the CTFMR aimed at strengthening capacity of members of the Task Force for documentation of the child rights violations and to identify and address challenges faced in promoting protection for children. The workshop also launched a peer network as a continued exchange platform to strengthen the child protection framework in Iraq. HRO continue monitoring and reporting on the protection of civilians, including on the six gave child rights violations, provision of technical advice and support to the Government of Iraq to promote measures for the protection of civilians and the implementation of the Action Plan for the implementation of on the recruitment and use of children.

UNAMI and UNICEF Co-Chair the CTFMR in Iraq.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.1 Gender-and-age sensitive protection and social protection services are progressively expanded to include all persons in Iraq.
planEntities.description:
In summer 2019, WFP conducted formative research across Iraq to gain an in-depth understanding of people’s lives, attitudes, beliefs, habits, and practices around nutrition-related behaviours. Based on the research findings, in early 2020 workshops were held with ministry representatives, key stakeholders, national NGOs, UN agencies, and practitioners working in Iraq to prioritise the behaviours which are currently contributing to the high rate of obesity, overweight and micronutrient deficiency. 
 For each of the prioritised behaviours, WFP will work with partners to develop effective social behaviour change interventions and communication activities. To achieve sustainable behaviour change, WFP is drawing on advances within the behavioural science field to develop a series of interventions to support positive behaviour change, create new habit cues, and encourage social commitment.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.48 - Strengthening Border Management and Security Practices at Points of Entry in Aqaba Governorate
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Improved Service Delivery for Human Capital Development and Poverty Reduction: Public Services in Health, Education, Social Protection, and Food and Nutrition Security have improved quality and are more accessible to vulnerable groups
planEntities.description:
IOM will support the Government of Jordan in their efforts to strengthen border management and security practices at Points of Entry (PoE) in Aqaba Governorate, and for Border Authorities to adhere to international standards and best practices for combatting transitional organized crime and terrorism at PoE while ensuring the continuity of cross-border traffic. The proposed interventions targets some of the country’s key PoE, focusing on the Seaport, the main land Border Crossing Point (BCP) and the international airport in Aqaba Governorate, the former being the principal PoE for commercial goods and travelers, and also situated alongside a regional drug-trade route, having seen regular seizures of trafficked drugs and other illicit goods in recent years.
Concretely, IOM will enhance the capacity of the Jordanian Border Authorities, namely the General Intelligence Department (GID), Borders and Residence Department (BRD), Jordan Customs and Anti-Narcotics Department (AND) by providing or upgrading technical equipment for enhanced border security and inspection, such as document verification devices, UV lights, magnifiers, etc. and based on identified needs, infrastructure for interview rooms, etc. IOM will also be supporting the development of protocols and operating procedures, based on identified needs and gaps, and by training frontline officers on key security elements of border management, such as identity documentation, risk analysis, and modus operandi of organized transnational crimes and terrorist groups in the region. The interventions will draw from IOM’s expertise in Integrated Border Management and Identity Management and Biometrics, while closely coordinating with other International Organizations, such as UNODC and ICMPD, to ensure that targeted interventions do not overlap with the ongoing activities of these actors but reinforce and is coherent with ongoing efforts to support the Government of Jordan in moving towards an Integrated Border Management system.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.49 - Mainstreaming COVID-19 Response into Humanitarian Border Management in Jordan
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Improved Service Delivery for Human Capital Development and Poverty Reduction: Public Services in Health, Education, Social Protection, and Food and Nutrition Security have improved quality and are more accessible to vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: Responding to the urgent need of the Jordanian Armed Forces (JAF) and Jordanian Royal Medical Services (RMS) to enhance response capacity to sufficiently be able to meet challenges related to the COVID-19 pandemic: to protect and reduce the risks of COVID-19 transmission for those crossing borders during emergencies, while ensuring that the security at border crossings is maintained. IOM will build the capacity of frontline officers at the North Eastern border lines to manage the border incorporating necessary health border and mobility management practices during the COIVD-19 crisis, while also enhancing infrastructural capacity, such as accommodation facility/ies equipped with solar panels, personal protective equipment (PPE) and other equipment as needed, and dedicated spaces for female officers which will also allow the JAF to increase the number of deployed female officers

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.50 -  Enhancing the Capacity of Jordan’s Border Authorities to Respond to COVID-19 and Mitigate its Socioeconomic Impact
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Improved Service Delivery for Human Capital Development and Poverty Reduction: Public Services in Health, Education, Social Protection, and Food and Nutrition Security have improved quality and are more accessible to vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: In light of the COVID-19 pandemic and its repercussions, this intervention aims to enhance the capacity of Jordan’s BA and the MoH to limit the spread of COVID-19 and the scope of the public health crisis, while also preventing the interruption of supply chains that border closures would cause, thereby mitigating the pandemic’s socioeconomic impact on Jordan.  This will be achieved by supporting BA with appropriate infrastructure and equipment, including Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), while also training staff present at Points of Entry (PoE) to screen, detect and safely handle, isolate, and refer suspected cases of COVID-19 and other communicable diseases, in line with IOM’s Health Border and Mobility Management (HBMM) framework.

planEntities.name: 2.1.3.11 - Providing Access to Basic Needs Assistance, Protection and Transportation Services for refugees in Jordan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.3 - Provision of Life-saving services: Basic needs of refugees and asylum-seekers are met
planEntities.description:
The objective of the project is to address priority needs identified in coordination with partners and building on previous support from PRM for the refugee response in Jordan, IOM’s planned interventions for 2021-2022 are grouped under the following three outcomes: 
- Outcome 1: Vulnerable refugees outside camps are better able to meet their basic needs. 
- Outcome 2: Enhanced protection of vulnerable refugees and strengthened sectoral coordination on gender-based violence risk mitigation.
- Outcome 3: Refugees in Jordan have access to safe and dignified transportation for family reunification, documentation needs, and exceptional support for spontaneous returns to Syria.

planEntities.description: LoCAL aims to promote climate change–resilient communities and economies by increasing financing for and investment in climate change adaptation at the local level in LDCs and other countries. LoCAL combines performance-based climate resilience grants (PBCRGs), which ensure programming and verification of climate change expenditures at the local level, with technical and capacity-building support. It is designed to re-enforce existing national and sub-national financial and fiscal delivery systems, and it uses the demonstration effect to trigger further flows for local adaptation — including national fiscal transfers and global climate finance for local authorities — through their central governments.​

This four-year project will increase institutional and technical capacity of stakeholders; develop climate information systems for prioritizing adaptation needs; mainstream climate change adaptation into social and economic development planning; and strengthen the capacity to monitor, review and report the National Adaptation Planning process in the country.

planEntities.name: 4.1.08 Montreal Protocol Compliance Assistance Programme
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Green Growth
planEntities.description: UNEP is the implementing agency for 4 projects funded under the Montreal Protocol Multilateral Fund. Activities include enforcement of licensing system, capacity building of government and private sector, development of standards and policies for low-GWP and flammable alternatives, certification of servicing technicians to sustain HCFC phase-out and preparation of HFC phase-down  strategy and implementation plan.

planEntities.name: 4.3.13 Building resilience of urban populations with ecosystems-based solution in Lao PDR
planEntities.parentName: 4.3 Resilience

planEntities.name: 4.1.18 Strengthening Lao PDR's institutional capacity to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Green Growth
planEntities.description: Strengthen Lao PDR's national capacity to track progress against actions identified in its NDC for domestic and international reporting requirements under the Enhanced Transparency Framework of the Paris Agreement.

planEntities.name: 4.1.22 Enabling Activities for the Preparation of Initial Biennial Transparency Report (BTR1) under the United Nations Framework  Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Green Growth

Lao People's Democratic Republic.name: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation
Lao People's Democratic Republic.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: 1.3.06 Capacity Development for Education (CapED) in Lao PDR: Capacity Development Support for Teacher Education in Lao PDR
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description:
"This sub-output aims to improve the quality, inclusiveness and gender responsiveness of teacher education and professional development, from early childhood to secondary education, in Lao PDR.

At the system level, it supports the development and implementation of the National Teacher Policy, professional standards and competency frameworks, including ICT-AI competencies, and strengthens teacher development and management systems. At the institutional level, it strengthens pre- and in-service teacher education through institutional capacity development, integration of gender-responsive and inclusive pedagogies into curricula and teaching practices, and capacity development of teachers, teacher educators and student teachers in gender equality, inclusion and diversity, and digital competencies."

planEntities.name: 1.3.07 Capacity Development for Education (CapED) in Lao PDR: Education Response to the COVID-19 Crisis
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description:
The CapED COVID-19 programme is aimed at supporting the MoES to enhance teachers' capacities in applying mixed-mode/blended approach and technologies to ensure the continuity of learning and the quality of pedagogy that is innovative and engaging, with a view to strengthening its education system to be more inclusive and resilient to crises. The main interventions are 
(1) Development of national capacity on blended learning modalities for teacher education in response to COVID-19 school closures and beyond, and 
(2) Enhancement of digital resilience through competency-based teacher training reforms to facilitate ICT-pedagogy integration

planEntities.name: 1.3.08 Technical Advice and capacity development to promote education for sustainable development to achieve SDG 4.7 through developing Education for Sustainable Development Country initiative  from 2022 to 2030;
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description: Techncial advice to implement the ESD Road Map to develop country level initiative on ESD in Lao PDR. -	The “Education Strategy to 2025, Vision to 2030 and Education and Sports Development Plan ESSDP (2016-2020) and (2021-2025), issued by the MOES, recognizes the need for “Sustainable Development” Even though, Laos doesn’t have obvious policies related to Education for Sustainable Development (ESD); however in many of the government policy documents such in National Social-Economic Development Plan and the Party resolution, the government tries to address ESD. A priority for MOES is to integrate ESD into curriculum and learning and teaching process.

planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Health
planEntities.description: Comprehensive SRHR package is integrated in Universal Health Coverage scheme. Strengthened capacity for implementation of evidence-based comprehensive SRHR policies, programmes and plans. Strengthened regulatory frameworks and education of professional midwives for improved quality of services across the development and humanitarian continuum.

planEntities.name: 1.2.03 Strengthened capacity of health providers to deliver high quality integrated comprehensive sexual and reproductive health information and services for all, with a focus on women and in priority districts, in particular for those in conditions of greater vulnerability, across humanitarian and development continuum
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Health
planEntities.description: Strengthened capacity of health care providers to provide good quality, integrated sexual and reproductive health information and services in health facilities and through telehealth modality, to all, including to adolescents and youth and the most vulnerable groups such as sex workers, people with disability, and those living in hard to reach areas.

planEntities.name: Strengthened national policies and institutional frameworks to support implementation of the National Rural Employment Strategy (NRES), including coordination with other relevant national strategies.

planEntities.name: 3.5.02 Strengthened capacities of the Lao Statistics Bureau and selected ministries to produce and utilize population data for planning and monitoring of the National Social-Economic Development Plan, sectoral plans, ICPD Programme of Action and the Sustainable Development Goals, including in humanitarian preparedness and response.
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 Public Administration Reform and Data Driven Governance
planEntities.description: Provide technical and financial support the government, especially LSB and line ministries to have capacity to conduct and produce high quality disaggregated  population data such as 5th population and housing census 2025 and other surveys(LSIS III) and CRVS data for monitoring and formulation of national, sectors and provincial plans as well as ICPD PoA and SDGs.

Lao People's Democratic Republic.name: United Nations Children's Fund
Lao People's Democratic Republic.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: 1.1.03 Child Protection Enabling Environment
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Protection
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to create an enabling environment conducive to the protection of children. UNICEF will adopt different strategies to strengthen the child protection system, including supporting legislative reform and policy engagement, evidence generation, strategy formulation, planning and coordination, developing and leveraging resource and partnerships with ministries, CSOs, UN, academia, and development and private sector partners to implement and monitor the National Plan of Action for Child Protection System Strengthening 2022-2026 and the National Plan of Action for Violence against Children 2021-2025 and strengthen M&E systems in order to inform planning and decision-making.

planEntities.name: 1.1.04 Systems Capacity For Delivery Of Quality Child Protection Prevention And Response Services
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Protection
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to accelerate the development of the social service workforce and their professionalization, capacity building and operationalization, as well as service delivery, including basic service provision at village level and tailored supports available at national and sub-national level (case management, MHPSS counsellling, rehabilitation, recovery, etc.) to address multiple protection issues, such as violence against children, child sexual exploitation abuse (including online), child marriage, etc. UNICEF will also create and strengthen multi-sectoral partnerships for greater coverage and coordinated implementation with allied sectors such as health, education, justice, information and communication, social welfare and social protection.

planEntities.name: 1.1.05 Knowledge, Skills And Practices – Protection And Harmful Practices
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Protection
planEntities.description: The sub-aim of the output is to provide parents and caregivers, as primary duty bearers, as well as children as rights holders, with the knowledge, skills, agencies and abilities along with a supportive community environment, to reject harmful practices (i.e. chlid marriage, child labour, corporal punishment, etc.), build on positive social norms, and adopt positive attitudes and practices (including birth registration) that protect children and reduce their risks and vulnerabilities. Activities include parenting education, adolescent social and life skills training, community mobilization, etc.

planEntities.name: 1.2.23 Primary Health Care Enabling Environment
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Health
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to improve capacity of health workers at national and subnational levels to increase accountability to develop quality of health legistlatation, planning and budgeting.

planEntities.name: 1.2.24 Systems Capacity for Delivery of Quality Primary Health Care
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Health
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to improve system capacity to provide direct service provision in targeted locations, expanding the coverage of quality primary health care complemented by a more resilient and sustainable community health approach, with special attention paid to underserved communities.

planEntities.name: 1.2.25 Health Knowledge, Skills and Practices
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Health
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to increase knowledge and skills among male and female caregivers to practice appropriate childcare, hygiene, feeding and early stimulation, as well as to demand quality services.

planEntities.name: 1.3.03 Education And Learning Enabling Environment
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to strengthen the enabling environment of the sector by ensuring there is capacity at national and sub-national levels to better plan, manage, coordinate, resource and monitor to improve sector performance. It also aims to ensure that the education system is resilient and effectively responds to emergencies.

planEntities.name: 1.3.04 Systems Capacity For Delivery Of Quality Early Childhood And Basic Education
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to strengthen the capacity of the MoES and key education service providers to support schools effectively and efficiently deliver quality education. It aims to ensure that schools have sufficient, qualified and committed teachers and school leaders; and that children have a conducive learning environment; and that there is effective monitoring of student learning outcomes with teachers equipped with knowledge and skills to provide immediate support to children lagging behind so that children, including adolescents complete the full cycle of basic education and are learning optimally.

planEntities.name: 2.3.08 Design and implementation of Cash transfers program for households with children living with disabilities in Lao PDR.
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Social Protection
planEntities.description: Design and implementation of Cash transfers program for households with children living with disabilities in Lao PDR.

planEntities.name: 2.3.09 Support the development of a comprehensive shock responsive age appropriate, welfare inclusive and disability sensitive social protection policy for Lao PDR.
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Social Protection
planEntities.description: Support the development of a comprehensive shock responsive age appropriate, welfare inclusive and disability sensitive social protection policy for Lao PDR.

planEntities.name: 2.3.10 Capacity building for government stakeholders on Humanitarian cash transfers and preparedness.
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Social Protection
planEntities.description: Capacity building for government stakeholders on Humanitarian cash transfers and preparedness.

planEntities.name: 3.1.03 Children and youth are aware of their rights and their soft skills are built in order for them to actively promote child rights related issues  (child marriage, early pregnancy, violence against children, education, nutrition, WASH, immunization, etc) through different platforms.
planEntities.parentName: 3.1 Civic Space and Participation
planEntities.description:
UNICEF interventions in this area will build children, adolescents and youth skills and child rights understanding in order for them to be engaged in discussions on issues important for them and take an active role in those areas, participating in different platforms. Civic engagement will be promoted through different interventions: 
- Capacity building of young people and youth media groups
- Peer-to-peer support network for the youth media groups in 18 provinces to help boost performance.
- Provision of platforms, including radio and digital platforms, for youth participation in priority provinces.
- Monitoring and evaluation of youth participation activities 
- Support for content creation including equipment

planEntities.name: 3.1.04 Provide child protection preventive services and promote child participation, including awareness-raising, adolescents life skills training, parenting education, community mobilization, etc.
planEntities.parentName: 3.1 Civic Space and Participation
planEntities.description:
Promotion of child and youth participation through:
- Provision of platforms for youth participation as active citizens
- Content Creation for and with youth

planEntities.name: 1.3.05 Household - Learning, Knowledge Skills And Practices
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to ensure that children, including adolescents and their families have access to the right information and programmes to enhance their knowledge and skills to demand for, and to contribute to improving the quality of education. Demand creation for quality education and beneficiary’s participation is key output which ensure the right knowledge and information to support children’s learning and overall development for them to help monitor delivery of quality schooling. It also aims to ensure that parents and caregivers –have the knowledge, skills, resources and commitment for a nurturing home environment for quality early childhood and basic education.

planEntities.name: 3.5.04 Data, Evidence, PFM And Planning For Children
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 Public Administration Reform and Data Driven Governance
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to contribute to an enabling environment for the wellbeing of the child by better positioning of children’s concerns, especially those of the most vulnerable children in public policies. This will be done by strengthening national capacity at national and sub-national levels to routinely generate disaggregated data and evidence on the situation of children, to use it for relevant analyses to inform the design of inclusive public policies and programmes and to monitor progress toward the implementation of national and subnational policies and strategies.

planEntities.name: 4.3.19 Government Capacity To Mitigate Natural Disaster And Climate Risks To Children
planEntities.parentName: 4.3 Resilience
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to strengthen capacity of government counterpart to implement disaster risk reduction (DRR) strategies and climate mitigation and adaptation, emergency preparedness and response, integrating behaviour change into health outreach programmes, equitable cost recovery and financing, developing multisectoral strategies and sectoral coordination.

planEntities.name: 1.4.05 Multisectoral Nutrition Enabling Environment
planEntities.parentName: 1.4 Nutrition and food security
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to improve good governance for nutrition, coordination of interventions as well as the adequate investment in nutrition through provide capacity development of the institution and administrative system for supporting accountability of governmental, civic and private sectors towards the provision of equitable quality nutrition services for children, adolescents and women. It will ensure transparency and accountability for prioritization, coordination and convergence of investments for nutrition across the life cycle and key five sectors will results in greater efficiencies.

planEntities.name: 1.4.06 Systems Capacity For Delivery Of Convergent Nutrition Services
planEntities.parentName: 1.4 Nutrition and food security
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance capacity in the five key systems – food, health, water and sanitation, education, and social protection – to deliver multiple, convergent, quality services across the lifespan. This involves leveraging human, technical, and financial resources from state, private, civic and academia entities operating within the five key systems to make them more responsive to improving the diets, services and practices for infants, children, adolescents, pregnant women and mothers across development and emergency contexts.

planEntities.name: 1.4.07 Nutrition And Care Knowledge, Skills And Practices
planEntities.parentName: 1.4 Nutrition and food security
planEntities.description: This sub-output will focus on conducting formative research on behaviour drivers, gender role analysis and channels, to inform delivery of SBCC for nutrition Strategy; Develop and provide package of essential nutrition SBCC messages adapted to needs of four major ethnic groups; and disseminate messages to target beneficiaries by group.

planEntities.name: 1.5.03 WASH Enabling Environment
planEntities.parentName: 1.5 Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH)
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to  strengthen capacity of Government technical, communication, regulatory, financial and planning for better deliver national WASH activities through improve the quality, resilience and sustainability of WASH services.

planEntities.name: 1.5.04 Systems Capacity For Delivery Of WASH In Communities And Institutions
planEntities.parentName: 1.5 Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH)
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to support Government to develop resilient, sustainable water supply designs, and work with government and the private sector to ensure that there are affordable, resilient, sustainable household sanitation designs and to assess the potential to make affordable household water treatment and MHM supplies of suitable quality available, even in remote communities.

planEntities.name: 1.5.05 WASH Knowledge Skills And Practices
planEntities.parentName: 1.5 Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH)
planEntities.description: 'This sub-output aims to strengthen capacity of beneficiaries to improve skills and knowledge to enhance their WASH practices, particularly in rural and poor urban areas through evidence based to inform communication approaches.

planEntities.description: Designing and piloting a Mother and Early Childhood Grant for 2000 beneficiaries in 3 districts.

The proposed UNIDO/GEF project focuses on promoting the use of solid biofuel for energy generation replacing coal usage. This area was selected due to its rapid scaling up and GHG emission reduction potential. These are in line with GEF-5 climate change focal area strategic programme CCM-3: Promoting the investment in RE technologies.

planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Green Growth

To facilitate the implementation of the Stockholm Convention on POPs in respect of sound management of PCBs and PCB-containing equipment and wastes including development of specific legislations, implementation of environmentally sound management practices, inventory, testing, labeling of at least 1000
electrical equipment and disposal/decontamination of 250 tones of PCB-containing equipment and wastes.

planEntities.name: 4.1.12 Demonstration of BAT and BEP in open burning activities in response to the Stockholm Convention on POPs
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 Green Growth
planEntities.description:
To create resource efficient  waste management systemsto reduce U-POPs emissionsthrough the introduction BAT/BEP in open burning sources. The aim of the project is to achieve sustainable release reduction of unintentionally produced-POPs (UP-POPs) in the open burning sector through the introduction of BAT and BEP

Regional programme (Cambodia, Lao PDR, Mongolia, Philippines and Vietnam)

planEntities.description: Provide capacity building, through a programme of training events, to enhance institutional compliance with internationally accepted best practice in the field of addressing AML/CFT, and to provide mentoring to improve the implementation and effectiveness of the aforementioned best practice by stakeholders (including the Office of the Supreme People's Prosecutor).

planEntities.name: 3.4.06 Precursor Control

planEntities.name: 3.4.07 Container Control
planEntities.parentName: 3.4 Transnational Organised Crime
planEntities.description: To enhance capacities to profile containers for inspection.

planEntities.name: 3.4.08 Wildlife Crime
planEntities.parentName: 3.4 Transnational Organised Crime
planEntities.description: To build capacities of law enforcement agencies to combat wildlife crime.

planEntities.name: 3.4.09 Enhanced data availability.
