planEntities.name: 1.1.1.45 - UNIDO: Mongolia Export Development Project: Strengthening certification services to enhance export competitiveness of small and medium agribusinesses
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - Development visions, strategies and plans that integrate the SDGs and are focused on poverty reduction, inclusive growth, economic diversification and resilience at the national and local level (including supporting evidence based policy making, and collecting and analyzing sex- and other types of disaggregated data to inform impact analysis of these policies on specific population groups).
planEntities.description: This project aims to build capacities of certification services for the agri-export products which addressed by several service modules of UNIDO and pilot those on selected sectors and SMEs. Accordingly, UNIDO envisions a programmatic approach for development of export product certification services which contain relevant components from UNIDO’s Food Safety Approach as well as non-food related agri-products, such as textile or leather. The key objective of the MoFALI-WBG-UNIDO project is to support Mongolian small and medium-size enterprises (SMEs) in the non-mining sectors to strengthen their export capabilities and expand access to export markets through enhancement of a Mongolian pool of local experts engaged in international certification-related services (training, coaching, mentoring and auditing) on selected export products and SME certification. The expected project outcomes related to the support of standard-setting, training of practitioners and coaching of SMEs on required changes as per product certification will be piloting in nature. The competences of Mongolian experts along with the institutional capacities of public, private and NGO service providers  will be strengthened to support the sustainability of the intervention, where UNIDO will assess current capacities and needs, translate relevant materials for female and male industry practitioners and conduct the training sessions on relevant ISO standards and food and non-food certification schemes, including wide usage of blended learning and practical training. In addition, the project will support the application process of international affiliation related to various product certification scheme for food and non-food products. Finally, UNIDO will supervise the delivery of developed advisory and auditing services to the industry.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.46 - UNIDO: Strategic cooperation framework between UNIDO and the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry of Mongolia 2021-2025
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - Development visions, strategies and plans that integrate the SDGs and are focused on poverty reduction, inclusive growth, economic diversification and resilience at the national and local level (including supporting evidence based policy making, and collecting and analyzing sex- and other types of disaggregated data to inform impact analysis of these policies on specific population groups).
planEntities.description:
Director General’s approval-in-principle to develop a Strategic Cooperation Framework (SCF) for 20212-2025, between  UNIDO and MOFALI came in response to the letter of the Minister of MOFALI, dated 1 July 2021, inviting UNIDO to consider the formulation of the SCF (see Annex 1). The Framework recognizes the cooperation between UNIDO and MoFALI since Mongolia become a UNIDO Member State in 1985, and the fruitful cooperation carried out since then in the fields of sustainable food, agriculture and light industrial development, which has made a positive contribution to Mongolia's sustainable development, particularly with regard to the industrial sector. The Framework recognizes the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted at the United Nations Summit in 2015, the Lima Declaration adopted at the fifteenth session of the UNIDO General Conference in 2013, as well as the Abu Dhabi Declaration adopted at the eighteenth session of the UNIDO General Conference in 2019 that welcomes UNIDO’s role in accelerating the achievement of SDG 9 along with all other industry-related goals of the 2030 Agenda with a primary objective to promote inclusive and sustainable industrial development (ISID) in its Member States.
The main objective of the Strategic Cooperation Framework (SCF) is to further strengthen the cooperation between MoFALI and UNIDO in the field of inclusive and sustainable industrial development (ISID) to advance the country’s capabilities in the food, agriculture and light industrial sectors. The SCF will define the broad areas of cooperation, based on UNIDO’s comparative advantages and Mongolia’s development priorities. The SCF is also expected to facilitate collaboration towards ISID, while contributing to the achievement of the SDGs and addressing issues of global concern, such as climate change and recovery from the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition, this Strategic Cooperation Framework (20212-2025) establishes priorities on which MoFALI and UNIDO agree to focus, and contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF), using UNIDO’s four main enabling functions of technical cooperation analytical and research functions and policy advisory services, normative functions and standards and quality-related activities, as well as convening and partnerships for knowledge transfer, networking and industrial cooperation.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.47 -  UNIDO: Assessment of the economic potential of disseminating modern sheep shearing technology and its training curriculum development
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - Development visions, strategies and plans that integrate the SDGs and are focused on poverty reduction, inclusive growth, economic diversification and resilience at the national and local level (including supporting evidence based policy making, and collecting and analyzing sex- and other types of disaggregated data to inform impact analysis of these policies on specific population groups).
planEntities.description:
UNIDO is a key partner with the Light Industry Department of MOFALI and is helping to coordinate the expansion of modern sheep wool supply chains in the country working with all stakeholders. 
The proposed Small Grant project will be catalytic as an essential step to a National Shearing Campaign by MoFALI. An assessment of the economic potential of disseminating modern sheep shearing and wool processing practices will establish a baseline for better understanding the wool supply chain in developing the National Shearing Campaign of modern technology as code of best practice for business sustainability and job creation by scaling up a standardized competency-based practical training process for rapid improvement of the wool supply chain.
The purpose of this Project, within the larger Theory of Change is to: (a) conduct an assessment on improving the sustainability and employment opportunities of the wool value chain by adopting modern technology. (b) Develop a national curriculum and model-training programme for qualified sheep shearers in line with the standards of the Australian and New Zealand basic shearer qualifications and (c) provide the basis for MOFALI national shearing campaign as code of best practice.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.39 - UNIDO: Technical and economic feasibility analysis on renewable energy generation from solar and wind in Mongolia
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - People based climate change adaptation and mitigation approaches tailored to the Mongolian context including national green economy strategies that generate new jobs and skills, promote clean technologies, and reduce environmental risks and poverty (in sectors such as agriculture, forestry, mining, industry).
planEntities.description:
The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) is a joint initiative of five UN Agencies: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the International Labour Organization (ILO), the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). PAGE responds to paragraph 66 of the Rio+20 outcome document "The Future We Want", which calls upon the UN system to support countries interested in pursuing green economy policies.

The partnership supports nations, regions in reframing economic policies and practices around sustainability to advance the 2030 Agenda to foster economic growth, create income, and jobs, reduce poverty and inequality, and strengthen the ecological foundations of their economies. PAGE, in collaboration with the national government, offers a comprehensive and coordinated package of technical assistance and capacity-building services to support the development, adoption, and implementation of green economy policies and strategies. 
The study aims to explore the potential of renewable energy generation to create significant opportunities for the agribusiness sector in Dund Govi province through expanding renewable energy deployment, creating green jobs, and reducing emissions.

planEntities.parentName: S1E1P1Les institutions nationales en charge du pilotage de l’économie possèdent les capacités pour la mise en place de partenariats publics-privés opérationnels favorisant la diversification de l’économie.
planEntities.description:
À travers cette activité,  la FAO compte appuyer le gouvernement mauritanien pour l'insitutitionnalisation la ZAKAT, comme dans plusieurs initiatives de développement agricole et rural, en œuvrant ensemble à rendre l'agriculture, la foresterie et la pêche plus productives et plus durables en adoptant des systèmes inclusifs et efficaces et en augmentant la résilience des moyens d'existence face aux menaces climatiques et aux crises.
A cet effet, il devient nécessaire de collecter des données, d’adopter des stratégies   pour une meilleure visibilité des produits de la Zakat. C’est dans ce contexte que la FAO travaille en partenariat avec les gouvernements et d'autres acteurs du développement aux niveaux mondial, régional et national pour élaborer des politiques et des environnements institutionnels favorables. Pour sa part, la FAO contribue au renforcement des capacités des pays afin qu'ils traduisent leur engagement politique en mesures concrètes visant à éradiquer la faim, l’insécurité alimentaire et la malnutrition dans le monde

planEntities.name: Sensibilisation et engagement accrus concernant l'institutionnalisation de la collecte et de la distribution de Zakat, avec un effort particulier pour atteindre le public féminin
planEntities.parentName: S1E1P3 L'administration publique et les autorités décentralisées ont les capacités techniques, financières et organisationnelles nécessaires pour mettre en œuvre des politiques de développement économique local sensible aux droits de l'Homme et au genre
planEntities.description: L’objectifs de cette activité est de sensibilisé, d’informé et mettre en confiance les parties prenantes pour promouvoir la zakat et son rôle potentiel au développement du pays, par l’importance de ses flux (monétaires  et en nature)   capable de contribuer aux bien êtres des ayants droits. Cette sensibilisation permettra aux parties prenantes ciblées de mieux comprendre et adhérer aux objectifs  d’institutionnalisation de la zakat, qui demeure informelle dans le pays. Les différents ateliers a été l’occasion d’échanges et débats fructueux, répondant  aux questionnements des différentes parties prenantes relatif a la problématique de la zakat en général et au processus de son institutionnalisation éventuel en Mauritanie.

planEntities.description: Construction et rehabilitation de mares et digues à destination des populations hôtes de la région.

planEntities.name: Mise en place d'un système de familles d'accueil pour le enfants non-accompagnés en besoin de protection de remplacement
planEntities.parentName: S2E3P6 Les institutions nationales ont les compétences et les capacités nécessaires pour planifier, budgétiser et coordonner une réponse systémique pour une protection effective des enfants, y inclus les réfugiés et les migrants.
planEntities.description: L’OIM, en collaboration avec l’UNICEF, soutien le MASEF pour la mise en place d’un système de familles d’accueil pour les enfants non-accompagnés en besoin de protection de remplacement. En 2021, OIM, UNICEF et MASEF ont organisé plusieurs ateliers et une consultance technique pour le gouvernement, comme résultat les outils pour mettre en place le système ont été développés et approuvés (formulaire d’identification et évaluation des familles, formulaire de suivi, étude législatif pour mettre ne place le système). La sélection des OSC locales qui vont tester le système aura lieu en 2022.

planEntities.name: Appui technique pour l'application complète des nouvelles lois de lutte contre la traite de personnes et le trafic de migrants
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P1 Le droit national est de plus en plus conforme aux principes et obligations du droit international des droits de l’Homme, ainsi que les recommandations des mécanismes internationaux des droits de l’Homme, et les acteurs de la justice disposent des connaissances et des capacités renforcées pour appliquer le droit international de manière indépendante et efficace.
planEntities.description: Les matériels de formation pour les sections de protection des lois de traite et trafic ont été développés par un expert national déployé par l’OIM. Les formations auront lieu en 2022. Le consultant a la charge aussi de développer un mécanisme de référencement aux services de protection pour les victimes de traite et les migrants objet de trafic.

planEntities.name: Redynamisation , création et formation de comités villageois
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Au travers de ces activités, l'OIM a créé et redynamisé de nouveaux comités villageois. Représentatif des communautés et nommés de façon transparente et directe par les villageois, les membres de ces comités ont reçus différentes formations direction liées à leurs fonctions : gestion du comité, prévention et gestion de conflits, gestion de l'accès aux ressources naturelles ou encore utilisation des systèmes d'alerte en cas de problème ou de crise.

planEntities.name: Développement et opérationnalisation des POS et code de conduite  sur le débarquement et prise en charge de migrants et réfugiés

planEntities.name: Faciliter l'accès à la documentation des migrants en situation de vulnérabilité

Les migrants ont bénéficié aussi d’un accompagnement légal de la part de l’OSC ALPD.

planEntities.name: Campagnes de sensibilisation auprès des migrants sur leurs droits et l'accès aux services
planEntities.parentName: S3E3P1 Les populations, y inclus les migrants et les réfugiés, reçoivent l'information et si nécessaire une assistance légale pour accéder à l'état civil.

planEntities.name: Enquêtes auprès des communautés transhumantes

planEntities.name: Mise en place d'un système de familles d'accueil pour le enfants non-accompagnés en besoin de protection de remplacement

En 2021, OIM, UNICEF et MASEF ont organisé plusieurs ateliers et une consultance technique pour le gouvernement, comme résultat les outils pour mettre en place le système ont été développés et approuvés (formulaire d’identification et évaluation des familles, formulaire de suivi, étude législatif pour mettre ne place le système). 1. Appui technique et financier à la prise en Charge de qualité des Adolescents, des femmes enceintes et les nouveaux-nés  à travers: la formation et la supervision formative des agents de santé, et des agents de santé communautaire; l'équipement et la mise à disposition des outils nécessaires; la coordination pour des soins de santé de qualité aux adolescents, aux femmes enceintes et aux nouveau-nés.

planEntities.name: Soutenir les efforts du Gouvernement dans l'éradication de la défécation à l'air libre en milieu rural et en zone péri urbaine.
planEntities.parentName: S2E2P3 Les populations vulnérables, y compris les réfugiés et les migrants, ont davantage accès aux ouvrages d’approvisionnement en eau potable et disposent davantage d’installations d’assainissement améliorées.
planEntities.description: Cette activité rentre dans le cadre de la contribution de l'UNICEF à la réalisation du résultat gouvernement pour l'éradication de la défécation à l'air libre en milieu rural et en zone péri urbaine. Elle vise à ce que 500 villages soient certifiés Fin de la défécation à l'air libre (FDAL) d’ici fin 2022 à travers la mise en œuvre de l'ATPC.  Un suivi post FDAL est planifié pour améliorer l'accès basique à l'assainissement des ménages au niveau 400 villages certifiés fin  de la défécation à l'air libre (FDAL). Dans ce cadre, une stratégie post F-DAL est élaborée et la gestion de la base de données de suivi des villages ATPC est consolidée.

planEntities.description: L’ONUDC assurera le suivi à travers la mise en place de mécanismes : élaboration de PV de médiation après chaque médiation entreprise ; mécanisme de vérification du respect des règles de déontologie/éthique ;  collecte de données sur les conflits résolus par les associations de jeunes etc… Le suivi permettra également de venir en appui des associations de jeunes en cas de difficultés lors des médiations.

planEntities.name: Organisation de campagne- par les associations de jeunes de la société civile - pour sensibiliser les communautés à l’importance de la réinsertion sociale et la réhabilitation des jeunes en conflit avec la loi
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: A travers cette activité, les organisations de jeunes seront mobilisées pour sensibiliser les communautés sur l’importance de la réinsertion sociale et de la réintégration des jeunes en conflit avec la loi, pour déconstruire les préjugés et stéréotypes et pour mieux faire comprendre aux communautés le vécu des jeunes en conflit avec la loi.

planEntities.name: Visites à domicile et causeries dans les familles menées par les associations de jeunes de la société civile afin d’accompagner la réinsertion familiale des jeunes en conflit avec la loi
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Les familles étant des acteurs clés pour la réintégration, des visites à domicile et causeries seront organisées avec les familles, et notamment les mères  des jeunes en conflit avec la loi.

planEntities.name: Partage d’expériences positives de réintégration dans la société à travers la mobilisation de jeunes anciennement en conflit avec la loi
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Un programme de peer education – impliquant des pairs qui ont connu des expériences similaires - sera mis en place pour offrir un soutien aux jeunes en conflit avec la loi, tirer des leçons de l’expérience des jeunes qui ont réussi à changer de vie en vue de faciliter la réinsertion/réintégration sociale d’autres jeunes.

planEntities.name: Mise en place de groupe de parole des jeunes dans les quartiers prioritaires de Kiffa pour renforcer leur participation citoyenne
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Lors de la consultation, les associations de jeunes ont exprimé le désir d’avoir des instances pour pouvoir partager leurs préoccupations et réfléchir à des solutions « de et pour les jeunes », c’est en ce sens que cette activité entend mettre en place des groupes de paroles donnant la possibilité aux jeunes de participer effectivement à la vie de leurs quartiers.

planEntities.name: Formation d’un Pool d’organisations de jeunes sur la justice pénale et l’accès aux droits des jeunes adultes et mineurs.
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Cette formation entend outiller un Pool d’organisations de jeunes sur les dispositions juridiques, législatives et réglementaires les concernant ; leurs permettre de découvrir le fonctionnement des institutions, de la justice et de ses acteurs ; de connaitre les moyens de recours devant la justice ; de se familiariser avec les spécificités de la justice des mineurs et d’appréhender les droits et obligations liés à la majorité.

planEntities.name: Journées d’échanges entre jeunes et acteurs de la chaine pénale en vue de renforcer les liens, la compréhension mutuelle, de favoriser un climat de confiance, et de faciliter  la prise en compte de la problématique « jeunes »  dans leur approche.
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Des rencontres d’échanges seront organisées afin de faciliter le rapprochement entre les acteurs de la chaine pénale (police et magistrats) et les jeunes, permettre de répondre aux interrogations de chacun et déconstruire les stéréotypes.

planEntities.name: Formation des acteurs de la chaine pénale sur l’importance de la prise en compte des spécificités des mineurs en conflit avec la loi.
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Cette activité vise à former les acteurs de la chaine pénale, qui agissent directement auprès des mineurs - magistrats, policiers – sur les droits et la protection des mineurs en conflit avec la loi (cadre juridique de la justice pour mineurs, y compris la Convention des Nations unies sur les droits de l’enfant, causes de la déviation juvénile, le traitement pénal des mineurs), sur les mesures alternatives à la détention et sur l’importance de la réhabilitation/réintégration des mineurs en conflit avec la loi.

planEntities.name: Sensibilisation des acteurs de la chaine pénale sur leurs rôles dans la prévention des drogues auprès des jeunes en conflit avec la loi
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: A travers cette activité de sensibilisation, les acteurs de la chaine pénale travaillant avec les jeunes en conflit avec la loi auront une meilleure connaissance des produits stupéfiants ; seront mieux outillés pour détecter et dialoguer avec les jeunes sous l’effet de dépendance des substances addictives ; et informés sur les risques liés à la  consommation et du trafic des drogues.

planEntities.name: Sensibilisation des acteurs de la chaine pénale sur leurs rôles dans la prévention des violences basées sur le genre.
planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: Pour adresser cette vulnérabilité spécifique de jeunes - notamment des jeunes filles - l’activité entend sensibiliser les différents acteurs en contact avec eux (agents de la police judiciaire, magistrats, personnel de santé, travailleurs sociaux et membres des organisations de la société civile, etc.) sur les violences basées sur le genre.

planEntities.parentName: S3E1P4 Les institutions nationales et les populations sont engagées et outillées pour lutter plus activement contre la radicalisation et renforcer la stabilité et la sécurité, tenant compte du contexte sous-régional, tout en revendiquant les droits de ces dernières.
planEntities.description: L’objectif étant de renforcer leurs compétences pour qu’ils puissent prendre en charge les jeunes en conflit avec la loi sous la dépendance des drogues et apporter des réponses plus appropriées aux situations rencontrées dans les postes de police, les tribunaux et les centres de détention.

Le BIT interviendra également pour faciliter la mise en œuvre dans les prisons de Dar Naim et de Nouadhibou d’un programme innovant « 1 journée, 1 métier », qui sera porté par les associations de jeunes de la société civile. planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1 - Relevant policies, regulatory frameworks and institutions enabled to ensure the conservation, sustainable use, access and benefit sharing of natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems, in line with international conventions and national legislation
planEntities.description:
The 2030 Agenda, adopted in 2015, includes SDG 15, which aligns closely with the UNCCD’s goals. SDG target 15.3 urges countries to achieve land degradation neutrality (LDN) by 2030. At COP.12, the UNCCD integrated this target, inviting countries to set voluntary LDN targets, monitor progress, and incorporate LDN into National Action Programmes, using it to attract sustainable financing for combating desertification and land degradation.

Decision 2/COP.12 supports establishing national LDN baselines and targets. The UNCCD’s new 10-year strategy enhances reporting with progress indicators and an implementation framework to monitor financing and national actions aligned with SDG goals.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the Implementation of National Biosafety Frameworks in Southern Africa
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1 - Relevant policies, regulatory frameworks and institutions enabled to ensure the conservation, sustainable use, access and benefit sharing of natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems, in line with international conventions and national legislation
planEntities.description:
The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (2003) led to initiatives like the SINBF project to strengthen biosafety in the DRC, Madagascar, and Namibia by 2026. SINBF aims to build national capacity for implementing the Protocol, establishing effective biosafety frameworks. Key goals include integrating biosafety into national strategies, setting regulatory systems, handling LMOs efficiently, ensuring monitoring and enforcement, and raising public awareness.

The project has three components:

A: Regulatory frameworks,
B: Institutional systems,
C: Administration and evaluation.
The outcome is robust, operational biosafety frameworks in the participating countries.

planEntities.name: Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting – GEF 7 EA Umbrella 1
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1 - Relevant policies, regulatory frameworks and institutions enabled to ensure the conservation, sustainable use, access and benefit sharing of natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems, in line with international conventions and national legislation
planEntities.description:
The international community through the UN member states adopted, in September 2015, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development with 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among these SDGs, Goal 15 is particularly relevant for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Through this goal, countries are urged to, Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss. The target 15.3 urges countries to combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive
to achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.
The twelfth session of the Conference of Parties (COP.12) of the UNCCD agreed in October 2015 to integrate the SDGs and related targets into the implementation of the Convention and decided that striving to achieve SDG target 15.3 is a strong vehicle for driving implementation of the UNCCD (decision 3/COP.12). COP.12 also endorsed the definition of land degradation neutrality (LDN) and invited Parties to (i) formulate voluntary targets to achieve LDN, (ii) use the UNCCD monitoring and evaluation framework, including progress indicators, to monitor, evaluate and communicate progress towards achieving the LDN target, (iii) explore options on how to integrate the voluntary LDN targets in their UNCCD National Action Programmes (NAPs), and (iv) promote the use of LDN targets and projects and other SLM initiatives as an effective vehicle for mobilizing additional sustainable financing and investments to address issues related to desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD). LDN has therefore become an important, while non mandatory, element of UNCCD implementation, while at the same time contributing to other SDGs, including those SDGs relating to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, food and
water security, disaster risk reduction, and poverty reduction.
Decision 2/COP.12 invites affected country Parties to establish national baselines and national-level voluntary LDN targets within their National Action Plans (NAPs). The New 10-year strategic plan and framework to enhance the implementation of the Convention paves the way for an enhanced reporting and review process within the UNCCD that considers the SDG framework. As such, UNCCD reporting and review system is based on (i) progress indicators to measure the progress against the future strategic framework of the UNCCD, and (ii) an implementation framework to assess actions at national and sub-national level relevant for UNCCD implementation. The reporting and review system addresses effective monitoring of financing for UNCCD implementation using refined methodologies in accordance with COP decisions.

planEntities.name: 5.1.10.3 - Reversing deforestation and degradation in Chilgoza Pine Forests - FAO
planEntities.parentName: Output 5.1.10 - Improved capacities of vulnerable small holder farmers and Government officials in climate resilient agriculture and smart water practices (CSA, NRM, DRR), climate change adaptation
planEntities.description:
In 2019, FAO supported the formation of 13 community level Chilgoza Forest Conservation and Protection Committees (CFPCC). CFPCCs will be leading a suite of activities to support conservation, restoration and value chain development of the Chilgoza forests. To reverse chilgoza forest degradation and support safe and  efficient chilgoza pine production, FAO distributed 150 sets of the toolkits to the members of CFPCC. Improved toolkits were used during the harvest season on rotational basis among all CFPCC members.
The stock taking exercise for the GEF funded Chilgoza project was completed. With the support of FOA PES specialist, Payment for Ecosystem Services opportunity identified for one the project areas (Chitral), action plan/next steps defined.

planEntities.name: 6.1.7.2 - Strengthening resilience in Pakistan - FAO
planEntities.parentName: Output 6.1.7 - Disaster prone communities enabled to better anticipate and cope with natural calamities related to the climate change
planEntities.description:
Achievements in 2019
1. Climate-smart agriculture profile for disaster risk reduction in Sindh. 
FAO developed Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) for disaster risk reduction in Sindh profile (to be launched in the beginning of 2020). CSA profile provides updated information and adaptation options to the policy-makers, practitioners and farming communities to support evidence based decision making. 
2. Strengthening Trout Fish Farming. 
To restore livelihoods of affected communities, and to build their resilience to cope with unforeseen disasters, FAO supported the District Fishery Department Chitral with two fish incubators. These fish incubators will be used for incubation and hatching of trout fish eggs in Chitral District of KP province and will ensure consistent fingerlings supply to the farmers, as well as support sustainability of the trout fish enterprises in the region and strengthen the extension services of the Government Fisheries Department in the province.

planEntities.name: 2.1.1.6 - Strengthening Compliance of Labour & Environmental Standards in SMEs (ILO)
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.1 - Institutional Strengthening for development and implementation of policies, frameworks and mechanisms aimed at promoting compliance with International Labor Standards (ILS).
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the International Labour and Environmental Standards Application in Pakistan’s SMEs (ILES) project, is to promote sustainable and inclusive growth in Pakistan by supporting the economic integration of Pakistan into global and regional economies and by improving the compliance with labour and environmental standards and increased competitiveness.

The specific objective is the promotion and implementation of and compliance with international labour and environmental standards through the implementation, application and enforcement of national legislation and standards by the public and private sectors in Pakistan.

The project:
1.	Assists public sector institutions, in consultation with social partners, to effectively strengthen, implement and enforce existing and new legislation and to promote respect for and compliance with international labour and environmental standards in Pakistan;
2.	Supports enterprises in the textile and leather sectors, and their associations, to institutionalize the implementation of, and compliance with, national labour and environmental legislation.

planEntities.description: ILO Internal Output: Workers protected from unacceptable forms of work in identified sectors and/or supply chains. The project aim to foster a partnership approach among the partners on promoting Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW) for a sustainable cotton supply chain in Pakistan. This project will contribute to the implementation of Decent Work in the cotton supply chain by supporting the implementation of FPRW in Pakistan. It will also support social dialogue on FPRW at the global, industry, workplace and community level with the aim of supporting a viable system of industrial relations.

planEntities.name: Basic needs of vulnerable people are met through provision of direct humanitarian assistance
planEntities.parentName: Output 6.1.1: Basic needs of vulnerbale people are met through provision of direct humanitarian assistance. (IOM)
planEntities.description: IOM in 2022 has responded to two crisis with humanitarian assistance. The Flood crisis and the Afghan crisis. Humanitarian assistance consisted in provision of emergency shelter assistance, NFI kits, winterization kits, WASH and Hygiene kits, and dignity kits. It also consisted in provision of shelter repair kits and cash for shelter repair. In terms of WASH support, it consisted in distribution of purifying sachets and installation of handpumps. People were also supported with multi-purpose cash assistance, individual livelihoods assistance which gives small grants to individuals to start their micro-enterprises, and through enterprise development fund grants which is a grant to businesses to create more jobs. Finally, it also consisted in providing HLP assistance and protection services. In total, 970,800 individuals were reached with humanitarian assistance. All these activities are supporting through evidence collected from the Displacement Tracking Matrix, collecting data on displacement and needs.

planEntities.description:
IOM Pakistan screened a high volume of refugees and migrants all across Pakistan. Improving health conditions of key populations and provided medical screening to vulnerable migrants.  As per the consolidated record of IOM clinics across Pakistan, almost 16,000 health assessments have been completed in this quarter. IOM medical teams also provided pre-departure health assistance to migrants who were accepted for resettlement in different countries. The pre-departure health check activities included assessment for fitness to travel, vaccinations as per the requirement of the receiving countries and COVID-19 PCR testing.

In addition, IOM provides health services via mobile clinics and delivers primary health care, SRH, ante and post natal care and MHPSS. It also trained over 300 medical and non-medical staff on psychological first aid.

planEntities.parentName: Output 8.1.5 - Assisting federal and provincial counterparts to enhance access to quality multi-sectoral sexual and reproductive health services and rights – spanning health care, justice, policing and safe spaces – while advocating for the integration of gender concerns into all health planning, policies and programmes.
planEntities.description:
UNFPA Internal Output: Gender Equality & Women Empowerment 
DESCRIPTION: The programme will address the root causes of gender inequality, in particular social norms and practices which pose structural obstacles and that prevent women from making informed decisions on their sexual and reproductive health and rights. The programme will promote legal and policy reforms to ensure that the accountability mechanisms toward gender equality are in place at national and sub-national level to enable women and girls especially the most vulnerable and marginalized, to claim their social, legal, sexual and reproductive health rights and be protected from violence and harmful traditional practices. The programme will strengthen capacities of the government to generate evidence for prevention and response to GBV, engaging with government machineries to ensure the design, implementation and strengthening of systems and policies that are gender transformative and enable the transitions between development and humanitarian settings to happen under a gender equality lens.

planEntities.description: This output will be achieved by generating data and using the same for improved planning and evidence to address bottlenecks affecting the enabling environment, coordination, governance, accountability, standards, monitoring and quality assurance for the priority areas of work in health. The work on social policy will focus on public finance for children and social protection schemes. This will involve analysis of public health spending in children and the identification of budget lines directly or indirectly related to children’s health.  This analysis will provide UNICEF Pakistan with evidence on the per capita investment on the right of children to health to advocate with provincial and federal governments on the importance of increasing public sector finance for children.  A second product of this work will analyse budget allocations versus budget expenditures to identify bottlenecks that contribute to low expenditure in the sector. Both analyses will inform the fiscal space and gap analysis that will build a case for improving and expanding public finance for children in the health sector.

planEntities.description:
This Key Activity' is associated with UNICEF Internal Output i.e "By 2022, more children, particularly girls and the most disadvantaged, benefit from equitable and appropriate early learning and basic education"
Description: UNICEF continued to reinforce upstream work for greater coherence and alignment of resources as Coordinating Agency for the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) in Sindh, Balochistan, and Punjab. UNICEF facilitated evidence-based policy dialogues and interactions amongst Local Education Groups, District Education Groups and Steering Committees, and also coordinated with the GPE Secretariat. Working closely with Education Departments, LEG members, and the WB and DFID respectively as Grant Agents, UNICEF played a key role in the preparation of submissions for ESPDG grants for Sindh and Punjab. These were approved by the GPE Secretariat, preparing the ground for sector analysis and sector planning in 2018.

planEntities.description: Programmes (ALPs) in Sindh and Balochistan, over 26,000 children and adolescents (46 per cent girls) participated in 559 ALP centres in community provided spaces, madrassas, private and government schools, with direct UNICEF support. The programmes reached disadvantaged children in urban slums (Karachi), cotton-growing areas of Sindh (IKEA), and disadvantaged rural districts in Balochistan. In Sindh, over 7,500 ALP students (51 per cent girls) or approximately half of all ALP students were mainstreamed into formal schools. Capacity building programmes improved skills and capacities of 325 NFE/ALP teachers (186 female) and 265 para-teachers (129 female) on child-friendly school approaches, play-based learning and interactive teaching methodologies. In both provinces, ALP data has been integrated into Non-Formal MIS developed by JICA.

planEntities.name: 7.1.1.3 - Families and communities actively support on-time enrolment, retention, completion and transition to lower-secondary education, especially for girls (UNICEF)
planEntities.parentName: Output 7.1.1 - System Strengthening - Innovations - Availability of strong evidence of successful and cost-effective innovations to improve access and learning for the most disadvantaged children (UNICEF)
planEntities.description:
In 2017, four of the six C4D benchmarks were prioritized under Output 3; development of strategic frameworks, evidence generation, capacity building and system strengthening. An analysis and summary of a draft KAP was completed, with actionable insights for the national C4D strategic framework for the upcoming UNICEF Country Programme. Synthesis and documentation of good practices, results, and lesson learnt of the ‘Every Child in School Initiative” which ended mid-2016 is in process. 
In terms of capacity building and system strengthening, provincial education departments in Punjab, Sindh, KP and FATA were supported to develop communication strategies. In Sindh, UNICEF as Coordinating Agency for the GPE supported the Education Department to develop a strategy for effective communication through electronic media with stakeholders and communities, including a complaint management system. In Punjab, an orientation workshop on Behaviour and Social Change Communication with district education managers prepared the ground for future development of a BSSC capacity enhancement strategy. Also, capacities to implement the Punjab Enrolment and Retention Plan were strengthened through divisional level workshops with education district staff, principals and teachers, along with software to collect OOSC data provided to the education department. 

UNICEF supported Departments of Education in enrolment campaigns in all four provinces and FATA, with focus on girls’ enrolment. In 2017, an estimated 740,000 children (40 per cent girls) enrolled in the early grades of government schools in 50 focus districts and FATA, of which an estimated 10-15 percent may not have enrolled without the interventions. In FATA, this was the first enrolment campaign, successfully mobilising government, community leaders and members, in a context of return and recovery. Through the campaign, provisional numbers show 126,000 children (35 per cent girls) newly enrolled against a target of 200,000. Although enrolment drives and social mobilization efforts are successful in enrolling more children, dropout/retention remains a challenge. As part of government programs to provide learning opportunities to over-age and disadvantaged children, nearly 26,000 children and adolescents (46 per cent girls) were enrolled in 559 ALP classes in urban slums (Karachi) and disadvantaged rural areas (Sindh, Balochistan, Punjab) with direct UNICEF support. Approximately 51,000 children and youth (48 per cent girls) in government schools and ALP centres participated in co-curricular activities that improved education quality and social cohesion competencies. 

Community led activities led to increased engagement of local education councils and parent teacher school management committees for effective school functioning and student enrolment. Members of 2,016 committees were trained on roles and responsibilities. As part of the EU-supported Basic Education programme in Balochistan, 567 PTSMCs in low-performing schools were trained and engaged in developing and implementing School Development Plans, which include improving the school environment and replenishment of missing facilities including WASH.

Pakistan Tanners Association, south Zone, Environmental Society, PTA(SZ)-ES is implementing UNIDO-GEF funded project “Transforming the leather processing industries towards low emissions and climate resilient development paths in Pakistan”, with the objectives to transform industrial processing zones in Sindh Province, towards the widespread adoption of low carbon technologies. Initiated in April 2019, the project is committed to assist the KLA to enhance product exportability and international acceptability by acquiring international sustainable certificates, labels and other brand requirements and to ensure that the sector .           
The overall objective of the project is therefore to transform the industrial processing zones in Sindh Province through the widespread adoption of low-carbon technologies. To achieve the overall aim, the project will contribute to strengthening the technical and management operations of the KLA cluster:  production processes, cleaner production facilities, sector level facilities (such as the CETP for KLA and proper waste management) and technical and professional capacities will be established and/or optimized to improve tannery efficiency and reduce GHG emissions. If identified during project implementation, feasible add-ons will be initiated to further reduce GHG emissions. 
In line with the GEF-6 Climate Change Mitigation focal area strategy, the project will i) contribute to the support of integrated approaches combining policies, technologies, and management practices with significant climate change mitigation potential.

planEntities.description:
UNOPS Pakistan is implementing this project in collaboration with the Ministry of Climate Change Pakistan (MoCC), Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR), Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA) and Public Health and Engineering Departments of Punjab & KP. 
The water-quality testing laboratories are being upgraded through a) procurement and installation of advanced laboratory equipment, b) performing minor upgrade works in laboratory buildings to ensure safe and efficient working environment for operation of equipment, c) training and capacity enhancement of the water-quality testing laboratories and the WASH Cell of the MoCC and, d) the rollout of a Management Information System (MIS) to strengthen coordination and water quality management.
WHO: 
HO provided state of art water filtration plants in Dadu, Karachi, Khairpur, Haripur, Temergarah, Landi Kotal. IT also refurbished 16 toilets inside hospitals in refugee areas and provided trainings on huygeine and WASH surveillance to 176 health care providers and local Government and an incinerator at Haripur. It also provided Wegtechs to 4 hospitals and 100 PCRWR water testing kits for community to local Government
GCF-Green Climate Fund Readiness Grant
On the directions of MoNHSR (Director General Health), a technical support from WHO Headquarter, RC Office WHO and Ministry of Climate Change (MoCC), a GCF readiness proposal of around 1 million US Dollar has been submitted to the National Designated Authority (MoCC). The proposal is pending for final submission to GCF after a ministerial meeting between MoNHSR and MoCC. 
Furthermore, a letter of endorsement is required from MoNHSR for MoCC to hasten the submission of the readiness grant to GCF.
Climate Change and Environmental Health Course
WHO, in collaboration with Agha Khan University, is developing a course on climate change and environmental health. The course outline has been developed by AKU expert faculty members. A list of potential participants from 20 different public entities that have direct mandate in the context of Climate Change and health are being listed to enlist the nominees. The approach is to design subsequent session for the selected cohort and lead to a fellow ship program as ‘’Leaders in Climate Resilient Health Systems’’. 
Health Co-Benefit Study
The Health Co-Benefit Study was conducted by MoCC and MoNHSR in conjunction with the WHO. The study provides Pakistan with a new lens on climate change’s contribution towards health problems in Pakistan. The key recommendations of the study are being incorporated into Pakistan’s NDCs.
SDG 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 Reporting/Validation for Pakistan to JMP 
 WHO supported MoCC and Bureau of Statistics to review the available data on the SDG indicators 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3. After the endorsement from the major federal and provincial stakeholders the data sheets were submitted to WHO for onward submission to JMP headquarter.
Revision of Health Chapter in the Climate Change Policy of Pakistan
MoCC initiated the policy review of National Climate Change Policy (NCCP), WHO supported in the consultative process to support the consultation for Climate Change and Health Chapter. The extensive consultation process and contextualization of RC 64, resolution resulted in development of policy brief with policy recommendations for the NCCP review.
Piloting Climate Resilient Health Facilities Tool 
Pakistan is selected as a country for piloting this tool in the EMRO region beside Iran.
Air Quality Compliance Framework
With the support of WHO, revision of Pakistan Clean Air Program was made and outline of compliance framework for air quality has been developed. 
WASH Activities Integrated in Nutrition Stabilization Context
Every effort is being made to integrate the WASH activities in nutrition Stabilization centres with WASH in HF approach

planEntities.description: During and after a major disaster where WFP assistance is required and requested, WFP will provide relief support through unconditional transfers  and early recovery support through conditional transfers. Assistance modalities will primarily be cash and/or food transfers, using cash when feasible; especially where markets are stable and have sufficient supply and security and implementation arrangements permit.  WFP will maintain its emergency response capacity and support clusters and working groups related to humanitarian coordination. When appropriate, WFP will support the government to operationalize its safety nets and other response mechanisms for relief. WFP will apply lessons from past experiences and assessment analysis to ensure accountability to affected populations and consider the specific needs and concerns of women, men, girls, boys and any specific vulnerable groups that may arise as a result of a crisis situation and intervention.

planEntities.description:
WFP will support the construction and repair of community assets through Food Assistance for Asset activities to increase access to food and support early recovery and rehabilitation of livelihoods of the most food-insecure in disaster-affected areas, particularly temporarily dislocated households returning to FATA. Such projects will follow WFP’s Food Assistance for Assets guidance manual, including application of the three-pronged approach and fostering participation by a wide-range of community representatives. An environmental screening will ensure that activities are designed to factor in environmental concerns. In mobilizing beneficiaries, WFP will work with its cooperating partners to engage women in the projects, including fostering gender balance on project management committees; actively supporting women to participate in activity design; community-based operation and management of the assets; and promoting shared decision-making on the use of cash/food and responsibility for household food security and nutrition.
60.	Both activities 1 and 2 will be implemented, under the overall supervision of the relevant government authority (e.g., the FATA Disaster Management Authority and the FATA Secretariat), through NGOs with the requisite technical capacity, while building the capacity of local responders. WFP will collaborate with relevant line departments and UN partners, particularly FAO, UNDP, UNICEF and UNHCR, wherever feasible.

- Build capacity at national and subnational levels in environmental health assessment, management,  and strategic planning
- Capacity building for preparedness and response to environmental emergencies including in the context of IHR, including WASH and occupational health & safety.
WHO:
GCF-Green Climate Fund Readiness Grant
On the directions of MoNHSR (Director General Health), a technical support from WHO Headquarter, RC Office WHO and Ministry of Climate Change (MoCC), a GCF readiness proposal of around 1 million US Dollar has been submitted to the National Designated Authority (MoCC). The proposal is pending for final submission to GCF after a ministerial meeting between MoNHSR and MoCC. 
Furthermore, a letter of endorsement is required from MoNHSR for MoCC to hasten the submission of the readiness grant to GCF.
Climate Change and Environmental Health Course
WHO, in collaboration with Agha Khan University, is developing a course on climate change and environmental health. The course outline has been developed by AKU expert faculty members. A list of potential participants from 20 different public entities that have direct mandate in the context of Climate Change and health are being listed to enlist the nominees. The approach is to design subsequent session for the selected cohort and lead to a fellow ship program as ‘’Leaders in Climate Resilient Health Systems’’. 
Health Co-Benefit Study
The Health Co-Benefit Study was conducted by MoCC and MoNHSR in conjunction with the WHO. The study provides Pakistan with a new lens on climate change’s contribution towards health problems in Pakistan. The key recommendations of the study are being incorporated into Pakistan’s NDCs.
SDG 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3 Reporting/Validation for Pakistan to JMP 
 WHO supported MoCC and Bureau of Statistics to review the available data on the SDG indicators 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3. After the endorsement from the major federal and provincial stakeholders the data sheets were submitted to WHO for onward submission to JMP headquarter.
Revision of Health Chapter in the Climate Change Policy of Pakistan
MoCC initiated the policy review of National Climate Change Policy (NCCP), WHO supported in the consultative process to support the consultation for Climate Change and Health Chapter. The extensive consultation process and contextualization of RC 64, resolution resulted in development of policy brief with policy recommendations for the NCCP review.
Piloting Climate Resilient Health Facilities Tool 
Pakistan is selected as a country for piloting this tool in the EMRO region beside Iran.
Air Quality Compliance Framework
With the support of WHO, revision of Pakistan Clean Air Program was made and outline of compliance framework for air quality has been developed. 
WASH Activities Integrated in Nutrition Stabilization Context
Every effort is being made to integrate the WASH activities in nutrition Stabilization centres with WASH in HF approach
NDCs Partnership on Health Adaptation Group (WHO is colead)
WHO has supported the adaptation working group meetings, helped in providing the recommendation and assisted in compilation of the first draft work for climate change and health under the NDCs. 
CBRN WHO tool piloting in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
Process under way

planEntities.name: Brindar asistencia técnica y acompañamiento a la CONFIEP para: 1) la elaboración de un diagnóstico y recomendaciones de política en lo relativo a la construcción de nuevos mecanismos (políticas y programas) de protección social que abarquen el sector informal; 2) desarrollo de una agenda propia en materia de Empresas y Derechos humanos que incluye capacitación a sus miembros y propuestas específicas relativas a la visión empresarial en torno a varias de las acciones previstas en el plan
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a aumentar la productividad, competitividad y formalización del aparato productivo nacional a través del fortalecimiento de cadenas productivas sostenibles, con base en una economía circular y generación de empleos verdes, con enfoque intergeneracional e intercultural y en condiciones de igualdad de género.
planEntities.description: La CONFIEP ha identificado la necesidad de reevaluar su posicionamiento en el debate de las políticas enfocadas al desarrollo, reclamando un rol clave en los grandes temas relativos al modelo de desarrollo y reducción de la pobreza en el país, como representante del sector privado. En este sentido, una agenda que se quiere reforzar es aquella que permita visibilizar y reflejar el compromiso del empresariado con los desafíos del Perú en materia de derechos humanos en un espectro amplio (derechos económicos, sociales, civiles y políticos). Asimismo, teniendo en cuenta el peso de la informalidad y su reducción en la resolución de algunos de estos debates sobre el logro de un país más justo y cohesionado, CONFIEP, quiere realizar una aportación propia a la discusión esencial sobre el refuerzo de las políticas de protección social, y en especial sobre su alcance en las poblaciones más desprotegidas por la informalidad, así como la mejora de la eficiencia y cobertura de los mecanismos actuales de protección social en las empresas y trabajadores formales.

planEntities.name: Brindar asistencia técnica y acompañamiento a las organizaciones de trabajadores para contribuir con los siguientes entregables: 1) Estrategia sindical diseñada y actualizada   orientada a nuevos grupos de trabajadores (que laboran a través de plataformas digitales y teletrabajo) con enfoque de género y mejora de los servicios de representación, defensa y tutela de sus derechos laborales y sociales, así como, de formación y desarrollo de liderazgos sectoriales y territoriales; lo mismo respecto al sector de la agricultura de exportación y las TRH.  2) Las organizaciones de trabajadores cuentan con mayor conocimiento para hacer uso de una arquitectura funcional de coordinación sindical construida para impulsar el diálogo social y elaboración de propuestas de política pública 3) Fortalecidos los conocimientos del movimiento sindical y acordadas acciones para una incidencia efectiva en la implementación de los ODS y el MCC y promover la aceleración de la Agenda 2030, en base al relevamiento del ODS 8. 4)
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a aumentar la productividad, competitividad y formalización del aparato productivo nacional a través del fortalecimiento de cadenas productivas sostenibles, con base en una economía circular y generación de empleos verdes, con enfoque intergeneracional e intercultural y en condiciones de igualdad de género.
planEntities.description: El objetivo estratégico de esta iniciativa es potenciar las capacidades de las organizaciones sindicales para elevar sus niveles de representatividad y una defensa efectiva de los trabajadores principalmente aquellos insertos en el marco de la economía de plataforma, modalidad de teletrabajo, economía informal, sector rural, economía del cuidado, así como fortalecer sus capacidades para la elaboración de propuestas y adopción de posiciones para promover el trabajo decente y los  derechos fundamentales con énfasis en libertad sindical y negociación colectiva en los diversos espacios de diálogo social desde donde e diseñan, ejecutan y/o de seguimiento a políticas públicas para una recuperación de la pandemia centrada en las personas, inclusiva, sostenible y resiliente. Se priorizará el trabajo en conjunto con las centrales sindicales y todas las acciones serán diseñadas y ejecutadas con perspectiva de género y de juventud.

planEntities.description:
El objetivo del proyecto es mejorar y aumentar los niveles de integración socioeconómica de los migrantes y refugiados venezolanos en sus países de acogida a través de un enfoque de trabajo decente. Con ese objetivo, la intervención buscará cuatro resultados:
* Mejora de la capacidad de los Institutos de Formación Profesional (IFP) para atender a la población nacional y a los migrantes y refugiados.
* Fortalecimiento del vínculo entre los Servicios Públicos de Empleo (SPE) y el mercado de trabajo para ofrecer oportunidades de empleo decente a los migrantes y refugiados venezolanos.
* Mejora de las oportunidades laborales para las mujeres venezolanas migrantes y refugiadas.
* Fortalecimiento de los sistemas de información del mercado laboral y de datos sobre migración laboral.

planEntities.description: Esta iniciativa tiene por objetivo fortalecer las capacidades de los actores del sector público y privado para abordar los principales retos de la formalización. Los resultados esperados son: (i) conocimiento generado sobre los obstáculos, beneficios e incentivos para la formalización en Perú para equipar mejor a los actores en la transición a la economía formal, (ii) capacidades fortalecidas de los actores para la identificación y aplicación de soluciones innovadoras, inclusivas y sensibles al género que promuevan una recuperación económica orientada a la transición a la economía formal, y (iii) evidencia generada sobre los incentivos a la formalización a través del pilotaje de nuevos enfoques para el diseño de estrategias o la revisión de las existentes. El grupo objetivo son las micro, pequeñas y medianas empresas (MIPYMES) formales con trabajadores informales, las MIPYMES informales y trabajadores informales por cuenta propia.

planEntities.name: SEGUIMIENTO EN TIEMPO REAL DE LAS AMENAZAS DE VIOLENCIA DE GÉNERO PARA MUJERES Y NIÑAS VENEZOLANAS DESPLAZADAS
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a ampliar la cobertura y el acceso, oportuno y de calidad a los servicios esenciales que promueven la protección y la atención de la violencia basada en género y otras prácticas nocivas en entornos humanitarios y de desarrollo.
planEntities.description:
"Contribuir a mejorar las estrategias de protección para prevenir la violencia de género y satisfacer las necesidades de las mujeres migrantes y refugiadas de Venezuela que son sobrevivientes de la violencia de género.
Este proyecto busca:
1) Identificar los riesgos de género, así como cómo, dónde y por qué ocurren para informar mejor estrategias preventivas y de protección.
2) Determinar qué servicios son más necesarios para las mujeres y niñas venezolanas refugiadas y migrantes y dónde, a lo largo de la ruta de migración, esos servicios serían más útiles y de más fácil acceso."

planEntities.name: Socioeconomic (Re)integratin Toolkit SA
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso al trabajo decente, a la vivienda digna y espacios públicos adecuados, y a un sistema integral de protección social, incluyendo un piso de protección social, que garantice seguridad económica, cobertura de salud y acceso a un sistema nacional de cuidados a lo largo de todo el ciclo vital, con énfasis en las poblaciones y territorios en situación de especial protección, o en situación de vulnerabilidad y/o precariedad, atendiendo las brechas de género, generacionales y por nacionalidad.
planEntities.description:
"Para ayudar a los gobiernos de América del Sur a fortalecer la recuperación socioeconómica posterior a la pandemia, la OIM está desarrollando un “juego de herramientas” de integración socioeconómica para que los funcionarios gubernamentales estén mejor equipados para facilitar la (re)integración de los migrantes y retornados en las economías nacionales y empoderar así a los migrantes y retornados como actores para el desarrollo sostenible.
Esto se logrará a través de dos componentes principales:
1) realizando una evaluación de evidencia rápida sensible al género para construir una base de evidencia sobre la (re)integración socioeconómica en América del Sur para el desarrollo e implementación de herramientas y;
2) poniendo a prueba el conjunto de herramientas y redactando un plan de implementación nacional para la (re)integración socioeconómica en los países piloto."

planEntities.description:
"Fortalecemiento de capacidades y competencias a Fiscales del Subsistema de Derechos Humanos y Terrorismo del Ministerio Público y  personal del Instituto de Medicina Legal, mediante el Curso Taller “Fortalecimiento de Competencias sobre Estándares Internacionales para la Investigación Fiscal de Violaciones a Derechos Humanos”, con el objetivo de garantizar una justicia pronta, efectiva e imparcial y, procurar la rendición de cuentas a favor de las víctimas y sus familiares.
Fortalecimiento de capacidades al Ministerio Público respecto a la aplicación de los estándares internacionales en derechos humanos y la jurisprudencia nacional e internacional, a través de un compendio que enfatice conceptos básicos en base a las principales sentencias nacionales e internacionales sistematizadas sobre derechos humanos, en particular, derecho a la protesta, reunión pacífica, uso de la fuerza y violaciones a derechos humanos.  
Fortalecer capacidades y competencias de los/as fiscales del Ministerio Público y el personal del Instituto de Medicina Legal, en el marco del Protocolo de Berkeley, el cual contiene los primeros Estándares internacionales para la sistematización e investigación de redes sociales como evidencias en violaciones a derechos humanos.
Fortalecer las capacidades y competencias de los y las fiscales del Ministerio Público y de Medicina Legal en la utilidad, importancia y uso práctico de los protocolos de Estambul y de Minnesota y las técnicas forenses de investigación"

planEntities.name: Gestión de residuos orgánicos en Perú: acelerando el progreso hacia un sector de residuos circular y neutro en carbono
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description:
"El objetivo general de los Proyectos de Apoyo a la NAMA o Acción de Mitigación Nacionalmente Apropiada (NSP) es acelerar la implementación de proyectos de tratamiento de residuos orgánicos y de captura de gases de vertedero, contribuyendo a la NDC de Perú y proporcionando importantes co-beneficios de desarrollo sostenible en el contexto de la recuperación de Covid-19, como la reducción de la contaminación, la inclusión social y la creación de empleos verdes. La NDC de Perú considera prioritario el sector de los residuos, y este NSP apoyará directamente todas las medidas incluidas en él.

Se espera que el  NPS apoye directamente el desarrollo de una cartera de aproximadamente 22 proyectos. Entre ellos se encuentran un proyecto de captura de gas de vertedero que genera electricidad limpia, seis proyectos de digestión anaeróbica y 15 proyectos de compostaje. Además, el NPS creará una cartera de 40 proyectos con estudios de prefactibilidad para aumentar la replicabilidad del modelo del NPS y atraer más inversiones."

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description: Contribuir a la resiliencia de 2 Reservas de Biosfera (RB) de la Amazonía peruana creando un modelo sostenible de relaciones entre las comunidades y el medio ambiente, a través del apoyo a las iniciativas de conservación y económicas que se desarrollan en las RB y sus alrededores. El proyecto tiene un componente de coproducción de conocimiento en cuatro temas: 1) acción climática y reducción del riesgo de desastres; 2) acciones integradas de conservación y desarrollo en apoyo a actividades productivas en 9 distritos (cafe, aguaymanto, piscicultura y apicultura); 3) conservación de bosques y manejo de incendios; 4) restauración de sistemas hídricos y forestales.

To achieve its goals, the project will work with the national network of training service providers to deliver the training on i) COVID OSH and ii) digitalization of business operations (e.g., digital entrepreneurship, e-commerce strategies and digital financial literacy). Through these Hubs and the affiliated satellites such as the local internet cafes, the project will provide the internet connectivity, co-working spaces, back-office services and linkage to the support programmes for the MSMEs.

planEntities.name: Safe and Fair: Realizing women migrant workers’ rights and opportunities in the ASEAN region
planEntities.parentName: Output 4: Social protection systems effectively shored.
planEntities.description:
SAFE AND FAIR: Realizing women migrant workers’ rights and opportunities in the ASEAN region (2018-2022) is part of the multi-year EU-UN Spotlight Initiative to Eliminate Violence Against Women and Girls. SAFE AND FAIR is implemented by the ILO and UN Women, led by the ILO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific. SAFE AND FAIR works in close cooperation with governments and social partners to achieve three inter-linking specific objectives:  

 

Specific objective 1: Women migrant workers are better protected by gender-sensitive labour migration governance frameworks;  

Specific objective 2: Women migrant workers are less vulnerable to violence and trafficking and benefit from coordinated responsive quality services; and  

Specific objective 3: Data, knowledge and attitudes on the rights and contributions of women migrant workers are improved

planEntities.name: Promoting Conflict Prevention, Social Cohesion and Community Resilience in BARMM in the Time of COVID-19
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description:
In light of the prevalent drivers of conflict in the region, including COVID-19, the project will seek to 1) fortify reintegration efforts for former women combatants by empowering them to engage and support peacebuilding, 2) support conflict understanding and prevention by promoting gender-responsive, inclusive, and culturally-sensitive legislation, policies and programmes, and 3) build the resilience of communities in conflict hotspots through collaborative socio-economic activities and inclusive community-based reconciliation mechanisms.    

The project will utilize a hybrid implementation strategy that will harness the relationships between the implementing agencies and the Bangsamoro authorities for institutional shifts, while utilizing the networks and community-knowledge of CSOs and local NGOs for interventions aimed at conflict-affected communities. This community-based approach, which will be supported by partners with strong community track records, will engage women and youth from conflict scenarios in the BARMM and ensure that the intervention is timely and relevant. The project will center all activities around women and youth participation and inclusion, in order to effectively drive conflict prevention, mediation and resolution at all levels of governance.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Resilience Against Climate-Related Security Risks in Conflict-Prone Communities in Mindanao, Philippines
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description: Rural poor communities in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) are the most vulnerable to climate emergencies considering their geography, low capacity to adapt and respond, and weak government systems. As BARMM anticipates the 2025 election, it is crucial that its institutions and communities are ready and resilient to climate emergencies to continue the region’s development and achieve the promises of the peace deal. To strengthen the resiliency of conflict-prone communities in BARMM against climate security related risks. IOM will ensure that regional and local climate change adaptation and response mechanisms are conflict-sensitive and evidence-based, and that conflict prone communities, including local enterprises and vulnerable individuals are informed, improved capacity, and have the resources to adapt to the impacts of climate change.

planEntities.name: Climate Change Adaptation and Community Resilience in the Philippines
planEntities.parentName: Output 10: Innovative finance effectively mobilized for green, climate and disaster risk reduction and inclusive investments
planEntities.description: The primary objective of this project is to support the Philippines to mitigate adverse impacts of climate-related events through enhancing policy and community-level interventions integrating safe and orderly migration as a tool of resilience for at-risk communities. This will be achieved through two Outcomes. The first deals with increasing the awareness and technical capacity of local government bodies, decision-makers, civil society, media and vulnerable communities to adapt to climate change and consider migration management as an opportunity to build community resilience. Secondly, the project will aid local government and community organizations to produce evidence-based climate adaptive programmes that consider migration in their planning, through the implementation of training and proposal writing workshops using updated and localized modules.

planEntities.name: Strengthened trade facilitation capacity to implement the Customs Modernisation and Tariffs Act (CMTA) and WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement (WTO TFA)
planEntities.parentName: Output 6: Resilience strengthened in all sectors and all levels of government
planEntities.description:
The support will target the Category C provisions notified by the Philippines under the WTO TFA relating to the training and other forms of technical assistance required to build the capacity of the human resources of the Bureau of Customs (BOC), as well as the Philippine Trade Facilitation Committee (PTFC), in strong coordination with government agencies such as the Bureau of International Trade Relations (BITR), and in alignment with the work ongoing at regional level (including ARISE Plus regional components). Support will also be provided for the implementation of the provisions contained in the CMTA in close collaboration with key relevant government agencies. In the context of the Philippines’ overall trade facilitation performance and taking into consideration the ongoing reforms of cross-border formalities in the framework of the Single Window initiative, ITC will adapt its interventions to support the Philippines in priority trade facilitation areas, in consultation with the BOC and other relevant public and private stakeholders. 

All proposed interventions are fully in line with the development priorities of the Philippines, including the PEDP 2018-2022, which requests removing unnecessary regulatory impediments and enhancing trade facilitation for improving the overall climate for export development. They also correspond to two pillars of the Philippines Inclusive Industrial strategy i.e. Pillar 2, which aims to ease doing business and investment environment through strengthening institutional and regulatory framework and addressing bureaucratic practices and Pillar 4 focused on capacity building and Human Resource development programmes, to enhance skills of government officials in their area of their responsibilities.

Overall, the activities under this cluster will contribute to enhanced cross-border trade environment in the Philippines and, in the longer-term, they will be instrumental for strengthening the country’s position in international rankings and positive perception of its procedural and regulatory framework. This facilitated environment in turn will be essential for supporting economic growth and attracting investments to the country.

planEntities.name: Government and private operators are better able to identify and implement export priorities
