planEntities.description: The support under this output will aim to identify, promote and support market opportunities, with the private sector as direct beneficiary. ITC will provide the private sector in the Philippines with customized information and intelligence, training and coaching to increase awareness of export opportunities, and to prepare for and establish new market linkages, focusing on the EU-GSP+ market, priority industries, Philippine MSMEs and start-ups. Support will also be provided for industrial and investment policy design and implementation, to address critical gaps to participation in global value chains.

planEntities.name: Quality management and control systems for exported food products are better aligned with international best practices
planEntities.parentName: Output 8: Untapped potential for agriculture-based inclusive growth and sustainable agri-food systems effectively leveraged.
planEntities.description: Project activities contributing to improve alignment with international best practices of quality management and control systems for exported food products will comprise a range of activities, grouped under two main clusters. The first will focus on technical training for export-oriented operators along the value chain on food safety best practices and international standards and the second on training for the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Department of Agriculture (DA) and attached agencies/bureaus to act as competent authorities for food exports to the EU. A series of webinar-based interactive sessions, training and coaching are planned under all activities, to the extent possible. ToT work will be carried out with remote supervision, targeting selected staff of export-oriented economic operators and public sector institutions. COVID-19 response will involve awareness-raising on standards and measures that can build resilience of enterprises and help recovery from the crisis. Gender equality will be given due consideration in selection of training participants and in consultative mechanisms.

planEntities.name: Protection and Promotion of Human Rights in the Philippines
planEntities.parentName: Output 4: Social protection systems effectively shored.
planEntities.description:
This three-year UN Joint Programme for the Promotion and Protection of Human
Rights in the Philippines focuses on technical cooperation and capacity-building
“with a view to improving further the situation of human rights in the Philippines,
to provide support for the country in its continued fulfilment of its international
human rights obligations and commitments.”

The Joint Programme focuses on six key areas, under three outcomes:

Outcome One: Duty-bearers’ capacities to respect, protect and fulfill human rights are strengthened, that they increasingly apply a Human Rights Based Approach; and that there is a substantial reduction in violations as a result of increased awareness and compliance with the state’s international obligations. 
This includes:
Strengthening National Mechanisms for Implementation, Reporting and Follow-Up
A Human Rights Based Approach to Counterterrorism
A Human Rights Based Approach to Drug Control

Outcome Two: Domestic accountability mechanisms to address human rights violations are strengthened, leading to increased accountability, justice and redress for victims. 

This includes:
Improved police data gathering on alleged violations
Strengthening Domestic Accountability Mechanism

Outcome Three: Rights holders, including victims of human rights violations and abuse, and their families, are better able to claim their rights.

This includes:
Civic space and engagement with civil society and the Commission on Human Rights - Philippines

planEntities.name: Promoting Conflict Prevention, Social Cohesion and Community Resilience in BARMM in the Time of COVID-19
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description:
In light of the prevalent drivers of conflict in the region, including COVID-19, the project will seek to 1) fortify reintegration efforts for former women combatants by empowering them to engage and support peacebuilding, 2) support conflict understanding and prevention by promoting gender-responsive, inclusive, and culturally-sensitive legislation, policies and programmes, and 3) build the resilience of communities in conflict hotspots through collaborative socio-economic activities and inclusive community-based reconciliation mechanisms.    

The project will utilize a hybrid implementation strategy that will harness the relationships between the implementing agencies and the Bangsamoro authorities for institutional shifts, while utilizing the networks and community-knowledge of CSOs and local NGOs for interventions aimed at conflict-affected communities. This community-based approach, which will be supported by partners with strong community track records, will engage women and youth from conflict scenarios in the BARMM and ensure that the intervention is timely and relevant. The project will center all activities around women and youth participation and inclusion, in order to effectively drive conflict prevention, mediation and resolution at all levels of governance.

planEntities.name: Women Peace and Humanitarian Fund
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description:
In 2021, the Philippines was selected to implement the Women’s Peace and Humanitarian Fund (WPHF), which was recognized for its potential to catalyze convergence between humanitarian, peace, security, and development finance as it focuses on enhancing women’s engagement, leadership, and empowerment across all phases of crisis, peace and security, and development. The 1st Call for Proposals (CfP) focused on increasing women’s participation in advocating for and ensuring accountability on the WPS agenda as well as on enhancing decision-making of women in conflict prevention processes and response, while the 2nd CfP aimed to support national and local women’s right organization working on women, peace, and security through dedicated institutional capacity. Following two (2) Calls for Proposals (CfP), first in September 2021 and second in February 2022, the National Steering Committee on WPHF chaired by the UN Office of the Resident Coordinator to Philippines and by Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) and other members have confirmed the eleven (11) implementing partner Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to implement various WPS and humanitarian action projects that started after the approval of the Partners Contract Agreement from June-July 2022.
With the overall goal of WPHF in creating an enabling environment for women, peace and security and strengthening conflict prevention mechanisms, it also increased opportunities for civic participation in UNSCR 1325 on WPS, prioritizing conflict-vulnerable/-affected communities across the country. Significantly, a total of two hundred twenty-seven (207) women-led civil CSOs were involved in design, budgeting, implementation, and monitoring & evaluation of the WPS agenda. The involvement and participation of CSOs is critical in harmonizing and localizing the efforts and commitments under the WPS Agenda. The CSOs through their local networks will serve a multiplier and will ensure that WPS was adopted and have influenced various programming of government instrumentalities, and local organizations.

Countries are expected to submit updated and more ambitious NDCs every five years which will become the main vehicle for illustrating their strategic vision on climate change in the context of sustainable development. "To mobilize resources for the implementation of the PBSAP, the Biodiversity Financing Initiative (BIOFIN) will contribute to closing the financing gap for the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity by identifying, accessing, combining and sequencing sources of biodiversity funding to meet national needs.  The specific objectives of the BIOFIN are to develop, test (in 36 countries) and disseminate:

•	a framework for mainstreaming biodiversity into national development and sectoral planning;
•	a methodology for assessing a country’s biodiversity financing needs; and
•	a framework for national-level biodiversity financing.

Specifically, the BIOFIN will undertake the following:
a.	policy and institutional review, the results of which were incorporated in the Philippine Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (PBSAP)
b.	public and private expenditure review to determine the level of biodiversity financing
c.	costing of the PBSAP and estimation of gap/surplus financing
d.	preparation of a biodiversity finance plan (BFP) to address the financing gap
e.	implementation of the finance solutions

planEntities.name: Assistance for Security, Peace, Integration and Recovery for Advancing Human Security in BARMM
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description:
ASPIRE is designed to promote the decommissioning and normalization aspects of the Bangsamoro peace process by addressing the challenge of personal firearms of both former MILF combatants as well as members of the private armed groups. Due to the significantly adverse ratio between decommissioned combatants and firearms “put beyond use,” this challenge has become a point of contention between the parties to the peace process. 

Moreover, this programme can be the first model case, which embodies the concept of “a new generation of human security” by systematically operationalizing a set of human-centred policy measures in post-conflict peacebuilding. In the era arising Anthropocene threats of existential nature, peacebuilding needs to respond cohesively and collectively, by accepting co-existence, to rising challenges despite differences over identity or political groups. Hence, the programme outcome aims at integrating comprehensive human security policy initiatives, raising from the ones that capture former combatants’ socio-economic needs to those that promote climate action and disaster risk reduction, which contributes to advancing the local implementation of SDGs among all the people in Mindanao who share the common future.

Civic space and engagement with civil society and the Commission on Human Rights - Philippines

planEntities.name: Promoting Conflict Prevention, Social Cohesion and Community Resilience in BARMM in the Time of COVID-19
planEntities.parentName: Output 13: Community-based conflicts reduced, community security effectively addressed, and community economic empowerment strengthened.
planEntities.description:
In light of the prevalent drivers of conflict in the region, including COVID-19, the project will seek to 1) fortify reintegration efforts for former women combatants by empowering them to engage and support peacebuilding, 2) support conflict understanding and prevention by promoting gender-responsive, inclusive, and culturally-sensitive legislation, policies and programmes, and 3) build the resilience of communities in conflict hotspots through collaborative socio-economic activities and inclusive community-based reconciliation mechanisms.    

The project will utilize a hybrid implementation strategy that will harness the relationships between the implementing agencies and the Bangsamoro authorities for institutional shifts, while utilizing the networks and community-knowledge of CSOs and local NGOs for interventions aimed at conflict-affected communities. This community-based approach, which will be supported by partners with strong community track records, will engage women and youth from conflict scenarios in the BARMM and ensure that the intervention is timely and relevant. The project will center all activities around women and youth participation and inclusion, in order to effectively drive conflict prevention, mediation and resolution at all levels of governance.

planEntities.name: Protection and Promotion of Human Rights in the Philippines
planEntities.parentName: Output 4: Social protection systems effectively shored.
planEntities.description:
This three-year UN Joint Programme for the Promotion and Protection of Human
Rights in the Philippines focuses on technical cooperation and capacity-building
“with a view to improving further the situation of human rights in the Philippines,
to provide support for the country in its continued fulfilment of its international
human rights obligations and commitments.”

The Joint Programme focuses on six key areas, under three outcomes:

Outcome One: Duty-bearers’ capacities to respect, protect and fulfill human rights are strengthened, that they increasingly apply a Human Rights Based Approach; and that there is a substantial reduction in violations as a result of increased awareness and compliance with the state’s international obligations. 
This includes:
Strengthening National Mechanisms for Implementation, Reporting and Follow-Up
A Human Rights Based Approach to Counterterrorism
A Human Rights Based Approach to Drug Control

Outcome Two: Domestic accountability mechanisms to address human rights violations are strengthened, leading to increased accountability, justice and redress for victims. 

This includes:
Improved police data gathering on alleged violations
Strengthening Domestic Accountability Mechanism

Outcome Three: Rights holders, including victims of human rights violations and abuse, and their families, are better able to claim their rights.

This includes:
Civic space and engagement with civil society and the Commission on Human Rights - Philippines

planEntities.name: Support to Bangsamoro Transition (SUBATRA)
planEntities.parentName: Output 12: Normalization and political tracks of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro effectively supported.
planEntities.description:
The Support to Bangsamoro Transition (SUBATRA) Programme is a five-year programme co-funded by the European Union (EU) and the Spanish Agency for International Cooperation and Development (AECID). The programme aims to contribute to a smooth and timely undertaking of the Bangsamoro transition by helping strengthen the capacities of the three branches of the Bangsamoro Government and its civil society. With support from SUBATRA, BARMM is hoped to create an enabling good governance environment, resulting in the achievement of policies and targets set forth by the transition plan. The SUBATRA Programme started in July 2020 and will run up until 30 June 2025.

SUBATRA focuses on four defined lines of effort: (1) Strengthening the capacity of the BTA’s executive branch superstructure to drive and coordinate key transitional policies; (2) Strengthening the capacity of the Parliament to exercise its law-making and oversight functions; (3) Strengthening the capacity of the Justice System to adjudicate litigations and improve access to justice; and (4) Strengthening the capacity of civil society to contribute to a peaceful transition to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region for Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The project takes on a people-centered approach and will upscale and expand on the multiplication and distribution of drought tolerant and early maturing seed and plant materials, replicating the model in Hela Province currently conducted, to other target provinces. Furthermore, agriculture activities such as; small livestock farming, apiculture, aquaculture and fresh food produce will be promoted and strengthened to address food and nutrition insecurity and for income generation. It is envisaged that this project will also help strengthen MSEs and SMEs, and contribute to the promotion of sustainable agricultural development within the target provinces. planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2 - PROSPERITY OUTPUT B: Markets are accessible connected at all levels
planEntities.description: The project Green Trade for Sustainable Development in Pacific Small Island Developing States of the MSG is funded from the United Nations Development Account. It is implemented in close collaboration with the MSG secretariat. The project’s main objective is to increase the capacity of the government officials of the Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) countries - Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and Solomon Islands - to identify and strengthen synergistic linkages between green trade promotion and their sustainable development in a regionally collaborative manner. The project will support the target countries to achieve coherence and cross-feeding of policy actions by (1) increasing transparency of non-tariff measures (NTMs) through NTM data collection; (2) building capacity for sustainable trade through an assessment of the voluntary sustainable standards (VSS); and (3) developing synergistic linkages between the MSG member countries. The project's actual implementation was delayed to late 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

planEntities.name: 4.1.2.9 - Enhancing political dialogue between the two Governments and the two Parliaments to ensure decisions around BPA implementation and referendum are progressed jointly
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.2 - PEACE Output 4.1.2: Service Providers' Capacity supported to provide quality services
planEntities.description:
Progress on implementation of the BPA has been slow, but steady. A target date for the referendum was set for 15 June 2019, and the BRC was established. The successful conduct of the referendum, as enshrined in the BPA and in the Constitution of PNG, will be critical to finding a lasting and peaceful solution to the conflict in Bougainville, one that is accepted by both parties. The political relationship between the GoPNG and ABG is complex but encouraging. Testament to this is the successful JSB meeting held in December 2017 and October 2018 where key resolutions were made which significantly lowered political tensions over payments and other issues related to the conduct of the referendum including the Referendum Question. 

At this critical juncture of the peacebuilding process, as the referendum target date draws near, this activity will enable the UN to maintain its support to the Bougainville peace process, continuing with timely and coordinated technical and logistical assistance to the JSB, the Joint Technical Team (JTT), and both parliaments. Women’s participation in these meetings remains low, therefore this activity will try to ensure that women are actively engaged in the political decision-making and the political dialogue processes. This activity also includes support to monitoring of the implementation of the BPA by the two parliaments, including inter-parliamentary dialogue, as well as awareness and training on critical aspects of the Agreement. 

At the JSB meeting of May 2016, the two governments endorsed moving forward with a second joint review of Bougainville’s autonomy arrangements. Throughout the consultation process for this project, the two governments requested for the UN to assist in implementing such a review, which will be done through technical and financial support. This activity holds 50 per cent of the costs of the review, with the remainder supported by GoPNG and ABG. This represents a unique opportunity for the parties to work together to assess how Bougainville’s autonomy arrangements are progressing and constitutes a tool for both governments to improve the operation of the autonomy arrangements. 

This activity will be implemented in close partnership with the range of institutions, departments and other key actors working to advance the peace process in Bougainville. This will include, among others, the Offices of both Chief Secretaries, NCOBA, DPAI as well as both parliaments. 

Key outputs from this activity are:

(i)	JSB meets regularly and its resolutions are implemented jointly by the two governments;

(ii)	The two parliaments make joint decisions on the BPA and referendum processes, including on the post-referendum period in close consultations with women and youth focused civil society organizations;

(iii)	Key government institutions with responsibilities for BPA implementation and coordination between the two governments are enabled to implement their functions effectively.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.1 - PEOPLE OUTPUT A: Policies adequately financed, implemented, monitored & evaluated
planEntities.description:
Support for learning continuity during COVID-19
UNESCO Office for the Pacific States in collaboration with HQ and some members of Global Coalition for Education conducted activities as response to COVID-19  by implementing the following activities: 
i.	Teachers’ use of applications to set up online classes at home presented by Lark (May 15, 2020); 
ii.	Curating and aligning open educational resources with national curriculum, focused on aligning open resources of Khan Academy with the national curriculum of the target countries by Library without borders (May 19, 2020); and 
iii.	Leveraging open-source Moodle to build national distance learning platforms by a team of facilitators from Moodle May 21, 2020). The impact of training was evaluated and the results is guiding the planning of further response. 
d.	Weekly on-line training on learning continuity on Best Practice in distance Education
e. Training by VHS for teachers and leaders  
PNG teachers and other stakeholders are among the participants in these webinars. Blended learning and Distance Learning are the most effective medium to provide a continuity of learning for students and is particularly crucial across the Pacific where isolation, natural disasters, pandemic, and limited resources all make access to quality education a challenge. Most of the activities were conducted as technical assistance to countries and the cost are estimated based on staff cost and estimated cost for collaborating partners.

The publication “Excellence in teaching: a review of professional standards for teachers in the Pacific SIDS” was launched on 5 October. PNG is one of the countries reviewed

UNESCO has secured GPE funding with other IAs on a PacREF Implementation Rolling Plan from 2022-2024. UNESCO support will focus on:
1. Support on EMIS enhancement and use of data;
2. Inclusion of non-cognitive skills in curricular and promotion of inclusive multi-sensory approach to education; 
3. Inclusive education.

planEntities.name: Comprehensive Condom Program Situation Analysis
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - People Output A: Policies adequately financed, implemented, monitored & evaluated
planEntities.description:
Background/Context:
In alignment with Government priorities for prevention of HIV and STI’s, Sexual Reproductive Health of Adolescent Youth and Family Planning, UNAIDS and UNFPA are supporting the development of a National Condom Programming Strategy in 2021 in partnership with the National Department of Health (NDoH) together with the National Aids Council Secretariat (NACS). 

Whilst significant progress has been made to improve access to HIV/AIDS and STIs services in many parts of the country over the recent years condom usage is still very low, especially among key populations and this continues to drive transmission of both HIV and STIs

The goal of condom programming is to ensure that sexually active persons including those at risk of HIV and STIs are motivated to use condoms, have easy access to quality condoms, and can use them consistently and correctly. In PNG this means all people are able to protect themselves, from STIs and HIV, and all people with STIs and HIV are able to access high-quality care, treatment and the support they need to maximize their health and the health of their families.

In alignment with the Government of PNG’s National STI and HIV Strategy 2018-2022 key strategic result area 3.0 Prevention and Continuum of Care, this means having the ‘right services, provided in the right places, accessed by the right people.’ The strategy importantly integrates key result areas that target prevention of and reduction in transmission of STI’s and HIV in both key/high risk populations and the general population. 

As such the first step in the development process is to undertake a comprehensive review of National Condom Programming in PNG. To do this we would like to coordinate and collaborate with the priority provinces of NCD, Morobe, Eastern Highlands and Western Highlands Provinces. This input together with contributions from relevant government of PNG departments, the identified key stakeholders from a range of sectors including civil society, local and International NGO’s, private sector supply and service providers and development partners, will ensure the review is inclusive and reflective of the diverse and collective experience of all.

National and provincial consultations, focus groups and interviews will be conducted in the provinces to better understand the experiences of successes, lessons learned and strategic priorities at a provincial level related to condom programming.

Results of the review will inform the revision and or development of the country’s future approach to National Comprehensive Condom Programming and the development of this will be aligned to Strategic Direction three under the current Papua New Guinea National STI and HIV Strategy 2018-2022.

planEntities.name: 1.2.2.26 - To improve the quality and expand coverage of health services in PNG, and thus strengthen immediate response and treatment of TB.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2 - PEOPLE OUTPUT B: Availability of equitable access to health, edu, soc. services, protection, food, WASH
planEntities.description: In collaboration with the World Bank, Government of Papua New Guinea, and the National Department of Health (NDOH), UNOPS is to implement the Emergency Tuberculosis Projects in order to improve the quality and expand coverage of health services in Western Province, Daru Island and National Capital District (NCD), and thus strengthen immediate response and treatment of TB. The programme supports an early detection of TB patients, effective treatment of drug susceptible and drug resistance TB and aims to strengthen the government system to manage the tuberculosis response. UNOPS assists NDOH in ensuring timely and efficient availability of TB diagnostics equipment and consumables including but not limited to Gen Expert Machines, mobile clinics with CAD4TB, digital X-ray machines and other laboratory and medical supplies in an attempt to support early detection and treatment of TB patients.

planEntities.name: 1.2.2.29 - Strengthening the Capacity and COVID-19 Response of Papua New Guinea Healthcare System through Emergency Procurement of Supportive Treatment Equipment and Supplies
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2 - PEOPLE OUTPUT B: Availability of equitable access to health, edu, soc. services, protection, food, WASH
planEntities.description: To respond swiftly and effectively to the rapidly evolving COVID - 19 health pandemic, UNOPS is working closely with the Government of Papua New Guinea (National Department of Health) to protect the health of people, and provide immediate assistance. UNOPS will undertake the procurement of supportive treatment equipment as well as drugs and other necessary medical supplies in order to sufficiently equip hospitals and health personnel in the priority areas and provide the much-needed care for patients.

planEntities.name: 1.2.2.32 - Papua New Guinea COVID -19 Emergency Response Project - Emergency Procurement of Medical Laboratory Equipment and Supplies
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2 - PEOPLE OUTPUT B: Availability of equitable access to health, edu, soc. services, protection, food, WASH
planEntities.description: The Papua New Guinea COVID -19 Emergency Response Project, funded by the World Bank Group (US $ 20 million) under the leadership of the National Department of Health, was developed to support the National Emergency Response Plan for COVID-19. UNOPS receives US $10.5 million to provide  emergency medical supplies, laboratory equipment, GeneExpert equipment, Polymerized Chain Reaction equipment, bio cabinets, a mobile laboratory, isolation facilities and 25,000 generic lab test kits to health centers across the country to strengthen its ability to effectively treat COVID-19 cases. UNOPS, following WHO guidance, is also providing logistical support for safe transportation of specimens within the country and Australia for COVID-19 quality testing.

planEntities.name: Support to the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) Policy 2015–2030 - Part II Papua New Guinea
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2 - PEOPLE OUTPUT B: Availability of equitable access to health, edu, soc. services, protection, food, WASH
planEntities.description: In line with the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Policy (WaSH) 2015 - 2030, the proposed Action aims to contribute towards improving the quality of life of Papua New Guineans through increased access to and utilization of safe, adequate and sustainable water supply, sanitation and improved hygiene practices in locations with high population concentrations (healthcare facilities, schools and major market places). The Action aims for: increased equitable access to safe, convenient and sustainable water supply and sanitation and improved hygiene practices; as well as long-term hygiene behavior change at the personal, household, community and institutional levels particular to urban areas that are currently under-served, in line with the national WaSH policy.

planEntities.name: 1.3.3.12 Sustainable Energy for Daru - Papua New Guinea
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3.3 - PEOPLE OUTPUT C: Citizens are aware of importance and demand /use quality services
planEntities.description:
The project’s main objectives are to develop practical and sustainable solutions to the provision of energy access in Daru, thereby introducing pathways between reliable electricity and development outcomes such as better incomes, health and increased education.

The project will assess the possibility of transitioning Daru Island to hybrid energy solutions and offer practical steps to improve energy transmission and distribution infrastructure needs. Through this project, UNOPS will conduct a detailed feasibility study of the Daru electricity mini-grid, and an assessment of the optimal technology mix in view of minimizing the use of diesel fuel generation.

This project falls under the Government-endorsed PNG Electrification Partnership (PEP), through which DFAT– alongside Japan, New Zealand, and the United States – is supporting PNG to meet its target of electrifying 70 percent of the country by 2030.

planEntities.name: 1.3.3.13  Sustainable Energy for Baiyer - Papua New Guinea
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3.3 - PEOPLE OUTPUT C: Citizens are aware of importance and demand /use quality services
planEntities.description:
The project’s main objectives are to develop practical and sustainable solutions to the provision of energy access in Mul-Baiyer  district (Baiyer River), thereby introducing pathways between reliable electricity and development outcomes such as better incomes, health and increased education.

The Bayer River solar project will assess the possibility of transitioning Mul-Baiyer  district to solar-hybrid energy solutions and offer practical steps to improve energy transmission and distribution infrastructure needs. Through this project UNOPS will conduct a detailed feasibility study for the electrification of Mul-Baiyer district. The study will cover the development of an independent hybrid mini-grid power system using solar PV and BESS (Battery energy storage system) with diesel generator backup. The option to upgrade the power generation facility to an on-grid solar system will be investigated. This option would enable excess solar power to be exported to the Ramu grid.

This project falls under the Government-endorsed PNG Electrification Partnership (PEP), through which DFAT– alongside Japan, New Zealand and the United States – is supporting PNG to meet its target of electrifying 70 percent of the country by 2030.

planEntities.name: 1.3.3.16 Sustainable Energy for Telefomin  - Papua New Guinea
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3.3 - PEOPLE OUTPUT C: Citizens are aware of importance and demand /use quality services
planEntities.description:
The project’s main objectives are to develop practical and sustainable solutions to the provision of energy access in Telefomin, thereby introducing pathways between reliable electricity and development outcomes such as better incomes, health and increased education.

Aim of this project is to undertake a scoping exercise to assess local energy needs, including the installation of PV solar panels for five (5) buildings in Telefomin, the installation of a new transformer, and a thorough audit of buildings, fuses, switchboards, power lines and power poles. In addition the project intends to provide a framework for introducing an optimal set of technologies for the local mini-grid, leading to a gradual phase out of diesel fuel generation as the primary source of energy. 

The Project will be implemented in a phased approach, with clearly identified checkpoints at the end of each phase to facilitate a review of past actions and the validation of next phase actions and budgets.

This project falls under the Government-endorsed PNG Electrification Partnership (PEP), through which DFAT– alongside Japan, New Zealand and the United States – is supporting PNG to meet its target of electrifying 70 percent of the country by 2030.

planEntities.description: Una EER proporciona una evaluación equilibrada de lo que se sabe (y lo que no se sabe) en la literatura científica sobre una intervención, un problema o una cuestión práctica, utilizando una metodología sistemática para buscar y evaluar críticamente los estudios empíricos. Sin embargo, para ser "rápida", una EER hace concesiones en relación con la amplitud, la profundidad y la exhaustividad de la búsqueda. La importancia de incorporar a la EER un enfoque que tenga en cuenta el género se debe a que la integración, la edad y la diversidad (es decir, el origen social/étnico) son variables cruciales que influyen en la trayectoria de (re)integración de los distintos grupos.

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.5 Implementadas políticas, acciones y medidas de prevención y reducción de la contaminación ambiental y de emisiones tanto en el ámbito urbano como rural.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto GCF readiness “Avanzando con un enfoque regional hacia la movilidad eléctrica en América Latina”  tiene el objetivo general de promover el avance en 14 países de la región de la descarbonización del sector transporte promoviendo la formación del ecosistema habilitante para la movilidad eléctrica. 

El proyecto tiene los siguientes objetivos especificos: 1) Se fortalece la capacidad regional para evaluar la tecnología de movilidad eléctrica en el contexto de estrategias más amplias de mitigación del cambio climático, 2) Se identifican y mejoran las políticas públicas y modelos de negocio habilitantes para ampliar la adopción de movilidad eléctrica, 3) Se fortalecen las estrategias de financiamiento climático y el pipeline nacional. 

En Paraguay las contrapartes del proyecto son la NDA- el Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible- y el Viceministerio de Transporte (MOPC- Ministerio Obras Públicas y Comunicaciones) en conjunto con la Secretaria Técnica de Planificación (STP).

Paraguay + Verde surge como reconocimiento del GCF, entidad financiadora, por la reducción de emisiones lograda por el país entre los años 2015 y 2017 por un valor de US$ 50 millones. planEntities.description:
La temporada  2020-2021 culminó en septiembre de 2021 con 17.052 hectáreas de siembra mecanizada de rubros de consumo y renta, incluyendo la habilitación de nuevas parcelas correspondientes a 1.674 hectáreas aptas para la mecanización en 43 distritos de los departamentos de San Pedro, Concepción, Canindeyú, Caazapá, Caaguazú, Alto Paraná, Horqueta, Cordillera y Guairá. 
12.846 personas fueron beneficiarios/as de DIAFPA en el 2020/2021, de las cuales el 44.2% son mujeres.
Las hectáreas trabajadas representan ingresos en comercialización por un total de 46.328.101.770 guaraníes (USD 6.914.642) en los rubros de sésamo, soja y maíz (grano seco y choclo).
28 MIPYMES rurales capacitadas en temas gerenciales, técnicos y administrativos; 50% de ellas lideradas por mujeres.
100% de las MIPYMES finalizaron el curso con planes comerciales específicos vinculados a cadenas de valor orientadas al mapeo e identificación de potenciales nichos de mercado, la diversificación de fuentes de ingresos y la construcción de redes empresariales de negocios.
Las 28 MIPYMES participantes decidieron firmar un acuerdo entre sí para la formación de una asociación nacional de segundo piso llamada Unión de productores y MIPYMES del Paraguay.
Luego de estas capacitaciones, se pudo ver un aumento en un 50% de participación de empresas locales en los llamados y/o procesos licitatorios de los proyectos.

planEntities.description:
8.000 kits de alimentos fueron distribuidos a familias de comunidades indígenas a través del Instituto Paraguayo del Indígena (INDI). 
Familias damnificadas en diferentes puntos del país fueron atendidas con la entrega de 38.500 kits de alimentos, 33.330 chapas de zinc y 3.330 colchones a través de la Secretaría de Emergencia Nacional (SEN).
Entrega de medicamentos y equipos biomédicos al Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social en Alto Paraná. Entre ellos, se destacan: 
38.000 unidades de Midazolam, 22.000 unidades de Besilato de Atracurio, 3.500 unidades de Noradrenalina, 2.000 unidades de Enoxaparina, 2.000 unidades de Ceftriaxona, 1.200 unidades de Levofloxacina, 1.200 unidades de Vancomicina  y 200 unidades de Colistina.  
12 ventiladores pulmonares, 8 camas eléctricas para terapias, 8 flujometros y 8 reguladores para oxígeno medicinal, 8 equipos generadores de alto flujo, 2 carros de paro, 1 electrocardiógrafo, 5.000 sets para bomba de infusión, 10 monitores multiparamétricos, 1 cardiodesfibrilador, 8 aspiradores portátiles de secreciones. 
Entrega de 14.840 unidades de placas petri a la Red Nacional de Laboratorios del Ministerio de Salud Pública y Bienestar Social, los cuales se utilizan para cultivar muestras en pruebas diagnósticas que beneficiarán a unas 15.000 personas aproximadamente.

planEntities.name: Wash and Health Promotion, Sensitization and Awareness on COVID-19 and other Communicable Diseases in the EAC Region
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3: National and sub-national institutions and communities have enhanced resilience and increased technical, institutional, and individual capacities to prevent, prepare and respond to shocks and emergencies
planEntities.description: The overall goal of this project is to increase awareness and enhance health and hygiene protective behaviours and practices to prevent the spread of zoonotic and water-borne infectious diseases including COVID-19, in selected high-risk areas along transport and water way corridors in Partner States (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi and Rwanda and South Sudan). The project will also install fixed handwashing facilities in each selected site. It is estimated to reach more than 1 million of individuals with health and hygiene promotion initiatives and to install 19 fixed handwashing facilities. This project is aligned with the EAC COVID-19 Response Plan (2020), the IOM Strategic Response and Recovery Plan launched in April 2021 and all health relevant regional plans of concerning stakeholders and agencies. Furthermore, the regional programme is contributing to the achievement of the regional migration strategy for East and Horn of Africa addressing the health component.

planEntities.name: National capacities supported and strengthened to effectively prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons in accordance with international standards and best practices, and to achieve sustainable impact through implementation of the National Action Plan against TiP
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description:
UNODC has been engaged with the Saudi Human Rights Commission (HRC), as chair entity of the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking (NCCHT) since February 2020 in a multi-phased project of technical cooperation in the field of combating trafficking in persons (TiP). Therethrough, UNODC supports national efforts spearheaded by the HRC/NCCHT in preventing and combating TiP through a victim-centred approach that upholds the rights of trafficked and potential victims to protection, support, and care in line with international standards and norms and best practices.
Achievements under Phase I (February 2020 - August 2022) include the launch of the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) on 31 March 2020 which is currently managed by a central team in Riyadh together with 13 sub-teams in all regions across the Kingdom for effective coordination in dealing with TiP cases; the establishment of TiP specialized courts in all regions of the Kingdom with 124 prosecutors; the creation of the first-ever anti-TiP specialized Prosecution Unit on 30 July 2022; the creation of a specialized TiP Data Management Team; the development and adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat TiP (2021-2023); the legislative review and reform of the Kafala sponsorship system; and the delivery of 33 capacity-building activities that benefited over 1,600 officials within government entities, institutions, and CSOs.
Phase II (3 years, launched in March 2023) focuses on sustaining the outcomes of Phase I and further supporting the Kingdom through the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) against TiP. Activities include reviewing and updating the NRM; developing the electronic format of the NRM to support the availability, accuracy, and timeliness of TiP-related data; building monitoring and evaluation capacities for the implementation of the NAP; raising awareness of labour dispute committees, the media, the private sector and through religious authorities; conducting legislative and policy reviews; strengthening national capacities of law enforcement and criminal justice for the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of TiP cases; supporting the creation of a national training resource/hub on preventing and combating TiP; and promoting the creation of partnerships for knowledge and best practices exchange.

planEntities.name: 2022 Project AMR MPTF “One Health” du SENEGAL
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1.3 - D’ici 2023, les institutions nationales ont la capacité de formuler et de mettre en œuvre une stratégie de mise en synergie des politiques sectorielles en faveur du développement de chaines de valeur
planEntities.description:
Le programme MPTF permet une consolidation des effort multisectoriel et multidisciplinaire sur la RAM dans une approche OH ; sous la direction du HCSSM et avec le soutien de la coopération tripartite représentée par le groupe technique RAM.
Avec son approche OH, le programme permet :
-	la mise en œuvre et/ou l'amélioration des politiques de lutte contre la RAM
l'harmonisation de la collecte des données, la réalisation d'antibiogrammes, l'analyse des données...
-	la prise de décision et l'amélioration de la coordination ;
-	l'approche intégrée et inclusive des différents secteurs dans le cadre du concept d'OH, qui permettra d'améliorer les résultats dans la lutte contre la RAM ;
-	une meilleure visibilité des données de la RAM dans tous les secteurs.

planEntities.description:
The ILO with funding from the EU through the Opportunity Salone Programme piloted a total of seven interventions; three in the cassava value chain, two in vegetables value chain and two in palm oil value chain in Port Loko, Bombali, Kenema and Bo districts to help SME partners and farmers improve their productivity and develop new products through the use of improved technologies. For example: 
1. Imam Moiwo Palm Oil Plantation was supported to use improved palm oil processing presser to produce high quality palm oil. This improved presser machine is able to squeeze more oil palm from the fruit thereby increasing palm oil production by over 30%.  
2. SEDMO Construction, Agriculture and General Services was encouraged to invest in the processing of palm kernel oil by collecting and processing the kernel nut, which is usually considered as waste after the extraction of palm oil. Entering into cost-sharing partnership arrangement with the Opportunity Salone Programme, SEDMO upgraded its processing machines and equipment to improved/ mechanised palm kernel cracker and processing machines, significantly increasing both the quality and quantity of palm kernel oil production. 
3. Bokatala Limited provides market linkage by buying and selling onion from groups of farmers in Lungi, Port Loko District. Over the years, they suffered huge losses due to poor storage and processing facilities, causing spoilage and often force them to auction their onion below market prices. Through the Opportunity Salone Programme, ILO supported Bokatala to establish an onion processing and storage facility that is equipped with a solar system. With this facility, Bokatala is able to process and preserve onion for longer periods before supplying the market. This has greatly reduced losses and offers Bokatala the leverage to barging better price for their onion.

planEntities.description:
Adamaris gari processing industry in Makeni, Bombali District received support to produce high value cassava flour for the backery industry. The enterprise worked with about 75 outgrower cassava farmer groups by providing them with tillage services, extension services, necessary farm inputs and ready market for their harvest. The outgrower farmers in turn supplied Adamaris with cassava, which is the main raw material used in the production of cassava flour. These farmers have since received entrepreneurship training from training of trainers (TOT) business coaches trained by Opportunity Salone to help them treat farming as a business. Staff of Adamaris have received training on occupational Safety and health in the workplace and productivity improvement. In addition, the factory has undergone a major upgrade to improve its capacity to produce more.
In addition, ILO conducted several capacity building workshops/ training programmes for district council staff, SME contractors, SME business enterises and rural women, youths amd persons with disabilities. These trainings include the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), Financial Literacy and MYCOP. In addition, ILO sponsored exchange visits through which government officials, including the Minister of Works and Public Assets, staff of Public-private Unit under the Vice President's Office, and SLRA visited other countries to learn about feeder road maintenence mechanisms that uses sustainable public-private financing.

planEntities.name: 1.1.1.8 - Build the capacity of youth and young women in agricultural production and value addition, through vocational skills and linking them to employment with agro-processing companies
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - Farmers especially women, youth and other vulnerable groups to have equal access to information and decision-making opportunities on land tenure, knowledge of improved agricultural practices, inputs, technology, financial services, linkage to markets, leveraging appropriate technologies and innovations
planEntities.description:
Adamaris gari processing industry in Makeni, Bombali District received support to produce high value cassava flour for the backery industry. The enterprise worked with about 75 outgrower cassava farmer groups by providing them with tillage services, extension services, necessary farm inputs and ready market for their harvest. The outgrower farmers in turn supplied Adamaris with cassava, which is the main raw material used in the production of cassava flour. These farmers have since received entrepreneurship training from training of trainers (TOT) business coaches trained by Opportunity Salone to help them treat farming as a business. Staff of Adamaris have received training on occupational Safety and health in the workplace and productivity improvement. In addition, the factory has undergone a major upgrade to improve its capacity to produce more.
In addition, ILO conducted several capacity building workshops/ training programmes for district council staff, SME contractors, SME business enterises and rural women, youths amd persons with disabilities. These trainings include the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), Financial Literacy and MYCOP. In addition, ILO sponsored exchange visits through which government officials, including the Minister of Works and Public Assets, staff of Public-private Unit under the Vice President's Office, and SLRA visited other countries to learn about feeder road maintenence mechanisms that uses sustainable public-private financing.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.6 - Improve the delivery of gender sensitive STEM education in Sierra Leone, through the use of Micro Science kits.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1 - Children, adolescents, young women and youth have increased access to comprehensive quality education services with improved learning outcomes
planEntities.description:
In order to reverse the negative trend in STEM education in Sierra Leone, UNESCO will join efforts with FEST Didactic  to implement a project tagged “Strengthening STEM delivery for sustainable development” in Sierra Leone based on existing training concepts and materials for upper secondary/tertiary levels with a special focus on women and girls 
 to achieve the following.
• Teacher training for effective and learner-friendly delivery of STEM teaching 
• Development and provision of STEM teaching facilities including Micro science kits.
• Mentoring of students; especially women and girls for STEM professions 
• Provision of adequate STEM teaching learning materials, equipments and laboratory  
• Digitization of curriculum with priority to Higher Education

planEntities.name: 3.1.3.1 - Support to review, update, and development of laws, policies, strategies, guidelines and tools that improve access, quality and patient safety toward achieving UHC
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.3 - The population has access to integrated people-centred health services to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC)
planEntities.description:
The team sustained its prioritization of the creation of an enabling policy and legislative environment for the attainment of the three transformative results in Sierra Leone. Following the enactment of the Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Act in January 2023, UN Agencies supported the Government in the rolling out of an implementation plan for the enforcement of the Act, which included building and strengthening the capacity of line ministries that are central to the implementation of the Act.

Further, four national strategies aimed at advancing reproductive health were developed; these are the RMNCAH Extended strategy, Supply Chain Strategy, the National Fistula Strategy and the National Strategic Policy on elimination of cervical cancer and accompanying Clinical Guidelines. A review of the National Strategy for the reduction of teenage pregnancy and child marriage was also undertaken to inform the formulation of the next strategy. UN also supported the launch of Sierra Leone’s rights-based family planning commitments made through the FP2030 partnership. Additionally, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Midwifery Census was undertaken which is expected to guide interventions and policy decision towards strengthening the Midwifery health work force in Sierra Leone.

planEntities.description:
The team sustained its prioritization of the creation of an enabling policy and legislative environment for the attainment of the three transformative results in Sierra Leone. Following the enactment of the Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Act in January 2023, UN Agencies supported the Government in the rolling out of an implementation plan for the enforcement of the Act, which included building and strengthening the capacity of line ministries that are central to the implementation of the Act.

Further, four national strategies aimed at advancing reproductive health were developed; these are the RMNCAH Extended strategy, Supply Chain Strategy, the National Fistula Strategy and the National Strategic Policy on elimination of cervical cancer and accompanying Clinical Guidelines. A review of the National Strategy for the reduction of teenage pregnancy and child marriage was also undertaken to inform the formulation of the next strategy. UN also supported the launch of Sierra Leone’s rights-based family planning commitments made through the FP2030 partnership. Additionally, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Midwifery Census was undertaken which is expected to guide interventions and policy decision towards strengthening the Midwifery health work force in Sierra Leone.

planEntities.description:
(a) Regulatory framework for renewable energy based mini-grids related to the legal provisions, cost recovery and tariff regulation developed which gets approval from the parliament. 
(b) Support Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to develop guidelines for minigrids and assit operators to secure Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) licence.
(c) Implement contractual mechanisms to enable Public Private Partnership agreement (PPP) with private operators so that the private sector invests (target-USD 13.9 Million), operates and maintains mini-grid based electricity generation and distribution.
(d) Provide technical assistance (TA) and institutional development (capacity building) to both government authorities and private sector stakeholders as part of the holistic approach to facilitate mini-grid development and long term sustainable operations. (UNOPS and UNIDO)

planEntities.name: 3.1.4.2 - Installation of Renewable Energy based Mini-grids for electrification of CHCs, schools, households and commercials:
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.4 - Population has improved access to renewable energy in rural areas
planEntities.description:
(a) Expansion of 50 previously constructed CHC solar power stations and installation of distribution networks in each village, creating independent mini-grids which can together provide around 7,000 households (47,740 HH members) and 400 businesses with electricity.
(b) Installation of 44 much larger mini-grids through a mixture of private sector investment by the operators and grant financing raching out to 21,000 HHs (143,220 HH members) and 500 businesses. Private operators to use their financing to construct the power generation facilities, complemented by distribution networks constructed by UNOPS.
(c) Connect 44 CHCs to minigrid based electrification system and provide improved service to around 180,000 patients .

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1 - Farmers especially women, youth and other vulnerable groups to have equal access to information and decision-making opportunities on land tenure, knowledge of improved agricultural practices, inputs, technology, financial services, linkage to markets, leveraging appropriate technologies and innovations
planEntities.description:
The ILO with funding from the EU through the Opportunity Salone Programme piloted a total of seven interventions; three in the cassava value chain, two in vegetables value chain and two in palm oil value chain in Port Loko, Bombali, Kenema and Bo districts to help SME partners and farmers improve their productivity and develop new products through the use of improved technologies. For example: 
1. Imam Moiwo Palm Oil Plantation was supported to use improved palm oil processing presser to produce high quality palm oil. This improved presser machine is able to squeeze more oil palm from the fruit thereby increasing palm oil production by over 30%.  
2. SEDMO Construction, Agriculture and General Services was encouraged to invest in the processing of palm kernel oil by collecting and processing the kernel nut, which is usually considered as waste after the extraction of palm oil. Entering into cost-sharing partnership arrangement with the Opportunity Salone Programme, SEDMO upgraded its processing machines and equipment to improved/ mechanised palm kernel cracker and processing machines, significantly increasing both the quality and quantity of palm kernel oil production. 
3. Bokatala Limited provides market linkage by buying and selling onion from groups of farmers in Lungi, Port Loko District. Over the years, they suffered huge losses due to poor storage and processing facilities, causing spoilage and often force them to auction their onion below market prices. Through the Opportunity Salone Programme, ILO supported Bokatala to establish an onion processing and storage facility that is equipped with a solar system. With this facility, Bokatala is able to process and preserve onion for longer periods before supplying the market. This has greatly reduced losses and offers Bokatala the leverage to barging better price for their onion.

planEntities.description: The project aims to support the establishment of a basis for the implementation of the Busha Cattle Breeding Genetic Conservation Program in the Stara Planina area. Support for the conservation and development of the breed would contribute to the income improvement opportunities for women and men, implementation of the Global Plan of Action for Animal Genetic Resources, adopted in 2007.

planEntities.name: 1.2.2.5 FAO- Increasing national capacities to assess the risk of diffuse agricultural soil pollution
planEntities.parentName: Serbia protects ecosystems, natural resources and biodiversity
planEntities.description: Main objective of the project is to increase national capacities for diffuse soil pollution management and proper use of remediation practices in the fields under agricultural production. To conduct research study on diffuse soil pollution at the selected region of Serbia and subsequently organize training for farmers including men and women in this region to decrease the risk of soil pollution and improve pesticide and fertilizer management. To identify the soil substances whose use causes special concern and chemicals that are long-term organic pollutants and improve monitoring of pesticide and fertilizer application contributing to the health protection of women and men.

planEntities.parentName: A greater share of economic activities transition towards circularity: changing how we produce, consume and trade
planEntities.description: Project will further strengthen institutional and technical capacities of the Republic of Serbia and various stakeholders in mobilizing green investments. It will improve the GCF country programme, and establish a solid baseline for the identification and development of bankable funding proposals for larger investments, taking into account country priorities, capacities of partner institutions and other processes in the country. The project will take into account gender issues during the development of the plans and target at least 30% of women as direct beneficiaries.

planEntities.name: 1.3.1.5 UNOPS- EU Support to Local Development Programme - EU PRO+
planEntities.parentName: Local development strategies adopt an area-based approach
planEntities.description:
EU PRO PLUS focuses its work on enhancing territorial development management, supporting economic growth, and improving social infrastructure and cohesion. 
Within efforts to Improve development planning and introduce integrated territorial investment concept, the Programme supports development of Sustainable Urban Development (SUD) and Integrated Territorial Investment (ITI) strategies using EU territorial mechanisms. The key beneficiaries are local self-governments and regional development agencies, along with institutions at institutions at local and regional levels. The Programme also supports design of the national model for integrated and sustainable territorial development at the national level, in partnership with the Ministry of European Integrations. 

In 2023, development of 12 territorial strategies is planned to be completed, and a grant scheme for implementation of projects deriving from these strategies launched. Additionally, EU PRO Plus will implement a number of capacity building activities for stakeholders at all levels. 

Equal opportunities and representation of women in activities related to capacity building are supported by inclusion elements of gender equality in the Plan for building the capacity of national institutions for the introduction of instruments of integral territorial development.

planEntities.name: 1.3.4.9 UNOPS- EU Support to Local Development Programme - EU PRO Plus
planEntities.parentName: Women and men have access to more decent job opportunities and fair competitive trade
planEntities.description:
EU PRO PLUS focuses its work on enhancing territorial development management, supporting economic growth, and improving social infrastructure and cohesion. 
Within efforts to achieve Enhanced economic growth in targeted municipalities, the Programme supports development of economic infrastructure which shall facilitate investments and enable job creation, contributes to enhanced competitiveness of businesses through activities implemented by business support organisations, and provides direct assistance to businesses and business start-ups to procure equipment and introduce services which will contribute to creation of new jobs and strengthening of value chains.
In 2023, support to 16 projects implemented by business support organisations will be concluded, while at least 100 enterprises micro and small enterprises will be supported directly through grants. Additionally, in mid-2023 the Programme will extend support to business start-ups owned by women and youth.
Equal opportunities are promoted through all activities, while support to women is stimulated through selection criteria by additional points awarded to companies owned by women or those that already employ women and have a plan to create additional jobs for them. The activities also promote corporate social responsibility as a mandatory part of direct support to enterprises. Additionally, gender mainstreaming in infrastructure will be considered to ensure that experiences of women and men, girls and boys, are an integral dimension of the planning process.

planEntities.description: (UNICEF) Depuis 2020, il existe une collaboration avec  26 radios communautaires par l’intermédiaire des Directions Régionales de la Planification (DRP) dans les 5 régions du pays. Les programmes des radios ont mis un accent particulier sur la pandémie et ses conséquences. Le ministère de santé a bénéficié d'un appui spécial qui a permis de contracter 10 radios à Lomé afin d’assurer la couverture complète du pays par les radios dans la lutte contre COVID-19. Les émissions réalisées et les spots diffusés chaque année touchent environ 5.008.000 personnes.

planEntities.name: Ensuring decent work and reducing vulnerabilities for women and children in the context of labor migration in Southeast Asia (TRIANGLE, PROTECT, Safe and Fair)
planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description:
This suboutput comprises of multiple ILO projects:
1. TRIANGLE in ASEAN (2011 - 2025)
2. TRIANGLE Partnerships (2026 - 2031)
3. Realizing Women Migrant Workers' Rights and Opportunities in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations - Safe and Fair (2018 -2023)
4. Ensuring decent work and reducing vulnerabilities for women and children in the context of labour migration in Southeast Asia - PROTECT (2024 - 2027) 
5. SEA on Labour Migration in the Fishing Sector (S2SR SEA Phase II, 2020 - 2024)
6. Ship to Shore Rights in SEA: Safe Migration for Decent Work in the Blue Economy (S2SR SEA Phase III, 2025 - 2028)

Focus areas for the ILO's labour migration programming include protecting and promoting of the rights of women and men migrant workers including on fair recruitment and working conditions; contributing to economic development and inclusive growth – in particular labour mobility, skills development and recognition, and increasing development impact; contributing to climate resilience; reintegration; advocacy (with UNHCR) on labour market access for refugees and forcibly displaced persons; supporting national and regional dialogues on labour migration; and improving harmonised data collection and statistics.

planEntities.name: State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women empowerment to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level to promote women peace and cybersecurity and digital literacy.
planEntities.parentName: Good governance, rule of law and social contract are enhanced for SDG acceleration
planEntities.description:
In 2023, following the advice of UN Women, the agency combined two sub-outputs and modified the sub-output statement accordingly. The original sub-output (SOU 7) aimed to enhance the knowledge and mechanisms of state and non-state actors to promote gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $60,000, but only $20,000 was available, and the expenditure was $56,426. To address this inconsistency, the available resource amount was adjusted to $56,426.

The second sub-output (SOU 11) focused on the Royal Thai Government (RTG) acquiring knowledge on gender-responsive approaches to prioritize gender equality and women's empowerment in budgeting and procurement at the local and national levels. The allocated resources for 2022 were $10,000, with $5,000 available and $2,000 expended.

Now, these two sub-outputs have been integrated into a revised sub-output (Revised SOU 7). The revised statement emphasizes that state and non-state actors have increased their knowledge and mechanisms to advance gender equality and integrate gender responsiveness at the national and local levels. Additionally, it includes a specific focus on gender-responsive budgeting as a means to promote the prioritization of gender equality and women's empowerment.


The original sub-output statement (SOU 7): State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and women's empowerment  and to integrate/mainstream gender-responsive approach in their policy or operational framework at national and local level
The original sub-output statement (SOU 11): The Royal Thai Government (RTG) gain the knowledge on gender-responsive approach to advance gender responsive budgeting/procurement at local and national level to ensure that gender equality and women's empowerment are prioritized.

The integrated sub-output is now (Revised SOU 7): "State and non-state actors have increased knowledges and mechanisms to advance and localize gender equality and to integrate/mainstream gender responsiveness at national and local level including gender-responsive budgeting to promote prioritization of gender equality and women empowerment. "

planEntities.description: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) is a collaborative initiative among five UN Agencies (UNEP, UNDP, UNIDO, UNITAR, and ILO) to support countries in transforming their economies towards green and inclusive models, aligned with the 2030 SDG Agenda and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. In Thailand, PAGE is led by UNIDO and the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC).Key Achievements:1) Greening National Policies and Strategies:Green Economy Policy Scoping Report: Highlights the reforms needed for decarbonization, promoting the Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) model, renewable energy, green finance, digitalization, and capacity development.Green and Inclusive Economic Recovery Policy Assessment Report: Recommends integrating SDGs, Nationally Determined Contributions, and BCG Economic Policy into government projects and budgeting. Developed training modules focused on green and inclusive development, measuring progress with green indicators, and principles of green industry and jobs.2) Carbon Cap and Trade for a Decarbonized Economy:Macroeconomic Planning for Green and Climate Policy Options Report and Training: Strengthens government capacity to make informed economic policy decisions, assessing socio-economic impacts of carbon tax, energy efficiency, renewable energy investments, and bio-circular-green economy investments.Emission Trading Scheme Development: Promotes national-level carbon market development, analyzing carbon pricing mechanisms and socio-economic impacts. Workshops and workplans were developed for implementing ETS in Thailand, covering all aspects from regulation to capacity building.3) Digitalization of Financing Mechanism for Sustainable Waste Management:Based on assessments and collaborations with the Department of Local Administration, mobile applications are being developed to enhance local government capacities in managing waste cycles sustainably.
