planEntities.name: Country capacity strengthened for health emergency preparedness, prevention, detection and response through enhanced health security systems, emergency operations, risk communication, community engagement, mass gathering preparedness, and implementation of the International Health Regulations (IHR).
planEntities.parentName: Capacities for low carbon society, resilience, post-COVID 19 and disaster recovery with capability to adapt and reduce the risks of disasters are enabled and strengthened.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Improving national capability to prepare, prevent, detect and respond to public health emergencies (PHE)" (ID 82366); "Regional health security and national risk assessment capacities strengthened" (ID 207683); "Emergency response operations and mass gathering preparedness supported" (ID 207684); "National health security capacities and IHR systems strengthened" (ID 207685); and "Risk communication and community-based emergency preparedness strengthened" (ID 207686). WHO supported the establishment of the Secretariat for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED) and strengthened national surveillance by integrating the Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment (QIRA) tool into the Standard Operating Procedures of National Situation Awareness Teams. Emergency response capacity was bolstered through procurement of essential supplies for the cholera response to spillover cases from Myanmar, the provision of shelter and psychosocial support materials for the border conflict response, and support to the Ministry of Public Health for mass gathering preparedness during the SEA Games. National preparedness was further enhanced through implementation of the Hospital Safety Index across Ministry of Public Health hospitals, strengthened provincial Emergency Operations Center capacities, upgraded Event-Based and genomic Surveillance for respiratory pathogens in high-tourism locations, and establishment of the National IHR Authority. Risk communication was advanced by piloting the Information Environment Assessment to address infodemics and by strengthening linkages between the Public Health Emergency Operations Center's risk communication channels and Village and Migrant Health Volunteer networks.

planEntities.name: Digital health and innovation advanced to improve service delivery through interoperable health information systems, strengthened health data governance, and scalable digital solutions that address emerging health challenges.
planEntities.parentName: Digital transformation, digital inclusion, and innovation for human capital optimization are enabled.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "Advance digital health and innovation for equitable service delivery" (ID 182897) and "Digital Health Platforms and Health Information System (HIS) is strengthened" (ID 82410). The digital health ecosystem was strengthened through improved governance, legislation and compliance with Health Information Exchange standards and cybersecurity protocols, alongside support to the Global Initiative on Digital Health architecture and promotion of safe, equitable use of artificial intelligence. A national strategy to standardize health data collection across public and private facilities was introduced, complemented by an Open Data approach enabling real-time public health data sharing among researchers and policymakers, as well as development of interoperability standards, health data governance frameworks, and virtual hospital and telemedicine platforms.

planEntities.name: Health and well-being improved through a transformed workforce and integrated action on the social, behavioural and environmental determinants of health,  including evidence-based parenting, violence prevention, road safety, healthy ageing, healthy cities, digital mental health services and NCD risk reduction.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Facilitate and enhance integrated care for older people through the use of mobile health technology" (ID 82412); "Progressive development of legislation on control of marketing of food and non-alcoholic beverage for children" (ID 82467); "Health policies and collective action against NCDs... (Strategies 1 and 2)" (ID 82468); "Evidence-based parenting and violence prevention programs scaled up" (ID 207692); and "Urban governance for Healthy Cities strengthened" (ID 207695). Integrated care for older people was advanced through mobile health technology, complementing broader NCD policy work that promoted increased investment in NCDs through targeted communication strategies based on Thailand's scale-up findings, aligned with NCD Strategies 1 and 2. Legislative development on marketing controls for food and non-alcoholic beverages targeting children was progressed through technical support and policy advocacy, contributing to the wider NCD risk-reduction agenda. Child protection and development were fostered through the scale-up of evidence-based parenting programmes and high-level advocacy, complemented by the 2nd global survey on Violence Against Children to generate data for policy formulation. Urban health governance was strengthened through capacity building for local authorities, with the Healthy Cities approach recognized through awards to four Thai cities for their commitment to health-promoting urban environments.

planEntities.name: Disease burden reduced through strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship, accelerated neglected tropical disease elimination efforts, and implementation of evidence-informed policies and multisectoral actions for noncommunicable disease prevention and control.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates eight former sub-outputs: "Promoting evidence-based advocacy and implementing robust health and economic monitoring mechanisms for managing NCDs... (Strategies 3, 4 & 5)" (ID 82469); "Improve the quality and reach of essential health services" (ID 182895); "National workforce strategies strengthened and National Health Assembly resolution 2024 on transforming workforce for healthy society" (ID 207682); "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) surveillance and stewardship enhanced" (ID 207687); "Neglected Tropical Disease elimination and treatment supported" (ID 207690); "Mental health promotion, surveillance, and digital services expanded" (ID 207691); "Healthy ageing and integrated care for older people promoted" (ID 207696); and "NCD risk factor reduction policies and enforcement mechanisms strengthened" (ID 207697). Multisectoral action on NCDs was enhanced through improved partnerships facilitated by the UN Thematic Working Group, aligned with NCD Strategies 3, 4 and 5, complementing the workforce strengthening achieved through enhanced HRH provider registries and a landscape analysis of the community non-professional workforce. Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) management was advanced through co-hosting a Multi-Country Meeting on AMR and Primary Health Care, a Point Prevalence Survey on healthcare-associated infections across 100 hospitals, and development of a national AMR burden methodology and antimicrobial stewardship tools. Progress towards elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases was supported through provision of diagnostic test strips for Lymphatic Filariasis and sustained treatment of leprosy cases through procurement and distribution of essential medication. Mental health services were expanded through the nationwide scale-up of the "Step-by-Step" digital application, the "Tor term Jai" platform, and the WHO LIVE LIFE suicide prevention package, alongside capacity building through the 3rd International Mental Health Workforce Training. Healthy ageing was promoted through implementation of the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach with Siriraj Hospital, alongside advocacy to address social isolation among older persons. NCD risk factor reduction was advanced through sustained advocacy for "Best Buys" policies, including health taxes, e-cigarette bans, food reformulation, Milk Code enforcement, and alcohol control policy assessment.

planEntities.name: Migrant health equity advanced through strengthened migrant health management systems, improved health literacy, and multisectoral action to support inclusive and people-centred health services for migrants and non-national populations.
planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs that together form WHO's Migrant Health Initiative: "Strengthening migrant health management system" (ID 82490) and "Improving the health literacy among migrants and their communities" (ID 82497), which receive an equal proportion of funding. Access to health services for migrants was improved through advancement of the Migrant Health Strategy and expansion of the HINT data platform to include migrant populations, alongside strengthened health literacy among migrants and their communities, including workplaces, through policy advocacy, networking, social movement and policy research to advance health equity for migrants and non-national populations. Operational capacity was further strengthened through field visits, training and improved human resource management for migrant health.

planEntities.name: Thailand’s role in shaping key global health agendas and advancing sustainable health development strengthened through enhanced leadership, knowledge sharing, evidence-informed decision-making, and international collaboration, while supporting implementation of national health priorities and Country Cooperation Strategy outcomes.
planEntities.parentName: Good governance, rule of law and social contract are enhanced for SDG acceleration
planEntities.description: This sub-output is carried forward from the former sub-output: "Promoting the demonstrated collective leadership and contributions of Thailand in global health" (ID 90382), under the CCS EnLIGHT priority area of the 2022-2026 Country Cooperation Strategy. It enhances Team Thailand's collective capacity for international engagement in global health governance, focusing on two core functions: advancing key global health agendas and supporting other Country Cooperation Strategy programmes and partner agencies. This is achieved through four strategic actions: evidence generation, capacity development, international engagement, and knowledge management, including the establishment of resource centres and platforms and effective policy communication to support policy decisions.

planEntities.name: Road safety strengthened, with a particular focus on motorcycle users, through a national master plan, strengthened road safety cooperation mechanisms, laws and policy implementation, and enhanced capacity of stakeholders and actors to address road safety challenges.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "A national master plan for motorcycle safety developed" (ID 199373) and "Road safety enhanced with a particular focus on motorcycle users... (RSF)" (ID 210025). WHO supported the development of Thailand's first national Master Plan focused specifically on motorized two-wheeler safety, in response to the country's high rate of road traffic fatalities, of which nearly 80 per cent involve motorized two-wheelers, in partnership with the Department of Disease Control (DDC) and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation. This was complemented by road safety initiatives advanced through engagement with the Parliamentary Advisory Committee, implementation of the UN Road Safety Fund project, and improved hospital injury surveillance systems to inform road safety interventions.

planEntities.name: By the end of 2026, Thailand will have fully integrated Inclusive Green Economy principles into the national development plan and BCG model by implementing evidence-based sectoral reforms. (PAGE)
planEntities.parentName: Green growth: An inclusive and sustainable economic growth premised on Thailand’s bio-circular-green model is supported.
planEntities.description: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) is a collaborative initiative among five UN Agencies (UNEP, UNDP, UNIDO, UNITAR, and ILO) to support countries in transforming their economies towards green and inclusive models, aligned with the 2030 SDG Agenda and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change. In Thailand, PAGE is led by UNIDO and the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC).Key Achievements:1) Greening National Policies and Strategies:Green Economy Policy Scoping Report: Highlights the reforms needed for decarbonization, promoting the Bio-Circular-Green (BCG) model, renewable energy, green finance, digitalization, and capacity development.Green and Inclusive Economic Recovery Policy Assessment Report: Recommends integrating SDGs, Nationally Determined Contributions, and BCG Economic Policy into government projects and budgeting. Developed training modules focused on green and inclusive development, measuring progress with green indicators, and principles of green industry and jobs.2) Carbon Cap and Trade for a Decarbonized Economy:Macroeconomic Planning for Green and Climate Policy Options Report and Training: Strengthens government capacity to make informed economic policy decisions, assessing socio-economic impacts of carbon tax, energy efficiency, renewable energy investments, and bio-circular-green economy investments.Emission Trading Scheme Development: Promotes national-level carbon market development, analyzing carbon pricing mechanisms and socio-economic impacts. Workshops and workplans were developed for implementing ETS in Thailand, covering all aspects from regulation to capacity building.3) Digitalization of Financing Mechanism for Sustainable Waste Management:Based on assessments and collaborations with the Department of Local Administration, mobile applications are being developed to enhance local government capacities in managing waste cycles sustainably.

planEntities.name: Support for Improvement of Locust Management
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2. National institutions, local communities, including women, children and vulnerable groups, and entrepreneurs/economic sectors are technically prepared for disasters and disaster response
planEntities.description: The central concept of the project "Support for Improvement of Locust Management " is locust preventive strategy, recognized worldwide as the only one able to adequately and sustainably address locust issues. It consists in close monitoring of locust populations in their habitats to allow early warning and early reaction with well-targeted control operations using updated techniques while reducing risks for human health and environment. The project includes six outputs. Under the first one, regional cooperation will be developed thanks to the circulation of locust information exchange of experience, joint activities and coordination of activities, both in the framework of the project and of the “Programme to improve national and regional locust management in CCA” as a whole. The second output is that national capacities will be strengthened by improving and updating knowledge and techniques (Training-of-Trainers, exposure visits) and by making available practical guidelines on different locust issues. Under the third output, locust monitoring will be improved thanks to the delivery of transportation means, positioning, communication and survey equipment as well as the introduction and/or support provided for the use of the Automated System for Data Collection (ASDC) and national Geographical Information System (GIS) named “Caucasus and Central Asia Locust Management System (CCALM)”, allowing collection and analysis of standardized field locust data. The fourth output is that locust control operations will be supported thanks to the delivery of vehicles, tractors and sprayers of different modifications; alternatives to conventional pesticides such as Insect Growth Regulators and biopesticides will also be promoted. The fifth output concerns risk reduction for human health and the environment: this will include mitigating impact of locust control operations on human health and the environment through delivery of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), a pilot activity on empty containers management and preparing extension documentation for local staff; it will also comprise the monitoring of impact of locust control operations through supporting Human Health and Environment Monitoring Teams and delivering health and environment monitoring equipment. The last and sixth input aims at developing awareness of the local populations and decision-makers to locust issues by producing informational, communication and advocacy materials. The project will focus on the provinces that are the most affected by locusts in the six Central Asian countries.

planEntities.description: The overall objective of the project "Integrated natural resources management in drought-prone and salt-affected agricultural production landscapes " is to scale up integrated natural resources management (INRM) in drought prone and salt affected agricultural production landscapes in the Central Asian countries and Turkey. This will be done through scaling up of sustainable management practices that minimize pressures and negative impacts on natural resources that reduce risks and vulnerability and, enhance capacity of rural communities to cope with or adapt to drought and salinity. In particular, adoption of integrated landscape management approaches and INRM practices should help stabilize and even reverse trends of soil salinization, reduce erosion, improve water capture and retention, increase the sequestration of carbon, and reduce loss of agrobiodiversity, thereby reducing the desertification trend in terms of extent and severity. The project objective will be achieved during a five-year period through four project components. It is structured as a program with one multi-country component addressing shared priorities at multi-county level (Component 1), two components at national level ensuring national implementation in selected production landscapes/land use systems (Component 2 and Component 3), and one M&E component (Component 4). The needs of disadvantaged groups, gender and age issues will be given consideration throughout the Project’s implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and are reflected in the Project design.

planEntities.description: In Turkmenistan, the demand for robust migration data has been on the rise. There is a growing realization that the current priorities of the Government - creating efficient mechanisms and developing a new migration management concept – can be attained only if accompanied by a thorough analysis of migratory processes taking place within and outside the country. Additionally, due to the considerable impact of migration on other spheres of the economy and society, migration statistics are also needed to develop strategies and programmes in other vital areas, such as demographic development, poverty reduction and overall economy development, regional integration.

planEntities.name: Support in development of policies that include Migration Environment and Climate Change nexus
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.4. Capacities of the GoT and other stakeholders are improved for climate analysis, assessment, monitoring, and reporting on climate change, environmental protection, and disaster risk reduction with focus on women, children and vulnerable groups
planEntities.description:
Climate change and its consequences are among the priority policy areas for the Government of Turkmenistan, and play a key role in the 2021-2025 United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). Turkmenistan is party to the major conventions and frameworks relating to climate change. In 2019, Turkmenistan further adopted a National Strategy on Climate Change and, in line with commitments under the Paris Agreement, Turkmenistan is currently developing the Fourth National Communication on Climate Change and the First Biennial Communication. It is planned that both documents will be submitted to the UN Secretariat in early 2023.

However, migration is not included into the national plans relating to climate change adaptation due to the limited awareness about the migration, environment and climate change nexus. There is a need to enhance data collection, risk analysis and sharing of information to better map, understand and manage human mobility related to the adverse impacts of climate change. Improving the understanding of the nexus between migration, environment and climate change in Turkmenistan would help develop the conditions necessary to unlock the adaptation potential of migration, reduce the risks related to migration, as well as formulate actionable recommendations to support well-managed migration. This, in its turn, has the potential to improve climate change adaptation in Turkmenistan by mainstreaming the migration and climate change perspective into the ongoing national adaptation planning efforts.

planEntities.description:
In 2022: Global Assessment of National Statistical System of Turkmenistan. Based on project: Strengthening national capacity in the most vulnerable UNECE countries for the sustainable development of statistics. The aim of the Global Assessment is to provide an in-depth and comprehensive analysis of the institutional, organizational and technical capacity of the national statistical office to produce official statistics that comply with international and European guidelines and recommendations, including the United Nations Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics (FPs) and the European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP). 

Support for population and housing census: Population and housing censuses are the foundation of statistical systems, providing benchmarks of a country's population and housing stock, and baseline information for the production of other statistics.

2023: To advance official statistics at the national and international levels for evidence-based policymaking and assessing progress towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and to ensure the coordination of statistical activities in the ECE region under the Conference of European Statisticians:
- Strengthening the institutional cooperation to produce institutional sector accounts
- Organizing Training on utilization of new data sources in the production of the CPI for National Statistical Offices

planEntities.name: The HCFC phase-out management plan (HPMP) is developed and implemented (stage I and II)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3. Government institutions, private sector, and civil society, trade unions have increased capacities to apply innovations, digital technology and green solutions contributing to efficient use of energy, water, land and other natural resources, renewable energy and development of sustainable cities and green economy with active participation of women, children and vulnerable groups of population
planEntities.description:
The hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) phase-out management plan (HPMP) was developed to enable Turkmenistan to meet its obligations under the Montreal Protocol and its amendments. The plan was prepared in close cooperation with the Government of Turkmenistan by the National Ozone Unit, the United Nations Industrial Development Organization and the United Nations Environment Programme. It was formulated in accordance with the processes and guidance set out in relevant decisions of the Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol and the Executive Committee of the Multilateral Fund.

The HPMP for Turkmenistan is implemented through a combination of investment and non-investment activities, structured in two stages and focused on the refrigeration and air-conditioning servicing sector. Stage I, implemented over a five-year period, aimed to achieve HCFC consumption reductions of 10% by 2015 and 35% by 2020. Stage II, covering the period from 2020 to 2040, is designed to achieve the complete phase-out of HCFCs, reaching a 100% reduction in consumption.

planEntities.description: The project focuses on further institutional strengthening and capacity-building of the Ministry of Agriculture and Environmental Protection and the National Ozone Unit in Turkmenistan, with the objective of ensuring that the Government meets its commitments under the Montreal Protocol related to ozone-depleting substances.

planEntities.name: Capacity building activities and training programmes aimed at strengthening criminal justice response to organized crime and enhancement of the international cooperation skills
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3. Civil service system provides conditions for establishing the pool of highly competent, motivated, impartial civil servants, who develop, plan and implement evidence-based, human centered public policy
planEntities.description:
UNODC technical assistance in Turkmenistan for the 2021-2025 period strategically pivoted to strengthening institutional capacities. UNODC placed significant emphasis on strengthening the operational and procedural competencies of law enforcement agencies and the judiciary to combat transnational threats and organized crime. This comprehensive support targeted the full spectrum of action, specifically enhancing national capacities for the detection, investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of organized crime, trafficking in illicit goods and drugs, corruption, and terrorism in line with international standards and best practices.

A core component of this work was dedicated to building robust capacities in evidence collection and investigative techniques, including trainings in Open-Source Intelligence methodologies. Furthermore, UNODC assistance actively facilitated and strengthened international cooperation, providing critical support for effective mutual legal assistance in cross-border cases. Through tailored workshops, simulation exercises, Mock-trials and the provision of practical guideline materials, UNODC equipped criminal justice practitioners and frontline professionals with the advanced skills and knowledge necessary to navigate complex, modern criminal investigations, thereby fortifying the entire chain of justice and enhancing international collaborative efforts.

planEntities.name: SDG FUND UNIDO Project: Innovative Finance for Clean Tech Solutions in Uruguay´s Renewable Energy Sector: The Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF)
planEntities.parentName: 1.3.2. Installed and functioning financial instrument to promote the second energy transition from renewable energies, incorporating a gender perspective, in coordination with comercial and multilateral banks.
planEntities.description: The purpose of the elaborated joint programme (JP) is to support Uruguay´s 2nd energy transition (2ET), and aligned with the 2030 Agenda and the principle of LNOB, focus on making the renewable energy sector a driver of inclusion across the economy. This JP seeks to decarbonize the industry and transport sectors; secure universal access to renewable sources; and increase the innovation and competitiveness of the energy sector through decreased energy costs and increased participation of women in the clean energy economy. The JP proposes an innovative financial mechanism i.e. the Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF) - and supporting actions to leverage public-private financing. Uruguay´s Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF) will provide financing for a range of new and emerging renewable energy technologies, ventures and activities aligned with its funding scope.

planEntities.name: GEF-7 Project “Promoting the Transition to a Circular Economy in Uruguay” under UNIDO GCIP platform
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1. Sustainable production and consumption models developped and validated in strategic sectors of the economy, that include and test new technologies/practices following the principles of circular economy, strengthen the development of the bioeconomy and favour resilience and inclusion.
planEntities.description: The project focuses in two main sectors of the country: i) Agri-food Systems with the promotion of cleantech waste valorization technologies (including bio-fuels and bio-fertilizers, biochemical products recovery) & ii) Country Renewable Energy Matrix, by promoting methods and technologies that allow the storage and use electrical energy surplus. The initiative focuses on the development and transfer of state-of-the-art technologies, contributing to the development of a professional sector in the field of engineering and consultancy that will lead to the improvement of the technological basis of the country.

planEntities.name: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE)
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1. Sustainable production and consumption models developped and validated in strategic sectors of the economy, that include and test new technologies/practices following the principles of circular economy, strengthen the development of the bioeconomy and favour resilience and inclusion.
planEntities.description: PAGE integrates technical capacities of five UN Agencies and supports countries wishing to embark on greener and more inclusive growth trajectories. Since 2018, Uruguay has become a partner country of the Programme and seven National Ministries (Office of Planning and Budget, Ministry of Industry, Ministry of Finance, National Agency for International Cooperation, Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Environment), work together to achieve national goals on green economy. Main technical areas of PAGE in Uruguay are: Planning for Green Economy, Circular Economy, Green Jobs, Green and Inclusive Production and Services, Capacity Building.

planEntities.name: E-Waste LAC Project: Strengthening of National Initiatives and Enhancement of Regional Cooperation for the Environmentally Sound Management of POPs in Waste of Electronic or Electrical Equipment (WEEE) in Latin-American Countries”.
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.1. Sustainable production and consumption models developped and validated in strategic sectors of the economy, that include and test new technologies/practices following the principles of circular economy, strengthen the development of the bioeconomy and favour resilience and inclusion.
planEntities.description: The objective is to implement actions leading to a system for environmentally sound management of e-waste. The project has two components: (1) the strengthening of national e-waste management initiatives; and, (2) the enhancement of regional cooperation on e-waste management. It will be funded by GEF and the resources will be used to support existing national activities and to strengthen the regional cooperation with regard to e-waste management.

planEntities.name: SDG FUND UNIDO Project: Innovative Finance for Clean Tech Solutions in Uruguay´s Renewable Energy Sector: The Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF)
planEntities.parentName: 1.3.2. Installed and functioning financial instrument to promote the second energy transition from renewable energies, incorporating a gender perspective, in coordination with comercial and multilateral banks.
planEntities.description: The purpose of the elaborated joint programme (JP) is to support Uruguay´s 2nd energy transition (2ET), and aligned with the 2030 Agenda and the principle of LNOB, focus on making the renewable energy sector a driver of inclusion across the economy. This JP seeks to decarbonize the industry and transport sectors; secure universal access to renewable sources; and increase the innovation and competitiveness of the energy sector through decreased energy costs and increased participation of women in the clean energy economy. The JP proposes an innovative financial mechanism i.e. the Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF) - and supporting actions to leverage public-private financing. Uruguay´s Renewable Energy Innovation Fund (REIF) will provide financing for a range of new and emerging renewable energy technologies, ventures and activities aligned with its funding scope.

planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed project is to reduce vulnerability to climate change in the Greater Mekong Sub-region. This objective will be achieved through three complementary outcomes: 
(1)	Climate change adaptation interventions, particularly EbA, implemented by vulnerable communities in the GMS to manage climate change impacts, particularly droughts and floods;
(2)	Enhanced knowledge and awareness of adaptation measures, including EbA, to shared climate change impacts in different ecosystems to promote regional cooperation, planning and implementation of adaptation in the GMS; and 
(3)	Strengthened regional cooperation.

planEntities.name: Build technical capacities of value chain actors for efficient and inclusive sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chains in Tanzania (AFDP)
planEntities.parentName: Relevant institutions have improved capacities to provide gender-responsive, market-oriented, quality programmes, infrastructure/facilities, products, and services to MSMEs and small holder farmers
planEntities.description:
Support to strengthen sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chain in Tanzania. i) designed to enhance market access, value addition, and private sector development for smallholder farmers. Its core strategy revolves around improving the seed business and fish market systems, with a strong emphasis on sustainable agricultural practices and inclusive growth. The programme aims to increase the use of quality seeds by supporting a sustainable supply of locally adapted and climate-resilient varieties. This effort targets 25% of local farming activities, enabling farmers to replace open-pollinated varieties every three years while building their capacity to maintain seed quality. To achieve its goals, AFDP focuses on four strategic areas. First, it establishes regional multi-stakeholder innovation platforms that bring together public, private, and associative actors. These platforms coordinate seed demand and supply, promote climate-smart agriculture, and support the development of professional seed producer and distributor organizations. They also facilitate annual stakeholder meetings and use digital tools for planning and monitoring seed-related activities. Second, the programme strengthens the supply and accessibility of improved seeds by developing agro-dealer networks and village input shops, particularly those managed by women and youth. It promotes partnerships between local agro-dealers and national seed producers, supports group purchases of seeds and inputs, and disseminates technical information through demonstrations and printed materials. Digital technologies are leveraged to enhance seed marketing and facilitate purchases by smallholder farmers.
Third, AFDP promotes farmer awareness and demand for improved seeds. It aims to reach 200,000 households across 40 districts in 10 regions, focusing on maize, sunflower, and pulses. Through farmer field schools, on-farm demonstrations, seed fairs, and nutrition education, the programme introduces farmers to new technologies and best practices. It also empowers local farmer organizations to provide advisory services and uses digital platforms to disseminate information. Financial services are facilitated to support input purchases.
Finally, the programme strengthens market linkages by fostering partnerships between farmers and agribusinesses. It encourages contract farming and pricing agreements with processors, connects farmers to structured trading platforms like G-Soko, and conducts market mapping studies. Support is also provided to youth entrepreneurs and cooperatives, and technical and business information is widely shared. AFDP collaborates with existing initiatives such as the Agricultural Market Development Trust (AMDT) and the Pan African Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) to maximize impact and promote best practices.

ii) The AFDP programme’s fish market development and value addition component focuses on reducing postharvest losses and increasing income opportunities, particularly for women and youth. It aims to improve infrastructure and introduce technologies that enhance the quality and marketability of fish products. These investments are expected to benefit over 30,000 artisanal fishers, processors, and traders, while creating direct and indirect employment for around 1,000 youth along the tuna value chain.
To achieve this, the programme will co-finance the establishment of eight ice-making plants, three cold chain and processing facilities, ten solar dryers for seaweed and small pelagic fish (dagaa), and 80 dagaa drying racks. Additionally, modern fish markets will be rehabilitated in Pangani and Bagamoyo, modeled after successful markets in Dar es Salaam. These facilities will be managed by cooperatives and small enterprises, with sustainable user-fee systems to ensure proper maintenance and long-term viability.
AFDP will also support access to finance for fishers’ cooperatives and associations through partnerships with financial institutions, facilitated by the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB). This will enable investment in equipment, infrastructure, and working capital, with a focus on youth and women-led groups.
In aquaculture, the programme will strengthen farmer clusters and link them with private hatcheries. It will establish aquaculture field schools to train youth and women, promote collective marketing, and improve access to inputs and cold storage. These clusters will coordinate production to ensure a steady supply of fish and engage in local governance and policy advocacy.
For the seaweed sector, which is predominantly female-led, AFDP will address challenges in processing and value addition. It will fund market analyses, strengthen cooperatives, and provide equipment such as drying racks, solar dryers, milling machines, and packaging materials. The programme will also support the development of seaweed-based small enterprises and link them to financial and business services. Partnerships with organizations like The Nature Conservancy and buyers such as Cargill will help scale market access and improve product quality. An inclusive business model from Zanzibar will be adapted to Pemba and mainland Tanzania to promote fair pricing, compliance with standards, and collective bargaining.

Violence and harassment is a daily reality especially for large number of women and children. In Tanzania its prevalence is high hence addressing it, is a central development goal in its own right and key to achieving other development outcomes for women, their families, communities and the nation. Violence also affects negatively on economic growth and on poverty reduction initiatives. Discrimination, gender based violence and violence against women are critical bottleneck in achieving National Development Goals. Violence prevents the Tanzanian economy from attaining its full economic potential as it is diverting resources from their optimal use and it has significant negative impact on attaining of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030, African Agenda 2063 - The Africa We Want, and the Tanzania Development Vision 2025 which target high quality livelihood, good governance and the rule of law.

planEntities.description: This project focuses on providing technical and financial support to employers and trade unions to build their capacity on collective bargaining for the purpose of reaching agreements and concluding CBAs that promote ending of harassment and violence against women at work places. in negotiating such CBAs special emphasis should be placed on the role of international labour standards, especially Convention 190 and other relevant standards, in ending all forms of violence and harassment at work. The CBAs to be concluded should recognize the words enshrined in Convention 190 that it is the right of everyone to a world of work free from violence and harassment, including gender-based violence and harassment, and that violence and harassment in the world of work can constitute a human rights violation or abuse, and that violence and harassment is a threat to equal opportunities, is unacceptable and incompatible with decent work. It is for these reasons that the Convention promotes the importance of a work culture based on mutual respect and dignity of the human being to prevent violence and harassment.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.1 - National and local authorities develop and adopt solutions in the areas of climate change adaptation and mitigation, energy and resource efficiency, renewables, chemicals, waste, sustainable management of natural resources, preparedness and response to environmental emergencies.
planEntities.description:
Ukraine is one of the largest producers and global exporters of grain. It is in the top-5 of global grain exporters, supplying more than 45 million tonnes of grain yearly to the global market. 
Plant protection is extremely relevant to facilitating plant exports, as all exported plants and plant products must meet the phytosanitary importing requirements established by importing countries, in order to make sure that pests are not moved in international trade. Unfortunately, the spread of plant pests and diseases enforced by the changing climatic conditions makes this task more and more challenging.
The presence of plant pests and diseases have had significant negative impact on the trade of Ukrainian grain. 
Insufficient phytosanitary verification systems can result in hurdles to export, while appropriate phytosanitary measures taken in relation to commodities relevant for export can facilitate access to export markets.
A number of countries (e.g. the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU), the EU, China, Indonesia or Turkey) require that some products can be imported only from areas that are free of certain pests .While the effectiveness of export inspections in detecting pests is limited, especially when the exported lots are large, or access to them is difficult, identification and establishment of pest free areas (PFAs) could provide additional guarantees of freedom from pests of the exported plants or plant products.
Based on the existing market challenges, there is a strong need to assess the spread of plant pests and diseases in Ukraine and to establish pest-free areas which could contribute to stabilised sale and support exports from Ukraine.

EU4Climate

planEntities.name: Rebuilding the energy system in Ukraine under the carbon neutrality and just transition concepts
planEntities.parentName: Energy and Environment
planEntities.description:
The objective of this project is to assess the size of the problem associated with rebuilding energy infrastructure in Ukraine and identify technology and policy options that need to be considered to design and implement a carbon neutral energy system. The project will assess the critical raw material (CRM) resource potential of Ukraine according to the United Nations Framework Classification of Resources (UNFC) and the United Nations Resource Management System (UNRMS) to support the low carbon energy transition. Attention is to be given to the social aspect of the proposed solutions. The project will assess various costs (social, economic, and environmental) that the suggested reconstruction strategy is likely to put on the local communities and social groups and explore measures that could be adopted to alleviate those negative impacts in the short, medium, and long term.
Proposed activities: 
A.1.1. Conduct analysis of the critical raw material resources in Ukraine following the United Nations Framework Classification for Resources (UNFC) and develop a report on the relevance of critical raw materials in the country to support its low carbon energy transition through the application of the United Nations Resource Management System (UNRMS). 
A.1.2. Online training workshop on the application of UNFC and UNRMS for critical raw material management in Ukraine. 
A1.3. Adapt the UNECE Framework on Carbon Neutrality to the conditions in Ukraine, develop a strategy (in a form of a report) for application of the adapted framework in the country, identifying the best technology and policy options to design a carbon neutral local energy system. 
A.1.4. Organize an online policy dialogue and launch UNECE partnership on rebuilding the Ukrainian energy system in accordance with the objectives of carbon neutrality and the concept of just transition.
A.2.1 Explore socio-economic aspects of the process of attaining a carbon neutral energy system in Ukraine, identify measures that need to be adopted in order to align the proposed strategy on attaining carbon neutrality with the premises of just transition (including gender equality), and develop a report summarizing the findings.

planEntities.name: Capacity-building on the use of PPPs as a mechanism to finance green, circular and sustainable infrastructure in Ukraine for its reconstruction.
planEntities.parentName: Inclusive Economic Growth
planEntities.description:
Build the capacity of public officials in Ukraine on the use of PPPs as a mechanism to finance green, circular and sustainable infrastructure to assist Ukraine with its reconstruction, through policy advisory support on the infrastructure projects identified by the Government of Ukraine in its post conflict reconstruction phase.

This will be achieved by preparing recommendations on the application of the UNECE PPP Evaluation Methodology for the SDGs to prepare, design and finance priority PPP projects in post conflict Ukraine. 

The capacity-building roundtable will be an opportunity for UNECE, the IFIs and the private sector to provide policy advice to Ukraine on its priority PPP projects based on its list of infrastructure projects needed in the post conflict reconstruction phase.

planEntities.parentName: Education
planEntities.description:
Evidence shows that Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) is critical in emergency and recovery contexts after exposure to trauma. It can promote emotional regulation, relational skills, effective communication, collaboration, compassion, empathy, and conflict resolution in educational contexts.

UNESCO is working alongside the Ministry of Education and Science to transform the provision of MHPSS inside the school system as part of the nationwide plan to enhance MHPSS in light of current and future challenges, led by First Lady Olena Zelenska.

This initiative adopts a three-domain approach of reforming policy, strengthening capacity, and creating supportive MHPSS tools and materials. Under this initiative, UNESCO will work with local implementation partners to train 15,000 school psychologists, 20,000 school personnel, parents, and caretakers, and reach 160,000 vulnerable children.

planEntities.name: Supporting labour migration governance to better respond to employer and labour market needs and skills matching while ensuring protection of migrant workers and enhancing development impacts in countries of origin and destination.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. By 2025, the capacities of national institutions and social partners are strengthened to design and implement effective and innovative Active Labour Market Policies, decent work and skills development programmes for the youth and adults (including NEET), women, informal workers, migrants, PWD to ensure inclusive and sustainable economic growth and reduced inequalities, including spacial and gender inequalities.
planEntities.description:
Building upon the findings and key recommendations of the research, the project aims to enhance the governance of labour mobility in the region for the benefit of both migrants and employers, as well as for countries of origin and destination more broadly. Given the current situation with newly-imposed sanctions on RF and their likely impacts on Central Asian migrant workers as well as Central Asian economies more broadly, the project also aims to support CA governments to facilitate reintegration and support the diversification of countries of destination. The project’s overall objective and proposed interventions operate according to the following Theory of Change:
If the key stakeholders on labour migration governance within Central Asia are better capacitated to coordinate their work and respond to the needs and expectations of employers and prospective migrants, then the use of regular channels for recruitment and employment will increase, improving skills matching, enhancing protection of workers, promoting greater financial inclusion, and enhancing the development benefits of labour migration in countries of origin and destination, because more efficient and effective systems to coordinate regular labour mobility will reduce the interest of employers and migrants to use informal channels of recruitment and migrant workers with formal contracts and regular status will receive better access to services for their social  and financial protection and inclusion.

planEntities.name: Promoting a victim centered approach to CTIP in Uzbekistan
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3. By 2025, the national social protection system is strengthened to deliver progressively universal inclusive and gender-responsive social security, social protection benefits and social services to address all forms of poverty, violence, social exclusion and other vulnerabilities
planEntities.description:
IOM is proposing with this action to implement measures to provide for the physical, psychological and social recovery of VOTs, in cooperation with GoU funded shelters, NGOs, ministries and other stakeholders, which also fall within the scope of the core UN human rights instruments and other international treaties, including the Palermo Protocol; 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
IOM will combine institutional capacitating with policy improvement on CTIP, while at the same time fostering social partnership based on victim-centered and human rights-based approaches.
The project will target national and international VOTs, both females and males, children and elderly, to be identified by partner-organizations according to IOM rules and procedures, as well as those VOTs receiving services at GoU funded shelters, with a focus on at-high-risk groups, including returning migrants vulnerable to TIP, without any distinction, exclusion, restriction or preference based on race, color, descent, national or ethnic origin, or gender, including LGBTQI+ individuals. The project will, inter alia, address the needs of VOTs to return home and receive individually tailored reintegration assistance.
Within the project, it is planned to contribute to increasing the capacities of the newly established government funded shelters in Uzbekistan, as well as to assist to building-up partnerships between the shelters and NGOs.

planEntities.description:
The proposed project aims to contribute to the protection of migrants and increase the resilience of vulnerable migrants, especially women, in Central Asia, in the context of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. 
The project will achieve this overall objective by accomplishing the following three outcomes at the individual and at the household/family level, at the community and at the structural levels: 
•	Outcome 1: Women in the context of migration are empowered to participate in the labour market in countries of origin and destination (at the individual, household/family levels) 
•	Outcome 2: Target communities in Central Asia adopt gender equitable attitudes and behaviours towards women in the context of migration (at the community level) 
•	Outcome 3: Strengthened national response to migrants’ vulnerabilities through consolidated coordination platforms, and cooperation among all relevant actors, also in the context of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic (at the structural level)

planEntities.description: BIOFIN was launched in October 2012 at the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) COP 11, as new global partnership seeking to address the biodiversity finance challenge in a comprehensive manner – to define biodiversity finance needs and gaps with greater precision through detailed national level assessments, to determine challenges and opportunities for resource mobilization, and to build a sound business case for increased biodiversity investment. Participating governments are interested in advancing their biodiversity conservation mandates in ways that are compatible with and promote national socio-economic development goals. UNDP Uzbekistan in collaboration with the government will be implementing the global BIOFIN Phase II Extended project, which is funded by the Governments of Germany running from 2021 to 2023.

planEntities.description: The objective of the project is to enhance the resilience of the ecosystems and livelihoods in Lower Amudarya and Aral Sea Basin (LADAB) through land degradation neutrality (LDN) compatible integrated land-water management in the productive landscapes around PAs and KBAs/IBAs. The four components proposed by this project have been designed within available GEF and co-financing framework to address the corresponding drivers of land, water degradation and biodiversity decline, which are directly linked to the diminishment and loss of lake, wetland and riparian biodiversity in this arid landscape. The project will deliver Global Environmental Benefits using a participatory approach that ensures promotion of women, youth and vulnerable groups and equitable participation opportunities.

planEntities.description: The programme will consolidate the multi-stakeholder commitment to the achievement of CRPD-compliant SDGs through a robust legislative and policy framework, sound coordination structures and meaningful participation of organizations of persons with disabilities. It will address the essential building blocks to the CRPD implementation that are legislative reform, strengthening the representativity and capacity of OPDs, and availability of inclusive services (UNPRPD Outcome 1). The programme specifically focuses on accessible person-centered and age-appropriate services in the community, aimed at supporting the autonomy and inclusion of children, women and men with disabilities and prevention of institutionalization, violence and abuse. Development of early identification and early intervention services for children with disabilities will be one of the focus areas of the programme, as will the inclusion of women and girls with disabilities in programmes addressing gender-based violence (UNPRPD Outcome 2). The programme also intends to strengthen disability mainstreaming within the implementing country-level UN agencies’ activities to ensure that national development assessments, plans, budgets, programs and monitoring mechanisms supported under the SDG processes advance disability-inclusive development in Uzbekistan (UNPRPD Outcome 3).

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3. By 2025, the economy is stimulated and decent working conditions are created by promotion of investment and trade, utilisation of new technologies and modern infrastructure, and harnessing opportunities opened by green transition
planEntities.description:
The Road Safety Performance Review (RSPR) was designed to help beneficiary country to strengthen the road safety management capacities and effectively address and improve national road safety records. The most critical road safety aspects and priority needs in the beneficiary country will identified. Based on RSPR findings, national capacity-building workshops will be organized to provide further training on the priority areas identified through RSPR and on accession and implementation of United Nations road-safety related legal instruments. Through workshops and capacity building events on the identified priority areas, RSP will raise the capabilities of key policy and decision makers on road safety management, safer vehicles and roads, road safety statistics, addressing drink-driving and speeding, etc. One of the most significant project results will be that the RSPRs findings and recommendations will led to concrete policy actions (update of national strategic documents and national legislation and improvements in road safety management) and road safety activities in the beneficiary country. 

Workshop on selected road safety issues in support of implemmentation of the RSPR recommendations and national road safety strategy, including enforcement.

planEntities.description:
The objective of the project is to support the ECE Working Party on Transport Trends and Economics (WP.5) in fulfilling its mandate to assume the unique role of a transport “think tank” in the framework of ITC. The objective of the working party is to enhance the understanding of the main inland transport trends and developments and strengthen international cooperation to develop sustainable Euro-Asian transport links. The objective will be achieved by implementing the following activities: 
A1.1. Conduct vulnerability assessments of a specific transport asset to climate change and extreme weather events in selected countries of Eastern Europe, South Caucasus, and Central Asia and integrate the collected data into the ITIO.
A.2.1. Develop and pilot a concept for international contingency management aimed at building resilience of transport systems in case of emergencies, including for rail, road, and inland waterway sectors.
A.3.1 – Support countries on Euro-Asian inland transport corridors in setting up coordination and performance review mechanisms inter alia through developing a concept for transport data inter-operability and dematerialization of transport documents and organizing ECE region wide workshops to discuss these proposals and initiate pilot studies.

planEntities.description: Consultations and discussions of the TVET strategy continued with respective local authorities and main TVET beneficiaries and private sectors in the project’s pilot regions, to bring together the views and suggestions of employers based on the regional context, and to discuss the initiatives and the prospects for development of interactions between the educational institutions and employers. Based on gathered information, the regional action plan, as well as series of documents on quality assurance, namely Quality processes for occupational standards, guideline defining the role and functions of SSC, manual guideline for training providers on “Quality Management System” were developed.

planEntities.name: Strengthened the governance, management and quality assurance structure for agricultural and irrigation skill development through the establishment and administration of a sector skill council and the creation of a qualifications network
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. By 2025, the capacities of national institutions and social partners are strengthened to design and implement effective and innovative Active Labour Market Policies, decent work and skills development programmes for the youth and adults (including NEET), women, informal workers, migrants, PWD to ensure inclusive and sustainable economic growth and reduced inequalities, including spacial and gender inequalities.
planEntities.description:
The project has supported the Government to develop the new TVET strategy with particular focus and action plan for Agriculture and Irrigation sectors, as well as to develop the first draft of the Quality Assurance Framework for TVET. After the consultation with the relevant stakeholders and collecting the feedback, second draft was presented for discussion in November 2022. After further discussions, the strategy is being reviewed according to the comments from the ministries to fit the format of national regulation. The third draft of the TVET strategy will be submitted to the government, for endorsement, in the first half of 2023. Based on gathered information, the regional action plan, as well as series of documents on quality assurance, namely Quality processes for occupational standards, guideline defining the role and functions of SSC, manual guideline for training providers on “Quality Management System” were developed. 
Furthermore, the offices of Sectors Skills Councils (SSCs) in Agriculture and Irrigation were equipped to support the SSCs for full operationalization. An opening ceremony of SSC in Irrigation was organized by the Ministry of Water Resources in November 2022. The opening ceremony for SSC in Agriculture is postponed to the first half of 2023 due to the renovation of their premises.

planEntities.name: Developed and piloted demand-driven qualifications and methods for skill development in agriculture and irrigation, as well as capacity development programmes college teaching staff and instructors in agriculture and irrigation
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. By 2025, the capacities of national institutions and social partners are strengthened to design and implement effective and innovative Active Labour Market Policies, decent work and skills development programmes for the youth and adults (including NEET), women, informal workers, migrants, PWD to ensure inclusive and sustainable economic growth and reduced inequalities, including spacial and gender inequalities.
planEntities.description:
In order to update the Sectoral Qualifications framework on agriculture and irrigation, aligned with the National Qualifications Framework (NQF), Occupational Maps were developed for agriculture and irrigation sectors based on the Skills Need Assessment (SNA) in the four targeted regions, followed by development of functional maps. Furthermore, based on these two documents, National Occupational Standards (NOS) for selected five qualifications were developed by international consultants together with local experts who were in the professions, as well as with SSC members. The NOSs are used as a base for development of curricula in related qualifications as well as the guideline to develop a list of required equipment for the newly developed and updated curricula. Proposals for curriculum development were received and evaluated by the project. The developed qualifications were:
•	Agricultural operative technician  
•	General farm worker - Crop Worker - Livestock Worker     
•	Livestock unit technician - Poultry Technician - Stockperson (Beef, Pigs, Sheep, Dairy)
•	Irrigation operative technician
•	Technician for water saving technology

planEntities.name: Support strengthening the capacity of  MoPE and its subordinate entities in designing, implementing and sustaining scale TPD models
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2. By 2025, Government and other educational stakeholders have increased capacity to provide access to equitable, inclusive, safe and quality education at all levels and promote lifelong learning in an integrated manner, including quality professional development system and decent work environment for education sector employees
planEntities.description:
UNESCO supported strengthening the capacity of MoPE and its subordinate entities in designing, implementing and sustaining at scale Teachers Professional Development model, based on research. While the previous TPD model of Uzbekistan was limited to offer professional development only once in five years, and to study only subject-based knowledge and pedagogical skills, the new TPD Model allows lifelong learning principles by enabling teachers access various professional courses anytime from anywhere flexibly and in cost-effective manner. Before the national launch, the Model was piloted in four regions: Karakalpakstan, Kashkadarya, Navoiy and Tashkent by offering updated curriculum and more than 30 courses for teachers. 
UNESCO also supported enriching and enhancing the learning management platform (https://onlinedu.uz), which optimized the process of assimilation of training materials and increased user friendliness as well as helped to expand professional learning communities (PLC) in the platform, where teachers reflect and assess their knowledge, and distance learning opportunities.

planEntities.description: The programme will consolidate the multi-stakeholder commitment to the achievement of CRPD-compliant SDGs through a robust legislative and policy framework, sound coordination structures and meaningful participation of organizations of persons with disabilities. It will address the essential building blocks to the CRPD implementation that are legislative reform, strengthening the representativity and capacity of OPDs, and availability of inclusive services (UNPRPD Outcome 1). The programme specifically focuses on accessible person-centered and age-appropriate services in the community, aimed at supporting the autonomy and inclusion of children, women and men with disabilities and prevention of institutionalization, violence and abuse. Development of early identification and early intervention services for children with disabilities will be one of the focus areas of the programme, as will the inclusion of women and girls with disabilities in programmes addressing gender-based violence (UNPRPD Outcome 2). The programme also intends to strengthen disability mainstreaming within the implementing country-level UN agencies’ activities to ensure that national development assessments, plans, budgets, programs and monitoring mechanisms supported under the SDG processes advance disability-inclusive development in Uzbekistan (UNPRPD Outcome 3).

Uzbekistan.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: National efforts for the improved competitiveness of high-value-added goods for exports are supported through the sustainable industrial development of the textile industry
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. By 2025, the capacities of national institutions and social partners are strengthened to design and implement effective and innovative Active Labour Market Policies, decent work and skills development programmes for the youth and adults (including NEET), women, informal workers, migrants, PWD to ensure inclusive and sustainable economic growth and reduced inequalities, including spacial and gender inequalities.
planEntities.description: In accordance with the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan about Accelerated Development Measures for Textile and Sewing and Knitting Industry no. 5285 dated 14 December 2018, Uzbekistan plans to increase the share of the textile industry in the economy, the volume and quality of textile products, improve the systems of standardization and certification in the field of the textile industry, as well as to introduce advanced information and communication technologies in the industry. To ensure sustainable development of the textile industry, the “Uztuqimachiliksanoat” (Uzbekistan Textile Industry Association) was established and assigned a wide range of tasks aiming at sustainable development of the textile clusters, which are expected to be supported through soft financing, the introduction of drip irrigation, and new methods of fertilization and harvesting. In the official letter to Mr. Li Yong, Former Director General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), dated 24 August 2021, Mr. Ilkhom Khaydarov, Chairmen of the Textile and Garment Industry Association of the Republic of Uzbekistan, expressed interest in implementing a UNIDO project to introduce and apply the extensive experience of UNIDO on "Sustainable modernization of the textile and clothing industry" in the textile sector and establish long-term and fruitful cooperation to implement the joint declaration for 2020-2024 between Ministry of Economic Development and Poverty Reduction of Uzbekistan and UNIDO. The project’s objective is to contribute to economic diversification and improved access to local and export markets of the textile and garment industries in Uzbekistan through strengthening productivity, competitiveness and collective export capacities of manufacturing companies, application of new innovative approaches and methodology for branding and marketing, product design, thereby strengthening national human and technical capacities in business networking, enhancing institutional partnerships among producers and global value chain operators.

planEntities.name: Improving Access to COVID-19 Vaccinations for Vulnerable Migrants in Humanitarian Settings
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Capacities of national systems including domestic financial capacity and institutions to deliver human rights-based, people centered, comprehensive essential social services and protection systems for all are enhanced.
planEntities.description: In agreement with national governments, Ministries of Health, and international prioritization standards such as SAGE, IOM promoted equitable access to COVID‑19 vaccines for vulnerable populations in humanitarian settings through a wide range of targeted activities. Implemented by IOM Headquarters in Geneva with SDC funding, the project supported 38 countries from July 2021 to March 2022 to expand vaccination access for high‑risk and underserved groups—including migrants, refugees, IDPs, and other populations often excluded from national immunization plans. Through close coordination with Gavi, WHO, UNICEF, Ministries of Health and global COVID‑19 response platforms, the initiative strengthened vaccination delivery systems, improved micro‑planning and outreach, and enhanced last‑mile delivery capacities in complex humanitarian contexts. Guided by IOM’s global COVID‑19 SRRP, the project further improved country‑level preparedness, risk communication, and operational readiness to reduce infection rates and ensure the inclusion of mobile and marginalized populations. Across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, this collective effort contributed to broader global health security by advancing equitable access to life‑saving COVID‑19 vaccines for those most at risk.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: Government institutions have stronger capacities for evidence-based (including gender analysis) decision making, accountability, and effective coordination for disasters and climate resilience, resilient infrastructures and the sustainable management of environment and natural resources ;
planEntities.description:
"The landfall of Tropical Cyclone Eloise in the night of 23 January 2021 and previously, the Tropical Storm Chalane on 30 December 2020, have deeply affected areas in Central Mozambique. While the initial response has kickstarted, there is an urgent need to scale up in the areas of Shelter/NFI, CCCM, Protection/MHPSS and DTM to ensure adequate response to the needs of those affected by Tropical Cyclone Eloise in Central Mozambique trough sound, safe and integrated measures in resettlement locations for those who cannot return home. Building directly on its existing field presence and structures, with added value and comparative advantage on the response, IOM proposes to respond to the immediate humanitarian needs by providing emergency humanitarian assistance using a multisectoral and people-centered approach, increasing local capacity and (human) resources focusing on the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: Affected populations have safe and sustainable settlements through multisector integrated approaches to address disaster displacement
Outcome 2: Informed humanitarian and resilient response through the evidence-based assessments to inform the response

planEntities.description:
"For over three years, the province of Cabo Delgado province in Mozambique has experienced brutal attacks by armed groups causing 697,538 (DTM Baseline Round #11) people to be displaced. As a result of insecurity in Cabo Delgado, the humanitarian situation is deteriorating in both hosting and displaced communities, and for those left behind. The situation in Northern Mozambique, facing a triple humanitarian crisis with a conflict, reoccurring impact of natural disasters and the Covid-19 pandemic has become incredibly complex. This project will consist of the following five components in response to the situation: 
Intervention I: CCCM 
Intervention II: COVID-19 ?
Intervention III: Shelter/NFI 
Intervention IV: Protection & MHPSS 
Intervention V: Security "

planEntities.description: To address the effects of violence and insecurity in northern Mozambique, IOM's multi-sectoral response will provide humanitarian aid to conflict-affected persons - especially internally displaced persons (IDPs), host communities, and those left behind - while reducing and responding to vulnerabilities and threats. The Action will include activities under the protection sector to address humanitarian needs in Cabo Delgado, Niassa, and Nampula provinces. To provide continuous and critical information on displacement numbers and trends as well as needs of conflict-affected persons, IOM will also implement Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) systems to collect and analyze data which will help humanitarian partners target interventions for context-specific assistance and programming. Mainstreaming of protection principles, including IOM's Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) guidelines, will be incorporated throughout the Action. IOM will also provide technical and operational support to government and partners in Mozambique, Botswana and South Africa to contribute to access to COVID-19 vaccines in humanitarian settings and migration affected communities.

planEntities.name: TACKLING OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH CHALLENGES: OPTIMIZING APPROACHES TO DETECTING AND ADDRESSING OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH ILLNESSES IN MOZAMBICAN MIGRANT WORKERS (Addendum: Integrating two Gaza Occupational Health Centres into the programme)

Government officials responsible for collecting, analyzing, and publishing migration data require greater understanding of the current migration situation within Mozambique and the skills to continue providing information on migration in order to better equip policymakers. This project intends to assist by developing a methodology for migration data collection, sharing, and analysis as well as through gathering information for a migration profile report which can serve as a baseline for further reporting.

planEntities.name: Assessing COVID-19's Impact on Mixed Migration Flows: Trafficking in Persons, Smuggling of Migrants, and Related Protection Risks in Malawi, Mozambique and Zimbabwe
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Policies, strategies, laws and regulations for the use of environmental & natural resources, climate and disaster resilience are developed and strengthened based on good practices and standards and are gender transformative and include the needs of refugees and IDPs.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of  this project, is  to contribute to strengthening of protection measures and national responses to trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants. This includes specific impacts on women, children and youth, as well as the evolving routes, stakeholders, modus operandi, as well as needs and vulnerabilities of migrant populations of focus . The proposed project aims to conduct field research in areas of high irregular migration movements and other identified hotspots for data collection pertinent to the smuggling and trafficking of migrants. The research will be qualitative and rely on the collection of primary data through direct interviews with  a variety of governmental and  non-governmental stakeholders and key informants, as well as direct field assessments to be conducted by the research team in collaboration with the relevant national authorities. The findings will inform follow up awareness raising activities, intended to both inform identified populations about the risks of trafficking and smuggling post-COVID as well as through political level advocacy aimed at facilitating the adaptation of policy and programming responses by government stakeholders. Capacity building activities will also be developed to strengthen the capacity of relevant stakeholders towards managing migration flows post-COVID.

planEntities.description: The project aims to build resilience to violent extremist influences in Cabo Delgado by understanding and addressing socio-economic needs in affected communities. It includes four core components of intervention: i) research, ii) individual assistance, iii) community assistance and iv) government capacity building. The research component will identify the areas of origin and driving factors for persons recruited into or otherwise joining violent extremist groups and inform targeted programming. Second, at the individual level, the project will provide a range of employment, training and income generation services intended to create sustainable livelihoods to up to 1000 beneficiaries and their dependents.

planEntities.description:
The project aims to build resilience to violent extremist influences in the Northern Region of Mozambique by understanding and addressing socio-economic needs in affected communities. Consistent with IOM’s Community Resilience and Peacebuilding (CRP) strategic approach, the project will build resilience and increase stability through programming addressing drivers of violent extremism in three outcomes:

1.       Empowered community members, particularly youth, contribute productively to households, communities and society

2.       Communities have stronger connections to, and more positive perceptions of, the government

3.       Social cohesion is increased as a protective factor against VE, and to promote stability

planEntities.description:
This project will contribute to promoting community stabilization and preventing violent extremism in Northern Mozambique, particularly in communities affected by conflict with a specific focus on youth, women and girls.

In pursuit of this objective, IOM will initiate activities to support community-led conflict prevention and creating a conducive environment for communities to live peaceful and productive lives through income generation, school-based peace clubs, community-based projects prioritized by communities and support to the Government of Mozambique to discuss mechanisms and frameworks for reintegration of former and eligible non-state armed group (NSAG) members. By focusing on addressing root causes in a context-specific way, IOM aims to promote stability, reduce vulnerability and build local resilience - contributing to Mozambique achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16, Peace, justice and strong institutions.
