planEntities.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

planEntities.parentName: Preparedness and resilience (especially of indigenous, poor, at-risk communities) against climate change, natural hazards, and disaster risks are strengthened.
planEntities.description:
Under this project, Mersing Islands (Malaysia) to demonstrate integrated waste management good practices in remote/island communities to reduce and prevent plastic waste leakage into the coastal and marine environment in line with the Regional Action Plan on Marine Litter (RAP MALI). 

Prior to project activities, no waste management practices existed in the Mersing Islands and plastic waste was largely littered or burned. Through the pilot, an integral waste management system was created with the community, and the population received education on reducing and segregating plastic for recycling and disposal. This includes the use of a plastic compacting machine and simple disposal and sorting infrastructure, so recyclables can be processed and taken to the mainland to be recycled. 

The pilot was implemented in partnership with Reef-Check Malaysia (USD 55,000 SSFA).

planEntities.parentName: Natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems are sustainably managed, adequately protected and conserved for long-term economic and environmental sustainability.
planEntities.description: This project aimed to generate informed recommendations and ideas for the development of an online knowledge sharing platform in the ASEAN region to support science-based decision system for coastal and marine biodiversity conservation and management. The project involved a stakeholder consultation process to explore the information and marine conservation capacity needs of natural resource managers, the business sector, and government organizations. This process of national and regional consultation was held with representatives and stakeholders from all 10 ASEAN Member States, and included national workshops, a regional experts forum, and an online survey. These activities were structured with the view to inform the design of the new platform. UNEP-WCMC provided technical advice and input on the consultations, and produced a discussion paper that synthesised all results and provided recommendations on development of the online knowledge sharing platform. The primary objective of the study is to identify and explore the drivers and pathways to both intended and unintended adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia, including the relationship with early marriage/union. The study's secondary objective is to develop policy and programming recommendations, co-created with adolescents, to effectively address adolescent pregnancy.

planEntities.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

The project was promoted and branded as the “Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project” (MAEESTA). The Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project (MAEESTA) which started being implemented in July 2014 was initially designed for a five-year duration. However, due to challenges faced while implementing the project especially to convince companies to invest in implementing energy efficiency measures and in the demonstration plant, and due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic which started affecting the country in early 2020, the project was approved to be extended for another three years, i.e. until June 2022.

The industrial sub-sectors stated in the project’s document mainly cover the raw material processing and manufacturing sectors. The hospitality sector (hotels and hospitals) was agreed to be included as one of the focused industrial sub-sectors during the second National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) meeting held on 16th December 2016. 

The project completed in June 2022. More details on achievements will be provided shortly.

It does so by promoting enhanced EU-ASEAN Member States partnerships, in support of ongoing efforts towards a circular economy transition, in line with the relevant policy frameworks, with four priority countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. 
UNEP is responsible for the legal components, examining the legal framework in the ASEAN region on waste trafficking and a legal comparative analysis of the four priority countries. planEntities.name: Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers as a program being adopted from Alzheimer’s Disease International where guidelines to develop the local content needs, Training Modules are modified to suit the local requirements.

The objectives of the training workshop are:
•Provide an understanding of Dementia
•Learning about the Impact of Dementia and how Person-Centred Care is important
•Communication Effectively with a Person with Dementia
•Importance on how to address Behavioural & Psychological Symptoms of Dementia
•Understanding Meaningful Activities and Engagement and how best to manage and roll out these activities
•Knowledge of Legal /Ethical Issues and the importance of Advanced Care Planning
• Pre-tests were conducted at the start of the Training session to determine the level of understanding of Dementia, Stages, and care skill
•Post-Test is also being conducted at the end of the course to understand how the Training Workshop had helped them in the understanding and Care for Person with Dementia
•VARK methodology was used in the Training Workshop as studies have proven Visual, Audiology, Reading/Writing, and Kinesthetic approach have a better way to retain what had been taught through the way of repeating the scenario in action.

The target audience for this Training Workshop were volunteers from Ministry of Health / Ministry of Welfare programs and the majority of volunteers had informal caregiving experience but not Dementia Care Skills.

planEntities.name: Survey of salt levels in street foods to strengthen salt reduction action in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
This project will strengthen the implementation of  Malaysia’s  Salt  Reduction Strategy through generating data about the salt levels in street foods and meals in Malaysia, with a view to: 
(1) providing evidence for accelerating the introduction of mandatory sodium labelling on packaged and street foods, 
(2) informing salt-reduction education messages about what high-salt foods to avoid and what alternatives to consume as part of a strategic behavior change communication plan; and
(3) identifying and engaging food industries producing high-salt foods in reformulation. Analysis of the sodium content will be conducted on street foods which include ready-to-eat foods usually sold by small- to medium-sized vendors in a street, hawker center, or food court. 
This proposal extends ongoing national salt reduction efforts since 2015 and a recent mid-term evaluation of its progress, which elucidated areas for enhancement to ensure the targeted 15% reduction in population salt intake is achieved by 2020.

Activities included following online conversational trends related to COVID-19 and COVID-19 vaccines, both in terms of volume and velocity, and a weekly in-depth analysis of not just prominent topics but the emotional and behavioural responses that result. 

Work also includes provision of daily reports as snapshots of the most important online conversations and rumours and misinformation so that MOH can quickly pick up on and respond to these issues. planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
WCO collaborated with the School of Population and Global Health, University of Melbourne, to build the capacity for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The findings of this study demonstrated the important contribution of the implemented public health measures in reducing the COVID-19 disease burden. Both vaccination and limiting mobility through lockdowns contributed to slowing the spread of infection, reducing severe illness and mortality and were cost-saving through reducing pressure on healthcare resource utilization. The activity also contributed to building capacity for economic evaluation within the Ministry of Health in preparation for future outbreaks.

WCO convened a partner’s forum in September to engage with civil society organizations (CSOs) in developing and implementing innovative evidence-based community engagement initiatives which address cross-cutting health issues pertaining to COVID-19. 

The forum analyzed enablers and barriers to getting COVID-19 vaccines, how to increase COVID-19 vaccine uptake among people at high risk of getting severely ill from COVID-19 in areas with low booster uptake, how to increase adherence to COVID-19 protective behaviors, prevention and control of NCDs amid the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 33 participants from 22 CSOs/NGOs attended the forum. Following the meeting, 25 concept notes were received, reviewed and sifted to 5 proposals for further review. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

planEntities.name: Addressing marine litter in South-East Asia
planEntities.parentName: Preparedness and resilience (especially of indigenous, poor, at-risk communities) against climate change, natural hazards, and disaster risks are strengthened.
planEntities.description:
Under this project, Mersing Islands (Malaysia) to demonstrate integrated waste management good practices in remote/island communities to reduce and prevent plastic waste leakage into the coastal and marine environment in line with the Regional Action Plan on Marine Litter (RAP MALI). 

Prior to project activities, no waste management practices existed in the Mersing Islands and plastic waste was largely littered or burned. Through the pilot, an integral waste management system was created with the community, and the population received education on reducing and segregating plastic for recycling and disposal. This includes the use of a plastic compacting machine and simple disposal and sorting infrastructure, so recyclables can be processed and taken to the mainland to be recycled. 

The pilot was implemented in partnership with Reef-Check Malaysia (USD 55,000 SSFA).

planEntities.description: This project aimed to generate informed recommendations and ideas for the development of an online knowledge sharing platform in the ASEAN region to support science-based decision system for coastal and marine biodiversity conservation and management. The project involved a stakeholder consultation process to explore the information and marine conservation capacity needs of natural resource managers, the business sector, and government organizations. This process of national and regional consultation was held with representatives and stakeholders from all 10 ASEAN Member States, and included national workshops, a regional experts forum, and an online survey. These activities were structured with the view to inform the design of the new platform. UNEP-WCMC provided technical advice and input on the consultations, and produced a discussion paper that synthesised all results and provided recommendations on development of the online knowledge sharing platform. This discussion paper is now being finalised, and a Phase 2 of the project is hoping to be developed to pursue development of the platform.

planEntities.name: Understanding Pathways to Adolescent Pregnancy in Southeast Asia
planEntities.parentName: Increased adoption of inclusive social norms and values and rejection of harmful practices, particularly against women and girls, and the creation of demand for services
planEntities.description:
This study, conducted in Malaysia as part of a wider Southeast Asia study, is a collaboration between the Burnet Institute, UNFPA, and UNICEF. The study aims to improve understanding of the drivers and pathways to adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia and inform effective policy and programming responses. The primary objective of the study is to identify and explore the drivers and pathways to both intended and unintended adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia, including the relationship with early marriage/union. The study's secondary objective is to develop policy and programming recommendations, co-created with adolescents, to effectively address adolescent pregnancy.

The report was launched on 18 October 2023 as a joint initiative by UNFPA Malaysia and UNICEF Malaysia and was developed by the Burnet Institute.  The report included in-depth interviews with 45 adolescent girls from three states in Malaysia – Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang, and highlighted six pathways to adolescent pregnancy. The reports underscore the importance of adolescent-responsive health services, comprehensive sexuality education, supportive relationships, and enabling environments that empower girls to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health and lives.

planEntities.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

planEntities.parentName: Transitioning national development towards a decarbonised pathway and a resource efficient economy through the adoption of green growth strategies and practices across all sectors.
planEntities.description:
efficiency and application of solar thermal systems in Malaysia” started its implementation in July 2014 and completed in June 2022. 
The project was promoted and branded as the “Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project” (MAEESTA). The Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project (MAEESTA) which started being implemented in July 2014 was initially designed for a five-year duration. However, due to challenges faced while implementing the project especially to convince companies to invest in implementing energy efficiency measures and in the demonstration plant, and due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic which started affecting the country in early 2020, the project was approved to be extended for another three years, i.e. until June 2022.
The project’s objective was to reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions by promoting and demonstrating sector-specific energy efficiency (EE) improvements and solar thermal technology utilization in industry. The industrial sub-sectors stated in the project’s document mainly cover the raw material processing and manufacturing sectors. The hospitality sector (hotels and hospitals) was agreed to be included as one of the focused industrial sub-sectors during the second National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) meeting held on 16th December 2016. 

The project completed in June 2022. More details on achievements will be provided shortly.

planEntities.parentName: Transitioning national development towards a decarbonised pathway and a resource efficient economy through the adoption of green growth strategies and practices across all sectors.
planEntities.description: The project contributes to the GEF 7 Global Electric Mobility Programme’s goal of reducing global transportation sector GHG emissions and additional global environmental benefits in the form of reduced air pollution by creating a policy ecosystem for accelerated adoption of RE powered EV fleets and derisking of private and public investment in technologies that facilitate the integration of renewables and charging infrastructure. The project also aligns with the programme’s objective of demonstration and capacity targeted at address the sustainable end-of-life use of batteries. Lessons learned from this project and chance to leverage lessons from abroad through participation in the regional and global programme’s platform, ensuring the child project contribute to the programme’s global impact.

planEntities.parentName: Competitive, sustainable and inclusive urban development that supports social and economic well-being for the population.
planEntities.description:
The project, Sustainable City Development in Malaysia, aims i) promote an integrated approach to urban planning and management that is guided by an evidence-based, multi-dimensional, and broadly inclusive planning process that balances economic, social, and environmental resource consideration; and 2. To build awareness and institutional capacity, and promote investment in climate risks mitigation technologies through demonstration projects. 
The project is being implemented in partnership with MIGHT and the State of Melaka (UPEN). The project launched Smart Melaka Blue Print 2035 in Aug (SMB2035). The SMB2035 serves a strategic document for Melaka State to deliver digital transformation towards a smart and sustainable state. To implement this SMB2035, interventions and flagships are planned. For example, Smart Melaka International Conference organized in 7-9 December 2022 aims to be an annual recurrent flagship event. Other planned interventions include Melaka Super App, Melaka Edu and Melaka 5G Smart Pole.

planEntities.name: Unwaste: tackling waste trafficking to support a circular economy in South East Asia.
planEntities.parentName: Transitioning national development towards a decarbonised pathway and a resource efficient economy through the adoption of green growth strategies and practices across all sectors.
planEntities.description:
Implemented by UNODC in cooperation with UNEP and UNITAR, aims to fight trafficking in waste between the EU and Southeast Asia. It does so by promoting enhanced EU-ASEAN Member States partnerships, in support of ongoing efforts towards a circular economy transition, in line with the relevant policy frameworks, with four priority countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. 
UNEP is responsible for the legal components, examining the legal framework in the ASEAN region on waste trafficking and a legal comparative analysis of the four priority countries. UNEP will also develop a policy paper on ‘obstacles waste trafficking poses to the develop of circular economy and best practices from EU and Asia’, and a mapping of existing multilateral mechanisms in place in Southeast Asia to prevent waste trafficking in support of the objectives of the Unwaste project.

planEntities.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

planEntities.name: Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers as a program being adopted from Alzheimer’s Disease International where guidelines to develop the local content needs, Training Modules are modified to suit the local requirements.

The objectives of the training workshop are:
•Provide an understanding of Dementia
•Learning about the Impact of Dementia and how Person-Centred Care is important
•Communication Effectively with a Person with Dementia
•Importance on how to address Behavioural & Psychological Symptoms of Dementia
•Understanding Meaningful Activities and Engagement and how best to manage and roll out these activities
•Knowledge of Legal /Ethical Issues and the importance of Advanced Care Planning
• Pre-tests were conducted at the start of the Training session to determine the level of understanding of Dementia, Stages, and care skill
•Post-Test is also being conducted at the end of the course to understand how the Training Workshop had helped them in the understanding and Care for Person with Dementia
•VARK methodology was used in the Training Workshop as studies have proven Visual, Audiology, Reading/Writing, and Kinesthetic approach have a better way to retain what had been taught through the way of repeating the scenario in action.

The target audience for this Training Workshop were volunteers from Ministry of Health / Ministry of Welfare programs and the majority of volunteers had informal caregiving experience but not Dementia Care Skills.

planEntities.name: Survey of salt levels in street foods to strengthen salt reduction action in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
This project will strengthen the implementation of  Malaysia’s  Salt  Reduction Strategy through generating data about the salt levels in street foods and meals in Malaysia, with a view to: 
(1) providing evidence for accelerating the introduction of mandatory sodium labelling on packaged and street foods, 
(2) informing salt-reduction education messages about what high-salt foods to avoid and what alternatives to consume as part of a strategic behavior change communication plan; and
(3) identifying and engaging food industries producing high-salt foods in reformulation. Analysis of the sodium content will be conducted on street foods which include ready-to-eat foods usually sold by small- to medium-sized vendors in a street, hawker center, or food court. 
This proposal extends ongoing national salt reduction efforts since 2015 and a recent mid-term evaluation of its progress, which elucidated areas for enhancement to ensure the targeted 15% reduction in population salt intake is achieved by 2020.

planEntities.name: Technical support for COVID-19 Geographical Information System (GIS) Mapping and Multisource Surveillance
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description: Monitored, compiled and disseminated media articles, press statements and other sources of relevant information. Extracted, validated and entered daily epidemiologic data relevant to GIS mapping, including but not limited to the number of active cases at the district level, clusters of COVID-19 cases and movement control order implementation areas. Conducted mapping of surveillance and program data using geographical information system (GIS) software, compile information on transmission clusters and tracked information on special interest areas including spot maps for COVID-19, as well as for polio and other diseases upon need. Assisted in the production of Situational Reports and Situational Update presentation materials. Participated in and brief epidemic situations at regular Incident Management Team meetings of COVID-19 in Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam and Singapore. Used GIS as a framework for gathering, managing, and analyzing data to produce maps and other graphic displays of geographic information for analysis and presentation for the WCO Incident Management Team Meetings.

planEntities.name: Social listening and rumours and misinformation management
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
Data collection conducted in partnership with research company, Media Measurement (MM) from the UK, to inform decision and policy making, including strategic communications at MOH. Activities included following online conversational trends related to COVID-19 and COVID-19 vaccines, both in terms of volume and velocity, and a weekly in-depth analysis of not just prominent topics but the emotional and behavioural responses that result. 

Work also includes provision of daily reports as snapshots of the most important online conversations and rumours and misinformation so that MOH can quickly pick up on and respond to these issues. In addition, a rumours and misinformation alert system and repository were created to track their impact and facilitate timely response. Additionally, there is bi-yearly, in-depth analysis of all key topics related to COVID-19, based on the methodology proposed by MM.

planEntities.name: Capacity building for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
WCO collaborated with the School of Population and Global Health, University of Melbourne, to build the capacity for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The findings of this study demonstrated the important contribution of the implemented public health measures in reducing the COVID-19 disease burden. Both vaccination and limiting mobility through lockdowns contributed to slowing the spread of infection, reducing severe illness and mortality and were cost-saving through reducing pressure on healthcare resource utilization. The activity also contributed to building capacity for economic evaluation within the Ministry of Health in preparation for future outbreaks.

planEntities.name: Partner’s forum in September to engage with civil society organizations (CSOs) in developing and implementing innovative evidence-based community engagement initiatives which address cross-cutting health issues pertaining to COVID-19
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
WCO convened a partner’s forum in September to engage with civil society organizations (CSOs) in developing and implementing innovative evidence-based community engagement initiatives which address cross-cutting health issues pertaining to COVID-19. 

The forum analyzed enablers and barriers to getting COVID-19 vaccines, how to increase COVID-19 vaccine uptake among people at high risk of getting severely ill from COVID-19 in areas with low booster uptake, how to increase adherence to COVID-19 protective behaviors, prevention and control of NCDs amid the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 33 participants from 22 CSOs/NGOs attended the forum. Following the meeting, 25 concept notes were received, reviewed and sifted to 5 proposals for further review. The selected proposal will be chosen for further activity implementation in 2023.

As a result of these initiatives, the most vulnerable individuals including those with significant medical conditions from over 20 nationalities were able to start new lives in more than 10 host countries, where they have access to healthcare, employment, formal education, and pathways to citizenship. In CY 2022 IOM facilitated the resettlement of 4,367 refugees including medical screening, vaccinations and treatment for communicable diseases, and cultural orientation prior to departure to a new country. planEntities.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

planEntities.name: Addressing marine litter in South-East Asia
planEntities.parentName: Preparedness and resilience (especially of indigenous, poor, at-risk communities) against climate change, natural hazards, and disaster risks are strengthened.
planEntities.description:
Under this project, Mersing Islands (Malaysia) to demonstrate integrated waste management good practices in remote/island communities to reduce and prevent plastic waste leakage into the coastal and marine environment in line with the Regional Action Plan on Marine Litter (RAP MALI). 

Prior to project activities, no waste management practices existed in the Mersing Islands and plastic waste was largely littered or burned. Through the pilot, an integral waste management system was created with the community, and the population received education on reducing and segregating plastic for recycling and disposal. This includes the use of a plastic compacting machine and simple disposal and sorting infrastructure, so recyclables can be processed and taken to the mainland to be recycled. 

The pilot was implemented in partnership with Reef-Check Malaysia (USD 55,000 SSFA).

planEntities.name: Mobilising Stakeholders to Inform the Development of a Science-based decision Support System for Coastal Wetlands in the ASEAN Region
planEntities.parentName: Natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems are sustainably managed, adequately protected and conserved for long-term economic and environmental sustainability.
planEntities.description: This project aimed to generate informed recommendations and ideas for the development of an online knowledge sharing platform in the ASEAN region to support science-based decision system for coastal and marine biodiversity conservation and management. The project involved a stakeholder consultation process to explore the information and marine conservation capacity needs of natural resource managers, the business sector, and government organizations. This process of national and regional consultation was held with representatives and stakeholders from all 10 ASEAN Member States, and included national workshops, a regional experts forum, and an online survey. These activities were structured with the view to inform the design of the new platform. UNEP-WCMC provided technical advice and input on the consultations, and produced a discussion paper that synthesised all results and provided recommendations on development of the online knowledge sharing platform. This discussion paper is now being finalised, and a Phase 2 of the project is hoping to be developed to pursue development of the platform.

planEntities.name: Understanding Pathways to Adolescent Pregnancy in Southeast Asia
planEntities.parentName: Increased adoption of inclusive social norms and values and rejection of harmful practices, particularly against women and girls, and the creation of demand for services
planEntities.description:
This study, conducted in Malaysia as part of a wider Southeast Asia study, is a collaboration between the Burnet Institute, UNFPA, and UNICEF. The study aims to improve understanding of the drivers and pathways to adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia and inform effective policy and programming responses. The primary objective of the study is to identify and explore the drivers and pathways to both intended and unintended adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia, including the relationship with early marriage/union. The study's secondary objective is to develop policy and programming recommendations, co-created with adolescents, to effectively address adolescent pregnancy.

The report was launched on 18 October 2023 as a joint initiative by UNFPA Malaysia and UNICEF Malaysia and was developed by the Burnet Institute.  The report included in-depth interviews with 45 adolescent girls from three states in Malaysia – Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang, and highlighted six pathways to adolescent pregnancy. The reports underscore the importance of adolescent-responsive health services, comprehensive sexuality education, supportive relationships, and enabling environments that empower girls to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health and lives.

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. planEntities.name: Understanding Pathways to Adolescent Pregnancy in Southeast Asia
planEntities.parentName: Increased adoption of inclusive social norms and values and rejection of harmful practices, particularly against women and girls, and the creation of demand for services
planEntities.description:
This study, conducted in Malaysia as part of a wider Southeast Asia study, is a collaboration between the Burnet Institute, UNFPA, and UNICEF. The study aims to improve understanding of the drivers and pathways to adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia and inform effective policy and programming responses. The primary objective of the study is to identify and explore the drivers and pathways to both intended and unintended adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia, including the relationship with early marriage/union. The study's secondary objective is to develop policy and programming recommendations, co-created with adolescents, to effectively address adolescent pregnancy.

The report was launched on 18 October 2023 as a joint initiative by UNFPA Malaysia and UNICEF Malaysia and was developed by the Burnet Institute.  The report included in-depth interviews with 45 adolescent girls from three states in Malaysia – Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang, and highlighted six pathways to adolescent pregnancy. The reports underscore the importance of adolescent-responsive health services, comprehensive sexuality education, supportive relationships, and enabling environments that empower girls to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health and lives.

The project was promoted and branded as the “Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project” (MAEESTA). The Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project (MAEESTA) which started being implemented in July 2014 was initially designed for a five-year duration. However, due to challenges faced while implementing the project especially to convince companies to invest in implementing energy efficiency measures and in the demonstration plant, and due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic which started affecting the country in early 2020, the project was approved to be extended for another three years, i.e. until June 2022.
The project’s objective was to reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions by promoting and demonstrating sector-specific energy efficiency (EE) improvements and solar thermal technology utilization in industry. The industrial sub-sectors stated in the project’s document mainly cover the raw material processing and manufacturing sectors. The hospitality sector (hotels and hospitals) was agreed to be included as one of the focused industrial sub-sectors during the second National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) meeting held on 16th December 2016. 

The project completed in June 2022. More details on achievements will be provided shortly.

To build awareness and institutional capacity, and promote investment in climate risks mitigation technologies through demonstration projects.

planEntities.parentName: Transitioning national development towards a decarbonised pathway and a resource efficient economy through the adoption of green growth strategies and practices across all sectors.
planEntities.description:
Implemented by UNODC in cooperation with UNEP and UNITAR, aims to fight trafficking in waste between the EU and Southeast Asia. It does so by promoting enhanced EU-ASEAN Member States partnerships, in support of ongoing efforts towards a circular economy transition, in line with the relevant policy frameworks, with four priority countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. 
UNEP is responsible for the legal components, examining the legal framework in the ASEAN region on waste trafficking and a legal comparative analysis of the four priority countries. UNEP will also develop a policy paper on ‘obstacles waste trafficking poses to the develop of circular economy and best practices from EU and Asia’, and a mapping of existing multilateral mechanisms in place in Southeast Asia to prevent waste trafficking in support of the objectives of the Unwaste project.

planEntities.name: Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers as a program being adopted from Alzheimer’s Disease International where guidelines to develop the local content needs, Training Modules are modified to suit the local requirements.

The objectives of the training workshop are:
•Provide an understanding of Dementia
•Learning about the Impact of Dementia and how Person-Centred Care is important
•Communication Effectively with a Person with Dementia
•Importance on how to address Behavioural & Psychological Symptoms of Dementia
•Understanding Meaningful Activities and Engagement and how best to manage and roll out these activities
•Knowledge of Legal /Ethical Issues and the importance of Advanced Care Planning
• Pre-tests were conducted at the start of the Training session to determine the level of understanding of Dementia, Stages, and care skill
•Post-Test is also being conducted at the end of the course to understand how the Training Workshop had helped them in the understanding and Care for Person with Dementia
•VARK methodology was used in the Training Workshop as studies have proven Visual, Audiology, Reading/Writing, and Kinesthetic approach have a better way to retain what had been taught through the way of repeating the scenario in action.

The target audience for this Training Workshop were volunteers from Ministry of Health / Ministry of Welfare programs and the majority of volunteers had informal caregiving experience but not Dementia Care Skills.

planEntities.name: Survey of salt levels in street foods to strengthen salt reduction action in Malaysia
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
This project will strengthen the implementation of  Malaysia’s  Salt  Reduction Strategy through generating data about the salt levels in street foods and meals in Malaysia, with a view to: 
(1) providing evidence for accelerating the introduction of mandatory sodium labelling on packaged and street foods, 
(2) informing salt-reduction education messages about what high-salt foods to avoid and what alternatives to consume as part of a strategic behavior change communication plan; and
(3) identifying and engaging food industries producing high-salt foods in reformulation. Analysis of the sodium content will be conducted on street foods which include ready-to-eat foods usually sold by small- to medium-sized vendors in a street, hawker center, or food court. 
This proposal extends ongoing national salt reduction efforts since 2015 and a recent mid-term evaluation of its progress, which elucidated areas for enhancement to ensure the targeted 15% reduction in population salt intake is achieved by 2020.

planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description: Monitored, compiled and disseminated media articles, press statements and other sources of relevant information. Extracted, validated and entered daily epidemiologic data relevant to GIS mapping, including but not limited to the number of active cases at the district level, clusters of COVID-19 cases and movement control order implementation areas. Conducted mapping of surveillance and program data using geographical information system (GIS) software, compile information on transmission clusters and tracked information on special interest areas including spot maps for COVID-19, as well as for polio and other diseases upon need. Assisted in the production of Situational Reports and Situational Update presentation materials. Participated in and brief epidemic situations at regular Incident Management Team meetings of COVID-19 in Malaysia, Brunei Darussalam and Singapore. planEntities.name: Social listening and rumours and misinformation management
planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
Data collection conducted in partnership with research company, Media Measurement (MM) from the UK, to inform decision and policy making, including strategic communications at MOH. Activities included following online conversational trends related to COVID-19 and COVID-19 vaccines, both in terms of volume and velocity, and a weekly in-depth analysis of not just prominent topics but the emotional and behavioural responses that result. 

Work also includes provision of daily reports as snapshots of the most important online conversations and rumours and misinformation so that MOH can quickly pick up on and respond to these issues. In addition, a rumours and misinformation alert system and repository were created to track their impact and facilitate timely response. Additionally, there is bi-yearly, in-depth analysis of all key topics related to COVID-19, based on the methodology proposed by MM.

planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
WCO collaborated with the School of Population and Global Health, University of Melbourne, to build the capacity for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The findings of this study demonstrated the important contribution of the implemented public health measures in reducing the COVID-19 disease burden. Both vaccination and limiting mobility through lockdowns contributed to slowing the spread of infection, reducing severe illness and mortality and were cost-saving through reducing pressure on healthcare resource utilization. The activity also contributed to building capacity for economic evaluation within the Ministry of Health in preparation for future outbreaks.

planEntities.parentName: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
planEntities.description:
WCO convened a partner’s forum in September to engage with civil society organizations (CSOs) in developing and implementing innovative evidence-based community engagement initiatives which address cross-cutting health issues pertaining to COVID-19. 

The forum analyzed enablers and barriers to getting COVID-19 vaccines, how to increase COVID-19 vaccine uptake among people at high risk of getting severely ill from COVID-19 in areas with low booster uptake, how to increase adherence to COVID-19 protective behaviors, prevention and control of NCDs amid the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 33 participants from 22 CSOs/NGOs attended the forum. Following the meeting, 25 concept notes were received, reviewed and sifted to 5 proposals for further review. The selected proposal will be chosen for further activity implementation in 2023.

planEntities.description:
RECONCILIATION AND REINTEGRATION OF FORMER ARMED NON-STATE COMBATANTS AND BOKO HARAM ASSOCIATES (S2R)	// Project Number: 00120397 // 1 January -  30 November 2022												
This project aims to enhance community preparedness for reintegration and reduction of rejection and stigmatisation of former associates in selected areas in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe States, preparing ground for community-based healing and reconciliation. The main outputs that the project seeks to achieve include: Communities are sensitised and prepared for reconciliation and reintegration; Community-level transitional / restorative justice mechanisms are developed; Conflict-sensitive community-prioritised livelihoods are created for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Stratified community-led activities increase community cohesiveness and coping mechanisms for the most vulnerable, low risk associates and non-state security providers; Process developed for non-state security providers to be disarmed, demobilised and reintegrated; Inclusive, responsive and accountable structures to manage DDRR activities are created between and across the various levels of government and communities. Specific interventions that will contribute to these outputs include: widespread advocacy and awareness campaigns; design and deployment of reconciliation and reintegration platforms, committees and volunteer groups; community-based and led reconciliation and restorative justice processes; strengthening community-level “peace dividends” advancing interventions in the form of community-led social impact project that help to build resilience to violence; and a multiple targeting approach, where selected community members received targeted assistance (along with low-risk former NSAG associates and CTJF/vigilante group members)."

planEntities.description: UNDP: The One UN Response to COVID-19 in Nigeria Project seeks to support national efforts towards optimum care of confirmed COVID-19 cases and to contain the spread of the outbreak through an inclusive and nationally owned response based on best practices from previous health emergencies as well as lessons learned and experiences from other countries during the COVID-19 crisis. Using the One UN approach, the project’s objective will be realized through six outputs: Output 1: Improved rapid procurement of disease commodity packages for surveillance, prevention and control, and clinical management; Output 2: Complementary ongoing risk communication strategies for sustained community engagement and cooperation (RCCE) are supported; Output 3: Development of tailored and decentralized response strategies at the state level that are aligned with the coordinated framework at the federal level supported; Output 4: Access to essential health services maintained through socio-economic analytics and proactive early recovery and social protection activities targeting vulnerable groups; Output 5: Capacities for R&D and modelling strengthened; Output 6: Coordination of partnerships and mobilization of resources for collective response improved. The project is enabled by support from public and private sector resources channelled through the One UN COVID-19 Response Basket Fund with WHO, UNICEF, UNDP, UN Women, UNFPA, UNAIDS, UNIDO and ILO as the participating UN agencies (PUNOs).

planEntities.name: 3.1.2.5 - Pillar 1 (SC): Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) Policies and Gender-sensitive Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Education National
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.2 - Policies and Strategies for infrastructural and private sector development, clean energy and Science Technology and Innovation developed to boost sectoral Growth and Productivity.
planEntities.description:
Within the framework of the Nigeria-UNESCO Special plan of cooperation, UNESCO is collaborating with  the Federal Ministry of Science and Technology to implement two activities 
i)	STI Mapping Training (GOSPIN + SAGA) for FMST Science Officers/Researchers, planned; with the following objectives; 
•	Reinforce and/ or upgrade participants' knowledge and understanding of STI policy review processes. 
•	Expose participants to new approaches and methodologies for reviewing and mapping STI policy.
•	 Foster necessary interactions and exchange of knowledge amongst the key stakeholders in the on-going STI policy review exercises
ii)	ii) Pre-Activity for Revision of the 2012 STI Policy; to produce STI performance evaluation document

UNESCO is assisting Nigeria to develop a project proposal on Science Technology Engineering and Mathematics Education (STEM). This is against the backdrop of the recommendation of the UNESCO global Open science dialogue on Covid-19……. “calls for countries to strengthen their national STI systems and build a global critical mass in STEM fields to make science work for all, leaving no-one behind”. The project concept and proposals be used to mobilize funds in 2021 towards implementation in Nigeria

planEntities.name: 3.3.1.11 - Pillar 2 (SC)- Water Security through scientific cooperation
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3.1 - Human and institutional capacities strengthened to ensure sustainable environmental management and food security.
planEntities.description:
UNESCO facilitated the participation of Nigeria in the e-Learning training on “ Flood Early Waring, Flood Hazard Mapping and Contingency Planning”. This training will enable Nigeria, set up and operate flood early warning systems. Participation included Nigerian Emergency management Agency (NEMA), National Water Resources Institute (NWRI), Nigerian Hydrological service Agency (NIHSA) and Regional Center for Integrated River Basin management (RC-IRBM)  
In 2020 a high level online Advocacy event tagged “Water and Climate Change: Women’s Coping Strategies In West Africa, was organized via zoom platform. This Online event was jointly organized by UNESCO Multisectoral Regional Office Abuja, UNESCO World Water Assessment Programme (WWAP) Perugia-Italy and UNESCO Category II Center namely; Regional Center for Integrated River Basin Management IRC-IRBM), Kaduna-Nigeria.   Participants/target beneficiaries included water and gender 35 experts from Nigeria ( Men 20: Women 15), The  event featured presentation of the 2019 WWAP Toolkit on sex-disaggregated water data.  “The toolkit contains a priority topic on water, migration, displacement and climate change, dedicated indicators and the related questions for the collection of data in the field, making it a valuable tool for the collection of much-needed and currently scarce sex-disaggregated water data. The tool kit will be used for the two technical trainings in 2021.

planEntities.name: 3.3.1.13 - Pillar 3 (SC)   Biosphere Reserves; towards the achievement of SDGs and targets related to biodiversity and climate change resilience
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3.1 - Human and institutional capacities strengthened to ensure sustainable environmental management and food security.
planEntities.description:
UNESCO assisted the Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) to prepare and submit a nomination dossier for designation of two Biosphere Reserves. (BRs). BRs promote Biodiversity conservation and are learning areas for sustainable development, creating mitigation, resilience and adaptation projects, aiming to make local communities take part in the fight against climate change 
In 2020 Due to the current COVID-19 health crisis and following the decision of the Bureau of the Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme, UNESCO facilitated the organisation of the 32nd Session of the International Coordinating Council of the MAB Programme (MAB-ICC)  which was held virtually on 27 and 28 October 2020.. A total of 273 participants attended. Several issues were discussed including approval of new Biosphere reserves

In collaboration with Nigerian Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (NiPBES), organized on 29th September 2020  a high level  online event tagged  “Science Advice for COVID-19 Pandemic: in the context of Biodiversity Conservation and Ecological Restoration”. Main objectives were to Receive recommendations on Science advice for Covid-19;  especially in the context of Biodiversity conservation;  and create awareness on the need for biodiversity conservation to allow safe space for a balanced and sustainable Human-nature interaction, in the context of protected areas and UNESCO Biosphere

Nigeria.name: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
Nigeria.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.7 - Strengthen capacity on effective investigation, prosecution and adjudication of terrorism offences in Nigeria.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Evidence based and gender sensitive policies and institutional mechanisms (including anticorruption, electoral support, rule of law, and access to justice and preventing human trafficking) enabled at the national/sub-national level for good governance.
planEntities.description:
In partnership with and guided by the Nigerian authorities and stakeholders, UNODC has been implementing a multi-phased programme of technical assistance since 2012. The overall objective of the partnership programme is to support Nigeria to strengthen its criminal justice responses to terrorism, enhancing capacity for effective implementation of counter-terrorism related provisions and good practices in accordance with the rule of law and with due respect for human rights. 
From April 2018, UNODC has been delivering the three-year EU-Nigeria-UNODC-CTED Partnership Project III: Supporting Nigeria to strengthen criminal justice measures for preventing and countering terrorism and violent extremism, funded by the European Union. The project aims to support Nigeria to strengthen its capacity to address terrorism and violent extremism, with a focus on the Northeast, by rendering investigation, prosecution and adjudication of terrorism-related offences  more effective, and accountable in line with international standards on human rights; supporting the development of strategies for the prosecution, rehabilitation and reintegration of persons associated with Boko Haram; and  building approaches for effectively countering violent extremism with an emphasis on prevention.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.8 - Enhance awareness of anti-corruption data and measures in Nigeria.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Evidence based and gender sensitive policies and institutional mechanisms (including anticorruption, electoral support, rule of law, and access to justice and preventing human trafficking) enabled at the national/sub-national level for good governance.
planEntities.description: As a follow-up to the first survey report (published 2017), the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) in Nigeria with the support of UNODC and funding of the UK Government conducted a second comprehensive corruption survey in 2019, interviewing over 33.000 households across all 36 States and the Federal Capital Territory. The report was launched 9 December 2019 (nationally) and 16 December 2019 (internationally, on the side line of the 8th Conference of State Party to UNCAC). The survey findings provide a crucial measure to assess actual impact of the Nigerian Government’s efforts to curtail corruption while providing concrete steps/actions for anti-corruption interventions/initiatives in Nigeria.  A gender and corruption report was launched 8 December 2020 using data from the corruption survey. The gender report presents the first empirical evidence on gender and corruption in the country and aims to encourage debate about whether and how gender equality in the public administration of Nigeria can contribute to an effective reduction in corruption

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.9 - Enhance national capacities to fight human trafficking in Nigeria.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Evidence based and gender sensitive policies and institutional mechanisms (including anticorruption, electoral support, rule of law, and access to justice and preventing human trafficking) enabled at the national/sub-national level for good governance.
planEntities.description: In the policy area, UNODC is currently supporting Nigeria to strengthen its strategic and policy framework against TIP/SOM through the development of a new National Action Plan against trafficking in persons under the leadership of NAPTIP. UNODC is also providing technical assistance to NAPTIP and NIS to build the agencies capacities in collecting, analyzing and using data for an evidence-based criminal justice response to these crimes. UNODC has also recently been supporting NAPTIP and other partners in establishing State Task Forces against human trafficking, as well as engaging with a broader range of partners (aviation sector, artists etc.) to enhance partnership in preventing trafficking. As concerns the criminal justice response, as of 2021 and building on the deployment of Nigerian liaison magistrates in Europe, UNODC will provide mentoring and training services to law enforcement agencies and prosecutors to increase the number of successful convictions for trafficking and smuggling cases. UNODC activities against trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants in Nigeria are currently funded by various governments including Canada, Switzerland, United States, Denmark and the Netherlands.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2.10 - Strengthening Nigeria’s response to the trafficking of wildlife and forestry products.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2 - Evidence based and gender sensitive policies and institutional mechanisms (including anticorruption, electoral support, rule of law, and access to justice and preventing human trafficking) enabled at the national/sub-national level for good governance.
planEntities.description:
In recent years, Nigeria has evolved into a primary transit hub for trafficking in illicit wildlife products. According to the UNODC World Wildlife Crime Report 2020, Nigeria has emerged as one of the leading source and transit point for the illicit trafficking in elephant tusks, pangolin scales, rosewood (Pterocarpus Erinaceus, known in Nigeria as “kosso”) and other endangered wildlife and forest products. 

To support the Government of Nigeria in tackling wildlife and forest crime, UNODC, with the support of the Government of Germany, is partnering with the Federal Ministry of Environment, the Nigeria Customs Service, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) and  other state and non-state actors to implement the Project, “Strengthening Nigeria’s Response to the Trafficking of Wildlife and Forestry Products”. The project commenced implementation in July 2020 and is expected to run for 30 months till 31 December 2022. The Project has three main outcome areas: Outcome 1: National policy frameworks and domestic coordination to address wildlife and forest crime strengthened; Outcome 2: Capacity of frontline officers to detect and intercept illegal shipments of wildlife improved; and Outcome 3: Prosecutorial and judicial capacity to investigate, prosecute and adjudicate wildlife and forest crime strengthened.
