planEntities.name: 2.1.2.29 - Support to HIV and health services in prisons and among people who use drugs
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2 - Strengthened health system to deliver an integrated package on high impact health, nutrition and HIV interventions including in emergency situations
planEntities.description:
Globally, HIV prevalence and new infections have drastically reduced however, Nigeria ranks third among the countries with high number of people living with HIV with an estimated 1.8 million people living with the infection in 2019. While some of the drivers of new infections in the society include low condom use, gender inequality and multiple sexual partners, new infections among people who use drugs and people in custodial centres are attributed to sharing of needles and other paraphernalia, drug use in custodial centres, forced sex and unprotected sexual intercourse in custodial centres amongst others.

People who inject drugs (PWIDs) are also particularly vulnerable to HIV and AIDS. According to UNODC survey on drug use in Nigeria, 9% of PWIDs in Nigeria live with HIV and AIDS. Prevention of the negative health and social consequences of drug use is critical for both drug users and the society at large. The introduction and scaling up of core interventions as outlined in the WHO, UNODC, UNAIDS “Technical Guide for Countries to Set Targets for Universal Access to HIV Prevention, Treatment and Care for Injecting Drug Users”, are important measures for prevention, treatment, and care of HIV among PWIDs in the community and in prison settings.

To effectively address the above, UNODC Country Office in Nigeria is supporting the Government of Nigeria on HIV testing services in Nigeria custodial centres, HIV care in prisons and linkages to healthcare in the community, Harm reduction and drug demand reduction activities (i.e Needle and Syringe Programme, Opioids Substitution Therapy) and in the conduct of further studies relating to HIV and drug use.

planEntities.name: 2.4.2.8 - Conduct capacity building for countering drug trafficking and drug abuse.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.4.2 - By 2022, protection systems and services are strengthened to more effectively prevent and respond to violence, abuse, exploitation (including trafficking) and harmful social norms in target states.
planEntities.description: To promote good governance, security and public health in Nigeria, this EU-funded project “Response to Drugs and Related Organized Crime in Nigeria” supports Nigeria’s efforts in fighting drug production, trafficking and use, and in curbing related organised crime including counterfeit narcotics and psychotropic substances. The project aims i) to support evidence-based policy formulation, and improve legislation and coordination; ii) to improve law enforcement and regulatory capacity in drug control and tackling organised drug-related crime; and iii) to enhance drug prevention, treatment and care services, adapted to Nigerian conditions.  The project focuses on where drugs and organised crime interlock, in line with relevant international conventions and with a balanced, human-rights-based approach rooted in international best practice and a quest for public health enhancement.

planEntities.name: HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services
planEntities.parentName: National & local institutions have strengthened capacity to monitor and scale up high quality HIV prevention, treatment and support services
planEntities.description:
Linked to UBRAF outcome 1: People living with, at risk of and affected by HIV obtain equitable access and reap equitable benefits from HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services.

Country summary of results:
HIV prevention was prioritized by the joint programme in 2022. WHO and UNAIDS contributed to the publication of the revised policy guidelines for PrEP and HIV Self-testing. PrEP and PEP for all along with innovations such as Cabotegravir and the Dapivirine ring were included in the revision. Advocacy continued for condoms and lubricants for key and priority populations, and UNFPA supported the launch of a campaign to increase accessibility and use of condoms for HIV and STI prevention particularly for AGYW and key-priority populations. UNAIDS guided the HIV Prevention Acceleration Team supported by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, to complete the HIV Prevention Self-Assessment Tool (PSAT) with AGYW. Findings suggested that there is a need for a costed, comprehensive, and tailored HIV prevention package of services for AGYW. Regarding HIV treatment, care, and support, DSD strategies were scaled across the country with technical support from the joint programme. UNICEF, WHO, and UNAIDS significantly contributed to the publication of the test, treat, and track Consolidated Guidelines for HIV Care in Ghana. The guideline closely aligns with 2022 WHO guidance on testing and treatment and was reviewed by WHO program experts in the Global Centre before publication. With advocacy from WHO Ghana, the guidelines included the adoption of the more efficacious and pediatric friendly anti-retroviral DTG-10 regime, and WHO supported a costed road map for DTG-10 transition for all. UNICEF led a study in the 5 highest burden regions to audit the care of 426 HIV exposed infants of which 189 were HIV positive. The study aim was to identify the factors contributing to new infant infections and develop context-specific interventions to eliminate MTCT and new postnatal infections. Regarding family-based testing, 179 PLHIVs were offered Family HIV Testing, 141 accepted and 309 children were tracked for testing. Among the children tracked, 284 were successfully contacted and 262 were tested for HIV. Of those tested, 53 were found positive and 46 (86.8%) of these children were linked to care. This pilot was meant to encourage accelerated scale up of family-based testing for all by the GF PRs. The joint programme supported capacity building to accelerate progress on the Global AIDS targets. UNESCO supported the Ministry of Education/Ghana Education Service, by building capacities of 4908 teachers on HIV Prevention Education in schools including schools for learners with disabilities. As a result, a total of about 43,000 learners continue to receive lessons on HIV prevention in schools through these trained teachers. Additionally, WHO provided technical support to build capacity and quality of DSD service delivery by providing access to an online training platform for health care workers (doctors, nurses, and pharmacists). The online course was completed by over 4000 health care workers who were awarded Continuous Professional Education credits. Finally, UNAIDS and WHO provided technical assistance to the Ghana AIDS Commisison and the National AIDS Control Programme to elaborate the GAM report, and the HIV Spectrum epidemic estimates. Also, technical advisory was provided to both entities to analyse information in the Situation Rooms.

planEntities.name: Communities and HIV resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers
planEntities.parentName: Key and marginalized populations are empowered to access quality HIV/AIDS services
planEntities.description:
Linked to UBRAF Outcome 2: Communities of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people, are empowered, enabled and effectively resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers of the HIV epidemic are removed.

Country summary of results: (*Note; UNDP activities included here were separately reported by UNDP. Therefore, we will not include financial data for that UNDP-led activity in this sub-output). 
The joint programme works across the domains of the Global AIDS Strategy (GAS) to ensure that the HIV response in Ghana is people-centered and optimized for communities and networks of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people. UNDP led a significant assessment on the structural drivers of stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra, the region with the highest burden of HIV in the country. The goal of the assessment was to strengthen stigma reduction efforts and ensure that health facilities and health care workers are equipped to provide nondiscriminatory services. UNDP in partnership with the NACP conducted health care worker baseline assessments, client stigma perception assessments, and capacity building trainings. As a result of findings of these assessments, 213 (162 women, 51 men) health workers in these 10 health facilities in Greater Accra Region have the requisite skills to provide non-discriminatory services to over 17,000 PLHIV. The population of PLHIV in Greater Accra includes all populations and is more likely to include AGYW networks and networks of PLHIV from KPs. Participants in the assessment, directors of the 10 health facilities, increased their knowledge, management of frontline healthcare workers to promote policies that eliminate stigma and discrimination, and capacities to champion policies and strategies, such as the National Human Rights Strategy to Eliminate Stigma and Discrimination, with the MOH, Ghana Health Service, and leadership in agencies such as the National Health Insurance Authority. The assessment resulted in a reduction of HIV related stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra and created health director champion advocates for the elimination of stigma and discrimination at HIV service delivery in the region with the highest HIV burden. Furthermore, in partnership with the Ghana AIDS Commission, UNDP provided capacity building to the leadership of the national and regional persons living with HIV (NAP+) to empower them to improve their skills in advocacy and knowledge sharing around the removal of social and structural barriers related to stigma and discrimination. The capacity building resulted in the championing of equitable access to HIV services from a people-centered, people-led human rights perspective. Community engagement and advocacy by the PLHIV were enhanced as they took greater leadership roles with the CCM and on national steering committees. As a result of the capacity building by UNDP and advocacy with Government partners, by UNAIDS and WHO, PLHIV played a more significant role in the implementation of the GF NFM III, particularly related to activities for AGYW and those lead by PLHIV community cadres to reduce new infections and ensure greater continuity of treatment and care by mothers and adolescents newly infected with HIV. UNAIDS and WHO served as technical leads on the steering committee of the CSO GF principal recipient and led advocacy for accountability around community engagement—always questioning the role of PLHIV, AGYW, and KPs in service delivery to ensure that the GAS is achieved with communities.

The joint programme works across the domains of the Global AIDS Strategy (GAS) to ensure that the HIV response in Ghana is people-centered and optimized for communities and networks of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people. UNDP led a significant assessment on the structural drivers of stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra, the region with the highest burden of HIV in the country. The goal of the assessment was to strengthen stigma reduction efforts and ensure that health facilities and health care workers are equipped to provide nondiscriminatory services. UNDP in partnership with the NACP conducted health care worker baseline assessments, client stigma perception assessments, and capacity building trainings. As a result of findings of these assessments, 213 (162 women, 51 men) health workers in these 10 health facilities in Greater Accra Region have the requisite skills to provide non-discriminatory services to over 17,000 PLHIV. The population of PLHIV in Greater Accra includes all populations and is more likely to include AGYW networks and networks of PLHIV from KPs. Participants in the assessment, directors of the 10 health facilities, increased their knowledge, management of frontline healthcare workers to promote policies that eliminate stigma and discrimination, and capacities to champion policies and strategies, such as the National Human Rights Strategy to Eliminate Stigma and Discrimination, with the MOH, Ghana Health Service, and leadership in agencies such as the National Health Insurance Authority. The assessment resulted in a reduction of HIV related stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra and created health director champion advocates for the elimination of stigma and discrimination at HIV service delivery in the region with the highest HIV burden. Furthermore, in partnership with the Ghana AIDS Commission, UNDP provided capacity building to the leadership of the national and regional persons living with HIV (NAP+) to empower them to improve their skills in advocacy and knowledge sharing around the removal of social and structural barriers related to stigma and discrimination. The capacity building resulted in the championing of equitable access to HIV services from a people-centered, people-led human rights perspective. Community engagement and advocacy by the PLHIV were enhanced as they took greater leadership roles with the CCM and on national steering committees. As a result of the capacity building by UNDP and advocacy with Government partners, by UNAIDS and WHO, PLHIV played a more significant role in the implementation of the GF NFM III, particularly related to activities for AGYW and those lead by PLHIV community cadres to reduce new infections and ensure greater continuity of treatment and care by mothers and adolescents newly infected with HIV. UNAIDS and WHO served as technical leads on the steering committee of the CSO GF principal recipient and led advocacy for accountability around community engagement—always questioning the role of PLHIV, AGYW, and KPs in service delivery to ensure that the GAS is achieved with communities.

planEntities.name: HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services
planEntities.parentName: National & local institutions have strengthened capacity to monitor and scale up high quality HIV prevention, treatment and support services
planEntities.description:
Linked to UBRAF outcome 1: People living with, at risk of and affected by HIV obtain equitable access and reap equitable benefits from HIV prevention, treatment, care and support services.

Country summary of results:
HIV prevention was prioritized by the joint programme in 2022. WHO and UNAIDS contributed to the publication of the revised policy guidelines for PrEP and HIV Self-testing. PrEP and PEP for all along with innovations such as Cabotegravir and the Dapivirine ring were included in the revision. Advocacy continued for condoms and lubricants for key and priority populations, and UNFPA supported the launch of a campaign to increase accessibility and use of condoms for HIV and STI prevention particularly for AGYW and key-priority populations. UNAIDS guided the HIV Prevention Acceleration Team supported by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, to complete the HIV Prevention Self-Assessment Tool (PSAT) with AGYW. Findings suggested that there is a need for a costed, comprehensive, and tailored HIV prevention package of services for AGYW. Regarding HIV treatment, care, and support, DSD strategies were scaled across the country with technical support from the joint programme. UNICEF, WHO, and UNAIDS significantly contributed to the publication of the test, treat, and track Consolidated Guidelines for HIV Care in Ghana. The guideline closely aligns with 2022 WHO guidance on testing and treatment and was reviewed by WHO program experts in the Global Centre before publication. With advocacy from WHO Ghana, the guidelines included the adoption of the more efficacious and pediatric friendly anti-retroviral DTG-10 regime, and WHO supported a costed road map for DTG-10 transition for all. UNICEF led a study in the 5 highest burden regions to audit the care of 426 HIV exposed infants of which 189 were HIV positive. The study aim was to identify the factors contributing to new infant infections and develop context-specific interventions to eliminate MTCT and new postnatal infections. Regarding family-based testing, 179 PLHIVs were offered Family HIV Testing, 141 accepted and 309 children were tracked for testing. Among the children tracked, 284 were successfully contacted and 262 were tested for HIV. Of those tested, 53 were found positive and 46 (86.8%) of these children were linked to care. This pilot was meant to encourage accelerated scale up of family-based testing for all by the GF PRs. The joint programme supported capacity building to accelerate progress on the Global AIDS targets. UNESCO supported the Ministry of Education/Ghana Education Service, by building capacities of 4908 teachers on HIV Prevention Education in schools including schools for learners with disabilities. As a result, a total of about 43,000 learners continue to receive lessons on HIV prevention in schools through these trained teachers. Additionally, WHO provided technical support to build capacity and quality of DSD service delivery by providing access to an online training platform for health care workers (doctors, nurses, and pharmacists). The online course was completed by over 4000 health care workers who were awarded Continuous Professional Education credits. Finally, UNAIDS and WHO provided technical assistance to the Ghana AIDS Commisison and the National AIDS Control Programme to elaborate the GAM report, and the HIV Spectrum epidemic estimates. Also, technical advisory was provided to both entities to analyse information in the Situation Rooms.

planEntities.parentName: Primary health care strengthened to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC).
planEntities.description:
In accordance with the terms and conditions of the Grant Agreement between Global Fund and WAPCAS, the Grant can fund the procurement of male condoms through the UNOPS Procurement mechanism, with the Global Fund executing a direct disbursement from the Global Fund to UNOPS. Condoms will be delivered to the Ghana Health Service – National Aids Control Program (NACP).

The project's Legal Agreement, signed on the 2nd of November 2021 and ending on the 31st of July 2022 has an implementation and delivery timeline of 8 months and a total budget of USD 490,000.11 (Four hundred and Ninety Thousand United States Dollars and Eleven Cents).  The project has been extended to March 2023.

However, over time, the project implementation period has been amended and extended to March 2023 following approval for the reprogramming of project savings for the procurement of an extra 9,000 gross (1,296,000 units) in addition to the original request for 52,780 gross (7.6 million units), as well as a new request for 53,820 gross (7,750,000 units) on an additional budget of USD 352,084, bringing the total budget to USD 842,084
UNDP also procured medical equipment and related logistics for health facilities and CHPS compounds in Accra Metropolitan Area and Ga Central municipality to strengthen essential health service delivery. In addition, UNDP in partnership with Ghana Health Service constructed a CHPS compound in Chorkor to further strengthen primary health care in urban slum areas

planEntities.name: Communities and HIV resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers
planEntities.parentName: Key and marginalized populations are empowered to access quality HIV/AIDS services
planEntities.description:
Linked to UBRAF Outcome 2: Communities of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people, are empowered, enabled and effectively resourced to lead HIV service delivery, advocate for and enjoy their right to health, and social and structural drivers of the HIV epidemic are removed.

Country summary of results: (*Note; UNDP activities included here were separately reported by UNDP. Therefore, we will not include financial data for that UNDP-led activity in this sub-output). 
The joint programme works across the domains of the Global AIDS Strategy (GAS) to ensure that the HIV response in Ghana is people-centered and optimized for communities and networks of people living with, at risk of and affected by HIV, including key populations, women and young people. UNDP led a significant assessment on the structural drivers of stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra, the region with the highest burden of HIV in the country. The goal of the assessment was to strengthen stigma reduction efforts and ensure that health facilities and health care workers are equipped to provide nondiscriminatory services. UNDP in partnership with the NACP conducted health care worker baseline assessments, client stigma perception assessments, and capacity building trainings. As a result of findings of these assessments, 213 (162 women, 51 men) health workers in these 10 health facilities in Greater Accra Region have the requisite skills to provide non-discriminatory services to over 17,000 PLHIV. The population of PLHIV in Greater Accra includes all populations and is more likely to include AGYW networks and networks of PLHIV from KPs. Participants in the assessment, directors of the 10 health facilities, increased their knowledge, management of frontline healthcare workers to promote policies that eliminate stigma and discrimination, and capacities to champion policies and strategies, such as the National Human Rights Strategy to Eliminate Stigma and Discrimination, with the MOH, Ghana Health Service, and leadership in agencies such as the National Health Insurance Authority. The assessment resulted in a reduction of HIV related stigma and discrimination in 10 of the largest health facilities in Greater Accra and created health director champion advocates for the elimination of stigma and discrimination at HIV service delivery in the region with the highest HIV burden. Furthermore, in partnership with the Ghana AIDS Commission, UNDP provided capacity building to the leadership of the national and regional persons living with HIV (NAP+) to empower them to improve their skills in advocacy and knowledge sharing around the removal of social and structural barriers related to stigma and discrimination. The capacity building resulted in the championing of equitable access to HIV services from a people-centered, people-led human rights perspective. Community engagement and advocacy by the PLHIV were enhanced as they took greater leadership roles with the CCM and on national steering committees. As a result of the capacity building by UNDP and advocacy with Government partners, by UNAIDS and WHO, PLHIV played a more significant role in the implementation of the GF NFM III, particularly related to activities for AGYW and those lead by PLHIV community cadres to reduce new infections and ensure greater continuity of treatment and care by mothers and adolescents newly infected with HIV. UNAIDS and WHO served as technical leads on the steering committee of the CSO GF principal recipient and led advocacy for accountability around community engagement—always questioning the role of PLHIV, AGYW, and KPs in service delivery to ensure that the GAS is achieved with communities.

planEntities.name: Enhanced land consolidation and mobility of the agricultural land market in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5 Sustainable and competitive rural economy
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, FAO, the European Union, and the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Water Economy (MAFWE) have worked together to enhance the policy, legal, and institutional framework for agricultural land reforms. To address the issue of abandoned agricultural land, FAO supported MAFWE in 2022 and 2023 by analyzing existing tools and implementing best practices from Europe, including mediation for agricultural land leases.  FAO's report "Analysis of Land Abandonment and Development of Agricultural Land Markets in the Republic of North Macedonia - Conclusions and Policy Recommendations" identified key issues like poor land conditions, fragmented farms, inefficient irrigation, and youth outmigration, and offered recommendations for amendments to the Law on Agricultural Land and the Law on Privatization of State-Owned Land. This led to the inclusion of key measures in the April 2023 amendments to address land abandonment and strengthen agriculture.

Since 2017, the European Union and FAO have supported the Macedonian Ministry in addressing land fragmentation, small farm sizes, and inadequate agricultural infrastructure. Through the EU-FAO MAINLAND project (2017–2022), the National Land Consolidation Programme became operational, with initial land consolidation projects setting the stage for further advancements. Building on this foundation, the EU-FAO project "Enhancing Land Consolidation in North Macedonia" has continued to advance these efforts since 2022.
In Dabjani, construction works were finalized in 2024, including the rehabilitation and construction of access roads to the fields spanning 742 hectares of agricultural land. These improvements, funded by the European Union, enhanced connectivity and productivity for 85 landowners, facilitating more efficient agricultural practices and market access. Similarly, in Chiflik, FAO's efforts led to the adoption of a re-allotment plan by the majority of landowners, consolidating 156 fragmented hectares into more manageable and productive land parcels. This initiative directly benefited 395 farmers, laying the groundwork for sustainable agricultural development. Preparations are underway for EU-funded investments in Chiflik, including upgrades to access roads, irrigation systems, and drainage infrastructure, further strengthening rural resilience and productivity.  The end date of the project is 31 January 2026. Total expected funding for the full duration, including years beyond 2025 is USD 1,053,740.

planEntities.name: Strengthened national animal health management in line with EU standards
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5 Sustainable and competitive rural economy
planEntities.description: Developing a roadmap for upgrading the national animal identification, registration and traceability system (Phase 1 - finalized in 2022 - FAO project TCP/MCD/3804/C3). Based on the developed technical documentation and implementation roadmap (Phase I) starting from 2023 (project TCP/MCD/3902) FAO has been supporting the FVA to put the new National Animal Information System in use (Phase 2) unlocking several modules and features presently not available in the obsolete Veterinary Information System (FAO project TCP/MCD 3902 - with end date 31.12.2025). Under this project, FAO is providing technical assistance to the Food and Veterinary Agency (FVA) to harmonize North Macedonia’s National Animal Health and Food Safety System (NAITS) with EU standards. This effort builds on the success of the FAO-developed NAITS software in Georgia as a model. The support includes integrating new modules and configuring system functionalities to create a modern, sustainable, and long-term solution. This upgraded system will enable efficient recording, analysis, and utilization of critical animal data throughout their lifecycle, enhancing management and traceability in the livestock sector. Ultimately, these improvements will contribute to stronger food safety measures and a more resilient agricultural system.

planEntities.name: Development of Country Digital Innovation Profile
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3 Enhanced policies and regulatory environment
planEntities.description: In coordination with the Ministry of Information Society and Administration, the Digital Innovation Profile is being developed to provide an accurate assessment of the ecosystem's capacity and maturity. The assessment is done through a series of events in which stakeholders from the ecosystem come together to analyze the current situation and co-create appropriate solutions via flagship projects and/or initiatives, and policies designed to close the digital innovation gap. The overall aim is to strengthen the digital innovation capabilities of the country. A series of co-creation workshops will be held with North Macedonian stakeholders, from the private sector, the public sector and academia, on recommendations and the assessment of the innovation ecosystem in the country.

planEntities.name: E-waste monitor for the Western Balkans
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.5 Waste reduction and efficient waste management
planEntities.description: Within the framework of the Global E-waste Statistics Partnership, the "ITU-UNEP-UNITAR joint project on 'E-Waste Monitor for the Western Balkans' aims to train on how to make and collect e-waste statistics as well as make an assessment of e-waste statistics, e-waste management practices and the e-waste legislation landscape in the beneficiary countries, including North Macedonia, to produce the Regional E-waste Monitor report for the Western Balkans. This will include the elaboration of a country profile, training, and national workshop raising awareness on the topic of e-waste. Measuring e-waste volumes is an important step towards addressing the e-waste challenge. Statistics help to evaluate developments over time, and set and assess targets, and policies. Better e-waste data will help minimize its generation, prevent illegal dumping, promote recycling, and create jobs in the reuse, refurbishment, and recycling sectors. Overall, the project aims to build foundations for making digitization and digitalization processes green and sustainable.

planEntities.name: Child Online Protection National Assessment

This assessment will be launched in July 2022 during a dedicated session with the Ministry of Information Society and Administration, and the Ministry of Education of North Macedonia. Follow-up will be discussed with the country.

planEntities.name: National Strategy on Digital Skills Development in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2 Quality and affordable education
planEntities.description: Upon request of the country, ITU has launched the Digital Skills Assessment technical assistance in Q4 2021. The outcomes of this initiative will contribute to the development of a national digital skills strategy. The program includes a national assessment, a series of interviews, workshops, and others. The assessment will focus on reviewing and evaluating digital skills in the private sector, academia, and the general public. It will result in a series of recommendations and suggestions to be considered during the further development of the digital strategy. The assessment will be launched in 2022.

•	Changes and effective implementation of anti-discrimination legislation •

planEntities.name: Improved air quality in five municipalities through better monitoring, capacity building, measures implementation and awareness raising
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3 Air pollution in urban areas decreased
planEntities.description:
The second phase of the SIDA funded project builds on the results and lessons learnt from the first phase of the project implemented in Skopje (Aerodrom-Lisice) and scale up the solutions in five other cities in the country that also have serious issues with the air pollution: Kavadarci (Fero-Nikel (FENI) Industry), Gostivar, Kumanovo, Strumica and Struga (use of wood for household heating, unsustainable waste management practices, agriculture, transport, etc.).  
In 2025 the focus will be put on implementing the selected priority measures from the improved Action Plans of the beneficiary municipalities: Kumanovo, Kavadarci, Strumica, Struga, and Gostivar. These measures were chosen through a structured decision-making process called the Community Forum, which involved active participation from local communities. The initiatives include expanding urban green areas, acquiring mechanization for cleaning the streets, implementing energy efficiency measures in public buildings, and creating bicycle paths.

planEntities.name: Development of Soil Protection Strategy and Law on soil protection with Guidelines for Establishing Soil Quality Monitoring Programme
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2 Integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources
planEntities.description:
UNEP:
The draft Law on Soil Protection was initiated, the main objective of which is to provide protection and prevent further soil pollution, as well as desertification from the intensification of agriculture, mining, road construction, and urban land use and climate change impacts.  
In parallel, UNEP will continue working on development of the Strategy and Law on Soil Protection (including analysis of the current legal and institutional framework), as well as update/development of the Local Environmental Action Plans for the targeted municipalities. 

The Strategy will provide a framework within which soil quality is protected from degradation, as well as mechanisms by which changes in soil quality can be measured and the effectiveness of remedial actions assessed. The Strategy will be accompanied by guidelines for establishing a national soil quality monitoring programme with soil quality indicators set.

planEntities.name: E-waste monitor for the Western Balkans
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.5 Waste reduction and efficient waste management
planEntities.description: Within the framework of the Global E-waste Statistics Partnership, the "ITU-UNEP-UNITAR joint project on 'E-Waste Monitor for the Western Balkans' aims to train on how to make and collect e-waste statistics as well as make an assessment of e-waste statistics, e-waste management practices and the e-waste legislation landscape in the beneficiary countries, including North Macedonia, to produce the Regional E-waste Monitor report for the Western Balkans. This will include the elaboration of a country profile, training, and national workshop raising awareness on the topic of e-waste. Measuring e-waste volumes is an important step towards addressing the e-waste challenge. Statistics help to evaluate developments over time, and set and assess targets, and policies. Better e-waste data will help minimize its generation, prevent illegal dumping, promote recycling, and create jobs in the reuse, refurbishment, and recycling sectors. Overall, the project aims to build foundations for making digitization and digitalization processes green and sustainable.

planEntities.name: Improved compliance of national policies, legal and institutional frameworks with international human rights and international protection standards
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1 Rule of Law, Access to Justice and Human rights
planEntities.description:
Technical advice and support to relevant state and non-state actors in aligning policies and legislation with international human rights and protection standards, including the EU acquis, as well as in strengthening their policy making and implementation capacities. Among other areas, focus will be placed on fundamental rights and freedoms, equality and non-discrimination,  gender equality, judicial reform, environmental justice, free legal aid, disability inclusion, and gender-based violence and other bias-motivated and violent crimes committed offline and online. Accountability, effective legal and judicial remedies for protection, support and redress will also be enhanced.  

•	Changes and effective implementation of anti-discrimination legislation •	
•	Review and update of gender equality legislation
•	Review of legal framework on hate speech 
•	Update the standard operating procedures used at the border entrance checkpoints. 
•	Support the change of law on international and temporary protection to guarantee equal treatment of all persons.
•	Advocate for the proposed amended Law on Foreigners to grant permanent residence for the remaining Kosovo refugees in the country to enter parliamentary procedure.
•	Raising awareness among authorities about the effects of immigration detention on children, assess the situation in the country against the international and EU standards and get agreement on an action plan for improving the situation

planEntities.name: Improved legislative framework, procedures, practices and capacities of the justice for children system
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1 Rule of Law, Access to Justice and Human rights
planEntities.description:
(i) Provide technical assistance to revise the legal framework pertaining to children in the justice system to adhere to international standards, with specific focus on the Justice for Children Law. 
(ii) Capacity building for key justice for children sector professionals, including police officers, judges, prosecutors, child protection workers, based on the newly developed training curriculum aimed at addressing cases of children in the justice processes in a multi-disciplinary fashion. (iii) Design and establish restorative justice models, including family group conferencing, victim offender mediation, victim impact panels, to incorporate in relevant social and judicial structures. (iv) Assess alternative solutions to detention, custody and the role of correctional educational facility. (v) Deliver multisectoral training to number of professionals in the justice system to introduce trauma informed concept, focusing on the impact of trauma, that emphasizes physical, psychological, and emotional safety of the child (vi) Support the State Council for Prevention of Juvenile Delinquency by delivery of capacity development activities aimed at incorporating innovative practices and approaches in conducting research and reaching out to beneficiaries and stakeholders at national and local level, and at development of a multi-year national strategy for justice for children (vii) Technical assistance for capacity development of professionals in the child protection system, for implementation of the revised legislation.


2024: (i) Capacity building based on the revised J4C legislative and policy framework. (ii) Technical assistance for development and implementation of specialized preventive and protection services and restorative justice models and alternative measures (iii) Support training institutions for delivery and embedment of the trauma informed approach training across social protection,  justice and education sectors (iv) Capacity development to frontline professionals to collect, integrate and generate child protection data related to children in contact with the law and child victims in their information and other related systems.

2025:  i)Provide technical assistance to law enforcement to establish reporting mechanisms and procedures for children at risk and missing children, as well as capacity building for successfully implementing the justice for children legislative framework; ii)Provide advocacy, policy advise and technical expertise to strengthen the implementation of restorative justice mechanisms and alternative measures for children in contact with the law; iii) Provide advocacy, policy advise and technical expertise to strengthen cross-sectoral collaboration and provision of rehabilitation and support for children with complex emotional needs who have been in contact with the law

Support the Ministry of Education and Science and the local authorities in improving evidence-based sector management by: 
2024: i) Organize consultations and coordination with local and national stakeholders on the school network optimization. ii) Support MoES capacities to generate, disseminate and utilize evidence (including on school feeding, student transport options, addressing the surplus/deficit of primary school staff) in decision-making processes including data needed for school optimization and new funding formula. iii) Support the MoES in gathering necessary data for calculations related to the implementation of the new primary school funding formula, as well as for developing a digital module for calculating the new primary formula; iv) Support the MoES in developing a new secondary school funding formula. v) Support the MoES to prioritize investments in the primary school network needed to support the optimization. 
2021-2023: i) assessing the allocation formulas for transfers from the Government to municipalities that fund primary and secondary education; ii) conducting a thorough analysis of the primary schools network and devise recommendations to improve the allocation of the limited resources to ensure all primary schools enable improved access and good quality teaching in accordance with national standards, laws and educational concepts.

planEntities.name: Completion of an evaluation on UNICEF interventions for inclusion of children with disabilities
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3 Social protection of all persons in need
planEntities.description: This summative evaluation aims to examine the extent to which programmes supported by UNICEF North Macedonia, including interventions designed and implemented as part of the COVID-19 response, have contributed to addressing critical system-level bottlenecks to ensure that children with disabilities have access to services, live in caring family environments, and are able to enjoy all their rights. The evaluation will be an important learning opportunity, both for UNICEF and its partners, especially the government. In particular, the evaluation would guide further programming related to inclusive education, inclusive and child-sensitive social protection, child poverty measurement and analysis and more equitable public finance for children.

planEntities.description:
The project aims to provide a model for a centrally coordinated infrastructure management approach, improve the Government ability to manage multiple projects ensuring value for money and the successful, timely and cost-effective delivery of large-scale public infrastructure projects. 

This will be achieved through providing a framework for establishing a unit/institution at the central government level - the Infrastructure Coordination Unit (ICU) and capacitating this unit for facilitating public infrastructure planning, management, delivery and oversight. The project will also entail a capacity building programme and launch/implement it with the ICU personnel or the nominated staff from respective institutions and other relevant stakeholders, triggering a coordination mechanism that will be further driven by the ICU. The project will also aim to upgrade the technical institutional capacities for infrastructure management through the provision of equipment and software solutions

planEntities.name: Support to strengthened health emergency preparedness and disaster risk management in the health sector;
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.4 Effective disaster risk reduction and response
planEntities.description:
In 2021, provided support to the COVID - 19 response through:
-	increasing national capacity for monitoring and risk assessment and management, early detection of public health threats events and vaccination
-	strengthening public health training, surveillance, and implementation of IHR core functions at national level; 
-	upgrading and reinforcing laboratory biosafety and biosecurity, 
-	strengthening capacities of IPH and the Public Health Centers to complete digitalization of the early warning system, investigations, and response and testing in case of communicable disease outbreaks;
-	reinforcing National Public Health response capacity related to COVID-19 and other respiratory public health threats, such as influenza or measles, by increasing the number of trained health professionals and expanding national testing capacity; 
-	introducing digitalized robust information and response performance management systems for assessing vulnerability and risk  

In 2022, the support will include:
1. Development of strategies and mechanisms for prevention of pandemic-/epidemic-prone diseases and their implementation:  
-Revision of the SPRP (pandemic preparedness plan)
-Development of a Joint Action Plan for improvement of intersectoral cooperation between the human and animal health sectors under the One Health approach.
2. Support health emergency capacities of the country by strengthening rapid detection and response
-Real time Early Warning system expanded (Alert 2) and functional (Complete Real Time Digital Information system in all Public Health Centers)
-Training of Emergency Operations Centers staff and Network to effectively use the digitalized early warning system
3. Support health emergency preparedness through strengthening capacities of the Public Health Emergency Operating Center and Network:
-Develop National Operation Plan for Public Health Emergency Operating Center and Network
-Develop and network performance framework and indicators, SOPs, guidance, and tool                                                                 
-Operationalizing the existing PHEOC and Networking with Regional CPH, through upgrading (HR, IT, and other digital system infrastructure and capacity building). 
-Develop Functional Networking of all Public Health Centers under PHEOC coordination.

The regional project will focus on strengthening technical capacities of and enabling environment in targeted countries (Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan) and is expected to produce: i) improved awareness of key national stakeholders and general public on the risks related to AMR for humans, food, animals, plants and the environment is improved and the food and agriculture sector is actively involved in the development of multi-sectoral National Action Plans (NAPs) on AMR; ii) improved ability of target countries to assess and analyze the existing AMR and AMU knowledge, and strengthened capacities and regulatory frameworks related to AMU in food, agriculture, fisheries and livestock; iii) integrated surveillance systems on AMR  supported by assessment and strengthened capacity of national laboratories and related infrastructure to collect and share data on detection of AMR and antimicrobial residue.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
GCP /SEC/011/GFF “Lifecycle Management of Pesticides and Disposal of POPs Pesticides in CA countries and Turkey” project is a regional project in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkiye. The project objective is to reduce Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) releases from obsolete pesticide stockpiles and contaminated sites and strengthen the capacity for the sound management of pesticides. Specific objectives of each component are to: safely destroy up to 900 tonnes of POPs and obsolete pesticides and remediate a pesticide-contaminated site (Component 1); strengthen the institutional and regulatory framework for managing pesticides through their life cycle (Component 2); and increase the successful uptake of alternatives to chemical pesticides on key crops (Component 3). These three components are supported by a horizontal project management, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) and communication component (Component 4) which will inform project execution decisions and create the necessary conditions for beneficiary knowledge and participation in project activities.
The project dates: 15-Oct-2018 - 31-Dec-2024 
The project document was signed by the Government of Kazakhstan in August 2021.

planEntities.name: Forest Restoration Improvement for Environmental Development and Sustainability (FRIENDS)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.3: Strengthened technical and institutional capacity of the Government to develop and implement policies and practices on sustainable urban and rural development
planEntities.description:
Forest Restoration Improvement for Environmental Development and Sustainability (FRIENDS) GCP /SEC/021/TUR project is a regional project for Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. The objectives of this project is to develop national capacities to successfully conduct large-scale forest and other wooded lands restoration, by enhancing know-how to prevent degradation. To achieve this objective, and considering the available financial resources, the project will have a pilot character to test and demonstrate the best and state-of-the-art methodologies. The project strategy will be based on four components: 1) Addressing drivers of degradation and identification of pilot areas; 2) Capacity development; 3) Piloting of restoration activities; and 4) Knowledge management and sharing. These four components will be based on cross-cutting principles relevant to climate change and gender equality. 
The duration of the project: 01-Apr-2022 - 31-Mar-2025

planEntities.description:
Integrated natural resources management in drought-prone and salt-affected agricultural production landscapes in Central Asia and Turkey (`CACILM2` (GCP /SEC/293/GFF) project is a regional project in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkiye, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The project completed a lLongitudinal/ panel study on migration and climate change in Ecuador, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to strengthen the evidence base on human mobility in contexts of disasters, environmental degradation, and climate change from the perspective of in mountainous areas from the perspective of in Kazakhstan, with special attention to high mountains. The project built an evidence base for the development of future MECC policy and programming in Kazakhstan based on the current policy and national legislation on the MECC nexus and drafted an inventory of relevant laws, policies, and strategies in Kazakhstan to ensure the cross-cutting nature of both migration and climate change are integrated in the analysis was discussed with national partners, and final recommendations developed.
2024:The longitudinal study on human mobility in the context of climate change in the mountainous areas of the Almaty oblast in Kazakhstan demonstrated the complex and multifaceted impacts of environmental and climate hazards on households in the mountain areas. As per the research results, rising temperatures, earthquakes, blizzards, strong winds, and abnormal heat and cold conditions put pressure on the local population, affecting physical safety, water security, and mental well-being. Despite the difficult environmental conditions in the study area this year, residents prefer to stay in their communities.

During the third and fourth quarters of 2023, the Extended Gender Theme Group (EGTG) conducted two significant meetings, bringing together key stakeholders to address gender-related issues and promote inclusivity. The co-chairs of the EGTG included the Deputy Head of the National Commission for Women, Family, and Demographic Policy under the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Deputy Head of Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Central Asia, and the United Nations Resident Coordinator for Kazakhstan, who later delegated the role to the UN Women Representative. The active participation of the Government of Kazakhstan, along with representatives from various Ministries, Diplomatic Missions, and international organizations, marked a collaborative and inclusive approach to the group's mission.

The EGTG meetings witnessed the active engagement of the Government of Kazakhstan, with representatives from the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Constitution Court, Ombudsperson for Human Rights, and other relevant entities. Furthermore, over 20 Diplomatic Missions in Kazakhstan, including Embassies of Austria, Belgium, Canada, Egypt, Finland, France, Germany, Jordan, Latvia, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Slovak Republic, UK, and US actively participated. International organizations and IFIs were well-represented by ADB, EBRD, EU Delegation, OSCE, USAID, and various UN entities.

The meeting on 20 September primarily focused on planning for the 2023 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence (GBV) campaign.
The meeting on 13 December centered on two key aspects: Reflections on the Impact of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence 2023 and Embassy Experiences, specifically focusing on engaging youth across Kazakhstan on GBV.
An internal GTG meeting was held on 5 October in a hybrid format, discussing various pertinent themes:

UNDP presented their STEM Initiative.
Joint initiatives in the framework of the "16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence" Campaign 2023 were discussed.
UNCT SWAP Gender Score Card Assessment update was presented.
The development of the GTG Newsletter for Q4-2023-Q1-2024 was discussed.
The Extended Gender Theme Group meetings served as valuable platforms for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and strategic planning. The commitment of the group to promoting gender equality, addressing intersectional issues, and fostering inclusive societies was evident in the depth of discussions and the diversity of perspectives represented. The participation of Diplomatic Missions, international organizations, and IFIs underscored the importance of a multi-stakeholder approach in achieving gender-related goals.

These tools will enhance care and support for SGBV survivors and improve sectoral practices. The M&E Tool has been designed to assess current practice against recommended aspects of service provision in the regional model of SOPs, to ensure comprehensive care and support, and more positive experiences for SGBV survivors who access essential services provided by health, psycho-social and police sectors. planEntities.description:
GAM Report.  The UNAIDS office provided crucial technical assistance to Kazakhstan, supporting the timely submission of 80 key indicators for the Global AIDS Monitoring Reports. They enhanced the capabilities of 50 epidemiologists and 20 lab specialists across 20 AIDS Centers, improving their capacity to track progress toward the 95-95-95 targets. This effort aligns with Kazakhstan's commitment to the UN Political Declaration to end AIDS by 2030, showcasing tangible progress and contributing to the global fight against HIV/AIDS. 
Establishing HIV-1 Recent Infection Surveillance among Persons Newly Diagnosed with HIV Infection in Kazakhstan. The UNAIDS office played a pivotal role in aiding the Kazakh Scientific Center for Dermatology and Infection Diseases, under the Ministry of Health of Kazakhstan in enhancing the capabilities of staff across 20 AIDS regional centers in Kazakhstan. The focus was on implementing HIV Recency testing, an innovative methodology crucial for identifying recent HIV infections and tracing potential routes of transmission. Recent infections are more prevalent among urban residents (21%), with sex workers (25%) and men who have sex with men (22%) showing the highest proportions among key populations. A training workshop equipped 40 specialists from 20 regional and city HIV prevention centers to utilize the Spectrum program for subnational data preparation. Preliminary evaluation data from 20 centers were processed in Spectrum programme. Insights from these efforts are instrumental in translating data into impactful HIV prevention actions. Three Technical Working Group meetings conducted involving the AIDS service NGOs, community of People Living with HIV, and national/international organizations, focusing on the 2023-2026 HIV Roadmap. Also, staff members from the Kazakhstan Scientific Centre of Dermatology and Infectious Diseases contributed to the Regional HIV Assessment Workshop in Chisinau, Moldova, held from February 27 to March 3.

planEntities.description:
UNAIDS and WHO joined forces in a collaborative effort to develop an Action Plan aimed at fulfilling the objectives set forth by the WHO Euro Regional Commission on the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (eMTCT). This comprehensive initiative involved conducting 17 expert interviews and engaging the expertise of 45 specialists from six different regions. Furthermore, the collaboration extended its reach by actively involving HIV service organizations.

The discussions held as part of this initiative covered crucial aspects such as human rights, HIV-related stigma, and discrimination. In a concerted effort, the organizations compiled a wealth of information, encompassing over 80 documents in English. These documents, inclusive of updated indicators, provided a comprehensive overview of the activities related to eMTCT at both national and regional levels.

Subsequent to the WHO Euro Regional Commission Verification mission on eMTCT, numerous recommendations were generated for the Ministry of Health and the Kazakh Scientific Centre for Dermatology and Infectious Diseases. However, acknowledging the extensive time required for the implementation of these recommendations, the decision has been made to temporarily close this activity. It remains subject to potential reopening at a later date, subject upon changes in the country's landscape concerning the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV

planEntities.name: Coordination of the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate all forms of HIV-related stigma and discrimination
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2: Increased capacity of policy makers and health service providers to improve access to selected quality health services and goods, including those related to COVID-19, HIV, reproductive and mental health related services, for everyone especially the most vulnerable groups of population.
planEntities.description:
In advancing the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate HIV-Related Stigma and Discrimination in Kazakhstan, the UNAIDS Country Office demonstrated significant progress through the appointment of a national consultant to drive key initiatives. This consultant played a pivotal role in cultivating collaboration among diverse stakeholders, including the Kazakh Scientific Centre for Dermatology and Infection Diseases under the Ministry of Health, the People Living with HIV community, civil society partners, and national/international organizations. After supporting the process of drafting, UNAIDS facilitated multi-stakeholder meetings to track the implementation of the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. The consultant's contributions were instrumental in bolstering AIDS service non-governmental organizations, particularly in areas such as advocacy for decriminalization of      HIV transmission/exposure and implementation of      the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. Notably, in partnership with the Kazakhstan Union of People Living with HIV, the consultant facilitated      two pivotal meetings in Almaty and Astana, convening over 40 participants from AIDS Service NGOs, governmental structures, and national/international organizations. These meetings aimed to establish a unified position among civil society organizations regarding the decriminalization of HIV transmission at the country level, as well as gather support to advocacy from select state authorities, along with a number of preparatory meetings. Furthermore, the consultant played a crucial role in supporting AIDS Service NGOs in contributing to a UN confidential report for Kazakhstan's 2023 review by the Committee against Torture, demonstrating proactive involvement and a commitment to transparency and international cooperation.

Despite these steps, transgender individuals in Kazakhstan continue to face legal barriers, stigma, and discrimination, negatively impacting efforts to end the HIV epidemic. Notable legal obstacles include the prohibition of gender-affirming treatment until the age of 21, sterilization requirements for legal gender recognition, and others. Recognizing the urgency of addressing these challenges, the UNAIDS office played a central role in co-organizing a significant meeting focused on overcoming barriers to accessing HIV services for transgender people. This collaborative effort, in partnership with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria and AlmaTQ, a transgender civil society initiative, drew more than 40 participants, including representatives from NGOs, AIDS Centers, and national/international organizations. Discussions centered on addressing challenges related to HIV-associated stigma and human rights, raising awareness, and fostering collaboration among diverse stakeholders. Additionally, the UNAIDS office provided crucial support in enhancing the capacity of the transgender community to pursue strategic lawsuits with the newly established Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan, aimed at reviewing legal provisions discriminating against transgender people. As a direct outcome of these efforts, legislation concerning legal barriers for transgender people underwent comprehensive analysis, two cases were referred to the Constitutional Court, and notably, a comprehensive Transgender Community Advocacy Strategy for 2023-2026 was successfully developed. These accomplishments underscore the UNAIDS Country Office's unwavering commitment to creating a more inclusive and supportive environment for people affected by HIV-related stigma and discrimination in Kazakhstan.

The 'Let Communities Lead' regional leadership campaign commenced with a dynamic three-day communications training for 10 community leaders across six countries. Focused on honing public speaking and media interaction skills, participants crafted engaging content for the campaign's social media drive in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Over 10 days, leaders were showcased on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram, amassing a remarkable total reach exceeding 300,000 views. This success underscores the campaign's efficacy in galvanizing and motivating communities through strategic communication. UNAIDS Kazakhstan, a key contributor to the regional initiative, enriched the UNAIDS Global World AIDS Day campaign with a compelling video showcasing how community groups connect at-risk clients to PrEP in Kazakhstan.

planEntities.description:
The UNAIDS office played a pivotal role in March 2023 by providing crucial technical support to the Kazakh National Center for Dermatology and Infection Diseases. This support was instrumental in the development of the approved HIV Road Map 2023-2026, which currently functions as a guiding document, effectively coordinating national efforts in HIV prevention and treatment.

As Kazakhstan endeavors to achieve the ambitious goal of eliminating AIDS as a public health threat by 2030, it becomes imperative to proactively plan for the continuation of HIV response achievements beyond the year 2025. To sustain these efforts and ensure adequate financial resources, Kazakhstan should prioritize the creation of Sustainability Roadmaps for the HIV Response within the next two years. This strategic planning will be crucial in maintaining momentum and ensuring a robust, enduring response to the HIV epidemic.

Teamed up with UNDP/CCM Secretariat to organize a webinar series, providing valuable insights on applying for Global Fund Fighting AIDS, TB, and Malaria funding for 2023-2025. Engaged approximately 100 participants from AIDS service NGOs and the People Living with HIV community. Also, UNAIDS together with partners assisted the Kazakh Scientific Center for Dermatology and Infection Disease in formulating a funding proposal for the Global Fund Fighting AIDS, TB, and Malaria (GFATM). Successfully secured $7,422,991US for 2023-2025 to combat HIV and AIDS at country level.

planEntities.name: Mentoring Programme for Women Living with HIV in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2:Increased capacities of state institutions and other relevant organizations to expand access to justice and combat discrimination with a focus on women and marginalized groups
planEntities.description: The ""Mentoring Programme for Women Living with HIV in Kazakhstan"" is an extension of the successful similia project, supported by UNAIDS Kazakhstan. Aimed at addressing the challenges faced by women with HIV, such as discrimination and lack of integration, the program focuses on reducing self-stigmatization, developing socio-economic skills, and facilitating social reintegration. In 2023, the program benefited 206 women across 10 regions, with 204 participating in self-help groups and 16 receiving training on HIV therapy adherence and mother-to-child transmission prevention. A Leadership School, a collaborative effort between UNAIDS and UN Women, empowered 26 women from 10 regions to take on leadership roles. Utilizing social media, the project shared 27 posts to keep the community informed and raise awareness about HIV-related challenges in Kazakhstan.

planEntities.name: Campaign to mobilize adolescent/teenagers, including teenagers living with HIV in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.3:  Increased participation of women and representatives of marginalized and vulnerable groups in decision-making in the public, quasi-public and private sector
planEntities.description: The UN's interventions prioritize the active involvement of marginalized groups, such as adolescents living with HIV. In Kazakhstan, UNAIDS empowers these adolescents through the Teenergizer movement, positioning them as leaders in the fight against HIV and advocates for youth rights. The project, implemented in hybrid format, includes face-to-face meetings in Almaty and online sessions in other regions. Weekly face-to-face meetings in Almaty enhance public speaking skills for 590 participants, while online sessions support 120 adolescents with HIV in improving public speaking and emotional intelligence. Additionally, 64 non-HIV interns engage in Teenergizer activities through internship courses. Teenergizer's impactful initiatives include video clips addressing HIV prevention and mental well-being, podcasts promoting tolerance, and advocacy efforts highlighting discriminatory legislation affecting PLHIV rights. Training sessions on HIV prevention, sexual health, substance use, and violence prevention reached 2392 participants through 59 sessions, with 34 trainings in Almaty and 25 in five regions of Kazakhstan. All media content and activities are accessible on the Teenergizer Instagram page and website.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description:
Project countries: Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Pakistan, Türkiye.
Project Manager: Gul Unal, Senior Economist, Division on Globalization and Development Strategies, UNCTAD (gul.unal@un.org)
Objective: To strengthen regional partnership and national capacities of developing integrated policy strategies in selected countries to achieve the resilient, green and transformative development for 2030 Agenda.

The project comprises three phases:
Phase I: Research collaboration with experts from the project countries to understand their constraints in achieving resilient, green, and transformative development. Research will also focus on China's policies since 2015 for economic resilience and high-quality development (HQD).
Phase II: Development of tailored integrated green development strategies with national partners, addressing capacity gaps through peer-learning with China (South-South Cooperation).
Phase III: Establishment of the Asian Green Development Partnership Network (AGDPN) based on the outputs of Phases I and II, facilitating regional policy coordination and economic cooperation.

planEntities.description: UNDP developed an innovative Digital Family Card digital platform capable of collecting, integrating, and processing information on the most vulnerable groups in Kazakhstan to provide state social support to key groups. The platform creates a holistic, gender-sensitive and efficient system to provide social support for the most vulnerable groups in society in Kazakhstan, prevent families from falling into poverty and empower local decision makers by providing them with real-time data on population categories in urgent need of support. The new Digital Family Card platform enables local and state agencies to proactively deliver social assistance to those most in need by consolidating real-time data from state databases and ensure transparent access to information about the socioeconomic status of families in Kazakhstan.
