UNDP Kazakhstan has been designated as the CCM Funding Recipient to receive and manage the funding on behalf of the CCM.

planEntities.name: Partnership for action on green economy (PAGE)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacities of national policy makers to develop and implement policies on economic diversification and transition to inclusive, resilient and sustainable economy
planEntities.description: The Programme brings together the expertise and credentials of five UN agencies (UNEP, ILO, UNITAR, UNIDO, UNDP) to support partner countries in implementing and accelerating initiatives and reforms in the inclusive green economy through policy assessment, strategic documents, technical expertise and analytical services. The aim of the Programme on national level is to facilitate reinforcement and integration of inclusive green economy (IGE) goals and targets into SDG-aligned national economic and development planning through multi-stakeholder collaboration in Kazakhstan. On sectoral level the Programme enables evidence-based sectoral and thematic reforms in line with national IGE priorities. PAGE focuses also on strengthening individual, institutional and planning capacities for IGE action at the national level and improvement of knowledge base for advancing IGE in the country.

planEntities.name: Supporting the Economic Empowerment of Afghan Women through Education and Training in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.3: Increased capacities of MMSEs and enterpenuers to create a conducive environment, to better integrate into the value chains, develop innovative approaches for enterpeneurial activities, and create decent job opportunities
planEntities.description:
The project is expected to help create new business and employment opportunities for Afghan women and their communities back in Afghanistan. According to the 2018 UNDP Human Development Report, 11 percent of all adult Afghan women have reached at least a secondary level of education and only 19.5 percent are employed, while these numbers are 37 percent and 87 percent for men, respectively. In 2016-2017, more than half of the Afghan population was living below the poverty line.
Between 2019 and 2025, 50 students will attend bachelor’s, master’s, and technical degrees in Agriculture, Statistics/Finance and Mining at academic establishments across Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
The overall objective of the project is to strengthen human capacity development in Afghanistan by increasing women’s access to quality higher education through expanding cooperation with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
The project was launched in June 2019

planEntities.name: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Key Globally Important Ecosystems for Multiple Benefits (Global Policy Centre on Resilient Ecosystems - 2021)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: The Project is aimed to improve the conservation and management of forest resources and adjacent grassland, floodplain and desert ecosystems, which are valuable for biodiversity conservation, land resources and welfare of local communities. The Project also focuses on promoting the gender equality and women empowerment as relevant and possible within the Project. In this direction, the Project will address the challenges of sustainable use of natural resources by promoting innovative gender-responsible solutions based on improved capacity, new knowledge, new opportunities, increased participation of women in the development and implementation of effective methods and approaches of sustainable forest and rangeland management, etc. To achieve the Project goal and reduce certain threats and barriers, the project structure involves 3 Components. Geographically, the target project areas coincide with the key biodiversity areas (KBA) identified in Kazakhstan, including the mountain, tugai and saxaul forests. The listed ecosystems, among which the mountain ecosystems are the main habitat of snow leopard, are forming part of 3 administrative oblasts, where the Project is planned to be implemented: East Kazakhstan oblast  (mountain areas of Altai and Saur-Tarbagatai), Almaty oblast (Zhongar Alatau, Northern and Central Tien Shan, floodplain forests of the Charyn and Ili rivers, and Pribalkhash saxaul forests), and South Kazakhstan oblast (mountain ecosystems of Western Tien Shan and floodplain forests of SyrDarya river)

planEntities.name: Biodiversity finance initiative – BIOFIN, Extended Phase II
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: BIOFIN supports countries with a methodology that provides innovative steps to measure current biodiversity expenditures, assess financial needs, identify the most suitable finance solutions, and provides guidance on how to implement these solutions to achieve their national biodiversity target. The 2nd phase of BIOFIN in Kazakhstan will be built on the lessons learned from the 1st phase and will aim to test six finance solutions: (1) subsidizing game breeding, (2) creating a basis for certification in the field of ecotourism, (3) capacity building of protected areas to improve financing, (4) biodiversity offsets, (5) carbon offsetting through an internal emission trading system (ETS) and (6) attracting foreign investment to implement projects to absorb greenhouse gases by forest ecosystems. The Phase II aims to establish the institutional and legal basis that will allow mobilizing financial resources for biodiversity through new financial solutions. Implementation of new finance solutions will be based on changing existing and preparing new legal standards, testing, studying the experience of other countries, approaches, capacity building of industry experts, providing extensive information on the problems and possibilities of biodiversity financing. The project also aims to highlight the key role of women in the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, as well as the need for the full involvement of women at all levels of decision-making by mainstreaming gender issues into new financial decisions.

planEntities.name: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) Phase II Implementation of Component I in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description:
UNDP KZ and the Global Policy Centre on Resilient Ecosystems and Desertification (GC-RED) in Nairobi are collaborating to implement the Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) in KZ. The project aims to formalize partnerships between scientists, policymakers, and practitioners to enhance synergy for sustainable conservation and management of biodiversity and ecosystem services (BES) in Kazakhstan. Recognizing the disproportionate vulnerability of women to climate change and the importance of their empowerment for environmental conservation, the project integrates gender-sensitive actions throughout its design and implementation. The collaboration focuses on four main components:

1. Creating a shared vision and collaboration model among science, policy, and practice communities for sustainable BES conservation and management.
2. Improving access to policy-relevant BES evidence and utilization of new knowledge through national ecosystem assessments.
3. Strengthening multi-sectoral stakeholder dialogue and networks at the regional level to analyze IPBES products and translate relevant messages into concrete decisions and actions.
4. Enhancing BES knowledge sharing through increased generation, dissemination, and communication of resources among science, policy, and practice communities.

planEntities.name: Assisting the Republic of Kazakhstan in meeting international commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by reducing the carbon footprint of electricity suppliers for leading technology company Bitfury
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: The purpose of the project is aimed at the implementation of complex measures in Kazakhstan to absorb CO2 emissions by forest ecosystems. The main objectives of the project will be achieved through activities to (1) reduce the carbon footprint produced by Bitfury's electricity suppliers in the Republic of Kazakhstan by 110% with a total consumption of 82 MW (2) support Kazakhstan's national initiative to create offset mechanisms to neutralize greenhouse gas emissions of gases as part of the commitments under the Paris Agreement (3) contribute to the achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goal of restoring 350 million hectares of forests worldwide by 2030 as part of the fight against climate change (4) assessment of the impact to project results on the health of men and women in the project areas.

planEntities.name: Irrigation and drainage in Kazakhstan, capacity building
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: This project seeks to develop the Kazvodkhoz Republican State Enterprise's capacity as a state-leading entity and its branch offices in Almaty and Turkestan regions through institutional change management and improved irrigation and drainage systems management governance, which would serve as an example throughout Kazakhstan. The project focuses on (i) Strengthening the institutional and human resources capacity of the central Kazvodkhoz office in Nur-Sultan and its branches in Almaty and Turkestan regions, as related to water delivery practices and better farmers' information services on-farm water management (water council & extension); (ii) Development of economic and financial instruments on irrigation and drainage water management; (iii) Development of a metered billing system for irrigation water management.

planEntities.name: Derisking renewable energy investment
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The objective of the project is to encourage private sector investment in renewable energy in Kazakhstan to achieve the objectives of the “Kazakhstan 2030” and “Kazakhstan 2050” strategies for renewable energy.
The project targets both large-scale and small-scale renewable energy sources. The ultimate goal of this project is to achieve the transformation of the energy market in Kazakhstan through a significant increase in the scale of the use of renewable energy sources in the field of electricity generation, from 0.77% to 10% - the share of RES by 2030, which is a 10-fold increase in electricity generation based on RES with the assistance of the project.
In terms of large-scale renewable energy sources, the project will help promote Kazakhstan as a prime target for foreign investment. Technologies will include wind power and photovoltaic solar power (PV).
For small-scale renewable energy sources, the project will stimulate investment in "Renewable energy sources for Urban Life", small-scale renewable energy sources for grid systems, intended for urban population and enterprises; and in RES for Rural Life, small-scale renewable energy sources for both grid and off-grid systems for farms and rural SMEs. Technologies may include solar PV (on rooftops), solar water heating and small-scale wind energy.

planEntities.name: Scale up the Energy Efficiency/Energy Saving and Retrofits in the Secondary School of the Turkestan Region of Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The cooperation project in question (hereinafter referred to as the “Project”) builds on the groundwork of the UNDP-GEF Energy-Efficient/Energy Saving projects and RES and on the premises of the Cooperation Agreement between UNDP and ACS; this new Project between ACS and UNDP, implemented with the consent and support of the Akimat of Turkestan region will focus on several areas that have shown signs of success, namely energy-efficient lighting and energy-efficient heating appliances and RES. The Project would raise awareness and capacities of relevant municipal stakeholders and city residents about green lighting, create more conducive local and national policy and regulatory frameworks and demonstrate practice institutional development models for design and demonstration of flagship municipal green lighting project in the Turkestan region of Kazakhstan. To realize this objective, the proposed Project will carry out several activities that will deliver specific outputs, such as replacing conventional lightning appliances with energy-efficient appliances in the highest energy-consuming public institutions, e.g., Secondary School in Turkestan oblast.

planEntities.name: Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions for Low-Carbon Urban Development
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project supports the development and implementation of climate change mitigation actions (NAMA) in Kazakhstan's urban sector. Through infrastructure investments, capacity-building, and technical assistance, it aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while enhancing urban services and citizens' quality of life. Aligned with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, the project focuses on accelerating the transition to renewable energy and green recovery. It includes components to enhance municipal planning, strengthen institutional structures, facilitate financing, and pilot urban NAMA in Nur-Sultan. The project will also harmonize with national emission reduction efforts, including monitoring and verification systems, aiming for direct emission reductions of 370,000 tons of CO2-eq. and indirect reductions from 1 to 5 million tons of CO2-eq.

planEntities.name: Creating conditions for the attraction of investors in energy efficiency in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The Project aims to advance energy efficiency of buildings, infrastructure, and other facilities in Kazakhstan by attracting investment from private investors, banks and international financial institutions via the design, piloting, and development of a partial credit guarantee scheme supporting bank loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that have limited access to credit due to their lack of suitable collateral.
By facilitating investment into this sector, the Project will stimulate economic growth and sustainability among SMEs, thus creating and preserving jobs and accelerating economic recovery from the COVID-19 crisis.  The Project will also help to fulfil Kazakhstan’s national strategic goals for decreasing energy intensity of the GDP.
Toward these goals, the Project will create and pilot the loan guarantee scheme, conduct supporting activity in training and monitoring, and scale up the loan guarantee fund on the basis of initial results.  Eligible businesses will include providers of energy-saving services and equipment; energy end-users seeking to upgrade efficiency of facilities and energy systems; and intermediaries (micro-finance organizations, leasing companies, factoring companies) that finance eligible businesses or projects mentioned above.

planEntities.name: Assistance in Enhancement of Kazakhstan’s Nationally Determined Contributions
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project aims to introduce a modern monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) system and include adaptation measures into the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) of the Republic of Kazakhstan. It is planned to develop a roadmap for implementation of obligations, which will indicate the main directions of national activities for adaptation and reduction of greenhouse gases, and which will provide technical guidance for the Government of Kazakhstan to achieve greenhouse gas emission reduction targets and adaptation measures.

planEntities.name: Development of Kazakhstan's Eighth National Communication and Preparation of Two (Fourth and Fifth) Biennial Reports to the UNFCCC
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project is aimed to enable Kazakhstan to prepare and submit the Eighth National Communication (8NC) and two Biennial Reports (BR4 and BR5) to the Conference of the Parties (COP) of the UNFCCC in accordance with the obligations of the Party to the Convention under Article 12 of the Convention and subsequent decisions of the COP. The project also plannes to update information on national circumstances, greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories and measures taken to mitigate climate change, assessment of vulnerability to climate change and ongoing adaptation efforts, public awareness, education and training, systematic observation and research, attraction and provision of financial resources and technology transfer. Additionally, the project is to enhance technical and institutional capacity in GHG inventory, GHG emission forecasting, vulnerability assessment and, in general, NC/BR preparation, and assist the Government in integrating climate change issues into sectoral and national development priorities.

planEntities.name: Creation of conditions for the reintroduction of the Turan tiger and assistance in the preservation of natural, historical and cultural objects of the Ulytau mountain range
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.3: Strengthened technical and institutional capacity of the Government to develop and implement policies and practices on sustainable urban and rural development
planEntities.description:
The Project is aimed at creating a sustainable base for reintroduction of tigers in historical habitats, spanning the Ile-Balkhash SNR, conservating the natural, historical and cultural heritage of Ulytau mountain range and adjacent territories, and promoting the tourist sites in this unique region. The Project's main results will be a comprehensive improvement of ecosystems along the Ile river delta and the Southern Balkhash region, strengthening Ile-Balkhash SNR and Ulytau SNNP (which is being created), developing a PAs network and tourism in Ulytau region, raising the level of environmental awareness by population and informing all stakeholders, creating a basis for joint ecosystems management with the project sites with benefits for biodiversity conservation and local communities. The
project will contribute to the enhancement of women’s role in the restoration and conservation activities, extensively applying gendered approach during implementation phase through capacity building, meaningful participation of women in decision-making and monitoring as well as inclusion of their needs and interest in project design.balkhash saxaul forests), and South Kazakhstan oblast (mountain ecosystems of Western Tien Shan and floodplain forests of SyrDarya river).

planEntities.name: Support of the Government with SDG Financing Strategy
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.1: Enhanced capacities of state actors in participatory, inclusive and gender sensitive budgeting and planning to implement the 2030 Agenda.
planEntities.description: This Joint Programme (JP) supports the Government of Kazakhstan in aligning policy and financing with SDG towards adopting an integrated national financing framework (INFF). The JP is expected to result in Kazakhstan implementing three critical building blocks towards adopting an INFF: i) developing a holistic SDG financing strategy to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of public spending and mobilize additional SDG financing; ii) align national planning, budgeting and financing with SDGs through the implementation of SDG budgeting, with a specific focus on mainstreaming gender and child dimensions; and iii) strengthening SDG monitoring and accountability mechanisms by involving non-government actors in the budgeting process. This will result in accelerating progress towards the SDGs by increasing SDG financing, including inclusive MSME financing and climate finance, as well as safeguarding fiscal space for social expenditures, paying attention to gender-responsive planning and budgeting and ensuring that vulnerable population groups, especially children and youth, are not left behind.

planEntities.name: Set-up of an SDGs Platform for Central Asia
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.1: Enhanced capacities of state actors in participatory, inclusive and gender sensitive budgeting and planning to implement the 2030 Agenda.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the project is to contribute to sustainable development through a knowledge-sharing platform supporting Central Asian countries to track and adjust key socio-economic policies by monitoring SDG progress and financing as well as improving the effectiveness of regional EU programmes towards this goal. The project aims to: 1. Contribute to SDGs achievement through modelling effectiveness of the socio-economic policies and their contribution to achieve SDGs. 2. Contribute to coordination of effort in assessing national financial gaps using the Integrated National Financing Framework (INFF) methodology and ongoing Development Finance Assessments and stimulating regional exchange of best practices. 3. Establish tools that can support evidence-based policymaking and track SDG progress and contribution (outcome) of the EU regional programmes in SDG achievement, focusing on policies with transboundary impact, including environment, water and biodiversity, trade, and social development. 4. Promote the use of innovative practices that can visualize key SDG progress showing possible trends and hotspots in Central Asia countries and communication.

planEntities.name: Capacity Building for Innovation in Governance and Digitalisation of Public Services
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description: The Project aspires to develop the capacities of civil servants to innovate in governance matters and for providing digitalized public services through differentiated channels of delivery, as well as to promote innovative practices. Its overall aim is to contribute towards improving the quality of life of citizens in the seven participating countries from Central Asia (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan), and from the Caucasus (Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia). To address these objectives, the UNDP/ACSH and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS) and the National Information Agency Society (NIA) of the Republic of Korea have initiated this project to adopt good practices in governance and in public service provision through digital channels. The expected result of this Project is enhanced knowledge of public officials in the participating countries on the concept and practice of innovation in government and on digitalisation processes in public service delivery, as well as enhance capacity of public officials in the participating countries to introduce innovative practices and provide public services through a multitude of digital channels.

planEntities.name: Alliances for Change – Ending Sexual and Gender-Based Violence and Harmful Practice in Central Asia
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description: The regional programme aims to broker the creation of the first Central-Asia-wide alliance to end all forms of sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and harmful practices. This Alliance will bring together state and non-state actors, including members of the legislature, representatives of ministries and other public agencies, justice and police, civil society organisations, public activists, survivors of violence, youth, men, and faith leaders. This Alliance is sought to provide a platform for the promotion of practical approaches, models, tools, and taskforces to increase the effectiveness and inclusiveness of state and non-state strategies to eliminate violence against women and change the culture of tolerance towards SGBV and harmful practices. The programme addresses specific legislative, policy and institutional gaps in prevention, protection, and multi-sectoral response to SGBV, provision of quality services for survivors.

planEntities.name: Support Development Vision Recalibration and Digital Transformation in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.3: Strengthened national systems of data collection and analysis for the formulation of evidence-based national human-rights and gender equality policies and development programmes aligned with international standards and SDGs

planEntities.name: Institutional Support to the Astana Civil Service Hub, Phase 4
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.3: Strengthened national systems of data collection and analysis for the formulation of evidence-based national human-rights and gender equality policies and development programmes aligned with international standards and SDGs
planEntities.description: The project's overall goal is to contribute to effective, transparent, and accountable governance and improved public service delivery in the region and beyond, through civil service excellence and regional cooperation. Since 2013, the ACSH operates as a multilateral and networking platform promoting supporting public service excellence, by assisting the efforts of the participating countries’ governments – particularly those in the immediate region – in building institutional and human capacity to cope with contemporary challenges and issues through three main pillars: (i) partnerships and networking; (ii) capacity building and peer-to-peer learning; and (iii) research and knowledge creation and management. It is worth noting that all ACSH activities are shaped by a flexible demand-driven agenda, which has proved its relevance in regional and international development cooperation over the years. The quality of its work has been highly acclaimed by the United Nations and its sister agencies, as well as by the European Union, and the Organisation for Economic Development and Cooperation and by many participating countries. The vision and mandate of this fourth phase of the project is to continue contributing to the establishment of modern, effective, efficient, and sustainable governance, public administration, and civil service systems in its participating countries and beyond, which meet society’s expectations for responsive, accountable, and transparent public institutions; in congruence with the SDG 16 and 17 objectives.

planEntities.name: Post-Crisis Support to the Government’s Reform Initiatives
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description: The project aims to contribute to the Government of Kazakhstan’s postcrisis measures and reform initiatives in response to January 2022 tragic events that started as peaceful meetings and turned to violent protests in different regions of Kazakhstan. The expected project activities focus on concrete measures aimed to (i) conduct quick portfolio review and identification of entry points (ii) support immediate post-crisis recovery; (iii) support the Government of Kazakhstan in recalibrating its social policy, (iv) propose solutions for integrated local development and (v) enhance governance, rule of law, and institutional reforms.

planEntities.name: UNDP Accelerator Lab
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description: Bring new ways of addressing complex development challenges through testing and scaling up new solutions, backed up by evidence and practice

planEntities.name: Almaty irrigation water supply and sanitation improvement
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: The project addresses the challenges of abandoned agricultural lands and inadequate WASH services in schools in the Almaty region. It aims to restore abandoned lands, enhance irrigation systems, and pilot effective WASH practices in selected schools. The project has three key outcomes: improving irrigation water supply systems, enhancing clean-up and remediation services in light of COVID-19, and strengthening institutional capacity in irrigation water management and municipal WASH services. Target areas include the Koksu, Eskeldi, and Akshi districts.

planEntities.name: Stockholm+50: a healthy planet for the prosperity of all – our responsibility, our opportunity
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.3: Strengthened technical and institutional capacity of the Government to develop and implement policies and practices on sustainable urban and rural development
planEntities.description: The Programme will be used as a vehicle to deliver on a time-bound set of complementary initiatives designed to support national consultations for the Stockholm+50 Conference in line with the terms and conditions of a separate Grant Agreement between the Government of Sweden and UNDP.

planEntities.name: Promoting Responsible Business Conduct in target countries where Japanese companies operate, with a particular focus on promoting human rights due diligence in global supply chains and leveraging the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights for a just recovery: (B+HR)
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description:
The B+HR Global project's outcome is to promote a just recovery while preserving the competitiveness of Japanese companies. The project will strengthen responsible business practices in Japan and the
target countries, including Kazakhstan, through improving the ability and understanding of national authorities, Japanese businesses, suppliers and partners to carry out Human Rights Due Diligence. First, the project targets to support Japanese companies, their suppliers and partners in their efforts to remain competitive and drive a just recovery by ensuring compliance with Human Rights Standards
throughout their value chains. Second, UNDP will assist Kazakhstan Government’s and state authorities in the development of national policy towards Business and Human Rights

planEntities.name: Support to the national human rights mechanisms and the rule of law reforms in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.2: Strengthened capacities of government authorities and CSOs for effective, efficient, timely and inclusive provision of specialized social services with a focus on the most vulnerable groups, including the context of the Covid-19 pandemic
planEntities.description:
The project aims at enhancing the technical capacities and expertise of the key rule of law, security, and human rights institutions in Kazakhstan in response to the immediate needs spawned by the crisis in the country while contributing to announced political reforms of the government. The project has two key objectives:
First, the project targets to strengthen the national human rights mechanism institutionally. With the newly adopted law (December 2021) providing a Human Rights Commissioner (HRC) a more robust mandate and the expected uplift of HRC's status to the constitutional level, there is a need for immediate assistance to the NHRI in developing its capacity and strategic vision in fulfilling its new mandates.
Second, UNDP will work to support transformative changes in the work of law enforcement and, specifically, the police, towards people-centered, human rights-based services.

planEntities.name: Capacity-Building of Foreign Policy and ODA Organizations of Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.3: Strengthened national systems of data collection and analysis for the formulation of evidence-based national human-rights and gender equality policies and development programmes aligned with international standards and SDGs
planEntities.description: The project targets to enhance Kazakhstan’s existing ODA practices by working with FPRI to identify the current challenges, gaps, and corresponding recommendations. Second, the project aims to accelerate the synergy of ODA practices through data integration with two digital tools for KazAID: a National ODA Accounting Dashboard and a Database of Kazakhstan Development Experts, with a specific focus on female professionals. Third, this project improves KazAID’s executive capacity to implement projects by engaging in joint activities and sharing experiences. The activity will focus on raising awareness of youth and strengthening women-led volunteering initiatives in UNDP’s traditional area of engagement – energy and environment. Third component is financially supported by the Romanian Agency for International Development.

planEntities.name: Leveraging Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to achieve net-zero emissions and climate-resilient development, in response to the climate emergency
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.3: Increased capacities of MMSEs and enterpenuers to create a conducive environment, to better integrate into the value chains, develop innovative approaches for enterpeneurial activities, and create decent job opportunities
planEntities.description: The Project aims to introduce new climate smart technologies that can be scaled up on most of the farms, in the field of renewable energy, digitalization for water use, and proper drought control for small- and medium-size agriculture enterprises facing both COVID-19 and climate crises at the same time. In addition, the Project will improve the existing meteorological surveillance system, which will increase the resilience to droughts. Capacity building activities envisages gender perspective by empowering emerging women scholars, practitioners and women-led SMEs in climate smart mechanization sector in partnership with UNDP STEM4All platform.

planEntities.name: UNDP Engagement Facility
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacities of national policy makers to develop and implement policies on economic diversification and transition to inclusive, resilient and sustainable economy
planEntities.description: Providing a rapid and flexible response mechanism to support UNDP upstream policy results and test innovations with scaling-up potential.

planEntities.name: Seventh Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme in Kazakhstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description: The project aims to empower local communities and organizations to enhance socio-ecological resilience and sustainable livelihoods across seven target landscapes, benefitting both local and global environments. It will achieve this by improving community-based capacities for ecosystem resilience through resource management planning and promoting the adoption of energy-efficient and renewable energy technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Focused on steppe and desert landscapes, the project will deliver cost-effective investments, processes, and tools within specific geographic areas. By fostering synergies among community interventions, it aims to maximize impacts and results on the landscape through cumulative efforts. Leveraging additional funds from various sources, including government and private sector initiatives, the project aligns closely with government priorities at both national and regional levels, facilitating collaboration with existing programs.

planEntities.name: Phase 2: Supporting the Economic Empowerment of Afghan Women through Education and Training in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.3: Increased capacities of MMSEs and enterpenuers to create a conducive environment, to better integrate into the value chains, develop innovative approaches for enterpeneurial activities, and create decent job opportunities
planEntities.description:
The Action represents an expansion of an ongoing EUR 2 million trilateral cooperation programme between the European Union, Afghanistan, and Central Asia. Like the ongoing programme, it aims at building resilience and promoting the academic, economic and social empowerment of women in Afghanistan especially vulnerable women living in challenging conditions by enhancing their capabilities, employability and future prospects through education and training in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and, within the context of this Action, Kyrgyzstan.
Phase 2 of the programme focuses on training of specialists in Agriculture/Agribusiness, Engineering/Construction, Marketing and ICT. Apart from promoting academic, economic and social empowerment of women in Afghanistan, the action will help to strengthen capacity of receiving institutions in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan to manage learning mobility programmes in interaction with UNDP and address gender inequalities in higher education and TVET.
The action is intended as a logical continuation of the ongoing project and aims to further facilitate the development of a sustainable system of academic exchange that will allow women from Afghanistan to benefit from higher education opportunities in Central Asia also beyond the project lifetime.

planEntities.name: Enhancing Effectiveness of Social Protection Programmes and Improving Access and Participation of Socially Vulnarable Groups (ph 3)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.2: Increased capacity of policy makers and health service providers to improve access to selected quality health services and goods, including those related to COVID-19, HIV, reproductive and mental health related services, for everyone especially the most vulnerable groups of population.

Kazakhstan.name: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

planEntities.name: Provide technical and expert support to the government for the development and adoption of national DRR Strategy and DRR strategy for Nur-Sultan
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
2021 narrative: In 2021, UNDRR conducted an analysis of national legislation and stakeholders in the disaster risk reduction system in Kazakhstan. UNDRR incorporated the key findings of the analysis into the recommendations for the DRR component of the National Concept of the Development of Civil Protection System of Kazakhstan that the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MES) is developing on behalf of the government.  UNDRR also shared with MES the recommendations for the outline of the National Concept.

UNDRR facilitated establishing a technical working group (TWG) at Akimat of Nur-Sultan (Center of Urbanism as a focal point) consisting of representatives of departments of Akimat and relevant line ministries, for conducting self-assessment of disaster resilience of the capital. On September 28, 2021, UNDRR and the TWG completed the preliminary assessment, and on November 30, 2021, UNDRR jointly with WHO and TWG assessed the public health sector’s resilience to disasters and shared the lessons learned during the COVID-19 pandemic.

planEntities.name: Provide technical and expert support for the establishment National Disaster Loss Database and its integration.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
2021 narrative: UNDRR supported establishing the national system of disaster loss accounting. UNDRR facilitated establishing a TWG consisting of 50+ representatives of the central and regional departments of the Ministry of Emergency Situations and Oblast Akimats. In a series of workshops and consultative meetings, a customized data card aligned to national legislation and compatible with the global DesInventar-Sendai system was developed. UNDRR provided training for the TWG on the use of the DesInventar-Sendai international reporting system and shared the required software.
On July, 2022, specialists of Analytical units of all regional Departments of ES got refresher training on DesInventar-Sendai system. To transfer all  historical data into the Disaster Loss Database a National Consultant was hired. UNDRR provided a server and a laptop to the Ministry of ES to integrate DesInventar-Sendai into the National Disaster Loss Accounting system.

planEntities.name: Provide technical and expert support for increasing commitments of local authorities to build local-level resilience
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
2021 narrative: UNDRR is implementing community-based disaster risk activities with total coverage of 10,000 populations of 10 vulnerable communities in the East Kazakhstan region. In each of the target communities, emergency committees were formed and trained. One school and the local Akimat received the set of equipment - the emergency preparedness kit that included motorized pumps and electrical generators, flashlights, blankets, and many more. On September 20-23, 2021, UNDRR conducted a monitoring visit to 5 out 10 target communities. During the visit, UNDRR, IFRC, and RCS discussed with the local community representatives and mayors the local resilience strengthening activities and the small-scale mitigation projects aimed at reduction of vulnerability to seasonal floods and other hazards.

In 2022, UNDRR with the implementing partners Red Crescent of Kazakhstan and IFRC completed 4 small-scale mitigation projects in 3 communities of Altay and Glubokovskii rayons. Each of 10 target communities received a set of equipment for non-structural mitigation.

planEntities.name: CAMCA (Central Asian Mammals and Climate Adaptation) project
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Solutions developed and resources mobilized for more sustainable use of ecosystems and natural resources for the improvement of the well-being of local communities and nature
planEntities.description:
The CAMCA (Central Asian Mammals and Climate Adaptation) project collaborates with Kazakhstan’s government, NGOs like ACBK, and local communities to strengthen the climate resilience of mountain wildlife and ecosystems. In Kazakhstan’s high-altitude ranges such as the Jongar-Alatau. The project assesses vulnerability of key species like snow leopards, argali, Tian Shan maral, and brown bears, and develops participatory, ecosystem-based adaptation tools for wildlife and pasture management. CAMCA also supports community capacity-building, awareness campaigns, and pilot initiatives to reduce human wildlife conflict and enhance livelihood options, with a view to safeguarding biodiversity under climate stress.

Project duration: 2021 - 2026.

planEntities.description: 2021: A media campaign is being prepared to empower people living with HIV (adults and young people/adolescents) to adhere to HIV treatment and reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination including self-stigma. For this, a media company called “7 Media” was selected through a competitive bidding. It first reviewed similar campaigns previously implemented in Kazakhstan and other countries and suggested to move away from traditional short videos demonstrated on TV and in digital media. Instead of one or several public service announcements, 7 Media developed a script for a single 20-minute feature film having consultations with people living with HIV, health professionals, opinion leaders and celebrities. By the end of 2021, the film was shot. After post-production refinements, soundtrack recording, poster and teaser production, the film will be released and heavily promoted on popular websites and communities in social media networks. The tentative launch date of the film is 14 February 2022 and it's expected to reach at least 100,000 views by 31 March 2022.

This includes the most vulnerable groups and takes into account the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic crisis. The joint project is implemented by UN Women, UNFPA and UNESCO until 2024. UNESCO has the following activities under this project: 1) Conducting a comprehensive analysis of national education policies and programs based on the UNESCO Gender in Education Toolkit to promote gender equality in and through education 2) Conducting anti-discrimination and gender-lensed expertise of educational materials to identify negative gender and/ or other biases and prejudices in order to provide specific recommendations and proposals for mainstreaming gender equality in the curricula and methodologies 3) Developing training programme for teachers and educators in instilling key competencies and skills for mainstreaming gender equality in and through education, as well as promote the teaching of a culture of equality and non-discrimination at all levels of education. 4) Training of teachers and educators in instilling key competencies and skills for mainstreaming gender equality in and through education, as well as promote the teaching of a culture of equality and non-discrimination at all levels of education.

planEntities.name: Provide technical assistance to 2022 VAWG survey conduction (preparation, data collection, data analysis and presentation of the results)
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.3: Strengthened national systems of data collection and analysis for the formulation of evidence-based national human-rights and gender equality policies and development programmes aligned with international standards and SDGs
planEntities.description:
In 2021, technical assistance was provided to the Bureau of National Statistics to prepare for the 2022 VAWG survey in Kazakhstan. This assistance included two national consultations: one with governmental partners to discuss indicators on violence against women and girls, and another with non-governmental partners to prioritize areas for the survey. Recommendations gathered from these consultations informed the development of the survey's questionnaire and methodology.
Eight specialists from the Bureau of National Statistics received training on methodological issues related to the survey, facilitated by international and national consultants. Twelve weekly discussions further delved into data collection methodology, sampling, and questionnaire formats.
The methodology and data collection instruments were developed and refined during these sessions, culminating in the finalization and translation of the survey questionnaire into Kazakh. A pilot survey was planned to be conducted in the Almaty region from mid-October to the end of January.

Technical assistance provided to BNS on 2022 VAWG survey and 2024 MICS results dissemination - the data validated, analytical reports developed and launched to government.

planEntities.name: Advocating social and economic rights for the refugees, asylum seekers and stateless persons
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1.1: Improved capacity of authorities at national and sub-national level to provide effective social protection programmes and social services, including COVID-19 related services, with the focus on the most vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
As part of a working group on formulating the Migration Policy for 2023-27 and Social Code, UNHCR supported the Government by providing its technical expertise and recommendations for development of a Migration Policy for 2023-2027 and Social Code to enhance the national legal framework on asylum, refugee integration, extending their socio-economic rights including access to social protection services and allowance and facilitating naturalization. In the framework of Joint work plan with Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, UNHCR conducted sequence of capacity building workshops for representatives of the Ministry and local executive bodies, and representatives of national refugee status determination commission.  
Bilateral meetings were conducted with line Ministries (MLSP, MoH, MoJ, MoEd), Members of the Parliament, Human Rights Ombudsman and other stakeholders, where the current situation of refugees, asylum-seekers and stateless persons in Kazakhstan, existing gaps in national legislation which hinder them from having effective access to social protection, employment, healthcare, education services, and necessary actions to be taken by the Government to promote and ensure the full realization of all human rights for all persons without discrimination in order to meet Kazakhstan’s obligations under international conventions were discussed. UNHCR recommendations were reflected in the Kazakhstan’s Human Rights action plan for 2022-2024. 
The refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review (VNR) under SDG 10 “Granting access to basic socio-economic rights to refugees and asylum-seekers on an equal basis with permanently residing foreigners during their stay in Kazakhstan” and under SDG 16 “Ensuring the protection of the rights and interests of refugee and stateless children, ensuring security and access to social and educational services”. 

The situation of refugees in Kazakhstan along with challenges faced by them were submitted in the framework of UN Human Rights commissions (CERD and CAT) with recommendations to the Government of Kazakhstan to facilitate socio-economic integration and naturalization of refugees in line with international standards.

planEntities.name: Develop and test sustainable models to expand children and young people’s access to skills training and opportunities for participation in social innovation and entrepreneurship.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2: Improved knowledge and life skills of People of Kazakhstan, especially vulnerable groups for sustainable development, well-being and resilience.
planEntities.description:
2021: UNICEF, in partnership with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Ministry of Labor and Social Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan and the NGO “Community of Youth Workers”, is piloting a sustainable model for developing the skills of adolescents and youth for employment, social innovation and entrepreneurship. The program is based on the internationally recognized Upshift approach. In Kazakhstan, it started in 2020 under the name Samgau, combining online training to strengthen skills for life and employment, hands-on workshops on innovation, mentoring and small grants to pilot developed solutions. The program is presented in the form of modules that can be adapted in different conditions and contexts (general education and special schools, innovation laboratories, children's and youth centers, etc.).

In 2021, UNICEF, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Science of the Republic of Kazakhstan and regional education departments, implemented this program in 10 rural schools and 5 regional youth centers in Aktobe, Atyrau, East Kazakhstan, Karaganda and Kyzylorda regions.
At present, the next stage of expanding the program in other schools and youth centers of the country is being prepared by selecting schools and centers with local authorities.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

UNHCR
Achievements: In the WASH Sector, UNCT, and the partners have continued to ensure the provision of 23,272 m3 total water supplied daily in all 13 refugee settlements across Uganda. WFP’s advocacy initiatives in collaboration with the Uganda Parliamentary Forum on Social Protection and the Ministry of Gender Labour and social Development contributed to the re-instating of the Senior Citizen’s Grant budget for financial year 2023/2024 from 20% to 100% worth USD 26.4 million. planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

planEntities.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.
