planEntities.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

planEntities.name: Support to the Chapter 12 Commissions Project - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1 Capacity of institutions and systems at national and sub-national levels is strengthened to discharge their mandate (human rights, rule of law, access to justice) in a transparent and accountable manner.
planEntities.description:
Independent Commissions supporting democracy established under Chapter 12 of the Constitution and in tandem with their common as well as specific mandate, are expected to address above shortfalls by enhancing the quality of governance, encouraging transparency and accountability, fostering inclusion, advancing gender equality, strengthening justice and the rule of law, and ultimately leading to national unity, peace, and reconciliation. The Chapter 12 Commissions execute various mandates to enable the realisation of the Constitution’s objectives and aspirations. Collectively, the Chapter 12 Institutions serve the common purpose of contributing towards a democratic Zimbabwean society by steering the country towards constitutionalism as a shared value as set out in Section 233 of the Constitution.  Further, the Commissions interact significantly with members of the public and are responsible for the implementation and providing redress on various human rights issues in pursuit of the Bill of Rights in the Constitution.

The overall goal of project interventions is to strengthen the capacity of Constitutional Independent Commissions responsible for promoting democracy in Zimbabwe. The project concept recognises that the Commissions grapple with limited human and financial resources, limited collaboration and challenges in enforcing standards of constitutionalism and perceived limitations to independence. Project interventions seek to contribute to Zimbabwe’s achievement of the Global Goals for Sustainable Development (SDGs), specifically SDG 16, 5, 10 and 17. Support is anchored on SDG 16 to “promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels.” Core elements of SDG 17 such as encouraging effective partnerships, enhancing capacities; promoting sustainable technologies; enhancing available reliable data and mobilising financial resources will be integrated in the implementation of the project to attain common objectives in Section 233 of the Constitution, towards entrenching a culture of democracy, addressing governance deficits and specific needs of the independent Commissions.

planEntities.name: Support to the Parliament of Zimbabwe - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: People especially the vulnerable and marginalized  including women, girls, adolescents and youth are empowered to effectively participate, claim their rights  and benefit from service delivery by institutions at national and sub national levels (Executive, legislative and judiciary)
planEntities.description: The Constitution of Zimbabwe promulgated in 2013 expanded the powers of Parliament in line with the doctrine of the Separation of Powers, between and amongst the Judiciary, the Executive and Parliament as outlined in Section 119 conferring Parliament with the power to protect the Constitution and promote democratic governance in Zimbabwe. This aligned with the institutional reform dating back to 1996 when the Parliament of Zimbabwe embarked on a comprehensive reform programme to; strengthen the capacity of Members of Parliament and staff to contribute effectively to Parliament proceedings, improve internal systems and procedures of the house and, increase public participation in legislative process and enhance the oversight role with emphasis on promoting efficient management of public resources.  Over the years, the institution has been strategic in improving democratic governance and increasing its demand on accountability through embarking on a legislative reform drive to align all pieces of legislation to the Constitution in accordance to best practices.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Biodiversity and Ecosystems Management and Climate-Smart Landscapes in the Mid to Lower Zambezi Region of Zimbabwe - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description: This 6-year GEF project focuses on reducing key threats for wildlife, habitat, and livelihoods of local communities (poaching, IWT, deforestation, and impact of climate change) in one of the key biodiversity country’s hotspots – Lower Zambezi Valley. The project strategy aims to strengthen the capacities of law enforcement agencies to fight wildlife and forest crime (Component 1); strengthen PA and Community Wildlife Conservancy management for wildlife and woodlands(Component 2); build strong sustainable NRM capacity for local communities and districts in cooperation with private sector (Component 3); and promote effective knowledge management (Component 4) to achieve the project objective: to promote an integrated landscape approach to managing wildlife resources, carbon and ecosystem services in the face of climate change in the protected areas and community lands of the Mid to Lower Zambezi Regions of Zimbabwe. The total project funding is US$ 57,436,964, including GEF contribution of US$ 10,025,964 and co-financing – US$ 47,411,000. This project forms part of the GEF Programmatic Approach to Prevent the Extinction of Known Threatened Species and falls under the GEF Programme Global Partnership on Wildlife Conservation and Crime Prevention for Sustainable Development (9071). Under this programmatic framework, with the coordination through the programme steering committee, coordinated knowledge management and cross-fertilisation of the individual projects will be assured.

planEntities.name: Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: People especially the vulnerable and marginalized including women, girls, adolescents and youth are empowered to cope with climate change and build resilience for household food, and nutrition and water security demonstrating optimal attitudes, knowledge and attitudes.
planEntities.description: The UNDP Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund (UNDP-ZRBF) Programme began in May 2015 with the objective of increasing the capacities of communities to protect development gains in the face of multiple shocks and stressors. The programme is seven-year, donor-funded initiative, with an overall budget of close to USD 86 million. It aims to assist communities in proactively making decisions on responding to severe economic, environmental, climatic, and social shocks and stresses in Zimbabwe's fluid development context. By building the resilience of at-risk labour-endowed households and communities to the shocks and stresses that they face, the Programme reduces communities’ dependence on external assistance in times of crisis, including in areas that have been perpetual recipients of emergency relief assistance. The Fund is managed by UNDP as the Administrative Agent, with the main government partner being the Ministry of Land, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development (MoLAFWRD) under a national implementation modality. The programme is supported by funds from the European Union (EU), the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), the Swedish Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA), the Danish Government and UNDP. The expected result of the programme’s interventions is enhanced food security and livelihood diversification strategies in targeted communities that increase resilience to recurrent stresses/shocks.

The project will support vulnerable communities and institutions’ adaptation and resilience capacity to climate shocks. This project will support the development of climate resilient, multiple water use and renewable energy infrastructure in vulnerable communities of Zimbabwe to enable continued access to water for productive and household use, including during droughts and floods, and improved access to clean and affordable energy to support economic activities with the intention of supporting more sustainable livelihoods’ outcomes. The project will align and contribute towards the Government of Zimbabwe's (GoZ) climate change priorities outlined in various strategies, such as its National Development Strategy, Nationally Determined Contributions, and the National Climate Policy among others. The project has a multifaceted approach to climate adaptation and resilience building.

planEntities.name: Zimbabwe Hydrochloroflouro Carbon Phase-out Management Plan Stage II (HCFC Phase out) - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description:
2021-2029 Stage II of the Hydrochloroflouro carbon Phase-out Management Plan (HPMP) will build upon the experience gained during implementation of stage I. The project will focus on the reduction of HCFC-22 through the adoption of energy efficient, ozone- and climate friendly refrigerants in the RAC sector, consistent with the provisions of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol. The HPMP Stage-II is expected to phase-out a total of 10.01 ODP tonnes of HCFCs used in the RAC servicing sector by 1st January 2030. The successful completion of HPMP Stage II will result in reduction of emissions by approximately 18 giga tonnes CO2 equivalent. Further reductions in CO2 emissions will be achieved through good refrigeration servicing practices resulting in lower amounts of refrigerant being emitted into the atmosphere during equipment operation and maintenance and reduced direct emissions of CO2 from thermal power stations which provide the major sources of electrical power for the RAC appliances in the country.
The activities will focus on strengthening the HCFC licensing and quota system and building the capacities of customs officers; training technicians in good servicing practices and servicing with alternatives; supporting training institutions; and continue implementing a certification system to sustain the long-term capacity development of technicians. No servicing tail is anticipated after 2030. 
The project which will be implemented in collaboration with UNEP, the lead agency, is aligned to the NDS1 Priority Area on Environmental protection, climate resilience and natural  resource management and is designed to contribute to Zimbabwe’s new climate promise under the  Nationally Determined Contribution. The National Ozone Unit under the Ministry of Environment, Climate and Tourism Hospitality.

planEntities.name: CAPRI Reduction of Ozone Depleting Substance HFC-134a in Domestic Fridges - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description: The objective of the project is to eliminate the use of the Ozone Depleting Substance HFC-134a in the domestic manufacturing of refrigerators and freezers in Zimbabwe by the adoption of Isobutane (HC-600a) as refrigerant. HC-600a is non-ODS, low-GWP alternative to HFC-134a and adoption of HC-600a in Zimbabwe will contribute to reducing the environmental impact of refrigeration and freezer production on global warming both in terms of the manufacturing process and the operating life of the appliances. The project will modify the two existing lines, one each for refrigerators and freezers. It is envisaged that this project will result in annual emission reduction of about 14.5 MT of HFC-134a.

planEntities.name: Stockholm+50 Climate Promise - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description:
The project aims to support Zimbabwe to turn its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) pledges into action towards net-zero, climate resilient and sustainable development pathways. Building on the
results, experience and momentum of the first phase, the initiative aims to scale-up support to deliver and track ambitious climate action across sectors and thematic areas to achieve the bold targets set
forth in revised and enhanced NDCs. Climate Promise supports countries to mobilize both public and private investments to realize NDC targets while also simultaneously achieving the UN Sustainable
Development Goals. A key lesson from Climate Promise 1 was that more include NDCs tend to be more ambitious. Inclusive stakeholder engagement and strong partnerships will help deliver on NDCs while supporting all actors to be agents of change and continuing to advocate for ambition. The project will also empower marginalized groups, such as women and youth, to bring their unique voices, leadership, and skills to NDC implementation.
